For example, a common use of .. to move up one directory (to change the current working directory to be the parent of the current directory): $ cd .. . 这一项也常出现在运行当前目录中可执行文件的命令里，即在命令前加上前缀 ./ 。例如，要运行当前工作目录中的 a.out ，用户应输入： The . entry also commonly appears in commands that run an executable file from the current directory by prefixing the command with ./ For example, to run a.out in the current working directory, a user would type the following: $ ./a.out 许多点文件是各种应用程序的配置文件（或存放配置文件的目录）。这些点文件包含应用程序特定的选项，可以改变应用程序的行为。程序在刚启动时会读取并解析它的点文件内容，以配置自己的行为。其中许多点文件可以由用户编辑，以定制他们所运行程序的行为。下面是这类点文件的几个例子： Many dot files are configuration files (or directories of configuration files) for different applications. These dot files contain application-specific options that can change how the application behaves. Application dot file contents are evaluated by a program when it first starts up to configure its behavior. Many of these dot files can be edited by a user to customize the behavior of the programs they run. Here are a few examples of these types of dot files: .bashrc ：bash shell 程序的配置文件，用于设置环境变量、定义命令别名，…… .bashrc : a configuration file for the bash shell program set environment variables, define command aliases, …​ .vimrc ：vim 编辑器的配置文件，用于定义配色和语法高亮方案、编码，…… .vimrc : a configuration for the vim editor define color and highlighting scheme, encoding, …​ .xsession ：在终端上登录后启动的 X Window 管理器的配置文件，用于设置背景颜色、定义一些默认行为、启动某些应用程序，或启动某个特定的窗口管理器（它有自己的配置点文件） .xsession : # a configuration file for the X Windows managers that are started after login on a terminal. set background color, define some default behavior start some applications, start a specific window manager (which has its own config dot files) 17.14.1. .bashrc 文件 17.14.1. The .bashrc File Unix shell 配置文件（例如 Bash shell 的 .bashrc ）包含改变 shell 行为的条目。通常，系统管理员会为系统设置一个默认的 .bashrc 文件。不过，个人用户常常希望进一步定制自己的 shell，他们可以通过编辑自己主目录中的 .bashrc 来做到这一点。 Unix shell configuration files (e.g., .bashrc for the Bash shell) contain entries that change the behavior of the shell. Typically a system administrator sets up a default .bashrc file for the system. However, individual users often want to customize their shell further, and they can do so by editing the .bashrc in their home directory. 原书注 注意 shell 在刚启动时读取 .bashrc 文件。因此，对 .bashrc 文件的修改不会生效，除非用户运行 source .bashrc 或重新启动 bash 。 The shell reads the .bashrc file when it first starts up. Thus, changes to the .bashrc file do not take effect unless the user runs source .bashrc or restarts bash . 用户常做的两种修改是：改变 shell 环境变量的定义，以及添加命令别名（用户为自己常运行的命令设置的简写）。 shell 环境变量 （shell environment variable）被 shell 用来决定某些 shell 功能如何工作。要列出所有环境变量，可以用 env 命令；要列出某个特定环境变量的值，可以用 echo $env_var_name 。例如： Two common changes that users make are changing the definition of shell environment variables and adding command aliases (a user’s shorthand for commands that they commonly run). Shell environment variables are used by the shell to determine how certain shell features work. To list all the environment variables, use the env command, or list the value of a particular environment variable using echo $env_var_name . For example: 译注 示例中的 $env 应为 $ env （ $ 是提示符，后面应有空格），否则 shell 会把 $env 当作对变量 env 的引用。 $ echo $GROUP # list your default unix file group users $env # list value of all env vars (a lot) SHELL=/bin/bash GROUP=users ... PATH=/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:/bin ... PATH 环境变量特别有意思——它列出了一组目录，当用户在 shell 提示符下输入命令时，shell 会（按顺序）在这些目录中查找程序。例如，按照上面给出的 PATH 定义，如果用户输入 ls 命令，shell 会先在 /usr/bin 目录中查找它（shell 查找名为 ls 的可执行文件），找到就运行它。如果在 /usr/bin 中没找到 ls ，shell 接着在 /usr/local/bin 中找；如果还没找到，再到 /bin 中找；如果仍然没找到，shell 就打印一条错误信息，说找不到 ls 命令。正是因为有 PATH 环境变量，用户在运行 ls 这样的常用命令时才不需要写出完整的路径名！ The PATH environment variable is particularly interesting—​it lists the set of directories in which the shell searches (in order) for programs when the user enters a command at the shell prompt. For example, given the definition of PATH shown above, if a user enter the ls command, the shell will first look in the /usr/bin directory for it (the shell looks for an executable file named ls ) and runs it if found. If ls is not found in /usr/bin , then the shell next looks in /usr/local/bin , and if it is not found, it next look in /bin , and if it is still not found, the shell prints out error message saying that the ls command is not found. The PATH environment variable is the reason why users do not need to list the full path name to common commands, like ls , when they run them! 由于同一个程序可能在不同位置有多个版本， $PATH 中目录名的顺序决定了运行的是哪一个。用户可以用 which 命令查看自己运行的是程序的哪个版本。例如： Because there may be multiple versions of the same program in different locations, the order of the directory names in $PATH determines which one is run. A user can see which version of a program they are running using the which command. For example: $ which ls /usr/bin/ls 用户还可以在自己的 .bashrc 文件中重新定义 PATH ，以改变 Bash 搜索路径的顺序或添加额外的搜索路径。例如，如果 Sarita 自己编写了一些常用的实用程序，她可能想把它们放在主目录下一个名为 mybin 的目录中，然后更新她的 PATH 环境变量，把这个目录包括进去，这样她每次运行这些程序时就不必写出完整的路径名。她可以修改 bashrc （即 .bashrc ）文件中已有的 PATH 定义，或者添加一条像下面这样的额外 PATH 定义： Users can also redefine PATH in their .bashrc files to change the order of the paths searched by Bash or to add additional search paths. For example, if Sarita creates her own utility programs that she often runs, she may want to put them in a directory named mybin in her home directory and then update her PATH environment variable to include this directory so that she can run them without listing their full path name each time. She could do this by modifying the existing definition of PATH in her bashrc file or by adding an additional definition of PATH like the following: PATH=$PATH:/home/sarita/mybin 这条定义把她的 mybin 目录追加到她现有 PATH 环境变量的末尾（把 PATH 设为 PATH 的当前值再加上另一个路径 /home/sarita/mybin ）。 This definition appends her mybin directory to the end of her existing PATH environment variable (set PATH to the current value of PATH with another path called /home/sarita/mybin ). 当 Sarita 启动一个新的 Bash shell，或者在当前运行的 Bash shell 中输入 source ~/.bashrc 时，她的路径就会更新，包含 /home/sarita/mybin/ 。 When Sarita starts a new Bash shell, or if she types source ~/.bashrc in a currently running Bash shell, her path will be updated to include /home/sarita/mybin/ . 对 .bashrc 文件的另一种常见修改，是为常输入的命令添加简写别名，或者添加能确保命令总是带着特定命令行选项运行的别名。一个常见的例子是给命令 rm -i 起别名 rm 。这样就能确保每当在命令行上输入 rm 命令时，shell 实际执行的是 rm -i ，它在删除文件之前会提示用户确认是否真的要删除。下面是在 .bashrc 文件中为 rm 添加这个别名的方法： Another common modification to a .bashrc file is to add shorthand aliases for either commonly typed commands or commands that ensure they are always run with specific command line options. A common example is to alias the command rm -i to be rm . This ensures that anytime the rm command is entered on the command line, the shell actually executes rm -i , which prompts the user to confirm that they really want to delete the file before removing it. Here is how to add this alias for rm in a .bashrc file: alias rm="rm -i" # add alias for rm to double check 类似地，如果 Sam 经常运行命令 cd ~/classes/CS31/ ，他可能想像这样在自己的 .bashrc 中为这条命令添加一个 Bash 简写别名： Similarly, if Sam is frequently running the command cd ~/classes/CS31/ , he may want to add a shorthand Bash alias for this command to his .bashrc like this: alias gt31="cd ~/classes/CS31" # goto (cd) into my CS31 directory 然后 Sam 就可以开始使用这些新别名了。例如： Then Sam could start using these new aliases. For example: $ source ~/.bashrc # source: make bash re-evaluate .bashrc file $ rm notes # rm is now an alias for rm -i rm: remove regular file 'notes'? n $ ls classes/ letters/ notes projects/ $ rm notes rm: remove regular file 'notes'? y $ ls classes/ letters/ projects/ $ gt31 $ pwd /home/sam/classes/CS31 17.14.2. 参考资料 17.14.2. Shell Programming shell 脚本常用来把一组应该一起执行的命令组合在一起。 shell 脚本 （shell script）是一个可执行的文本文件，由一串 shell 命令组成，运行时按顺序执行这些命令。shell 还有循环和条件这样的语言结构，可以用来编写复杂而功能丰富的脚本。这些 shell 编程结构既可以用在命令行上，也可以用在 shell 脚本里。下面我们给出几个 Bash shell 编程的例子。其他 shell（例如 zsh 、 sh 、 tcsh ）有它们自己的 shell 编程语言语法，但提供的功能都差不多。 Shell scripts are often used to group a set of commands that should execute together. A shell script is an executable text file that consists of a sequence of shell commands that, when run, execute those commands in order. Shells also have language constructs such as loops and conditionals, which can be used to create complex featureful scripts. These shell programming constructs can also be used at the command line and in shell scripts. Below, we present a few examples of Bash shell programming. Other shells (e.g. zsh , sh , tcsh ) have their own shell programming language syntax, but they all provide similar functionality. Bash 脚本的第一行以一个特殊的注释开头： # 后跟一个感叹号 ! （bang），再跟执行该脚本文件内容的程序的路径。下面是一个简单 Bash 脚本的例子， simplescript.sh （注意，按照惯例，shell 脚本的文件名带 .sh 后缀）。 The first line of a Bash script starts with a special comment # followed by a bang ! and the path to the program that executes the contents of the script file. Below is an example of a simple Bash script, simplescript.sh (note that by convention shell scripts are named with a .sh suffix). #!/bin/bash pwd whoami date 在运行之前， simplescript.sh 文件需要被赋予可执行权限。用户可以运行 ls -l 检查它的权限，如果没有设置可执行权限，就用 chmod 设置。例如： Before it can be run, the simplescript.sh file needs to be given the executable permission. A user can check its permissions by running ls -l and set the executable permission using chmod if it is not set. For example: $ ls -l simplescript.sh -rw------- 1 sam users 31 Mar 28 18:26 simplescript.sh $ chmod u+x simplescript.sh $ ls -l simplescript.sh -rwx------ 1 sam users 31 Mar 28 18:26 simplescript.sh 一旦被标记为可执行，脚本就可以像任何可执行文件一样在命令行上运行，脚本中列出的命令会按顺序执行： Once it is marked as executable, the script can be run on the command line like any executable file, and the sequence of commands listed in the script will execute in order: $ ./simplescript.sh /home/sam/ sam Tue 28 Mar 2023 06:27:38 PM EDT Unix shell 程序支持迭代（即 for 和 while 循环）和条件（即 if-else）这样的语言结构。虽然这些结构可以在命令行上使用，但它们更常用在 shell 脚本中，用来描述更复杂的执行结构。shell 脚本还可以使用命令行参数和变量，这有助于脚本处理不同的输入值。 Unix shell programs support language constructs such as iteration (i.e., for and while loops) and conditionals (i.e., if-else). Although these constructs can be used at the command line, they are more commonly used in shell scripts to specify more complicated execution structure. Shell scripts can also make use of command line arguments and variables, which help the script work with different input values. 下面是几个使用了这些更高级特性的 Bash shell 脚本例子。第一个是 runsh.sh ，它把某个程序的计时运行重复若干次。在这个例子中，可执行文件名和重复运行的次数作为命令行参数传给脚本。这个例子还展示了如何检查命令行参数的某些约束。这里，程序可执行文件这个命令行参数是运行脚本所必需的，而重复运行的次数是一个可选的命令行参数（如果用户运行脚本时没有指定这个命令行选项，脚本就用默认值 5）。脚本用 if-elif 结构检查命令行选项。它还展示了一个 for 循环的例子，用来按调用者指定的次数重复运行。 Below are a couple examples of Bash shell scripts using some of these more advanced features. The first, runsh.sh , is a script that repeats some timed executions of a program. In this example, the executable file name and the number of executions to repeat are given as command line arguments to the script. This example also shows how to test for some constraints on command line arguments. Here the program executable command line argument is required to run the script, but the number of executions to repeat is an optional command line argument (the script uses a default value of 5 when a user runs the script without specifying this command line option). The script uses the if-elif construct to test for command line options. It also shows an example of a for loop used to repeat the number of runs specified by the caller. 译注 链接文字「runsh.sh」与实际文件名不一致，链接指向的、下文一直使用的都是 run.sh 。另外，下面的脚本实际用的是两个独立的 if 语句，并没有用到 elif 。 #!/bin/bash # this script performs a number of timed runs of a # program given as a required command line argument # the number of runs is an optional cmdln arg # script variable N for the number of runs # assigning N default value of 5 N=5 # get command line arguments # 1: name of program is required # 2: number of runs is optional # $@ is the array of command line args (like argv) # $# is the number of command line args (like argc) # get the program executable name # note: space between "[ $" and between "0 ]" is important! if [[ $# -eq 0 ]] then echo "Error, usage: ./run.sh ./a.out [num times]" exit 1 else PROG=$1 fi # if they gave the optional cmdln arg, set N to it if [[ $# -gt 1 ]] then N=$2 fi # it's useful to output some info about what is run: echo "running $PROG $N times: " date echo "======================= " # do N timed runs of PROG: for((n=1; n <= $N; n++)) do echo " " echo "run $n:" time $PROG done 这个脚本中有几点值得注意。第一，Bash 脚本中没有类型，因此要由用户根据值隐含的类型恰当地使用它们。 There are a few things to note in this script. First, there are no types in Bash scripts, so it is up to the user to use values appropriately based on their implied types. 第二，注意 Bash shell 变量用 = 运算符赋值，用 $var_name 引用它们的值： Second, note that Bash shell variables are set using = operator and their values are referenced using $var_name : N=5 # set N to 5 n <= $N # use value of N 第三，注意在 Bash 脚本中访问命令行参数的语法： Third, note the syntax for accessing command line arguments in the Bash script: $@ 是命令行参数的数组，类似于 C 中的 argv 。 $@ is the array of command line arguments, which is similar to argv in C. 译注 与 C 的 argv 不同， $@ 只包含 $1 、 $2 、……，不包含脚本名；脚本名在 $0 中。译者在 Mac 上用 bash argt.sh x y 验证： $@ 展开为 x y ， $# 为 2， $0 是脚本路径。这与下一条所说 $# 不计脚本名是一致的。 $# 是命令行参数的个数，类似于 C 中的 argc ，区别是 Bash 脚本文件名不算作参数之一（即不带命令行参数运行的 Bash 脚本， $# 的值为 0 ；而不带命令行参数运行的 C 程序， argc 的值为 1）。 $# is the number of command line arguments, which is similar to argc in C except that the name of the Bash script file does not count as one of the arguments (i.e., a Bash script run with no command line arguments has a value of 0 for $# , whereas a C program run with no command line arguments has a value of 1 for argc ). 第四，注意 if-else 的语法及其一般形式： Fourth, note the if-else syntax, and its general form: if [[ cond ]] then # if true stmts else # if false stmts fi Bash 用 then 、 else 和 fi 分别表示 if 块的开始、else 块的开始和 if-else 语句的结束。 [[ 和 ]] 符号用来括起条件语句，它们与条件之间的空格非常重要（没有这些空格，Bash 就无法正确解析这条语句）。条件运算符的语法是： -gt 表示大于， -lt 表示小于， -eq 表示等于，其他运算符也使用类似的记法。 Bash uses then , else , and fi to denote the start of the if block, the start of the else block, and the end of the if-else statement. The [[ and ]] symbols are used to denote the conditional statement, and the space chars between them and the condition are very important (without these Bash will not correctly parse this statement). The conditional operator syntax is -gt represents greater than, -lt represents less than, -eq represents equal to, and others use similar notation. 最后，注意 for 循环的语法与 C 中的 for 循环类似：for 循环体用 do 和 done 标出， init; cond; step 三部分写在双括号内。下面是这类 Bash for 循环的一般形式（Bash 实际上有不止一种形式的 for 循环）： Finally, note the syntax of the for loop is similar to for loops in C, where the body of the for loop is denoted by do and done and contains the init; cond; step parts inside double parentheses. Here is the general form of this type of Bash for loop (Bash actually has more than one form of for loop): for ((init; cond; step)) do # for loop body statements done 下面是 run.sh 脚本的几次运行示例： Below are some sample runs of the run.sh script: $ ./run.sh Error, usage: ./run.sh ./a.out [num times] $ ./run.sh ./myprog 2 running ./myprog 2 times: Wed Mar 29 11:34:34 AM EDT 2023 ======================= run 1: myprog result = 300000 real 0m0.060s user 0m0.003s sys 0m0.006s run 2: myprog result = 300000 real 0m0.059s user 0m0.003s sys 0m0.006s $ ./run.sh ./myprog running ./myprog 5 times: Wed Mar 29 11:34:37 AM EDT 2023 ======================= run 1: myprog result = 300000 real 0m0.057s user 0m0.008s sys 0m0.000s run 2: myprog result = 300000 real 0m0.057s user 0m0.004s sys 0m0.004s run 3: myprog result = 300000 real 0m0.057s user 0m0.010s sys 0m0.000s run 4: myprog result = 300000 real 0m0.056s user 0m0.009s sys 0m0.000s run 5: myprog result = 300000 real 0m0.055s user 0m0.004s sys 0m0.004s 使用 run.sh 这类产生大量输出的脚本时，把输出保存到一个文件中，等运行结束后再查看，常常很有帮助。一种做法是用 I/O 重定向 把脚本的输出重定向到文件。下面是用命令行选项 ./myprog 和 10 运行 run.sh 脚本的例子，它把脚本的 stderr 和 stdout 输出重定向到一个名为 results 的文件： Often when using scripts like run.sh that produce a lot of output, it is helpful to save the output to a file that can be examined after completion. One way to do this is to use I/O redirection to redirect the script’s output to a file. Below is an example run of the run.sh script with the command line options ./myprog and 10 that redirects its stderr and stdout ouput to a file named results : $ ./run.sh ./myprog 10 &> results 除了支持类似 C for 循环的语法之外，Bash 还支持遍历一组元素的 for 循环语法。下面列出的 Bash 脚本 forloops.sh 中有几个这类 for 循环的例子，展示了获得被遍历元素集合的不同方式。 In addition to supporting syntax similar to a C for loop, Bash supports for loop syntax for iterating over a set of elements. The forloops.sh Bash script (listed below), has a few examples of this type of for loop, showing different ways in which the set of elements iterated over is obtained. #!/bin/bash echo "for loop over set of values" # iterate over a set of given values # repeats once for each element in the list for i in cat dog bunny do echo "next animal is: $i" done echo echo "for loop over sequence" # {1..5} is the set of values in the sequence: 1,2,3,4,5 # this iterates over "infilei" where i: 1,2,3,4,5 for i in infile{1..5} do echo "next file is: $i" done echo echo "for loop over set created with ls" # this iterates over all the files in a subdirectory named input # $(ls input/): creates a set of value that are all the file # and directory names in the input/ subdirectory for i in $(ls input/) do echo "next input/ file is: $i" done 运行时，输出为： When run, the output is: $ ./forloops.sh for loop over set of values next animal is: cat next animal is: dog next animal is: bunny for loop over sequence next file is: infile1 next file is: infile2 next file is: infile3 next file is: infile4 next file is: infile5 for loop over set created with ls next input/ file is: albums next input/ file is: artists next input/ file is: bands next input/ file is: songs 一般来说，把 Unix 命令与循环、条件、命令行、变量等 Bash shell 语言结构结合起来，用户就能编写出强大的 shell 脚本来完成复杂的操作。本节只展示了几个例子。更多信息请参阅 Bash shell 编程指南。 In general, combining Unix commands with Bash shell language constructs like loops, conditionals, command lines, and variables, allow a user to write powerful shell scripts to perform complex actions. We have shown just a few examples in this section. See a Bash shell programming guide for more information. 17.15.1. 参考资料 17.15.1. h: 从非 Unix 操作系统用 SSH 远程连接
x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/Appendix2/ssh_scp.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 17.3. Remote Access 用户常常想远程登录到 Unix 机器，或者把文件从一台机器复制到另一台机器。安全外壳（Secure Shell，SSH）可以用来从另一台运行 Unix、或运行 Windows 和 MacOS 等其他操作系统的机器远程登录到一台 Unix 机器。安全复制（Secure Copy，SCP）可以用来把文件从一个系统复制到另一个系统。 Often times users want to remotely log into to Unix machines or copy files from one machine to another. Secure Shell (SSH) is useful for remotely logging into a Unix machine from another machine that running Unix or running another operating systems like Windows and MacOS. And Secure Copy (SCP) is useful for copying files from one system to another. 17.3.1. 远程登录 17.3.1. Remote Login 可以用 ssh 命令登录到远程 Unix 机器。 ssh 在你运行 ssh 的主机与你连接到的远程机器之间提供加密的通信。 You can log into a remote Unix machine using the ssh command. ssh provides encrypted communication between the host machine that you run ssh from and the remote machine that you connected to. 要通过 SSH 登录到远程机器，写出远程机器上的用户名，后跟这台机器的互联网主机名。例如，如果 Sarita 想从她的笔记本电脑远程登录到 cs.college.edu 网络上的机器 cs87 中她的 sarita 账户，她会输入下面的命令（为了明确每条命令在哪台机器上执行， laptop$ 提示符是 Sarita 笔记本电脑上的 shell 提示符， cs87$ 提示符是远程机器上的 shell 提示符）。 To SSH into a remote machine, list the username on the remote machine followed by the machine’s Internet hostname. For example, if Sarita wanted to remotely log into her sarita account on the machine cs87 on cs.college.edu network from her laptop, she would enter the following command (to clarify which machine is executing each of these commands, the laptop$ prompt is the shell prompt on Sarita’s laptop, and the cs87$ prompt is the shell prompt on the remote machine). laptop$ ssh sarita@cs87.cs.college.edu 如果连接成功，远程机器上运行的 ssh 服务器会要求用户输入其在那台机器上的密码。一旦成功远程登录， ssh 就会在远程机器上启动一个 Unix shell，用户可以通过它访问远程系统上的文件并运行应用程序。 If successfully connected, the ssh server running on the remote machine will ask the user to enter their password on that machine. Once successfully remotely logged in, ssh starts a unix shell on the remote machine through which the user can access files and run applications on the remote system. laptop$ ssh sarita@cs87.cs.college.edu sarita@cs.college.edu's password: cs87$ 从非 Unix 操作系统用 SSH 远程连接 Remotely connecting with SSH from non-Unix OSs 要从非 Unix 系统 ssh 到 Unix 系统，你可能需要先在自己的机器上安装一个 SSH 客户端，不过它很可能已经装好了。然后你需要一个终端窗口来运行 ssh 。在 MacOS 上，打开并使用终端（Terminal）应用程序。在 Windows 机器上，可以使用 PowerShell，或者安装并使用 Putty 。 To ssh into a Unix system from a non-Unix system you may need to first install an SSH client on your machine, however it is likely already installed. You then need a terminal window to run ssh On MacOS, open and use the terminal application. On Windows machines, you can either use PowerShell or install and use Putty . 17.3.2. 远程文件复制 17.3.2. Remote File Copy 如果你想在远程系统的机器之间传输文件，可以使用 scp （secure copy，安全复制）。 scp 命令看起来与 cp 命令很像，只是源或目标之一被指定为远程机器上的路径名。与 ssh 一样， scp 要求用户输入远程机器上该用户的密码，以便访问远程系统上被复制或要复制到的文件。如果 scp 成功，它会显示关于所复制文件的一些统计信息，包括文件的字节数、平均传输速率和总传输时间。 If you want to transfer files to or from a machine on a remote system you can use scp (secure copy). The scp command looks much like the cp command except that one of either the source or the destination is specified as a pathname on a remote machine. Like, ssh , scp requires the user to type the password of the user on the remote machine to allow access to the files being copied or from on the remote system. If scp is successful, it displays some statistics about the file being copied including the size of the file in bytes, the average transfer rate, and the total transfer time. 例如，要把名为 prog.c 的文件从你家里的机器复制到 cs87.cs.college.edu 机器上的 sam 用户那里，你会输入： For example, to copy the file named prog.c from your home machine to the sam user on the cs87.cs.college.edu machine, you would type: # scp prog.c into home directory on cs87.cs.college.edu laptop$ scp prog.c sam@cs87.cs.college.edu:. sam@cs.college.edu's password: prog.c 100% 282 56.4KB/s 00:00 # scp prog.c into CS31 subdirectory on cs87.cs.college.edu laptop$ scp prog.c you@cslab.cs.college.edu:./CS31/. sam@cs.college.edu's password: prog.c 100% 282 56.4KB/s 00:00 你也可以把远程路径名作为 scp 的源命令行参数，把文件从远程机器复制到本地机器。例如，要把远程系统上 sarita 用户文件中的远程文件 unix_notes/basics 复制到你家里机器上的当前目录，这样做： You can also copy files from a remote machine to a local machine using the remote path name as the source command line argument to scp . For example, to copy a remote file unix_notes/basics from the sarita user’s files on the remote system to the current directory on your home machine, do: laptop$ scp sarita@cs87.cs.college.edu:./unix_notes/basics ./ sarita@cs.college.edu's password: basics 100% 78 86.3KB/s 00:00 如果你想传输许多文件，先把它们打包成单个归档文件会很有用。然后复制这个归档文件，再解包得到那些文件。此外，在传输之前压缩文件会减少总的传输时间。 tar 工具是打包和解包文件的一种方式， gzip 和 bzip2 是文件压缩工具的两个例子。关于使用 tar 和文件压缩的更多信息，见 归档与压缩一节 。 If you want to transfer many files, it is useful to package them up into a single archive file first. Then copy over the archive file, and unpack it to get the set of files. In addition, compressing the file before transfer will decrease the total transfer time. The tar utility is one way to pack and unpack files, and gzip and bzip2 are two examples of file compression utilities. See [targzbz] for more information on using tar and file compression. 原书旁注 · 生成 SSH 密钥（Generating SSH Keys） 远程连接 Linux 机器时，你不需要生成 ssh 密钥；默认情况下，ssh 用你在所连接的远程系统上的用户名和密码进行身份认证。然而，对于某些网站（例如 GitHub），你可能需要把你的 ssh 公钥上传到它的 Web 服务器上，才能访问它的某些资源。 ssh 使用公钥-私钥加密来加密要通过网络连接安全发送的数据。ssh 使用的这类加密称为非对称加密：你主机（客户端）上的私钥用来加密通过网络发送给服务器的外发数据，服务器用你的公钥来解密你的消息。服务器在把响应通过网络发回给你之前，用你的公钥加密它，ssh 客户端收到消息后用你的私钥解密。为了让这一切能够工作，你首先需要创建一对 ssh 公钥-私钥，然后把公钥上传到服务器（并把私钥私密地保存在你的客户端机器上）。 要生成 ssh 密钥，运行 ssh-keygen -t rsa 。它会提示你输入密钥的存放位置（默认在你的 ~/.ssh 目录中），并要求你为正在生成的 ssh 密钥输入一个口令（passphrase）： $ ssh-keygen -t rsa Generating public/private rsa key pair. ... 如果成功，它会在你的 ~/.ssh 目录中创建两个新文件： id_rsa ：你的私钥（不要分享这个） id_rsa.pub ：你的公钥（可以上传到 Web 服务器的那个） 然后你可以把 id_rsa.pub 文件的内容复制粘贴到需要它的 Web 服务器上。 你也可以用这种方法把公钥上传到远程主机上，以便用密钥口令而不是密码来连接。 For remotely connecting to a Linux machine, you don’t need to generate ssh keys; by default ssh uses your username and password on the remote system you are connecting to for authentication. However, for some websites, like GitHub, you may need to upload your public ssh key to its web server to access some of its resources. ssh uses public-private key encryption to encrypting data to be sent securely over a network connection. The type of encryption ssh uses is known as asymmetric encryption, where your private key on your host machine (the client) is used to encrypt outgoing data that is sent over the network to a server, and the server uses your public key to decrypt your message. The server encrypts its response using your public key before sending it back to you on the network, and when the ssh client receives the message it is decrypted using your private key. In order to get this to work, you first need to create an ssh public-private key pair, and then upload your public key to the server (and keep your private key private on your client machine). To generate an ssh key, run ssh-keygen -t rsa . It will prompt you for a key-location, which by default is in your ~/.ssh directory, and ask you to enter your passphrase for the ssh key you are generating: $ ssh-keygen -t rsa Generating public/private rsa key pair. ... If successful, this creates two new files in your ~/.ssh directory: id_rsa : your private key (don’t share this one) id_rsa.pub : your public key (the one you can upload to web servers) You can then copy and paste the contents of your id_rsa.pub file to the web server that requires it. You can also use this method to upload your public key to remote hosts to connect using your key passphrase rather than your password. 译注 · SSH 实际上怎样加密数据 上面对加密过程的描述并不准确。按 SSH 传输层协议规范 RFC 4253 ，连接建立时双方通过密钥交换（例如 Diffie-Hellman）生成一次性的 会话密钥 ，之后的数据用协商好的 对称加密 算法加密，并用由共享密钥算出的 MAC 保护完整性。你的公钥-私钥对是在这条加密通道建立之后，用于 身份认证 的（让服务器确认你持有与已登记公钥相配的私钥），并不是用来加密通信内容的，服务器也不会用你的公钥加密响应。 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· SSH 密钥的新默认值 Ed25519 成为默认 ：OpenSSH 9.5 起， ssh-keygen 默认生成 Ed25519 密钥（不再需要也不必写 -t rsa ）。发布说明指出，Ed25519 公钥体积小、用起来很方便，OpenSSH 自 6.5 版（2014 年 1 月）起就已支持。生成的文件相应地叫 id_ed25519 和 id_ed25519.pub 。 OpenSSH 9.5 发布说明 RSA/SHA-1 签名默认停用 ：OpenSSH 8.8 起默认禁用使用 SHA-1 哈希的 RSA 签名，因为 SHA-1 已被攻破。不过发布说明也指出，对大多数用户这一变化是无感的，不需要替换现有的 ssh-rsa 密钥，它们会自动改用 RSA/SHA-256/512 签名。 OpenSSH 8.8 发布说明 17.3.3. 参考资料 17.3.3. References 更多信息参见： For more information see: 手册页（例如 man ssh ） The man pages (e.g., man ssh ) linuxhandbook.com 上的 ssh 基础 ssh basics from linuxhandbook.com Putty Putty VNC Viewer VNC Viewer

b: Dive Into Systems 中英对照
x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/Appendix2/sysinfo.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 17.16. Getting System Information 有许多工具可以获取系统状态信息： top 和 htop 动态地提供系统资源及其使用情况（例如 CPU 和内存使用）的摘要信息； /proc 和 /sys 伪文件系统包含系统当前状态的详细信息（还有 lscpu 、 lsmem 和 lsgpu 这样的命令，以更易读的形式显示 /proc 和 /sys 中的部分信息）。 There are many tools available for obtaining information about the system’s state: top and htop provide dynamic summary information about system resources and resource use, such as CPU and memory use; and the /proc and /sys pseudo file systems contain detailed information about the current state of the system (there are also commands like lscpu , lsmem , and lsgpu that display some information from /proc and /sys in an easier to read form). 译注 · macOS /proc 、 /sys 和 lscpu 都是 Linux 特有的。译者在 macOS 上验证，这两个目录都不存在，系统也没有 lscpu 。在 Mac 上可以用 sysctl （参见第 11 章、第 14 章的译注）、 top 或「活动监视器」查看类似信息。 17.16.1. top 与 htop 17.16.1. top and htop 在命令行上运行 top 或 htop ，可以动态查看系统状态的摘要信息。按 q 退出 top 和 htop 。两者都显示内存和 CPU 使用信息，但 htop 比 top 更多地用图形显示某些使用统计数据，尤其是用图表显示内存使用情况和每个核心的 CPU 利用率。两者默认都会列出当前占用 CPU 时间最多的任务的信息。任务（task）是 Linux 对进程或线程的统称。这些工具运行时每秒更新一次，显示系统使用摘要数据的变化。注意，由于显示每秒更新一次，进程的排列顺序会随着它们的执行、根据各自占用的 CPU 时间而变化。两者也都高度可配置，可以显示关于进程和系统状态的不同信息。 Running top or htop at the command line provides dynamic summary information about the state of the system. Typing q quits top and htop . Both show memory and CPU usage information, but htop displays some of the usage statistics more graphically than top does, particularly showing memory usage and each core’s CPU utilization as a graph. Both also, by default, list information about the tasks currently using the most CPU time. A task is the Linux generic term for either a process or a thread, These tools update every second as they run, showing changes in summary system use data. Note that as the display updates every second, the ordering of processes will change as they execute according to how much CPU time they are using. Both are also very configurable to display different information about processes and system state. 图 1 是 htop 的一张截图示例。 Figure 1 shows an example screenshot from htop . 图 1. htop 截图示例 Figure 1. Example htop screenshot). 在最顶部， htop 以带百分比标注的使用率图表显示这个系统上 12 个核心各自当前的 CPU 使用率，接着是当前的内存使用情况（ Mem ）、平均 CPU 负载的摘要信息（ Load average ）、系统中运行的任务总数（ Tasks ）和线程总数（ thr ），以及交换分区的使用信息（ Swp ）。它们下面是系统中占用 CPU 时间最多的任务列表。注意，在 图 1 中，排在前五位的任务都是运行 a.out 无限循环程序的进程，所以它们占用大量 CPU 时间也就不足为奇了。显示界面的底部是一排功能键，用来以不同方式调整所显示的数据。 At the very top, htop displays the current CPU usage of each of the 12 cores on this system as a usage graph annotated with percentages, followed the current memory usage ( Mem ), summary information about the average CPU load ( Load average ), the total number of tasks ( Tasks ) and threads ( thr ) running in the system, and information about swap partition usage ( Swp ). Under these is a listing of the tasks using the most CPU time in the systems. Note that in Figure 1 the top five tasks listed are processes running the a.out infinite loop program, and thus they are unsurprisingly using up a lot of CPU time. At the bottom of the display are function keys for changing the data presented in different ways. top 程序显示的数据与 htop 非常相似（只是顶部没有图形显示），它同样提供了一个界面，可以在运行时以不同方式调整所显示的数据。例如，用户在 top 中按「1」键，就可以查看每个核心的 CPU 使用率。 The top program displays very similar data to htop (but without the graphical displays at the top), and it similarly provides an interface to change the data presented in different ways as it runs. For example, users can view the CPU usage per core in top by hitting the “1” key. 除了运行时高度可配置之外， top 和 htop 都有大量命令行选项，用来配置显示什么以及怎样显示。例如， top 默认不显示每个线程的统计数据（只显示每个进程的），但用 -H 命令行选项运行时就会显示。 In addition to being very configurable when running, both top and htop have a large number of command line options to configure what they show and how they show it. For example, by default top does not show per-thread statistics (only per-process), but by running with the -H command line option it will. 17.16.2. /proc 与 /sys 17.16.2. /proc and /sys /proc 和 /sys 是伪文件系统，通过它们可以获取操作系统关于系统中运行的进程的信息，以及关于系统状态和资源（例如设备、总线、内存、CPU）的信息。 伪文件系统 （pseudo file system）看起来像一个文件系统，可以通过文件系统接口与之交互，但它实际上并不存储文件数据。相反，用户通过 /proc 和 /sys 中的伪文件与操作系统交互；读取 /proc 和 /sys 中的伪文件（例如 cat /proc/filename ）是从操作系统获取系统状态信息的一种方式。 /proc 和 /sys 中的某些文件也可以写入，这可以触发操作系统改变某项策略，或改变与系统中某个特定进程或资源相关的状态。例如，像 GDB 这样的调试器可能会写入与被调试进程相关的某个 /proc 文件来设置断点，或者读取某个 /proc 文件来检查其栈内存的当前内容。 /proc and /sys are pseudo file systems that provide access to operating system information about process running in the system and to information about system state and resources (e.g., devices, buses, memory, cpu). A pseudo file system looks like a file system and can be interacted with via the filesystem interface, but it doesn’t actually store file data. Instead, through pseudo files in /proc and /sys a user can interact with the operating system; reading from pseudo files in /proc and /sys (e.g., cat /proc/filename ) is a way to obtain information about system state from the OS. Some files in /proc and /sys can also be written to, which can trigger the OS to change a policy or change the state associated with a particular process or resource in the system. For example, a debugger like GDB may write into a /proc file associated with the process it is debugging to set a breakpoint, or it may read from a /proc file to examine the current contents of its stack memory. 下面是读取 /proc 中的文件可以获得的几类信息的例子。在关于 多核处理器上的缓存 的那一节中，我们展示了一些从 /sys 中的文件获取 CPU 缓存信息的例子。 Below are a few examples of the type of information that can be obtained from reading files in /proc . In our section on caching on multicore processors we show some examples of how to get information about CPU caches from files in /sys . 系统中运行的每个进程在 /proc 中都有一个以其进程 ID 命名的子目录，里面有许多伪文件，作为访问该进程状态的接口。例如，假设我们想从 /proc 中获取像下面这样在后台运行的 a.out 进程的一些信息： Each process running in the system has a subdirectory in /proc named with its process ID that contains many pseudo files that are interfaces to the process’s state and status. For example, suppose we want to get some information from /proc about the a.out process running in the background like this: $ ./a.out & 我们先运行 ps 命令得到它的进程 ID： We first get its process ID by running the ps command: $ ps PID TTY TIME CMD 246477 pts/0 00:00:00 bash 246541 pts/0 00:01:59 a.out 246879 pts/0 00:00:00 ps 然后就可以用文件系统命令，通过进程 ID 246541 获取正在运行的 a.out 程序的信息（注意，你只能访问 /proc 中属于你自己拥有的进程的子目录）。例如： We can then use file system commands to get information about the running a.out program using its process ID 246541 (and note that you can only access subdirectories in /proc associated with processes that you own). For example: $ ls /proc/246541/ # list all pseudo files for this process $ cat /proc/246541/comm # list its executable file name $ cat /proc/246541/status # list its status information status 伪文件列出了大量信息，其中包括： The status pseudo file lists a lot of information, including the following: State: R (running) # its state: running, blocked, exited, ... VmStk: 132 kB # size of its stack (in its virtual memory (Vm)) nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches: 59593 # context switches due to OS CPU scheduling 这个示例 a.out 程序包含一个无限循环；随着它持续运行，上下文切换的次数不断增加，它的状态始终是 R （表示运行），直到用 CTRL-C 把它杀死为止。 This example a.out program contains an infinite loop; as it continues to run, the number of context switches increases, and its state will always be R (for running), until it is killed with CTRL-C . /proc （以及 /sys ）中的伪文件也可以用来从操作系统获取全系统范围资源的信息。下面是从 /proc 获取信息的一些例子（在存储器层次结构一章中，我们展示了一个从 /sys 获取 多核处理器上的缓存 信息的例子）： Pseudo files in /proc (and in /sys ) can also be used to get information from the OS about system-wide resources. Here are some examples of getting information from /proc (in the Memory Hierarchy chapter we show an example of getting caching on multicore processors from /sys ): cat /proc/meminfo # info about system memory and its current use cat /proc/cpuinfo # info about each hyperthreaded core cat /proc/swaps # info about swap partitions and their use cat /proc/stat # lots of system statistics Linux 提供了一些实用工具，把 /proc 和 /sys 中的部分信息汇总成一种通常比直接读取 /proc 和 /sys 中的文件更易读的形式。 lshw 、 lscpu 和 lsgpu 就是这类命令的例子，它们分别列出机器上的系统硬件、CPU 和 GPU 设备的信息。 Linux provides utilities that summarize some information in /proc and /sys in a form that is often easier to read than the output from directly reading files in /proc and /sys . The lshw , lscpu , and lsgpu are example commands that list information about the system hardware, the CPU, and GPU devices on a machine. 例如，要知道一台机器上物理核心的数量，用户可以运行 lscpu ： For example, to find the number of physical cores on a machine a user cat run lscpu : CPU(s): 32 On-line CPU(s) list: 0-31 Thread(s) per core: 2 Core(s) per socket: 8 Socket(s): 2 输出表明这台机器上总共有 16 个物理核心（2 个插槽/芯片，每个插槽/芯片 8 个核心）。它还表明每个核心都是双超线程的（ Thread(s) per core 为 2），使这台 16 核机器在操作系统看来是一台 32 核机器。请注意，较新的 Intel 架构引入了 P 核（性能核）和 E 核（能效核）。对于这些架构，列出的 CPU 总数可能大于物理核心数乘以插槽数再乘以硬件线程数。更多信息请参见 第 14 章 。 The output shows that there are a total of 16 physical cores on the machine (2 Sockets/chips, and 8 cores per socket/chip). It also shows that each core is dual-hyperthreaded (2 Thread(s) per core ), to make the 16-core machine appear to the operating system a 32-core machine. Please note that newer Intel architectures introduce P-cores and E-cores. For these architectures, the total listed CPU(s) may be higher than the number of physical cores multiplied by the number of sockets and hardware threads. See Chapter 14 for more information. 17.16.3. 参考资料 17.16.3. You can read manual pages using the Unix man command. The apropos command can be used to search for Unix commands and library functions related to a topic supplied by a search pattern given as its command line argument. Many Unix and C library man pages are also available online, such as at kernel.org . Unix 手册分为几个部分（section）。前三部分最常用。 The Unix manual is divided into several sections. If c is not an unsigned char value, or EOF, the behavior of these functions is undefined. RETURN VALUE The value returned is that of the converted letter, or c if the conversion was not possible. CONFORMING TO ANSI C, BSD 4.3 BUGS The details of what constitutes an uppercase or lowercase letter depend on the current locale. For example, the default C locale does not know about umlauts, so no conversion is done for them. In some non-English locales, there are lowercase letters with no corresponding uppercase equivalent; the German sharp s is one example. NAME、DESCRIPTION 和 RETURN VALUE 这几部分给出了函数功能的简短和详细描述，说明了它的参数是什么，以及它返回什么： The NAME, DESCRIPTION, and RETURN VALUE, parts give short and long descriptions of what the function does, what its parameters are, and what it returns: NAME toupper, tolower - convert letter to upper or lower case DESCRIPTION toupper() converts the letter c to upper case, if possible. RETURN VALUE The value returned is that of the converted letter, or c if the conversion was not possible. SYNOPSIS 部分指出使用这个函数是否需要包含某些头文件，以及编译可执行文件时是否需要显式链接某些库。它还列出了完整的函数原型： The SYNOPSIS part indicates if any header files need to be included to use this function, and if it is necessary to explicitly link in any libraries to compile an executable. It also lists the full function prototype: SYNOPSIS #include < ctype.h > int toupper (int c); 这个概要表明，要调用 toupper ， .c 文件必须 #include <ctype.h> ，而调用这个函数的程序不需要显式链接任何库。 The synopsis indicates that to call toupper a .c file must #include <ctype.h> , and that no library needs to be explicitly linked into a program that calls this function. SEE ALSO 部分列出了其他相关的函数。然后可以对它们运行 man 来进一步了解（例如 man isalpha ）。 The SEE ALSO part lists other related functions. You can then run man on these to learn more about them (e.g., man isalpha ). SEE ALSO isalpha(3), setlocale(3), locale(7) 手册页有时还包含如何调用函数的示例。 Man pages sometimes include examples of how to call the function. 17.2.2. apropos 17.2.2. apropos 有时你并不知道想用的函数或命令叫什么名字。 apropos 命令在 Unix 手册页的描述中搜索与你作为命令行选项给出的搜索模式匹配的关键词，并列出它认为合适的命令/函数。例如，如果你想找到一个获取当前工作目录的函数的名字，但记不起这个函数叫什么，可以问 apropos： Sometimes you do not know the name of a function or command that you want to use. The apropos command searches Unix manual page descriptions for key words that match the search pattern you list as a command line option and lists commands/functions that it thinks are appropriate matches. Unix Editors Unix 系统上通常装有好几种不同的编辑程序，用来创建和编辑文本文件。文本文件常用于程序源代码、程序数据和文档。Unix 不会根据文件后缀来解释文件内容的含义。不过，用户通常会为许多文件采用后缀命名惯例。例如， .c 后缀是 C 源代码文件的命名惯例（例如 myprog.c ）， .h 后缀是 C 头文件的命名惯例（例如 stdio.h ）。 Typically, there are often several different editing programs installed on Unix systems to create and edit text files. Text files are commonly used for program source code, program data, and documentation. Unix does not interpret file suffixes to mean anything about a file’s content. However, users typically use suffix naming conventions for many of their files. For example, a .c suffix is the naming convention for C code source files (e.g., myprog.c ), and a .h suffix is the naming convention for C header files (e.g., stdio.h ). 虽然不必学会每一个编辑程序，但用户至少应该学会一个，以便在 Unix 系统上创建和编辑文件。 While it is not important to learn every editor program, users should learn at least one to create and edit files on Unix systems. Vim（vi improved，改进版 vi）和 Emacs 是大多数系统上都有的两个编辑器，而 vim（或 vi）在每个 Unix 系统上都一定有。这些编辑器采用基于文本的界面，而不是基于图形界面（不过两者也都有图形界面版本）。一般来说，与使用菜单和指点式界面的图形界面编辑器相比，基于文本的编辑器需要多花一点功夫来学习。然而，基于文本的编辑器运行时通常占用更少的计算机资源，在远程连接到你想编辑文件的系统时尤其有用。 Vim (vi improved) and Emacs are two examples of editors that are available on most systems, and vim (or vi) is always available on every Unix system. These editors have a text-based interface rather than a GUI-based interface (although both have GUI-based versions as well). In general, text-based editors require a bit more effort to learn to use than GUI-based editors that use menus and point-and-click interfaces. However, text-based editors typically use fewer computer resources to run, and they are particularly useful when remotely connected to systems on which you want to edit files. 网上有许多学习 Vim 和 Emacs 的资源。没有必要两个都学，而且关于 Emacs 和 Vim 哪个最好，有一些非常强烈的观点（ https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Editor_war ）。不过，由于 Vim（或 vi）在每个 Unix 系统上都有，我们会更详细地介绍一些 vim 编辑器的基础知识，以及如何学习使用 Vim（和 vi）。我们还会介绍一些 Emacs 和 Nano 的基础知识，并给出这三者的进一步参考资料。 There are many online resources for learning both Vim and Emacs. The Vim Editor vim （和 vi ）编辑器是 Unix 系统上最普遍可用的编辑器。它是一个高效、轻量而强大的文本编辑器，只要学会几条基本命令就很容易使用，而这些命令可以通过学完 vimtutor 教程来掌握。 vim 在通过 ssh 连接远程工作时尤其有用。它还有许多高级功能，并且可以通过 .vimrc 配置文件中的设置进行高度定制。 The vim (and vi ) editor is the most widely available editor on Unix systems. It is an efficient, lightweight, and powerful text editor that is easy to use after learning a few basic commands, which you can learn by running through the vimtutor tutorial. vim is particularly useful when working remotely over an ssh connection. While you’re not required to configure vim to use it, you may find it helpful to customize the color scheme or adjust some other settings. 在你的主目录中添加一个名为 .vimrc 的 vim 配置文件。启动时， vim 会检查这个文件，为这次 vim 会话设置各种配置选项，包括配色方案和默认窗口大小。 In your home directory add a configuration file for vim, named .vimrc . On start-up, vim examines this file to set different configuration options for the vim session, including setting a color scheme and default window size. 在你的主目录中运行 ls -a ，列出你所有的点文件（dot file），确定是否已经存在 .vimrc 文件： Run ls -a in your home directory to list all your dot files and to determine if a .vimrc file already exists: $ cd $ ls -a ~/ # ~/ is shorthand for /home/you/ 如果 .vimrc 文件已存在，你可以在 vim 中打开它，像编辑其他文件一样编辑它： If the .vimrc file exits, you can open it in vim and edit it like any other file: $ vim .vimrc 如果不存在，你可以在主目录中创建一个 .vimrc ，把朋友的或在网上找到的现成的 .vimrc 示例文件复制进去。例如： If not, you can create a .vimrc in your home directory and copy an existing example .vimrc file of a friends or that you find online into it. For example: $ pwd /home/sarita/ $ vim .vimrc 网上有许多关于配置 vim 设置的资源。 There are many on-line resources information about configuring vim settings. 17.4.2. Emacs 编辑器 17.4.2. The Emacs Editor Emacs 是 Unix 系统上几乎总能找到的另一个编辑器。没有必要同时学习和使用 Vim 和 Emacs，但学会其中一个是有用的，对另一个也许只需了解几个基本操作（至少知道如何退出每一个）。 Emacs is another editor that is almost always available on Unix systems. It is not necessary to learn and use both Vim and Emacs, but it is useful to know one, and perhaps to know just a few basics about the other (at least how to exit each one). 与 Vim 不同，Emacs 是单模式编辑器，即它运行在单一的插入模式下，命令（例如保存文件）通过 CTRL 、 ALT 和 SHIFT 键的特殊组合来发出。Vim 和 Emacs 之间的主要权衡在于：Emacs 的命令按键序列比 Vim 的复杂，但它没有 Vim 那种需要用户来回切换的两种模式。Emacs 就像一把瑞士军刀，它有丰富的宏和命令，可以用于各种各样的任务（包括一些不常用的功能）。因此，Emacs 通常不会安装在内存受限的系统上，因为它通常比 Vim 这样的应用程序需要更多的内存。 Unlike Vim, Emacs is a single-mode editor, meaning that it runs in a single insertion mode where commands, like saving the file, are issued through special key combinations with the CTRL , ALT , and SHIFT keys. The main trade-off between Vim and Emacs is that Emacs has more complicated key sequences than Vim for commands, but it doesn’t have the two modes that the user needs to switch between like Vim does. Emacs is like a swiss army knife in that it has a rich assortment of macros and commands that can be used for a wide assortment of tasks (including features that are not commonly used). For this reason, Emacs is typically not installed on memory-constrained systems as it usually requires more memory than an application like Vim. 要启动 emacs，只需在命令行上对要编辑的文件运行它。例如，要在 emacs 中编辑 myprog.c ： To start emacs, just run from the command line on the file you want to edit. For example, to edit myprog.c in emacs: $ emacs myprog.c 用户输入普通的按键时，输入的字符会被加到文件中光标之后的位置。 When the user types in regular keystrokes, the characters entered are added to the file after the cursor. Emacs 命令参考 Emacs Command Reference 下面列出了常用的 Emacs 命令。在学习 Emacs 的过程中，你可能会发现回头查阅这份列表很有帮助。 Here is a list of common Emacs commands. You may find it helpful to refer back to this as you are learning Emacs. 文件控制（这些命令涉及多键序列）： CTRL-x CTRL-s 表示按住 CTRL 键，先按 x ，再按 s CTRL-x CTRL-s 保存对文件的编辑 CTRL-x CTRL-c 退出 Emacs File Control (these involve multi-sequences): CTRL-x CTRL-s is hold down the CTRL key and type x followed by s CTRL-x CTRL-s save the file edits CTRL-x CTRL-c exit Emacs 移动光标 CTRL-n 光标移到下一行 CTRL-p 光标移到上一行 CTRL-b 光标后退一个字符 CTRL-f 光标前进一个字符 Moving the cursor CTRL-n move the cursor forward one line CTRL-p move the cursor backward one line CTRL-b move the cursor back one character CTRL-f move the cursor forward one character 删除内容 CTRL-d 删除一个字符 CTRL-k 删除一行 Deleting Content CTRL-d deletes a character CTRL-k deletes a line. 复制内容 CTRL-k 复制一行 CTRL-y 粘贴 Copying Content CTRL-k copy a line. CTRL-y past 搜索 CTRL-s 搜索某个模式 Search CTRL-s search for a pattern 其他命令： CTRL-g 退出 emacs 的命令序列（在你输错了什么的时候很有用） CTRL-x-0 关闭当前的缓冲区窗口 CTRL-x-1 关闭除当前缓冲区之外的所有其他缓冲区 CTRL-x-2 在下方打开缓冲区窗口 CTRL-x-3 在右侧打开缓冲区窗口 CTRL-x-o 切换到另一个缓冲区 ESC-x 进入 meta 模式（在 Emacs 文档以及本表接下来的部分中，记作 M-x ） M-x goto-line n 跳到文件的第 n 行 M-x linum-mode 打开行号显示 M-x ansi-term 在当前缓冲区中打开一个 bash shell Misc. Commands: CTRL-g quit out of emacs command sequence (useful if you type in something wrong) CTRL-x-0 close the current buffer window CTRL-x-1 close all other buffers except the current one CTRL-x-2 open buffer window below CTRL-x-3 open buffer window to the right CTRL-x-o switch to another buffer ESC-x enters meta mode (in Emacs documentation and in this table forward, it is listed as M-x ) M-x goto-line n go to line n in the file M-x linum-mode turn on line numbering M-x ansi-term open a bash shell in the current buffer 与 Vim 一样，Emacs 也有一套丰富的命令，支持复杂的编辑任务。它也可以通过配置文件 ~/.emacsrc 进行配置，你可以在其中定制 emacs 的功能和外观。 Like Vim, Emacs has a rich set of commands that support complicated editing tasks. It is also configurable via a configuration file, ~/.emacsrc , in which you can customize functionality and the look of emacs. 17.4.3. Nano 编辑器 17.4.3. The Nano Editor Nano 是另一个文本编辑器，适合对文件做较小的修改。它很容易使用，但缺少 Emacs 和 Vim 中那些使它们适用于更大、更复杂编辑任务的功能。Nano 也是像 Emacs 那样的单模式编辑器，用特殊的按键组合来执行移动光标或保存文件之类的命令。 Nano is another text editor that is useful for making smaller edits on files—it is easy to use, but lacks some of the features of Emacs and Vim that make them useful for larger, more complicated editing tasks. Nano is also a single-mode editor like Emacs that uses special key combinations for commands like moving the cursor or saving the file. Nano 的运行方式与 Vim 和 Emacs 类似；要打开一个文件进行编辑，在命令行上输入 nano 和要编辑的文件： Nano is run similar to Vim and Emacs; to open a file for editing type nano and the file to edit at the command line: $ nano myprog.c 运行 nano 时，它会在底部列出一些最常用的命令。在这个列表中， M- 通常表示 ALT （meta）键加另一个键， C- 表示 CTRL 键。一般来说，nano 命令的控制序列比 emacs 的简单。例如，用 CTRL-x 退出 nano。 When you run nano it lists some of its most common commands at the bottom. In its listing, M- usually means the ALT (meta) key plus another key, and C- is the CTRL key. In general, nano’s control sequences for commands are simpler than in emacs. For example, CTRL-x is used to exit nano. 17.4.4. 设置默认编辑器 17.4.4. Setting your default editor 默认编辑器是其他程序在其部分功能需要启动编辑会话时自动打开的那个编辑程序。例如，Git 这样的版本控制软件会启动一个编辑器，让你为一次提交添加注释。在 Linux 系统上，可以用 echo 打印 EDITOR 和 VISUAL 环境变量，查看你的默认文本编辑器： Your default editor program is the one that is automatically opened by other programs that start an editing session for some of their functionality. For example, revision control software such as Git starts an editor for adding comments to a commit. You can see your default text editor on Linux systems by echo’ing your EDITOR and VISUAL environment variables: $ echo $EDITOR nano $ echo $VISUAL nano 要设置默认编辑器，在你的 .bashrc 文件中添加或编辑这两个环境变量的定义，然后运行 source ~/.bashrc 使改动生效。下面是把两者都设为 vim 的例子： To set your default editor, add or edit the definitions for these two environment variables to your .bashrc file, and then source ~/.bashrc to see the changes. Here is an example to set both to vim : $ vim ~/.bashrc export EDITOR=vim export VISUAL=vim $ source ~/.bashrc $ echo $EDITOR vim $ echo $VISUAL vim 在 点文件一节 中，我们会更详细地讨论环境变量和 .bashrc 。 In the dot files section we talk about environment variables and .bashrc in more detail. 17.4.5. 参考资料 17.4.5. References 网上有许多学习 Vim、Emacs 或 Nano 的资源，包括一些教程视频。下面只是几个参考资料和教程的链接： There are many resources for learning Vim, Emacs, or Nano on the web, including several tutorial videos. Searching: grep and find 一项常见的任务是搜索特定的文件，或者在文件中搜索特定的内容。 find 命令适合查找名字符合特定模式的文件或目录，而 grep 命令适合在一个文件或一组文件中搜索特定的模式。 A common task is to search for specific files or for specific content within files. The find command is useful for finding a file or directory whose name has a specific pattern, whereas the grep command is useful for searching for a specific pattern within a file or set of files. 17.6.1. find 命令 17.6.1. The find Command find 命令（从目录结构中给定的起点开始）对文件系统进行递归搜索，查找任何文件。使用 -name <search pattern> 命令行选项运行时， find 搜索名字与给定搜索模式匹配的所有文件（和目录）。搜索模式是一个正则表达式，它包含字符字面量，以及指定一般模式的特殊字符或子模式。正则表达式中常用的一个特殊字符是 * ，它的意思是「匹配零个或多个任意字符」。所以对于搜索模式 "hello*" ， hello1 、 hellothere 和 hello_123_XYZ 都与之匹配。下面是用 find 命令查找文件的几个例子： The find command performs a recursive search of a filesystem (at a given start point in the directory structure), to find any files. When run with the -name <search pattern> command line option, find searches for all files (and directories) with a name matching the given search pattern. The search pattern is a regular expression that includes character literals and special characters or sub-patterns that specify general patterns. One special character commonly used in regular expressions is `*`. It means “match with zero or more of any character”. So for the search pattern "hello*" , hello1 , hellothere , and hello_123_XYZ all match the pattern. Here are a few examples of the find command to find files: 译注 严格说来， find -name 使用的是 shell 风格的通配符（glob）模式，而不是正则表达式（ man find 中 -name 的说明写的是「special shell pattern matching characters」）；在通配符里 * 本身就表示「零个或多个任意字符」，而在正则表达式里 * 表示「前一个字符重复零次或多次」（下面 grep 的例子用的就是后一种含义）。 $ find ./ -name dog.c # from current directory (./) find all files named dog.c $ find ./ -name "*.c" # from ./ find all files that end with .c $ find ./ -name "temp*" # from ./ find all files that that start with temp find 命令还有许多其他命令行选项，让用户能以不同的方式配置它的搜索行为。更多信息参见它的手册页。 There are many other command line options to the find command, allowing users to configure its search behavior in different ways. The grep Command grep 命令在一个文件或一组文件中查找模式。它可以根据模式匹配把数据从源过滤到目标。 grep 命令接收两个命令行参数：一个作为搜索模式的正则表达式，以及要在其中搜索匹配模式的一个文件（或一组文件）。它输出文件（或这组文件）中每一个含有该模式匹配项的行。与 find 一样， grep 也有许多命令行选项来定制它的搜索。下面是用 grep 命令在文件中查找模式的几个例子。这些例子中用到的文件之一是 temp 文件，它的内容如下： The grep command finds patterns within a file or within a set of files. It can filter data from a source to a destination based on pattern matching. The grep command takes two command line arguments, a search pattern regular expression, and a file (or set of files) to search in for matching patterns. It outputs every line in the file (or set of files) that has a matching occurrence of the pattern. Like find , grep also has many command line options to tailor its search. In this example, because the search pattern has space characters in it, the pattern needs to be inside double quotes. $ grep "hello there" temp hello there 在匹配结果中包含文件的行号（ -n 命令行选项），并在模式中忽略大小写（ -i 命令行选项）： $ grep -n -i "hello there" temp 4:hello there 5:hello There Include the file line numbers with matches ( -n command line option) and ignore case in the pattern ( -i command line option): $ Viewing and Changing File Permissions 每个 Unix 文件（和目录）都受一组权限（permission）的约束，权限定义了对它的访问权利。与文件相关的权限有： Every Unix file (and directory) is governed by a set of permissions, which defines its access rights. The permissions associated with a file are: r ：对文件或目录的读权限 r : read access to the file or directory w ：对文件或目录的写权限 w : write access to the file or directory x ：对文件或目录的执行权限（对于目录，这意味着你可以 cd 进入它；对于文件，这意味着你可以在命令行上执行它（例如 ./filename ））。编译器会自动为生成的可执行文件设置所有者的 x 权限。 x : execute access to the file or directory (for a directory, this means you can cd into it, for a file it means you can execute it at the command line (e.g., ./filename ). The compiler automatically sets the target executable file with x permission for the owner. 每个文件的权限还指定了三组用户：文件的用户/所有者（ u ）；与文件所属组同组的用户（ g ）；以及其他人（ o ），即其他所有人。通过修改文件的权限，你可以针对这几组不同的用户，以不同的方式保护或共享文件。例如，可以把文件权限设置为：所有者拥有读写权限，文件所属组中的用户拥有读权限，而其他所有人既不能读也不能写。 Each file’s permissions also specifies three sets of users: the file user/owner ( u ); users in the same group as the file’s group ( g ); and other ( o ) or everybody else. By changing the file permissions with a file, you can protect or share files in different ways these different sets of users. For example, file permission can be set to give the owner read and write access, users in the file’s group read access, and everybody else no read or write access. 要列出文件和目录的权限，使用 ls 的 -l 命令行选项： To list file permissions with files and directories use the -l command line option of ls : $ls -l drwx------ 3 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:49 classes/ drwx------ 2 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:54 letters/ -rw-r----- 1 sam pals 78 Mar 26 12:51 notes drwx------ 2 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:48 projects/ ls -l 的输出采用下面的格式（以 notes 的列表为例）： The output from ls -l is in the following format (showing the listing of notes as an example): type permissions links owner group size modification date name u g o - rw- r-- --- 1 sam pals 78 Mar 26 12:51 notes d rwx --- --- 3 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:49 classes/ type 对于目录是 d ，对于普通文件是 - 。文件权限列表分为三组 rwx ，分别指定文件的用户或所有者（ u ）、组（ g ）和其他人（ o ）的权限。例如，与 notes 文件相关的 -rw-r----- 表示：文件所有者 sam 对文件有读写权限（ rw- ），文件所属组 pals 只有读权限（ r-- ），其他人没有访问该文件的任何权限（ --- ）。列表中的其他字段显示了文件所有者的用户名（ sam ）、文件所属组的名字（ pals ）、文件的字节数（ 78 ）、文件最后修改的时间（ Mar 26 12:51 ）以及文件名（ notes ）。列出的还有该文件的硬链接数（ 1 ），即目录结构中引用同一个文件的名字的数目。 The type is d for directories and - for regular files. The file permission listings are in three groups of rwx specifying permissions for the file user or owner ( u ), group ( g ), and others ( o ). For example, the -rw-r----- associated with the notes file means that the file owner sam has read and write access to the file ( rw- ), that the file’s group, pals has read permission only ( r-- ), and others have no permissions to access the file ( --- ). The other fields in the listing show the username of the file owner ( sam ), the name of the file’s group ( pals ), the size of the file in bytes ( 78 ), the last time the file was modified ( Mar 26 12:51 ) and the name of the file ( notes ). Also listed are the number of hard links to the file ( 1 ), which is the number of names in the directory structure that refer to this same file. classes 的列表是 drwx------ ，这表示 classes 是一个目录，文件所有者 sam 有读、写和执行权限（ rwx ），而目录所属组（ users ）和其他人没有任何访问权限（ --- ）。换句话说，这是用户 sam 的私有目录；其他任何人都不能访问这个目录。我们注意到，目录必须设置了执行（ x ）权限才能 cd 进入。目录的链接数大于 1 ，因为目录名（例如 classes ）和目录中的名字 ./ （以及它的任何子目录中的名字 ../ ）都引用同一个目录。由于 classes 有一个子目录 CS31 ，它的链接数是 3 。 The listing for classes is drwx------ , which means that classes is a directory, the file owner sam has read, write, and execute permissions ( rwx ), and that the directory’s group ( users ) and others have no access permissions ( --- ). In other words this is a private directory to the user sam ; no one else can access this directory. We note that a directory must have execute ( x ) permission set in order to cd into it. Directories have link sizes greater than 1 because both the directory name (e.g., classes ) and the name ./ in the directory (and the name ../ in any of its subdirectories) refer to the same directory. Because classes has one subdirectory, CS31 , its link value is 3 . 17.7.1. chmod 17.7.1. chmod chmod 命令修改文件或目录的权限。它接收的命令行参数指定如何修改与每个文件相关的三组用户（用户/所有者、组和其他人）的权限。 The chmod command changes the permissions on a file or directory. It takes command line arguments that specify how to change the permissions for the three sets of users associated with every file: user/owner, group, and other. 运行 chmod 的一种方式，是给出一个三位数字作为命令行参数，它编码了如何设置权限。第一位数字指定文件用户/所有者的权限，第二位指定文件所属组的权限，第三位指定其他所有用户的权限。例如， chmod 700 letters 把 letters 变成一个私有目录； 7 把用户的权限设为 rwx ， 0 把组和其他人的权限设为 --- 。 One way to run chmod is to give a three digit number as a command line argument that encodes how to set the permissions. The first digit specifies the permissions for the file user/owner, the second digit specifies the permissions for the file group, and the third for all other users. For example, chmod 700 letters makes letters a private directory; 7 sets the user’s permissions to rwx , and 0 set permissions to --- for group and others. 要理解这些数字的含义，把每一位数字看作一个三位二进制数，对于 rwx 这三项， 1 表示授予该权限， 0 表示不授予。 表 1 给出了一些例子。 To understand what the digits mean, consider each digit represented as a three bit binary number where a 1 means grant the permission and 0 means don’t grant it for the set rwx . Table 1 shows some examples. 表 1. chmod 权限编码示例 Table 1. chmod Permission Encoding Examples 数字 二进制 权限 7 111 设置 rwx 权限 5 101 只设置 r 和 x 权限 4 100 只设置 r 权限 6 110 只设置 rw 权限 0 000 清除所有权限…​无法访问 Digit Binary Permission 7 111 set rwx permissions 5 101 set r x permissions only 4 100 set r permission only 6 110 set rw permissions only 0 000 clear all permissions…​no access 例如，如果 sam 想让其他所有用户都能读 notes 文件，并给自己读写权限，他会运行下面的命令： For example, if sam wants to give read access to the notes file with all other users and give himself read and write access, he would run the following command: $ chmod 644 notes $ ls -l drwx------ 3 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:49 classes/ drwx------ 2 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:54 letters/ -rw-r--r-- 1 sam pals 78 Mar 26 12:51 notes drwx------ 2 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:48 projects/ 644 把 notes 的权限设为 -rw-r--r-- ： 6 给文件所有者 rw- 权限； 4 给文件所属组 r-- 权限； 4 给其他人 r-- 权限。 The 644 sets the permissions on notes to -rw-r—​r-- : 6 gives the file’s owner rw- access; 4 gives the file’s group r-- access; and 4 gives other r-- access. chmod 命令也可以使用 [u,g,o][+,-][permissions] 这种设置格式。例如，如果 sam 想给 users 组对 projects 目录的写权限，他可以用 g+w （给组加上写权限）来指定这个权限；如果他想去掉其他人对 notes 的读权限，可以指定 o-r （从其他人那里去掉读权限）： The chmod command can also use the [u,g,o][+,-][permissions] setting format too. For example, if sam wants to give the users group write access to the projects directory, he can specify this permission using g+w (add write permission to group), and if he wants to remove read access from notes to others, he can specify o-r (remove read permission from all): $ chmod g+w projects $ chmod o-r notes $ ls -l drwx------ 3 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:49 classes/ drwx------ 2 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:54 letters/ -rw-r----- 1 sam pals 78 Mar 26 12:51 notes drwx-w---- 2 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:48 projects/ 当他意识到给 users 组对 projects 目录的写权限是个糟糕的主意时，可以用 g-w 去掉它： And when he realizes that giving the users group write access to his projects directory was a terrible idea, he can remove it using g-w : $ chmod g-w projects $ ls -l projects drwx------ 2 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:48 projects/ chmod 命令还有其他命令行选项，包括一个递归选项，可以递归地修改整个子目录内容的权限。更多细节参见手册页。 The chmod command has other command line options, including a recursive flag to recursively change permissions on a full subdirectory’s contents. See the man page for more details. Linux 还支持 访问控制列表 （access control list，ACL），它允许把丰富得多的权限集合与文件和目录关联起来。 getfacl 和 setfacl 的手册页包含关于 ACL 的信息，不过细节超出了我们的介绍范围。 Linux also supports access control lists (ACLs), which allow a much richer set of permissions to be associated with files and directories. The man page for getfacl and setfacl contain information about ACLs, but the details are beyond the scope of our coverage. 17.7.2. chgrp 17.7.2. chgrp chgrp 命令可以用来修改与文件或目录关联的组。Unix 组通常需要由拥有系统 root 权限的系统管理员来创建（root 用户是 Unix 的超级用户账户，它拥有普通用户所没有的文件系统访问权利）。 The chgrp command can be used to change the group associated with a file or directory. Unix groups typically need to be created by a system administrator who has root access on the system (the root user is the Unix superuser account that has access rights to the filesystem that a regular user does not have). 如果用户 sam 和另外两个用户同属于一个名为 proj3 的组， sam 就可以修改他的 projects 目录所属的组并设置权限，只给这个组对该目录更高的权利。例如： If the user sam is part of a group named proj3 with two other users, sam can change the group and set permissions on their projects directory to give just this group elevated rights to the directory. For example: $ chgrp proj3 projects # change the projects directory's group to proj3 $ ls -l drwx------ 3 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:49 classes/ drwx------ 2 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:54 letters/ -rw-r----- 1 sam pals 78 Mar 26 12:51 notes drwx------ 2 sam proj3 4096 Mar 26 12:48 projects/ $ chmod 750 projects # give proj3 group members r and x access to directory $ ls -l drwx------ 3 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:49 classes/ drwx------ 2 sam users 4096 Mar 26 12:54 letters/ -rw-r----- 1 sam pals 78 Mar 26 12:51 notes drwxr-x--- 2 sam proj3 4096 Mar 26 12:48 projects/ 类似地， chown 命令修改文件的所有者，但你需要有 root 权限才能运行它。 Similarly, the chown command changes the owner of a file, but you need to have root privileges to run it. 原书注 · 文件所属组的设置与默认权限（File group setting and default permissions） 每个用户都有默认的权限和默认的组，它们会自动与该用户创建的所有新文件和目录关联起来。两者都可以在 shell 的配置文件（例如 .bashrc ）中修改。关于点文件的更多信息，参见 第 17.14 节 。 你的默认组由名为 GROUP 的 shell 环境变量指定。可以用 echo $GROUP 列出它的值： $ echo $GROUP GROUP=users 你的默认文件权限由 .bashrc 文件中的 umask 设置配置。可以用 umask 列出它的值： $ umask 77 umask 为 77 （即 077 ）会让我所有的文件和目录都成为私有的（它把组和其他人的权限设为 00，即 ------ ）。可以把 umask 编码看作 chmod 编码的某种反向（例如，在 umask 中 7 去掉所有权限（ rwx ），而在 chmod 中 7 授予所有权限）。 Each user has default permissions and a default group that will automatically be associated with all new files and directories the user creates. Both of these can be modified in your shell’s config file (e.g., .bashrc ). See Section 17.14 for more information about dot files. Your default group is specified in the shell environment variable named GROUP . You can list its value using echo $GROUP : $ echo $GROUP GROUP=users Your default file permission are configured from the umask setting in your .bashrc file. You can list its value using umask : $ umask 77 A umask of 77 (or 077 ) makes all my files and directories private (it sets the group and other permissions to 00 or ------ ). You can think of the umask encoding as being sort of like the inverse of the chmod encoding (e.g., 7 removes all permissions ( rwx ) in umask but grants all in chmod). 17.7.3. 参考资料 17.7.3. Archiving and Compressing Files tar （tape archive，磁带归档）工具用来把一组文件打包成单个文件（ 归档文件 ，archive file，或 tar 文件 ）。 tar 命令也用来从 tar 文件中解出文件。归档文件（或 tar 文件）包含组成该 tar 文件的所有文件的数据，以及描述其内容的额外元数据。 tar 需要这些元数据才能从 tar 文件中解出单个文件。 The tar (tape archive) utility is used to package up a set of files into a single file (an archive file or a tar file ). The tar command is also used to extract the files out of a tar file. An archive file (or tar file) contains all the file data from the files that make up the tar file plus additional meta-data that describe its contents. The meta-data are necessary for tar to extract the individual file(s) out of a tar file. tar 文件常用来分发一组文件，或者把一组文件从一台机器传到另一台机器。它们也可以用来存放成组文件的备份（文件归档）。例如，如果用户想把一组文件从一个系统传到另一个系统，他会先用 -c 命令行选项运行 tar ，创建一个包含所有这些文件的单个 tar 文件，然后用 scp 把得到的 tar 文件传到远程机器上。在远程机器上，他再用 -x 运行 tar ，从 tar 文件中解出文件。 Tar files are often used to distribute a set of files or to transfer a set of files from one machine to another. They also may be used to store backups of sets of files (file archives). For example, if a user who wants to transfer a set of files from one system to another, they would first run tar with the -c command line option to create a single tar file containing all of the files, then scp the resulting tar file to the remote machine. On the remote machine they would then run tar with -x to extract files from the tar file. tar 命令有许多命令行选项，可以用不同的方式配置它的行为。 表 1 列出了一些例子。 The tar command has many command line options for configuring its behavior in different ways. Table 1 lists some examples. 表 1. tar 的命令行选项 Table 1. tar command line options 选项 说明 -c 从一组文件创建一个 tar 文件 -x 解包（即 untar）一个 tar 文件 -t 列出 tar 文件的内容 -v 详细模式，在运行命令时打印出信息 -f <tar file name> 指定 tar 文件的名字 Option Description -c create a tar file from a set of files -x extract, or untar, a tar file -t list the contents of a tar file -v verbose mode, prints out information as runs command -f <tar file name> specifies the name of the tar file 要创建 tar 文件，需要使用 -c ，用 -f 指定输出 tar 文件的名字，然后给出要包含在 tar 文件中的文件（和目录）列表（目录的全部内容都会被包含进来）。 To create a tar file you need to use -c , specify the name of the tar output file with -f and then give the list of files (and directories) to include in the tar file (full directory contents will be included). 下面是一个例子，展示如何从三个普通文件（ main.c 、 process.c 、 Makefile ）和一个目录的内容（ inputfiles/ ）创建一个 tar 文件： Here is an example of how to create a tar file from three regular files ( main.c , process.c , Makefile ) and the contents of a directory ( inputfiles/ ): $ tar -c -v -f mytarfile.tar main.c process.c Makefile intputfiles/ -v 是详细输出的命令行选项。它会在 tar 执行时列出被打包的文件的一些信息。 -v is the verbose command line option. It lists some information about the files being tar’ed up as tar executes. tar 的命令行选项也可以用另一种更紧凑的语法来指定（你看到的 tar 例子中常常用这种写法）： The command line options to tar can also be specified using an alternate, more compact, syntax (this is often used in tar examples you see): $ tar -cvf mytarfile.tar main.c process.c Makefile intputfiles/ $ tar cvf mytarfile.tar main.c process.c Makefile intputfiles/ 或者，你可以创建一个目录，把想打包的文件复制进去，然后从这个目录生成一个 tar 文件。例如： Alternatively, you can create a directory and copy the files you want to tar into it, and generate a tar file from that directory. For example: $ mkdir mytardir $ cp *.c mytardir/. $ cp -r inputfiles mytardir/. $ tar cvf mytarfile.tar mytardir 要列出 tar 文件中的文件，使用 -t 命令行选项： To list the files in a tar file, use the -t command line option: $ tar -tvf mytarfile.tar 要从 tar 文件中解出文件，使用 -x 命令行选项： To extract files from a tar file, use the -x command line option: $ tar xvf mytarfile.tar 17.8.1. 文件压缩 17.8.1. file compression 文件压缩常常与 tar 一起使用，以减小 tar 文件的大小。这既能减少存放 tar 文件所需的存储空间，也能在用 scp 把 tar 文件复制到远程机器时减少通过网络发送的数据量。 gzip 和 gunzip 用 gzip 压缩算法压缩和解压文件， bzip2 和 bunzip2 用 bzip 压缩算法压缩和解压文件。下面是一些调用示例： Often times file compression is used along with tar to reduce the size of the tar file. This is useful for both reducing the storage space required for the tar file, and also to reduce the amount of data that are sent over the network when a tar file is copied to a remote machine using scp . The gzip and gunzip are used to compress and uncompress a file using gzip compression, and bzip2 and bunzip2 are used to compress and uncompress a file using bzip compression. Here are some example calls: $ ls -l -rw-r--r-- 1 sarita users 40840 Apr 12 16:55 file $ gzip file # compress using gzip $ ls -l -rw-r--r-- 1 sarita users 13258 Apr 12 16:55 file.gz $ gunzip file.gz # uncompress a gziped file $ ls -l -rw-r--r-- 1 sarita users 40840 Apr 12 16:55 file $ bzip2 file # compress using bzip2 $ ls -l -rw-r--r-- 1 sarita users 12568 Apr 12 16:55 file.bz2 $ bunzip2 file.bz2 # uncompress a bzip2ed file $ ls -l -rw-r--r-- 1 sarita users 40840 Apr 12 16:55 file tar 与文件压缩 tar and file compression 文件压缩常常用在 tar 文件上。用户可以在 tar 创建 tar 文件之后再对它运行文件压缩工具，并在运行 tar 从 tar 文件中解出文件之前先运行工具解压它。不过，由于文件压缩与 tar 文件一起使用得非常普遍， tar 有一些命令行选项，可以用不同的压缩算法创建压缩的 tar 文件（以及从压缩的 tar 文件中解出文件）（例如， -j 使用 bzip2 ， -z 使用 gzip）。 File compression is often used on tar files. A user can run file compression utilities on a tar file after tar creates it and run utilities to uncompress the tar file before running tar to extract files from the tar file. However, because file compression is so commonly used with tar files, tar has command line options to create compressed tar files (and to extract files from compressed tar files) using different compression algorithms (for example, -j uses bzip2 , and -z uses gzip). 下面是给 tar 加上 -z 选项（使用 gzip）或 -j 选项（使用 bzip）一步完成 tar 文件压缩的一些例子： Here are some examples of compressing the tar file in one step using the -z option to gzip or -j option for bzip: to tar : # use -z option to compress tar file using gzip: $ tar -czvf myproj.tar.gz myproj/ $ ls myproj/ myproj.tar.gz # or use -j option to compress tar file using bzip2: $ tar -cjvf myproj.tar.bz2 myproj/ $ ls myproj/ myproj.tar.bz2 或者，下面是把创建 tar 文件和压缩分成两步的例子（先创建 tar 文件，再用 gzip （或 bzip2 ）压缩）： Alternatively, here is an example of separating the tar file creation and compression into two steps (create tar file, then compress using gzip (or bzip2 ): $ tar cvf myproj.tar myproj/ # create a tar file from myproj $ ls myproj/ myproj.tar $ gzip myproj.tar # gzip the tar file $ ls myproj/ myproj.tar.gz # OR could use bzip $ bzip2 myproj.tar # bzip the tar file $ ls myproj/ myproj.tar.bz2 你也可以用一步法或两步法从压缩的 tar 文件中解出文件。例如，下面是一步完成的方法（ -z 指定先用 gzip 解压文件）： You can also use the one-step or two-step method to extract files from a compressed tar file. For example, here is the single step way ( -z specifies to uncompress the file first using gzip): $ tar -xzvf myproj.tar.gz $ ls myproj/ myproj.tar.gz 或者，下面是从压缩的 tar 文件中解出文件的两步法（先用 gunzip 或 bunzip2 解压，再 untar）： Alternatively, here is the two-step method to extract files from a compressed tar file (first uncompress with gunzip or bunzip2, then untar): $ ls myproj.tar.gz $ gunzip myproj.tar.gz $ ls myproj.tar $ tar -xvf myproj.tar $ ls myproj/ myproj.tar # or using bunzip2 for bzip'ed file $ ls myproj.tar.bz2 $ bunzip myproj.tar.bz2 $ ls myproj.tar $ tar -xvf myproj.tar $ ls myproj/ myproj.tar 17.8.2. 综合运用 17.8.2. putting it all together 下面的例子展示了如何用 tar 把一个目录的内容从一台机器（ laptop ）传到一台远程机器（ ada.cs.college.edu ）。它用 scp 命令在两台机器之间远程复制文件（关于 scp 的更多信息，参见 第 17.3 节 ）。 Below is an example of using tar to transfer a directory’s contents from one machine ( laptop ) to a remote machine ( ada.cs.college.edu ). It uses the scp command to remotely copy the file between the two machines (see Section 17.3 for more information about scp ). 首先，用户在 laptop 上创建压缩的 tar 文件（注意：我们用两步法来创建并压缩 tar 文件，是为了展示 tar 文件中文件的列表，但压缩的 tar 文件也可以用 -cjvf 命令行选项一步创建出来）： laptop$ ls myproj/ Makefile input1.txt input2.txt main.c mux.c mux.h laptop$ tar -cvf myproj.tar myproj/ # create a tar file from myproj laptop$ ls myproj/ myproj.tar laptop$ tar -tf myproj.tar # list tar file contents myproj/ myproj/Makefile myproj/input1.txt myproj/input2.txt myproj/main.c myproj/mux.c myproj/mux.h laptop$ gzip myproj.tar # compress the file First, the user creates the compressed tar file on laptop (note: we show the two-step method to create and compress the tar file in order to show the listing of the files in the tar file, but the compressed tar file could also be created in one-step using the -cjvf command line options): laptop$ ls myproj/ Makefile input1.txt input2.txt main.c mux.c mux.h laptop$ tar -cvf myproj.tar myproj/ # create a tar file from myproj laptop$ ls myproj/ myproj.tar laptop$ tar -tf myproj.tar # list tar file contents myproj/ myproj/Makefile myproj/input1.txt myproj/input2.txt myproj/main.c myproj/mux.c myproj/mux.h laptop$ gzip myproj.tar # compress the file 然后，他用 scp 把这个单个的 tar 文件传到远程机器上： laptop$ scp myproj.tar sam@ada.cs.college.edu:. # scp single tar file sam@ada.cs.college.edu's password: Then, they scp the single tar file to the remote machine: laptop$ scp myproj.tar sam@ada.cs.college.edu:. # scp single tar file sam@ada.cs.college.edu's password: 然后，用户可以 ssh 登录到远程机器，并对 myproj.tar 文件 untar 以解出文件： laptop$ ssh sam@ada.cs.college.edu sam@ada.cs.college.edu's password: ada$ ls classes/ letters/ myproj.tar projects/ ada$ tar -xjvf myproj.tar # extract contents of tar file ada$ ls classes/ letters/ myproj/ myproj.tar projects/ Then the user can then ssh into the remote machine, and untar the myproj.tar file to extract the files: laptop$ ssh sam@ada.cs.college.edu sam@ada.cs.college.edu's password: ada$ ls classes/ letters/ myproj.tar projects/ ada$ tar -xjvf myproj.tar # extract contents of tar file ada$ ls classes/ letters/ myproj/ myproj.tar projects/ 译注 · 文件名与压缩选项前后不一致 第 1 步最后执行的是 gzip myproj.tar ，它会把文件变成 myproj.tar.gz （gzip 格式），原来的 myproj.tar 就不存在了。所以第 2 步应当传送 myproj.tar.gz ，第 3 步应当用对应 gzip 的 -z 选项解包： tar -xzvf myproj.tar.gz 。书中第 3 步用的 -j 对应的是 bzip2；同理，第 1 步括号中提到的一步法若要与这里一致，应使用 -czvf 。 如果用户想把目录 untar 到主目录以外的某个地方，可以用 mv 把目录移到想要的位置（或者也可以在 untar 之前先把 tar 文件移到想要的位置）。例如，把它移到 project 目录下作为子目录： If the user wanted to untar the directory somewhere other than in their home directory, they could use mv to move the directory where they want (or they could have also moved the tar file to where they want it before untaring it). For example, to move it as a subdirectory under the project directory: ada$ ls classes/ letters/ myproj/ myproj.tar projects/ ada$ mv myproj project/. ada$ ls classes/ letters/ myproj.tar projects/ ada$ cd project ada$ ls myproj/ untar 一个 tar 文件之后，用户常常会删除那个 .tar 文件： Often after untaring a tar file, the user removes the .tar file: rm myproj.tar ls 17.8.3. 参考资料 17.8.3.
