Process Control 当你在 shell 提示符下运行一个程序或命令时，shell 通常会创建一个新进程来运行这个程序或命令（进程是操作系统对正在运行的程序的抽象）。有少数 shell 内置命令 （built-in shell command）由 shell 进程自己执行（例如 cd ），但大多数命令都作为独立的进程运行。关于进程的更多信息，参见 第 13 章：操作系统 。 When you run a program or command at the shell prompt, the shell usually creates a new process that will run the program or command (a process is the operating systems abstraction of a running program). There are a few built-in shell commands that the shell process executes itself (e.g., cd ), but most are run as separate processes. See Chapter 13: The Operating System for more information about processes. Unix shell 支持 进程控制 （process control）功能，即指定 shell 如何运行一个程序的方式，以及在进程运行时与之交互的方式。 The unix shell supports process control features, which are ways to specify how a program is run by the shell, and ways to interact with the process as it runs. 17.9.1. 在前台和后台运行 17.9.1. Running in the foreground and background 在 shell 提示符下运行一个程序时，它默认 在前台运行 （runs in the foreground），即程序运行完毕之后，shell 程序才会再次运行并打印出下一个提示符。不过，程序也可以 在后台运行 （run in the background），即 shell 启动程序运行，但不等它完成就打印出下一个提示符；这让用户能在程序仍在运行时输入另一条命令。要告诉 shell 在后台运行一个程序，用户在命令行的末尾加上 & 。例如，下面展示了如何告诉 shell 在后台运行一个 a.out 程序： When a program is run at the shell prompt, it runs in the foreground by default, meaning that the program runs to completion before the shell program runs again and prints out the next prompt. However, programs can also be run in the background , meaning that the shell starts the program running but does not wait until it completes before printing out the next prompt; this allows a user to enter another command while the program is still running. To tell the shell to run a program in the background, the user adds an & at the end of the command line. For example, here is how to tell the shell to run an a.out program in the background: $ ./a.out & $ ps 命令可以用来列出 shell 中运行的所有程序。例如，这里我们启动两个在后台运行的 a.out 程序，然后输入 ps ： The ps command can be used to list all the programs running in the shell. For example, here we start two a.out programs running in the background, and then type ps : $ ./a.out & $ ./a.out & $ ps PID TTY TIME CMD 2729 pts/72 0:03.91 bash 3582 pts/72 0:00.00 ./a.out 3583 pts/72 0:00.00 ./a.out 3584 pts/72 0:00.00 ps 在这个输出示例中，可以看到除了 Bash shell 进程和 ps 进程之外，还有两个 a.out 进程在运行。每个进程都列出了它的 process id （进程 ID），即操作系统为每个进程维护的唯一标识符（例如， bash 进程的 ID 是 2729 ，运行 a.out 程序的两个进程的 ID 是 3582 和 3583 ）。 In the example output, you can see two a.out processes are running in addition to the Bash shell process and the ps process. With each process is listed its process id , a unique identifier the operating system keeps for each process (i.e., the bash process id is 2729 and the two processes running the a.out program have process ids 3582 and 3583 ). 可以用 fg 命令把一个在后台运行的进程移到前台： A process running in the background can be moved to the foreground using the fg command: $ ./a.out & # run a.out in the background $ ps PID TTY TIME CMD 2729 pts/72 0:03.91 bash 3584 pts/72 0:00.00 ./a.out $ fg # move a.out to the foreground (the shell waits for it to exit) $ ps # run ps at the shell prompt (a.out has exited) PID TTY TIME CMD 2729 pts/72 0:03.91 bash 按下 CTRL-Z 可以中断并挂起一个在前台运行的进程，即暂停它的执行（它不再运行）。这会让 shell 再次运行并打印出 shell 提示符。如果用户输入 bg ，被挂起的进程会继续运行，但现在是在后台运行。如果用户输入 fg ，被挂起的进程会继续在前台运行。下面是一些例子： By typing CTRL-Z a process running in the foreground can be interrupted and suspended meaning that its execution is paused (it is not running). This causes the shell to run again and print out a shell prompt. If the user types bg , the suspended process will continue running, but now run in the background. If the user types fg the suspended process will continue running in the foreground again. Here are some examples: $ ./a.out # run a.out in the foreground # type CTRL-Z to suspend a.out [1] Stopped ./a.out $ ps PID TTY TIME CMD 2729 pts/72 0:03.91 bash 3588 pts/72 0:00.00 ./a.out $ bg # unsuspend a.out and run in background $ ps PID TTY TIME CMD 2729 pts/72 0:03.91 bash 3588 pts/72 0:00.00 ./a.out $ fg # run backgrounded process in the foreground 17.9.2. 终止正在运行的进程 17.9.2. Killing a running processes kill 和 pkill 命令用来从 shell 进程向另一个进程发送信号。信号是一个进程通知另一个进程去做某件事的一种方式。每个信号都会触发一种默认行为，退出和忽略是两种常见的默认选项（关于信号的更多信息，参见 第 13 章：操作系统 ）。 The kill and pkill commands are used to send a signal from the shell process to another processes. Signals are a way in which one process can notify another process to do something. Every signal triggers a default behavior, exiting or ignoring are two common default options (see Chapter 13: The Operating System for more information about signals). kill 命令接收要发送信号的进程的进程 ID（PID）， pkill 命令接收要发送信号的命令或可执行文件的名字（ pkill 把信号发送给运行 pkill 的用户所拥有的、具有指定名字的所有正在运行的进程）。 kill 和 pkill 都接收一个可选的命令行参数，用来指定要发给进程的具体信号。如果不指定具体的信号，两者默认都向指定的进程发送终止信号（ SIGTERM ）。 The kill command takes the process id (PID) of the process to send the signal, and the pkill command takes the name of the command or executable file to which to send the signal ( pkill sends the signal to all running processes with the specified name that are owned by the user running pkill ). Both kill and pkill take an optional command line argument that species the specific signal to send to the process. Without specifying the specific signal, both default to sending a termination signal ( SIGTERM ) to the specified process(s). 这些命令的一个常见用途是向进程发送信号，让它退出（这就是 kill 这个不幸的名字的由来）。注意，在前台运行的进程也可以用 CTRL-C 终止，它向在前台运行的进程发送一个 SIGINT 信号，这个信号默认让进程退出。 A common use of these commands is to send a process a signal to tell it to exit (this is where kill gets its unfortunate name). Note that a process running in the foreground also can be killed by typing CTRL-C , which sends the process running in the foreground a SIGINT signal that by default tells the process to exit. 下面是调用 pkill 终止所有 a.out 进程的例子： Here is an example call to pkill to kill all a.out processes: $ ps PID TTY TIME CMD 3032597 pts/72 00:00:00 bash 3033074 pts/72 00:00:04 a.out 3033076 pts/72 00:00:03 a.out 3033089 pts/72 00:00:02 a.out 3033105 pts/72 00:00:00 ps $ pkill a.out [1] Terminated ./a.out [2]- Terminated ./a.out [3]+ Terminated ./a.out $ ps PID TTY TIME CMD 3032597 pts/72 00:00:00 bash 3033128 pts/72 00:00:00 ps 下面是调用 kill 终止某个特定 a.out 进程的例子，给出的是它的 PID（第一个 ps 列表中的第二个进程）： Here is an example call to kill to kill a specific a.out processes given its PID (the second process in the first ps listing): $ ps PID TTY TIME CMD 3032597 pts/72 00:00:00 bash 3033870 pts/72 00:00:03 a.out 3033883 pts/72 00:00:02 a.out 3033886 pts/72 00:00:01 a.out 3033897 pts/72 00:00:00 ps $ kill 3033883 [2]- Terminated ./a.out $ ps PID TTY TIME CMD 3032597 pts/72 00:00:00 bash 3033870 pts/72 00:00:18 a.out 3033886 pts/72 00:00:16 a.out 3033974 pts/72 00:00:00 ps 注意， kill 只终止了 PID 匹配的那个特定进程，而不是每一个运行同一程序（ a.out ）的进程。 Note that kill only killed the specific process with a matching pid value and not every process running the same program ( a.out ). 在这两个例子中，我们都没有指定要发送的信号。在没有任何可选命令行选项的情况下， kill 和 pkill 向进程发送终止信号（ SIGTERM ，即信号编号 15 ）。默认情况下， SIGTERM 让收到信号的进程退出。有时你会看到在调用 kill 和 pkill 时带有一个不同的信号编号。在这种情况下，信号编号作为命令行参数指定（ -<信号编号> ）。例如，我们可以加上信号编号 -9 ，向进程发送 SIGKILL 信号（又一种让进程退出的方式）： In both of these examples, we are not specifying the signal to send. Without any optional command line options, kill and pkill send the process the terminate signal ( SIGTERM or signal number 15 ). By default, SIGTERM tells the signaled process to exit. Sometimes you will see calls to kill and pkill that include a different signal number. In this case the signal number is specified as a command line argument ( -<signal number>'). For example, we could have included the signal number `-9 to send them the SIGKILL signal (yet another way to tell a process to exit): $ pkill -9 a.out $ kill -9 3033883 一般来说，这些命令可以用来向进程发送任何信号。例如，要向进程发送一个 SIGALRM 信号（信号编号为 14 ），可以这样做： In general, these commands can be used to send any signal to a process. For example, to send a process a SIGALRM signal (which is signal number 14 ), you could do this: $ kill -14 3033883 如果进程没有 SIGALRM 信号的信号处理程序，默认行为是这个 SIGALRM 信号被简单地忽略。 If the process doesn’t have a signal handler for the SIGALRM signal, the default behavior is that the SIGALRM signal is just ignored. 译注 这一说法有误。按 signal(7) 手册中的信号列表， SIGALRM （alarm(2) 发出的定时器信号）的默认动作是 Term ，即终止进程，而不是忽略。所以如果进程没有为 SIGALRM 注册处理程序，执行 kill -14 <pid> 会让它退出。默认动作为忽略（Ign）的是 SIGCHLD 等少数信号。 signal 的手册页列出了系统中定义的最基本的信号集合（及其信号编号）： man 7 signal 。 The man page for signal lists the minimal set of signals (and their signal numbers) that are defined in the system: man 7 signal . 17.9.3. 参考资料 17.9.3. References 更多信息参见： For more information see: 这些命令的手册页（例如 man ps 、 man pkill 、 man 7 signal ） The man pages for these commands (e.g., man ps , man pkill , man 7 signal ) cheat-sheets.org 上的 最常用的 Unix 命令 most used Unix commands from cheat-sheets.org gnu.org 上的 Bash 参考手册 。 Bash Reference Manual from gnu.org.

x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/Appendix2/makefiles.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 17.5. make and Makefiles 在本节中，我们讨论 make 命令和 Makefile。我们会给出一些例子，从简单的 Makefile 开始，逐步构建出一个更复杂、更通用的 Makefile（ 第 17.5.10 节 ），它适合作为大多数用途的起点。关于编写 Makefile 的更多信息，参见 GNU Make 手册 。 In this section we discuss the make command and Makefiles. We present some examples starting from simple Makefile and building up to a more complex and more generic Makefile ( Section 17.5.10 ) that is a good starting point for most uses. For more information about writing Makefiles see the GNU Make Manual . 17.5.1. 关于 make 17.5.1. About make Unix 的 make 工具简化了程序的编译。用户（或程序）在 Makefile 中写好要执行的规则。用户只需运行 make ， make 程序就会从 Makefile 中读入告诉它如何编译程序的规则。 The Unix make utility simplifies compiling programs. A user (or a program) writes the Makefile with the rules to execute. A user just runs make and the make program reads in rules from the Makefile that tell it how to compile a program. make 的一个好处是，只需输入 make 就能执行复杂的命令来构建可执行文件，而不必每次都由用户输入很长的 gcc 命令来构建。较大的程序常常被拆分成由多个 .c 和 .h 文件组成的独立模块。它们还可能要链接多个库，或者把头文件和库文件存放在非标准的位置。所有这些都会让编译变得更复杂， gcc 命令行也更长、更复杂。在这些情况下，在 shell 提示符下手动输入完整的 gcc 命令行既费时又容易出错。例如，下面是一条很长的 gcc 命令行，手动输入它会很繁琐： One benefit of make is that it can execute complex commands to build executable files simply by typing make versus the user having to type in long gcc commands to build each time. Larger programs are often split into separate modules consisting of multiple .c and .h files. They may also link in multiple libraries, or store header and library files in non-standard locations. All of these make compiling more complicated, and gcc command lines longer and more complex. In these cases, manually typing the full gcc command line at the shell prompt is both time consuming and error prone. For example, here is a long gcc command line that would be tedious to type by hand: gcc -Wall -g -I../includes -I. -o mycc emitter.c init.c lexer.c symbol.c parser.c ast.c error.c symbol_table.c codegen.c emitcode.c main.c -L../libs -lmylib -lpthread 有了 make ，用户只需输入 make ，就能执行 Makefile 中列出的命令。 With make the user simply types make to execute the commands listed in the Makefile. make 的另一个好处是，它只重新构建那些需要重新构建的东西，即那些依赖于自上次构建以来被修改过的文件的目标文件和可执行文件。对于大型程序，从头开始编译所有东西可能非常耗时，因此 make 只重新构建需要重新构建的东西，可以节省大量的编译时间。 Another benefit of make is that it only rebuilds those things that need to be rebuilt — just the object and executable files that depend on files that have been modified since the last time they were built. For large programs, compiling everything from scratch can be very time consuming, and thus make can save a lot of compilation time by only rebuilding those things that need to be rebuilt. 用户通常自己编写 Makefile，写好让 make 执行的规则。也有一些程序（例如 CMake 和 GNU Autotools）可以生成 Makefile。它们通常用于构建大型软件，以及方便地支持跨不同系统的编译，包括在特定系统上找到所需的编译器和其他软件、库以及头文件。 A user typically writes the Makefile with the rules for make to execute. There are also programs, like CMake and GNU Autotools, that generate Makefiles. These are typically used for building large software and for easily supporting compilation across different systems that includes finding needed compilers and other software, libraries, and header files on a particular system. 17.5.2. 使用 make 17.5.2. Using make 使用 make 的步骤是： The steps for using make are: 创建一个 Makefile，列出构建可执行文件的规则。默认情况下，这个文件应当命名为「Makefile」。这只需要做一次，除非程序中加入了新的模块（.c 或 .h 文件），这时就需要更新 Makefile，给现有的规则加上新模块的依赖，或者加入新的规则把它们纳入编译。 Create a Makefile listing the rules for building the executable. By default the file should be named ‘Makefile’. This only has to be done once, except when new modules (.c or .h files) are added to the program, then the Makefile needs to be updated to add new module dependencies to existing rules or to add new rules to include them in compilation. 编辑了程序文件之后，输入 make 重新构建可执行文件： $ make 可以这样输入来执行 Makefile 中某条特定的规则： $ make target_label 例如，要执行 rm 命令删除下面列出的示例 Makefile 所构建的所有文件，输入： $ make clean After editing program file(s), rebuild the executable by typing make: $ make A specific rule in the Makefile can be executed by typing: $ make target_label For example, to execute the rm command to remove all built files in the example Makefile listed below, type: $ make clean 17.5.3. 创建 Makefile 17.5.3. Creating a Makefile Makefile 通常以一些变量定义开头，后面是一组用于构建特定目标（通常是构建 .o 文件和可执行文件）的规则（或称目标条目）。每条规则由一个目标标签和一组为该目标运行的相关命令（有时称为配方，recipe）组成。下面是规则的一般格式： A Makefile typically starts with some variable definitions which are then followed by a set of rules (or target entries) for building specific targets (typically for building .o and executable files). Each rule consists of a target label and a set of associated commands (sometimes called recipes) that are run for the target. The following is the general format of a rule: # comment # (note: the <tab> in the command line is necessary for make to work) target: dependency1 dependency2 ... <tab> command 下面是一个例子： Here is an example: # target entry to build program executable from program.o # and util.o object files # program: program.o util.o gcc -o program program.o util.o 原书警示 · make 与空白字符（Make and whitespace characters） make 对空白字符非常挑剔。例如，在 Makefile 目标条目的命令部分所在行之前的 <tab>，对 make 正确解析目标条目并执行命令部分非常重要。例如，如果你用空格字符代替 <tab>， make 就不能正确解析这个目标条目，也不会运行它的相关命令。 make is very picky about whitespace characters. For example, the <tab> on the line before the command part of a Makefile target entry is very important for make to correctly parse the target entry and execute the command part. If, for example, you use space characters in place of the <tab>, then make will not correctly parse the target entry and will not run its associated command. 17.5.4. 一个简单的 Makefile 17.5.4. A Simple Makefile 下面是一个简单的 Makefile 示例，它从单个名为 myprog.c 的 .c 文件构建一个可执行文件： Here is an example simple Makefile that builds an executable from a single .c file named myprog.c : # build an executable named myprog from myprog.c all: myprog.c gcc -g -Wall -o myprog myprog.c clean: rm myprog 输入 make 会触发与 all 目标标签相关联的命令：如果文件 myprog.c 的修改日期比文件 myprog 的修改日期新，或者 myprog 不存在，就运行 gcc -g -Wall -o myprog myprog.c 。注意，名字 all 并没有什么特别之处，默认情况下， make 选择 Makefile 中的第一个目标标签来执行。要执行除列出的第一条规则之外的某条特定规则，在 make 命令行上写出目标名即可。例如， make clean 运行 rm myprog 命令，删除之前构建的可执行文件 myprog 。 Typing make triggers the command associated with the all target label to run gcc -g -Wall -o myprog myprog.c if the modification date on the file myprog.c is newer than the modification date on the file myprog or if myprog doesn’t exist. Note that the name all isn’t special, by default make picks the first target label in the Makefile to execute. To execute a specific rule other than the first one listed in the makefile, list the target name on the make command line. For example, make clean runs the rm myprog command to remove the previously built executable file myprog . 在 第 17.5.8 节 中，我们会展示如何用 Makefile 变量编写这个 Makefile 更通用的版本，只需复制并稍作修改，就能为构建另一个程序创建新的 Makefile。 In Section 17.5.8 we show how to use Makefile variables to write more generic versions of this Makefile—​one that can be copied and minimally edited to create a new Makefile for building a different program. 17.5.5. 用于多个源文件的 Makefile 17.5.5. A Makefile for multiple source files 下面是一个从多个 .c 和 .h 文件构建可执行文件的 Makefile 示例。它先把每个 .c 编译成一个 .o 文件，然后把各个 .o 和库链接在一起，构建出可执行文件。由于它为每个 .o 文件列出了依赖关系，如果修改了某一个 .c 文件，就只需要重新构建一个 .o （依赖于被修改的那个 .c 的那个），而不会重新构建所有的 .o 文件。对于由许多 .c 文件组成的较大程序，这是一个特别好的特性，能加快编译时间。 Below is an example Makefile for building an executable from multiple .c and .h files. It first compiles each .c into a .o file, and then links the .o and libraries together to build the executable. Because it lists dependencies for each .o file, if one .c file is modified only one .o needs to be rebuilt (the one that is dependent on the modified .c ) and it does not rebuild all .o files. This is a particularly nice feature that speeds up compile time for larger programs consisting of many .c files. # Example Makefile for a program with many .c modules # make: build count executable program # make clean: clean-up all built files all: count # To create the executable file count we need the object files # countwords.o, counter.o, and scanner.o: count: countwords.o counter.o scanner.o gcc -g -Wall -o count countwords.o counter.o scanner.o # To create the object file countwords.o, we need the source # files countwords.c, scanner.h, and counter.h: countwords.o: countwords.c scanner.h counter.h gcc -g -Wall -c countwords.c # To create the object file counter.o, we need the source files # counter.c and counter.h: counter.o: counter.c counter.h gcc -g -Wall -c counter.c # To create the object file scanner.o, we need the source files # scanner.c and scanner.h: scanner.o: scanner.c scanner.h gcc -g -Wall -c scanner.c # To start over from scratch, type 'make clean'. This # removes the executable file, as well as old .o object # files and *~ backup files: clean: rm -f count *.o *~ 第一次运行 make 之后，如果修改了 counter.c 文件，那么下次运行 make 时，只会执行下面这两条规则（因为它们依赖于 counter.c 或 counter.o ）： After running make the first time, if the counter.c file is modified, then on the next run of make , only these two rules are executed (due to their dependency on counter.c or counter.o ): counter.o: counter.c counter.h gcc -g -Wall -c counter.c count: countwords.o counter.o scanner.o gcc -g -Wall -o count countwords.o counter.o scanner.o 在 第 17.5.9 节 和 第 17.5.10 节 中，我们会展示如何利用 Makefile 变量、Makefile 隐式规则和自动依赖生成，来编写更通用的 Makefile。 第 17.5.10 节 中的 Makefile 是一个很好的通用 Makefile，适用于由许多 .c 和 .h 文件构建、并且构建时可能要用到存放在非标准位置的头文件或库的应用程序。 In Section 17.5.9 and Section 17.5.10 we show how to use Makefile variables, implicit Makefile rules, and automatic dependency generation, to write more generic versions of a Makefile. However, for loops are a more natural language construct for definite loops (like iterating over a range of values), whereas while loops are a more natural language construct for indefinite loops (like repeating until the user enters an even number). As a result, C provides both to programmers.

A variable’s scope defines when the variable has meaning (that is, where and when in your program it can be used) and its lifetime (that is, it could persist for the entire run of a program or only during a function activation). The Stack 执行栈 （execution stack）记录程序中处于活动状态的函数的状态。每次函数调用都会创建一个新的 栈帧 （stack frame，有时也称 活动帧 或 活动记录 ，activation frame / activation record），其中包含该次调用的形参和局部变量的值。栈顶的帧是活动帧，它代表当前正在执行的函数调用，只有它的局部变量和形参在作用域内。调用一个函数时，会为它创建一个新的栈帧（ 压入 栈顶），并在新帧中为它的局部变量和形参分配空间。函数返回时，它的栈帧被从栈中移除（从栈顶 弹出 ），调用者的栈帧重新回到栈顶。 The execution stack keeps track of the state of active functions in a program. Each function call creates a new stack frame (sometimes called an activation frame or activation record ) containing its parameter and local variable values. The frame on the top of the stack is the active frame; it represents the function activation that is currently executing, and only its local variables and parameters are in scope. When a function is called, a new stack frame is created for it ( pushed on the top of the stack), and space for its local variables and parameters is allocated in the new frame. When a function returns, its stack frame is removed from the stack ( popped from the top of the stack), leaving the caller’s stack frame on the top of the stack. 对于前面的示例程序，在执行到 max 即将执行 return 语句的那一刻，执行栈的样子如 图 1 所示。回想一下， main 传给 max 的实参值是 按值传递 的，也就是说 max 的形参 x 和 y 被赋予了 main 中调用时对应实参 a 和 b 的值。尽管 max 函数修改了 x 的值，这一修改并不会影响 main 中 a 的值。 For the example preceding program, at the point in its execution right before max executes the return statement, the execution stack will look like Figure 1 . Arrays and Strings 数组 （array）是 C 的一种构造，它创建一个由相同类型的数据元素组成的有序集合，并把这个集合与一个程序变量关联起来。 有序 的意思是每个元素在值的集合中都处于特定的位置（即有位置 0 的元素、位置 1 的元素，依此类推），而不是说这些值一定已经排好序。数组是 C 把多个数据值组织在一起、并用单个名字引用它们的主要机制之一。数组有好几种形式，最基本的是 一维数组 ，它可以用来在 C 中实现类似列表的数据结构和字符串。 An array is a C construct that creates an ordered collection of data elements of the same type and associates this collection with a single program variable. Ordered means that each element is in a specific position in the collection of values (that is, there is an element in position 0, position 1, and so on), not that the values are necessarily sorted. Arrays are one of C’s primary mechanisms for grouping multiple data values and referring to them by a single name. Arrays come in several flavors, but the basic form is a one-dimensional array , which is useful for implementing list-like data structures and strings in C. 1.5.1. 数组简介 1.5.1. Introduction to Arrays C 数组可以存储多个 相同 类型的数据值。本章讨论 静态声明 （statically declared）的数组，即数组的总容量（数组最多能存储的元素个数）是固定的，在声明数组变量时就确定了。下一章我们会讨论 动态分配的数组 和 多维数组 。 C arrays can store multiple data values of the same type. In this chapter, we discuss statically declared arrays, meaning that the total capacity (the maximum number of elements that can be stored in an array) is fixed and is defined when the array variable is declared. In the next chapter, we discuss dynamically allocated arrays and multi-dimensional arrays . 表 1 给出了一个程序的 Python 版本和 C 版本，该程序初始化一组整数值并把它们打印出来。Python 版本用内置的列表类型存储这组值，而 C 版本用一个 int 类型的数组来存储。 Table 1 shows Python and C versions of a program that initializes and then prints a collection of integer values. The Python version uses its built-in list type to store the list of values, whereas the C version uses an array of int types to store the collection of values. 总的来说，Python 为程序员提供了一个高级的列表接口，隐藏了大部分底层实现细节。而 C 则把底层的数组实现暴露给程序员，由程序员自己去实现更高级的功能。换句话说，数组提供的是底层的数据存储，没有 len 、 append 、 insert 等更高级的列表功能。 In general, Python provides a high-level list interface to the programmer that hides much of the low-level implementation details. C, on the other hand, exposes a low-level array implementation to the programmer and leaves it up to the programmer to implement higher-level functionality. ", my_arr[i]); } return 0; } 这个程序的 C 版本和 Python 版本有几处相似之处，最明显的是都可以通过 下标 （indexing）访问单个元素，并且下标值都从 0 开始。也就是说，两种语言都把集合中的第一个元素称为位置 0 上的元素。 The C and Python versions of this program have several similarities, most notably that individual elements can be accessed via indexing , and that index values start at 0 . That is, both languages refer to the very first element in a collection as the element at position 0 . 这个程序的 C 版本和 Python 版本的主要区别，在于列表或数组的容量，以及如何确定它们的大小（元素个数）。 The main differences in the C and Python versions of this program relate to the capacity of the list or array and how their sizes (number of elements) are determined. 对于 Python 列表： For a Python list: my_lst[3] = 100 # Python syntax to set the element in position 3 to 100. my_lst[0] = 5 # Python syntax to set the first element to 5. 对于 C 数组： For a C array: my_arr[3] = 100; // C syntax to set the element in position 3 to 100. my_arr[0] = 5; // C syntax to set the first element to 5. 在 Python 版本中，程序员不需要事先指定列表的容量：Python 会根据程序的需要自动增加列表的容量。例如，Python 的 append 函数会自动增大 Python 列表的大小，并把传入的值添加到末尾。 In the Python version, the programmer doesn’t need to specify the capacity of a list in advance: Python automatically increases a list’s capacity as needed by the program. C dictates the array layout in program memory, whereas Python hides how lists are implemented from the programmer. In C, individual array elements are allocated in consecutive locations in the program’s memory. For example, the third array position is located in memory immediately following the second array position and immediately before the fourth array position. 1.5.2. 访问数组的方法 1.5.2. Array Access Methods Python 提供了多种访问列表元素的方式。而 C 只支持前面介绍的下标访问。有效的下标值范围是从 0 到数组容量减 1。下面是一些例子： Python provides multiple ways to access elements in its lists. C, however, supports only indexing, as described earlier. Valid index values range from 0 to the capacity of the array minus 1. Arrays are used to create an ordered collection of data elements of the same type, whereas structs are used to create a collection of data elements of different types . It does, however, support defining structured types, which are like the data part of classes. A struct is a type used to represent a heterogeneous collection of data; it’s a mechanism for treating a set of different types as a single, coherent unit. Thus, a struct variable can be assigned the value of another struct variable using a simple assignment statement. The field values of the struct on the right side of the assignment statement are copied to the field values of the struct on the left side of the assignment statement. In other words, the contents of memory of one struct are copied to the memory of the other. Here’s an example of assigning a struct’s values in this way: student2 = student1; // student2 gets the value of student1 // (student1's field values are copied to // corresponding field values of student2) strcpy(student2.name, "Frances Allen"); // change one field value 图 2 展示了执行完这条赋值语句和 strcpy 调用之后两个学生变量的值。注意，图中把 name 字段画成了其中存放的字符串值，而不是完整的 64 字符数组。 Figure 2 shows the values of the two student variables after the assignment statement and call to strcpy have executed. The sizeof operator can be used on any C type, including struct types, to see how much memory space a variable of that type needs. ", student2.name, student2.age, student2.gpa, student2.grad_yr); /* Print the size of the struct studentT type. */ printf("number of bytes in student struct: %lu
", sizeof(struct studentT)); return 0; } 运行时，这个程序输出如下内容： When run, this program outputs the following: name: Kwame Salter age: 20 gpa: 3.5, year: 2020 name: Frances Allen age: 20 gpa: 3.5, year: 2021 number of bytes in student struct: 76 原书旁注 · 左值（lvalues） 左值 （lvalue）是可以出现在赋值语句左边的表达式，它代表一个内存存储位置。随着我们介绍 C 的指针类型，以及把数组、结构体和指针组合起来创建更复杂结构的例子，仔细思考类型、记住哪些 C 表达式是合法的左值（可以用在赋值语句左边）就变得很重要。 就我们目前对 C 的了解，基本类型的单个变量、数组元素和结构体都是左值。静态声明的数组的名字 不是 左值（你不能改变静态声明的数组在内存中的基地址）。下面的示例代码片段根据不同类型的左值属性，说明了哪些 C 赋值语句合法、哪些不合法： struct studentT { char name[32]; int age; float gpa; int grad_yr; }; int main(void) { struct studentT student1, student2; int x; char arr[10], ch; x = 10; // Valid C: x is an lvalue ch = 'm'; // Valid C: ch is an lvalue student1.age = 18; // Valid C: age field is an lvalue student2 = student1; // Valid C: student2 is an lvalue arr[3] = ch; // Valid C: arr[3] is an lvalue x + 1 = 8; // Invalid C: x+1 is not an lvalue arr = "hello"; // Invalid C: arr is not an lvalue // cannot change base addr of statically declared array // (use strcpy to copy the string value "hello" to arr) student1.name = student2.name; // Invalid C: name field is not an lvalue // (the base address of a statically // declared array cannot be changed) An lvalue is an expression that can appear on the left side of an assignment statement. It’s an expression that represents a memory storage location. As we introduce C pointer types and examples of creating more complicated structures that combine C arrays, structs, and pointers, it’s important to think carefully about types and to keep in mind which C expressions are valid lvalues (which can be used on the left side of an assignment statement). From what we know about C so far, single variables of base types, array elements, and structs are all lvalues. The name of a statically declared array is not an lvalue (you cannot change the base address of a statically declared array in memory). The following example code snippet illustrates valid and invalid C assignment statements based on the lvalue status of different types: struct studentT { char name[32]; int age; float gpa; int grad_yr; }; int main(void) { struct studentT student1, student2; int x; char arr[10], ch; x = 10; // Valid C: x is an lvalue ch = 'm'; // Valid C: ch is an lvalue student1.age = 18; // Valid C: age field is an lvalue student2 = student1; // Valid C: student2 is an lvalue arr[3] = ch; // Valid C: arr[3] is an lvalue x + 1 = 8; // Invalid C: x+1 is not an lvalue arr = "hello"; // Invalid C: arr is not an lvalue // cannot change base addr of statically declared array // (use strcpy to copy the string value "hello" to arr) student1.name = student2.name; // Invalid C: name field is not an lvalue // (the base address of a statically // declared array cannot be changed) 译注 这段示例只为说明左值规则，省略了 main 函数结尾的 return 0; 和 } ，而且其中标为 Invalid 的语句本来就无法通过编译。 1.6.4. 把结构体传给函数 1.6.4. Passing Structs to Functions 在 C 中，所有类型的实参都是 按值传递 给函数的。因此，如果函数有一个结构体类型的形参，那么用结构体实参调用它时，实参的 值 会被传给形参，也就是说形参得到的是实参值的一份副本。结构体变量的值就是它的内存内容，这正是我们可以用一条赋值语句把一个结构体的各字段赋成与另一个结构体相同的原因： In C, arguments of all types are passed by value to functions. Thus, if a function has a struct type parameter, then when called with a struct argument, the argument’s value is passed to its parameter, meaning that the parameter gets a copy of its argument’s value. The value of a struct variable is the contents of its memory, which is why we can assign the fields of one struct to be the same as another struct in a single assignment statement like this: student2 = student1; 由于结构体变量的值代表其内存的全部内容，把结构体作为实参传给函数，形参得到的是实参结构体全部字段值的一份 副本 。如果函数修改了结构体形参的字段值，这些修改对实参的对应字段值 没有影响 。也就是说，对形参字段的修改只改变形参中这些字段所在内存位置的值，而不会改变实参中这些字段所在内存位置的值。 Because the value of a struct variable represents the full contents of its memory, passing a struct as an argument to a function gives the parameter a copy of all the argument struct’s field values. If the function changes the field values of a struct parameter, the changes to the parameter’s field values have no effect on the corresponding field values of the argument. That is, changes to the parameter’s fields only modify values in the parameter’s memory locations for those fields, not in the argument’s memory locations for those fields. 下面是一个使用 checkID 函数（它接收一个结构体参数）的 完整示例程序 ： Here’s a full example program using the checkID function that takes a struct parameter: #include <stdio.h> #include <string.h> /* struct type definition: */ struct studentT { char name[64]; int age; float gpa; int grad_yr; }; /* function prototype (prototype: a declaration of the * checkID function so that main can call it, its full * definition is listed after main function in the file): */ int checkID(struct studentT s1, int min_age); int main(void) { int can_vote; struct studentT student; strcpy(student.name, "Ruth"); student.age = 17; student.gpa = 3.5; student.grad_yr = 2021; can_vote = checkID(student, 18); if (can_vote) { printf("%s is %d years old and can vote.
", student.name, student.age); } else { printf("%s is only %d years old and cannot vote.
", student.name, student.age); } return 0; } /* check if a student is at least the min age * s: a student * min_age: a minimum age value to test * returns: 1 if the student is min_age or older, 0 otherwise */ int checkID(struct studentT s, int min_age) { int ret = 1; // initialize the return value to 1 (true) if (s.age < min_age) { ret = 0; // update the return value to 0 (false) // let's try changing the student's age s.age = min_age + 1; } printf("%s is %d years old
", s.name, s.age); return ret; } 当 main 调用 checkID 时， student 结构体的值（其所有字段内存内容的一份副本）被传给形参 s 。当函数修改其形参的 age 字段值时， 不会 影响实参（ student ）的 age 字段。运行这个程序就能看到这一行为，它的输出如下： When main calls checkID , the value of the student struct (a copy of the memory contents of all its fields) is passed to the s parameter. When the function changes the value of its parameter’s age field, it doesn’t affect the age field of its argument ( student ). This behavior can be seen by running the program, which outputs the following: Ruth is 19 years old Ruth is only 17 years old and cannot vote. 输出表明，当 checkID 打印 age 字段时，反映的是函数对形参 s 的 age 字段所做的修改。然而，函数调用返回后， main 打印出的 student 的 age 字段值与调用 checkID 之前相同。 图 3 展示了 checkID 函数即将返回时调用栈的内容。 The output shows that when checkID prints the age field, it reflects the function’s change to the age field of the parameter s . However, after the function call returns, main prints the age field of student with the same value it had prior to the checkID call. Figure 3 illustrates the contents of the call stack just before the checkID function returns. 图 3. 从 checkID 函数返回之前调用栈的内容 Figure 3. The contents of the call stack before returning from the checkID function 译注 · 图中内容 把 student 结构体传给 checkID 时，形参得到它全部内容的副本。checkID 把 age 字段改成 19，修改只作用于它的本地副本；main 中 student 结构体的 age 字段仍是 17。 当结构体含有静态声明的数组字段（如 struct studentT 中的 name 字段）时，理解结构体参数的按值传递语义尤为重要。把这样的结构体传给函数时，结构体实参的全部内存内容，包括数组字段中的每个数组元素，都会被复制给形参。如果函数修改了形参结构体中数组的内容，这些修改在函数返回后 不会 保留。考虑到我们之前了解的 数组传给函数的方式 ，这种行为可能显得有些奇怪，但它与前面描述的结构体复制行为是一致的。 Understanding the pass-by-value semantics of struct parameters is particularly important when a struct contains a statically declared array field (like the name field in struct studentT ). When such a struct is passed to a function, the struct argument’s entire memory contents, including every array element in the array field, is copied to its parameter. If the parameter struct’s array contents are changed by the function, those changes will not persist after the function returns. This behavior might seem odd given what we know about how arrays are passed to functions , but it’s consistent with the struct-copying behavior described earlier.

Key Assembly Takeaways 本书的这一部分介绍了汇编的基础知识。虽然如今大多数人用高级程序设计语言编程，但理解汇编能让程序员更好地理解自己的程序和编译器在做什么。对于为嵌入式系统和其他资源受限环境设计软件的人，以及从事漏洞分析的人来说，汇编知识也是必不可少的。本书汇编部分的各章涵盖了 64 位 Intel 汇编（x86-64）、32 位 Intel 汇编（IA32）和 64 位 ARM 汇编（ARMv8-A）。 This part of the book has covered the basics of assembly. While most people today code in a high-level programming language, an understanding of assembly increases a programmer’s ability to better understand what their programs and compilers are doing. A knowledge of assembly is also essential for anyone who designs software for embedded systems and other resource-constrained environments, and for people who work in vulnerability analysis. The chapters contained in the assembly part of this book have spanned 64-bit Intel assembly (x86-64), 32-bit Intel Assembly (IA32), and 64-bit ARM assembly (ARMv8-A). 共同特征 Common Features 无论学的是哪一种具体的汇编语言， 所有 汇编语言都有一些值得强调的共同特征。 Regardless of the specific assembly language that one learns, there are some common features to all assembly languages worth highlighting. ISA 定义了汇编语言 一台机器上可用的具体汇编语言由这台机器的 指令集架构 （ISA）定义。要识别某台 Linux 机器的底层体系结构，使用 uname -m 命令。 The ISA defines the assembly language The specific assembly language available on a machine is defined by the instruction set architecture (ISA) of that machine. To identify the underlying architecture of a particular Linux machine, use the uname -m command. 寄存器存放数据 每种 ISA 都定义了一组基本的 寄存器 ，CPU 用它们来处理数据。有些寄存器是 通用 的，可以存放任何类型的数据；另一些寄存器是 专用 的，通常由编译器保留作特定用途（例如栈指针、基址指针）。通用寄存器可读可写，而有些专用寄存器是只读的（例如指令指针）。 Registers hold data Every ISA defines a set of basic registers that the CPU uses to operate on data. Some registers are general purpose and can hold any kind of data, whereas other registers are special purpose and are typically reserved by the compiler for specific uses (e.g., stack pointer, base pointer). While general purpose registers are readable and writable, some special purposes registers are read-only (e.g., the instruction pointer). 指令规定了 CPU 能做什么 ISA 还定义了一系列 指令 ，规定 CPU 可以执行的操作。每条指令都有一个指明它做什么的 操作码 （opcode），以及一个或多个指明所用数据的 操作数 （operand）。ISA 规定了用于数据移动、算术运算、条件判断、分支和内存访问的具体指令。这些核心指令常常组合起来，用于表示数组、结构体和矩阵等更复杂的数据结构。 Instructions specify what the CPU can do The ISA also defines a series of instructions that specify operations that the CPU can perform. Each instruction has an operation code (opcode) that specifies what the instruction does, and one or more operands that specifies the data to be used. The ISA documents specific instructions for data movement, arithmetic operations, conditionals, branches, and accessing memory. These core instructions are often combined to represent more complex data structures like arrays, structs, and matrices. 程序栈存放与特定函数相关的局部变量 编译器使用进程虚拟地址空间中的栈（即栈内存）来存放临时数据。在所有现代系统上，程序栈都向 低 内存地址方向增长。编译器用栈指针和基址指针来指定一个 栈帧 ，它界定了栈中与某个特定函数或过程相关的区域。每次函数调用都会在栈上添加一个新的栈帧，界定与被调用函数相关的栈区域。函数返回时，与它相关的栈帧被从栈中移除。通常，函数结束时栈指针和基址指针会恢复为原来的值。虽然这种簿记工作暗示局部变量已从栈中「清理」掉了，但旧数据通常会以垃圾值的形式残留下来，有时会导致难以调试的行为。恶意攻击者还可以利用对 ISA 栈簿记方式的了解，制造缓冲区溢出等危险的安全攻击。 The program stack holds local variables associated with a particular function The compiler uses the stack (or stack memory) of a process’s virtual address space to store temporary data. On all modern systems, the program stack grows toward lower memory addresses. The compiler uses the stack pointer and base pointer to specify a stack frame that defines the area of the stack that is associated with a particular function or procedure. A new stack frame is added to the stack with every function call and defines the stack region associated with the callee function. The stack frame associated with a particular function is removed from the stack when that function returns. Typically, the stack and base pointers return to their original values when a function ends. While this bit of bookkeeping suggests that local variables are “cleaned” from the stack, old data usually sticks around in the form of junk values, which can sometimes lead to hard-to-debug behaviors. Malicious actors can also use knowledge of an ISA’s stack bookkeeping to create dangerous security exploits, like buffer overflows. 安全 虽然所有系统都容易受到缓冲区溢出之类的安全漏洞的影响，但相对较新的 ARMv8-A 有机会吸取影响较老的 Intel 体系结构的一些安全缺陷的教训。不过，第一道防线永远是程序员。即使有额外的保护措施，也没有哪种 ISA 能完全免受潜在安全缺陷的影响。用 C 编程时，程序员应尽可能使用 长度说明 ，以减少因越界而导致安全漏洞的可能性（见 表 1 ）。 Security While all systems are vulnerable to security vulnerabilities like buffer overflow, the relatively recent ARMv8-A has had the opportunity to learn from some of the security flaws that affected older Intel architectures. However, the first line of defense is always the programmer. Even with additional protections, no ISA is invulnerable to potential security flaws. When coding in C, programmers should use length specifiers whenever possible to reduce the chance of security vulnerabilities resulting from boundary overruns (see Table 1 ). 表 1. 带长度说明的 C 函数 Table 1. C functions with Length Specifiers 不要用： 改用： gets(buf) fgets(buf, 12, stdin) scanf("%s", buf) scanf("%12s", buf) strcpy(buf2, buf) strncpy(buf2, buf, 12) strcat(buf2, buf) strncat(buf2, buf, 12) sprintf(buf, "%d", num) snprintf(buf, 12, "%d", num) Instead of: Use: gets(buf) fgets(buf, 12, stdin) scanf("%s", buf) scanf("%12s", buf) strcpy(buf2, buf) strncpy(buf2, buf, 12) strcat(buf2, buf) strncat(buf2, buf, 12) sprintf(buf, "%d", num) snprintf(buf, 12, "%d", num) 译注 · 表中有两处仍会溢出 ** scanf("%12s", buf) 应为 %11s **： %s 的宽度只限制读入的字符数， scanf 还要在后面再写一个 '\0' ，所以 %12s 最多写 13 字节，对 12 字节的 buf 正好越界 1 字节。译者用 clang 编译这一行，会得到警告： 'scanf' may overflow; destination buffer in argument 2 has size 12, but the corresponding specifier may require size 13 。 fgets(buf, 12, stdin) 和 snprintf(buf, 12, ...) 的 12 则是包含 '\0' 在内的缓冲区总大小，是对的。 strncat 的第三个参数不是目标缓冲区的大小 ，而是最多从源串追加多少个字符；目标缓冲区至少要有 strlen(dst) + strnlen(src, n) + 1 字节（见 strncat(3) ）。若 buf2 中已有内容， strncat(buf2, buf, 12) 照样会溢出，安全的上限应是 sizeof(buf2) - strlen(buf2) - 1 。 strncpy(buf2, buf, 12) 不会溢出，但当 buf 的长度不小于 12 时，它不会写入 '\0' ， buf2 将不是一个合法的字符串（参见第 2 章关于字符串函数的译注）。 延伸阅读 Further Reading 本书只让你初步领略了几种最流行的汇编语言。想更深入地理解汇编，建议查阅各个 ISA 的规范： This book offers just a taste of some of the most popular assembly languages in use. For more in-depth understanding of assembly, we encourage you to check out the ISA specifications: Intel 64 与 IA-32 体系结构手册 Intel 64 and IA32 Manuals 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· 延伸阅读的新地址，以及第四种值得了解的 ISA Intel 手册 ：原书链接所在的 software.intel.com 页面已迁到 Intel 开发者网站。Intel 64 与 IA-32 体系结构软件开发者手册仍免费提供，分为合订本、四卷本和十卷本，三套内容完全相同；截至 2026 年 10 月的页面，各卷 PDF 为第 093 版，其中第 2A–2D 卷是按字母排序的指令参考，查某条指令的确切语义时最常用。 Intel：Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer Manuals RISC-V ：除了本书讲的 x86 和 ARM，开放的 RISC-V 指令集也值得一看。它的规范在 GitHub 上公开维护，分为第一卷「非特权架构」（普通程序可用的指令，相当于本书各章讲的内容）、第二卷「特权架构」（操作系统使用的部分）和第三卷「Profiles」，各卷前言注明了哪些版本已由 RISC-V International 正式批准。 GitHub：riscv/riscv-isa-manual ARM Cortex-A 程序员指南 ARM Cortex-A Programmer’s Guide 对学习 32 位汇编感兴趣的读者，下面这些免费资源也可能有用： The following free resources may also be useful for those who are interested in learning 32-bit assembly: IA32 编程网络旁注 （Randal Bryant、David O’Hallaron 著） IA32 Programming Web Aside (Randal Bryant and David O’Hallaron) 32 位 ARM 汇编 （Azeria Labs） 32-bit ARM Assembly (Azeria Labs) 下面这些书也对汇编有深入的讨论；它们不是免费的，但都是很好的延伸阅读资源： The following books also feature in-depth discussions of assembly; these aren’t free, but they are great resources for further reading: Intel 系统： Computer Systems: A Programmer’s Perspective （中译本《深入理解计算机系统》，Randal Bryant、David O’Hallaron 著） Intel systems: Computer Systems: A Programmer’s Perspective (Randal Bryant and David O’Hallaron) ARMv8： Computer Organization and Design （中译本《计算机组成与设计：硬件/软件接口》，David Patterson、John Hennessy 著） ARMv8: Computer Organization and Design (David Patterson and John Hennessy)

Storage and the Memory Hierarchy 尽管设计和实现高效的算法通常是编写高性能程序 最 关键的一环，但还有另一个常被忽视、却可能对性能产生重大影响的因素：内存。也许出人意料的是，两个渐近性能相同（最坏情况下的步数相同）的算法，在相同的输入上运行时，由于执行它们的硬件的组织方式不同，实际表现可能大相径庭。这种差异通常源于算法的内存访问，尤其是它们把数据存放在哪里，以及访问数据时呈现出什么样的模式。这些模式称为 内存局部性 （memory locality）；要获得最佳性能，程序的访问模式需要与硬件的内存安排相契合。 Although designing and implementing efficient algorithms is typically the most critical aspect of writing programs that perform well, there’s another, often overlooked factor that can have a major impact on performance: memory. Perhaps surprisingly, two algorithms with the same asymptotic performance (number of steps in the worst case) run on the same inputs might perform very differently in practice due to the organization of the hardware on which they execute. Such differences generally stem from the algorithms’ memory accesses, particularly where they store data and the kinds of patterns they exhibit when accessing it. These patterns are referred to as memory locality , and to achieve the best performance, a program’s access patterns need to align well with the hardware’s memory arrangement. 例如，考虑 表 1 所示的、求 N × N 矩阵中各值平均数的函数的两个变体。尽管两个版本访问的内存位置相同、次数也相同（N 2 次），但在真实系统上，左边代码的执行速度大约是右边代码的五倍。差异来自它们访问这些内存位置的模式。在本章的末尾，我们会用内存剖析工具 Cachegrind 来分析这个例子。 For example, consider the following two variations of a function for averaging the values in an N × N matrix, as shown in Table 1 . Despite both versions accessing the same memory locations an equal number of times (N 2 ), the code on the left executes about five times faster on real systems than the code on the right. The difference arises from the patterns in which they access those memory locations. Toward the end of this chapter we analyze this example using the memory profiling tool Cachegrind . 译注 · 在 Apple M1 Pro 上实测 译者把这两个函数原样放进一个测试程序，用 malloc 逐行分配一个 8192×8192 的 int 矩阵（数组的数组），在 Apple M1 Pro 上计时： -O0 编译时 v1 约 0.09 秒、v2 约 0.66 秒； -O2 编译时 v1 约 0.035 秒、v2 约 0.26 秒，两种情况下 v2 都慢约 7 倍。具体倍数随机器和矩阵大小变化，但「按行访问远快于按列访问」的结论很稳定。 表 1. 访问 N x N 矩阵每个元素的函数的两个版本。它们的唯一区别是对矩阵的下标顺序。 Table 1. Two versions of a function that accesses every element of an N x N* matrix. They only differ in their memory indexing into the matrix.* float averageMat_v1(int **mat, int n) { int i, j, total = 0; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (j = 0; j < n; j++) { // Note indexing: [i][j] total += mat[i][j]; } } return (float) total / (n * n); } float averageMat_v2(int **mat, int n) { int i, j, total = 0; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (j = 0; j < n; j++) { // Note indexing: [j][i] total += mat[j][i]; } } return (float) total / (n * n); } 寄存器、CPU 缓存、主存和磁盘上的文件等存储位置，在访问时间、传输速率和存储容量上都有显著差别。编写高性能应用程序时，重要的是要考虑数据存放在哪里，以及程序访问每种设备上数据的频率。例如，程序启动时访问一次慢速磁盘，很少会成为大问题。另一方面，频繁访问磁盘则会大大拖慢程序。 Storage locations like registers, CPU caches, main memory, and files on disk all feature remarkably different access times, transfer rates, and storage capacities. When programming a high-performance application, it’s important to consider where data is stored and how frequently the program accesses each device’s data. For example, accessing a slow disk once as the program starts is rarely a major concern. On the other hand, accessing the disk frequently will slow down the program considerably. 本章描述多种多样的存储设备，并介绍它们在现代 PC 中是如何组织的。有了这些背景，我们就能看到如何把各种不同的存储设备组合起来，利用典型程序的内存访问模式中所具有的局部性。 This chapter characterizes a diverse set of memory devices and describes how they’re organized in a modern PC. With that context, we’ll see how a collection of varied memory devices can be combined to exploit the locality found in a typical program’s memory access patterns.

x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C11-MemHierarchy/devices.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 11.2. Storage Devices 系统设计者根据程序访问数据的方式，对 存储器层次结构 中的设备进行分类。CPU 上的程序可以直接访问 主存储 （primary storage）设备。也就是说，CPU 的汇编指令编码了指令要取的数据的确切位置。主存储的例子包括 CPU 寄存器和主存（RAM），汇编指令直接引用它们（例如在 IA32 汇编中分别写作 %reg 和 (%reg) ）。 Systems designers classify devices in the memory hierarchy according to how programs access their data. Primary storage devices can be accessed directly by a program on the CPU. That is, the CPU’s assembly instructions encode the exact location of the data that the instructions should retrieve. Examples of primary storage include CPU registers and main memory (RAM), which assembly instructions reference directly (for example, in IA32 assembly as %reg and (%reg) , respectively). 与之不同，CPU 指令不能直接引用 辅助存储 （secondary storage）设备。要访问辅助存储设备的内容，程序必须先请求该设备把数据复制到主存储（通常是内存）中。最常见的辅助存储设备是硬盘驱动器和固态硬盘这样的磁盘设备，它们持久地存储文件数据。其他例子还有软盘、磁带盒，甚至远程文件服务器。 In contrast, CPU instructions cannot directly refer to secondary storage devices. To access the contents of a secondary storage device, a program must first request that the device copy its data into primary storage (typically memory). The most familiar types of secondary storage devices are disk devices such as hard disk drives and solid-state drives, which persistently store file data. Other examples include floppy disks, magnetic tape cartridges, or even remote file servers. 尽管你以前可能没有用这些术语思考过主存储和辅助存储的区别，但很可能已经在程序中遇到过它们的差异。例如，声明并赋值普通变量（主存储）之后，程序可以立即在算术运算中使用它们。而处理文件数据（辅助存储）时，程序必须先 把文件中的值读到内存变量中 ，才能访问它们。 Even though you may not have considered the distinction between primary and secondary storage in these terms before, it’s likely that you have encountered their differences in programs already. For example, after declaring and assigning ordinary variables (primary storage), a program can immediately use them in arithmetic operations. When working with file data (secondary storage), the program must read values from the file into memory variables before it can access them. 对存储设备进行分类的其他几个重要标准，来自它们的性能和容量特征。最值得关注的三个度量是： Several other important criteria for classifying memory devices arise from their performance and capacity characteristics. The three most interesting measures are: 容量 （capacity）：设备能存储的数据量。容量通常以字节为单位度量。 Capacity : The amount of data a device can store. Capacity is typically measured in bytes. 延迟 （latency）：设备在接到执行数据读取操作的指令后，到给出数据所需的时间。延迟通常以秒的若干分之一（例如毫秒或纳秒）或 CPU 周期数来度量。 Latency : The amount of time it takes for a device to respond with data after it has been instructed to perform a data retrieval operation. Latency is typically measured in either fractions of a second (for example, milliseconds or nanoseconds) or CPU cycles. 传输速率 （transfer rate）：在某段时间内，能在设备和主存之间移动的数据量。传输速率也称为 吞吐量 （throughput），通常以每秒字节数来度量。 Transfer rate : The amount of data that can be moved between the device and main memory over some interval of time. Transfer rate is also known as throughput and is typically measured in bytes per second. 考察现代计算机中的各种设备就会发现，它们在这三个度量上的性能都相差悬殊。性能差异主要来自两个因素： 距离 ，以及实现设备所用的 技术不同 。 Exploring the variety of devices in a modern computer reveals a huge disparity in device performance across all three of these measures. The performance variance primarily arises from two factors: distance and variations in the technologies used to implement the devices. 距离之所以有影响，是因为归根结底，程序想用的任何数据都必须送到 CPU 的运算部件 ALU 那里处理。CPU 设计者把寄存器放在离 ALU 很近的地方，以尽量缩短信号在两者之间传播的时间。因此，尽管寄存器只能存几个字节、数量也不多，但其中存放的值几乎可以立即供 ALU 使用！与之不同，磁盘这样的辅助存储设备要通过各种控制器设备把数据传到内存，这些控制器之间用更长的导线相连。额外的距离和中间处理大大拖慢了辅助存储。 Distance contributes because, ultimately, any data that a program wants to use must be available to the CPU’s arithmetic components, the ALU, for processing. CPU designers place registers close to the ALU to minimize the time it takes for a signal to propagate between the two. Thus, while registers can store only a few bytes and there aren’t many of them, the values stored are available to the ALU almost immediately! In contrast, secondary storage devices like disks transfer data to memory through various controller devices that are connected by longer wires. The extra distance and intermediate processing slows down secondary storage considerably. 原书旁注 · 格蕾丝·霍珀的「纳秒」（Grace Hopper’s “Nanoseconds”） 计算机先驱、美国海军少将格蕾丝·霍珀（Grace Hopper）在演讲时，经常给听众分发 11.8 英寸（约 30 厘米）长的电线。这些电线代表电信号在一纳秒内传播的最大距离，被称为「格蕾丝·霍珀纳秒」。她用它们来说明卫星通信的延迟局限，并演示为什么计算设备必须做得小才能快。霍珀讲解她的纳秒的录像 可以在 YouTube 上找到 。 When speaking to an audience, computing pioneer and U.S. Navy Admiral Grace Hopper frequently handed out 11.8-inch strands of wire to audience members. These strands represented the maximum distance that an electrical signal travels in one nanosecond and were called “Grace Hopper nanoseconds”. She used them to describe the latency limitations of satellite communication and to demonstrate why computing devices need to be small in order to be fast. Recordings of Grace Hopper presenting her nanoseconds are available on YouTube . 底层技术也会显著影响设备的性能。寄存器和缓存由相对简单的电路构成，只包含少量逻辑门。它们体积小、复杂度低，保证了电信号能快速地通过，从而降低了延迟。另一个极端是传统硬盘，它包含能存储数百 GB 数据的旋转磁盘片。尽管它们的存储密度高，但由于需要通过机械方式把部件对准并旋转到正确的位置，访问延迟相对较高。 The underlying technology also significantly affects device performance. Registers and caches are built from relatively simple circuits, consisting of just a few logic gates. Their small size and minimal complexity ensures that electrical signals can propagate through them quickly, reducing their latencies. On the opposite end of the spectrum, traditional hard disks contain spinning magnetic platters that store hundreds of gigabytes. Although they offer dense storage, their access latency is relatively high due to the requirements of mechanically aligning and rotating components into the correct positions. 本节余下的部分考察主存储和辅助存储设备的细节，并分析它们的性能特征。 The remainder of this section examines the details of primary and secondary storage devices and analyzes their performance characteristics. 11.2.1. 主存储 11.2.1. Primary Storage 主存储设备由 随机存取存储器 （random access memory，RAM）构成，这意味着访问数据所需的时间不受数据在设备中位置的影响。也就是说，RAM 不需要操心把部件移到正确位置或倒带之类的事情。有两种广泛使用的 RAM： 静态 RAM （SRAM）和 动态 RAM （DRAM），两者在现代计算机中都起着重要作用。 表 1 描述了常见主存储设备的性能度量以及它们使用的 RAM 类型。 Primary storage devices consist of random access memory (RAM), which means the time it takes to access data is not affected by the data’s location in the device. That is, RAM doesn’t need to worry about things like moving parts into the correct position or rewinding tape spools. There are two widely used types of RAM, static RAM (SRAM) and dynamic RAM (DRAM), and both play an important role in modern computers. Table 1 characterizes the performance measures of common primary storage devices and the types of RAM they use. 表 1. 2020 年典型工作站的主存储设备特征 Table 1. Primary Storage Device Characteristics of a Typical 2020 Workstation 设备 容量 大致延迟 RAM 类型 寄存器 4–8 字节 < 1 ns SRAM CPU 缓存 1–32 MB 5 ns SRAM 主存 4–64 GB 100 ns DRAM Device Capacity Approx. latency RAM type Register 4 - 8 bytes < 1 ns SRAM CPU cache 1 - 32 megabytes 5 ns SRAM Main memory 4 - 64 gigabytes 100 ns DRAM SRAM 把数据存储在小型电路（例如 锁存器 ）中。SRAM 通常是最快的存储器类型，设计者把它直接集成到 CPU 中，用来构建 寄存器 和缓存。SRAM 的制造成本、运行成本（功耗）和占用的面积都相对较高。这些成本合在一起，限制了 CPU 能包含的 SRAM 存储量。 SRAM stores data in small electrical circuits (for example, latches ). SRAM is typically the fastest type of memory, and designers integrate it directly into a CPU to build registers and caches. SRAM is relatively expensive in its cost to build, cost to operate (power consumption), and in the amount of space it occupies. Collectively, those costs limit the amount of SRAM storage that a CPU can include. DRAM 使用一种叫作 电容 的、能保持电荷的电子元件来存储数据。它之所以被称为「动态」的，是因为 DRAM 系统必须频繁地刷新电容中的电荷，才能保持所存储的值。现代系统用 DRAM 在内存条上实现主存，内存条通过一种称为 内存总线 （memory bus）的高速互连与 CPU 相连。 DRAM stores data using electrical components called capacitors that hold an electrical charge. It’s called “dynamic” because a DRAM system must frequently refresh the charge of its capacitors to maintain a stored value. Modern systems use DRAM to implement main memory on modules that connect to the CPU via a high-speed interconnect called the memory bus . 图 1 展示了主存储设备相对于内存总线的位置。要从内存中取一个值，CPU 把它想取的数据的地址放到内存总线上，并发出信号让内存模块执行一次读操作。经过短暂的延迟后，内存模块通过总线把存放在所请求地址处的值发送给 CPU。 Figure 1 illustrates the positions of primary storage devices relative to the memory bus. To retrieve a value from memory, the CPU puts the address of the data it would like to retrieve on the memory bus and signals that the memory modules should perform a read. After a short delay, the memory module sends the value stored at the requested address across the bus to the CPU. 图 1. 主存储与内存总线体系结构 Figure 1. Primary storage and memory bus architecture 尽管 CPU 和主存在物理上只相距几英寸，但数据在 CPU 和主存之间移动时必须经过内存总线。它们之间额外的距离和电路，使主存的延迟比 CPU 上的存储更高、传输速率更低。因此，内存总线有时被称为 冯·诺依曼瓶颈 （von Neumann bottleneck）。当然，尽管性能较低，主存仍然是必不可少的部件，因为它能存储的数据比 CPU 上能放下的多出几个数量级。与其他形式的存储一样，容量和速度之间存在明显的权衡。 Even though the CPU and main memory are physically just a few inches away from each other, data must travel through the memory bus when it moves between the CPU and main memory. The extra distance and circuitry between them increases the latency and reduces the transfer rate of main memory relative to on-CPU storage. As a result, the memory bus is sometimes referred to as the von Neumann bottleneck . Of course, despite its lower performance, main memory remains an essential component because it stores several orders of magnitude more data than can fit on the CPU. Consistent with other forms of storage, there’s a clear trade-off between capacity and speed. CPU 缓存 （cache，读音同「cash」）无论在物理位置上，还是在性能和容量特征上，都介于寄存器和主存之间。CPU 缓存通常直接在 CPU 上存储几 KB 到几 MB 的数据，但在物理上，缓存离 ALU 不像寄存器那么近。因此，访问缓存比访问主存快，但要让数据可用于计算，它比寄存器多需要几个周期。 CPU cache (pronounced “cash”) occupies the middle ground between registers and main memory, both physically and in terms of its performance and capacity characteristics. A CPU cache typically stores a few kilobytes to megabytes of data directly on the CPU, but physically, caches are not quite as close to the ALU as registers. Specifically, a system improves performance by moving the subset of data that a program is actively using into storage that lives close to the CPU’s computation circuitry (for example, in a register or CPU cache). Even though the program accesses each array element only once, a modern system loads more than one int at a time from memory to the CPU cache. Exactly how many additional integers get moved into the cache depends on the cache’s block size — the amount of data transferred into the cache at once. 例如，在块大小为 16 字节时，系统每次从内存向缓存复制四个整数。因此，访问第一个整数要付出访问主存的相对较高的代价，但接下来三个整数的访问都由缓存满足，即使程序以前从未访问过它们。 For example, with a 16-byte block size, a system copies four integers from memory to the cache at a time. Thus, accessing the first integer incurs the relatively high cost of accessing main memory, but the accesses to the next three are served out of cache, even if the program has never accessed them previously. 在许多情况下，程序员可以有意编写具有良好局部性模式的代码来帮助系统。例如，考虑访问 N × N 矩阵每个元素的嵌套循环（本章引言中出现过同一个例子）： In many cases, a programmer can help a system by intentionally writing code that exhibits good locality patterns. For example, consider the nested loops that access every element of an N × N matrix (this same example appeared in this chapter’s introduction): 表 1. 访问 N x N 矩阵每个元素的函数的两个版本。它们的唯一区别是对矩阵的下标顺序，但版本 1（左）的执行速度大约快五倍。 Table 1. Two versions of a function that accesses every element of an N x N* matrix. They only differ in their memory indexing into the matrix, but version 1 (left) executes approximately five times faster.* float averageMat_v1(int **mat, int n) { int i, j, total = 0; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (j = 0; j < n; j++) { // Note indexing: [i][j] total += mat[i][j]; } } return (float) total / (n * n); } float averageMat_v2(int **mat, int n) { int i, j, total = 0; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (j = 0; j < n; j++) { // Note indexing: [j][i] total += mat[j][i]; } } return (float) total / (n * n); } 在两个版本中，循环变量（ i 和 j ）和累加变量（ total ）都表现出良好的时间局部性，因为循环在每次迭代中都会反复使用它们。因此，执行这段代码时，系统会把这些变量存放在 CPU 上的快速存储位置中，以提供良好的性能。 In both versions, the loop variables ( i and j ) and the accumulator variable ( total ) exhibit good temporal locality because the loops repeatedly use them in every iteration. Thus, when executing this code, a system would store those variables in fast on-CPU storage locations to provide good performance. 然而，由于 矩阵在内存中按 行优先顺序 组织 ，第一个版本的代码（左）的执行速度大约是第二个版本（右）的五倍。这种差距来自空间局部性的差异：第一个版本按内存中的顺序（即按连续的内存地址）访问矩阵的值。因此，它能受益于系统把大块数据从内存加载到缓存的做法，因为每个块的值只需付出一次访问内存的代价。 However, due to the row-major order organization of a matrix in memory , the first version of the code (left) executes about five times faster than the second version (right). The disparity arises from the difference in spatial locality — the first version accesses the matrix’s values sequentially in memory (that is, in order of consecutive memory addresses). Thus, it benefits from a system that loads large blocks from memory into the cache because it pays the cost of going to memory only once for every block of values. 译注 严格说来，这两个函数的参数是 int ** （数组的数组），各行是分别 malloc 出来的，行与行之间不一定相邻；但每一行内部是连续的，所以 v1 逐行访问时同样具有良好的空间局部性。本章引言的译注中，译者在 Apple M1 Pro 上测得 v2 约慢 7 倍。 第二个版本访问矩阵的值时，在不连续的内存地址之间反复跨行跳跃。它在相继的内存访问中 从不 读取同一个缓存块，因此在缓存看来，这个块似乎不再需要了。于是，它每读一个矩阵值都要付出访问内存的代价。 The second version accesses the matrix’s values by repeatedly jumping between rows across nonsequential memory addresses. It never reads from the same cache block in subsequent memory accesses, so it looks to the cache like the block isn’t needed. Thus, it pays the cost of going to memory for every matrix value it reads. 这个例子说明了程序员如何能影响程序执行的系统级开销。编写高性能应用程序时，尤其是以规则模式访问数组的程序，要牢记这些原则。 This example illustrates how a programmer can affect the system-level costs of a program’s execution. Keep these principles in mind when writing high-performance applications, particularly those that access arrays in a regular pattern. 11.3.2. 从局部性到缓存 11.3.2. From Locality to Caches 为了帮助说明时间局部性和空间局部性的概念如何促成缓存的设计，我们来看一个用现实生活中熟悉的物品——书——构成的示例场景。假设菲奥娜（Fiona）在宿舍的书桌上完成所有作业，书桌空间很小，只能放三本书。她的房间外面有一个书架，空间比书桌大得多。最后，校园的另一头有一座藏书极其丰富的图书馆。这个例子中的「图书存储层次结构」大致如 图 1 所示。在这个场景下，我们来探讨局部性如何帮助指导菲奥娜决定把书放在哪个存储位置。 To help illustrate how the concepts of temporal and spatial locality enable cache designs, we’ll adopt an example scenario with familiar real-world objects: books. Suppose that Fiona does all of her homework at a desk in her dorm room, and the desk has a small amount of space that can store only three books. Just outside her room she keeps a bookshelf, which has much more space than the desk. Finally, across campus her college has a library with a huge variety of books. The “book storage hierarchy” in this example might look something like Figure 1 . Given this scenario, we’ll explore how locality can help guide which storage location Fiona should use to store her books. 图 1. 一个假想的图书存储层次结构 Figure 1. A hypothetical book storage hierarchy 11.3.3. 时间局部性 11.3.3. Temporal Locality 时间局部性表明，如果有一本书菲奥娜经常用，她就应该把它放得离书桌越近越好。如果她偶尔需要把它挪到书架上，腾出临时的工作空间，代价也不算太高；但如果第二天还要用，却把书还回图书馆，那就太傻了。反过来也成立：如果有一本书占着书桌或书架上的宝贵空间，而她已经很久没用过它了，那么这本书看来就很适合还回图书馆。 Temporal locality suggests that, if there’s a book Fiona uses frequently, she should keep it as close to her desk as possible. If she occasionally needs to move it to the shelf to clear up temporary work space, the cost isn’t too high, but it would be silly to take a book back to the library if she’s just going to need it again the next day. The inverse is also true: if there’s a book taking up valuable space on her desk or shelf, and she hasn’t used it for quite a while, that book seems like a good candidate for returning to the library. 那么，菲奥娜应该把哪些书放到她宝贵的书桌上呢？在这个例子中，真实的学生可能会看看接下来的作业，挑出他们预计最有用的那些书。换句话说，为了做出最好的存储决策，他们最好能掌握关于 未来使用情况 的信息。 So, which books should Fiona move to her precious desk space? In this example, real students would probably look at their upcoming assignments and select the books that they expect to be most useful. In other words, to make the best storage decision, they would ideally need information about future usage . 遗憾的是，硬件设计者还没有找到构建能预测未来的电路的方法。作为预测的替代方案，可以设想一个系统，要求程序员或用户事先告诉系统程序将如何使用数据，以便优化数据的放置。这种策略在访问模式 非常 规则的专门应用（例如大型数据库）中可能很有效。然而，在个人计算机这样的通用系统中，要求用户事先告知负担太重：许多用户不愿意（或者没有能力）提供足够的细节来帮助系统做出好的决策。 Unfortunately, hardware designers haven’t discovered how to build circuits that can predict the future. As an alternative to prediction, one could instead imagine a system that asks the programmer or user to inform the system in advance how a program will use data so that it’s placement could be optimized. Such a strategy may work well in specialized applications (for example, large databases), that exhibit very regular access patterns. However, in a general-purpose system like a personal computer, requiring advance notice from the user is too large a burden — many users would not want to (or would be unable to) provide enough detail to help the system make good decisions. 因此，系统不依赖未来的访问信息，而是把过去当作预测未来 可能 发生什么的依据。把这个思路应用到书的例子上，就得到一种管理图书存放空间的相对简单（但仍然很有效）的策略： Thus, instead of relying on future access information, systems look to the past as a predictor of what will likely happen in the future. Applying this idea to the book example suggests a relatively simple (but still quite effective) strategy for governing book storage spaces: 当菲奥娜需要用一本书时，她把这本书从它当前所在的地方取来，放到书桌上。 When Fiona needs to use a book, she retrieves it from wherever it currently is and moves it to her desk. 如果书桌已经放满了，她就把 最近最少使用 （least recently）的那本书（即在书桌上放着、最长时间没碰过的那本）挪到书架上。 If the desk is already full, she moves the book that she used least recently (that is, the book that has been sitting on the desk untouched for the longest amount of time) to her shelf. 如果书架也满了，她就把书架上最近最少使用的那本书还回图书馆，腾出空间。 If the shelf is full, she returns the shelf’s least recently used book to the library to free up space. 尽管这个方案可能并不完美，但它的简单性很有吸引力。它只需要能在各存储位置之间移动书，以及少量关于这些书之前被使用的先后顺序的元信息。此外，这个方案很好地实现了时间局部性最初的两个目标： Even though this scheme may not be perfect, the simplicity makes it attractive. All it requires is the ability to move books between storage locations and a small amount of metainformation regarding the order in which books were previously used. Furthermore, this scheme captures the two initial temporal locality objectives well: 经常使用的书很可能一直留在书桌或书架上，避免了不必要的图书馆往返。 Frequently used books are likely to remain on the desk or shelf, preventing unnecessary trips to the library. 不常用的书最终会成为最近最少使用的那本，到那时把它还回图书馆就是合理的。 Infrequently used books eventually become the least recently used book, at which point returning them to the library makes sense. 把这一策略应用到主存储设备上，看起来与书的例子惊人地相似：当数据从主存加载到 CPU 寄存器时，在 CPU 缓存中为它腾出空间。如果缓存已满，就把最近最少使用的缓存数据 驱逐 （evict）回主存，以腾出缓存空间。在 接下来关于缓存的小节 中，我们会探讨现代缓存系统中是如何构建这类机制的。 Applying this strategy to primary storage devices looks remarkably similar to the book example: as data is loaded into CPU registers from main memory, make room for it in the CPU cache. If the cache is already full, make room in the cache by evicting the least recently used cache data to main memory. In the following caching section , we’ll explore the details of how such mechanisms are built in to modern caching systems. 11.3.4. 空间局部性 11.3.4. Spatial Locality 空间局部性表明，菲奥娜去图书馆时，应该多借几本书，以减少以后再去图书馆的可能性。具体来说，她应该把所需那本书「附近」的其他书也借回来，因为附近的书看来很可能就是以后会让她再跑一趟图书馆的那些书。 Spatial locality suggests that, when making a trip to the library, Fiona should retrieve more than one book to reduce the likelihood of future library trips. Specifically, she should retrieve additional books that are “nearby” the one she needs, because those that are nearby seem like good candidates for books that might otherwise turn into additional library visits. 假设她正在上一门关于莎士比亚历史剧的文学课。如果课程第一周布置她读《亨利六世》上篇，那么当她到图书馆去借这本书时，很可能会在书架上附近找到中篇和下篇。即使她还不知道课程是否会布置另外两篇，认为她 可能 需要它们也并非没有道理。也就是说，正因为它们就在她需要的那本书旁边，需要它们的可能性要比图书馆里随便哪本书高得多。 Suppose that she’s taking a literature course on the topic of Shakespeare’s histories. If in the first week of the course she’s assigned to read Henry VI, Part I , when she finds herself in the library to retrieve it, she’s likely to also find Parts II and III close by on the shelves. Even if she doesn’t yet know whether the course will assign those other two parts, it’s not unreasonable to think that she might need them. That is, the likelihood of needing them is much higher than a random book in the library, specifically because they are nearby the book she does need. 在这个场景中，可能性之所以提高，是因为图书馆在书架上摆放书的方式；程序在内存中组织数据的方式也与之类似。例如，数组或 struct 这样的编程结构把一组相关的数据存放在一块连续的内存区域中。依次遍历数组中的连续元素时，所访问的内存地址显然具有空间上的规律。把这些空间局部性的经验应用到主存储设备上，意味着系统从主存取数据时，也应当把紧挨着它的周边数据一起取回来。 In this scenario, the likelihood increases due to the way libraries arrange books on shelves, and programs similarly organize data in memory. For example, a programming construct like an array or a struct stores a collection of related data in a contiguous region of memory. When iterating over consecutive elements in an array, there is clearly a spatial pattern in the accessed memory addresses. Applying these spatial locality lessons to primary storage devices implies that, when retrieving data from main memory, the system should also retrieve the data immediately surrounding it. 在下一节中，我们会描述缓存的特征，并介绍硬件自动识别和利用局部性的机制。 In the next section, we’ll characterize cache characteristics and describe mechanisms for the hardware to make identifying and exploiting locality happen automatically.

Cache Analysis and Valgrind 由于缓存对程序性能有显著的影响，大多数系统都提供了测量程序缓存使用情况的剖析工具。Valgrind 的 cachegrind 模式就是这样一种工具，本节用它来评估缓存性能。 Because caches significantly influence program performance, most systems provide profiling tools to measure a program’s use of the cache. One such tool is Valgrind’s cachegrind mode, which this section uses to evaluate cache performance. 译注 Valgrind 不能在 Apple Silicon Mac 上运行（见第 3 章的现代更新）。要跟做本节，可以在 ARM64 或 x86-64 的 Linux 虚拟机、容器里安装 Valgrind。 考虑下面这个生成随机 N × N 矩阵的程序： Consider the following program that generates a random N × N matrix: #include <stdio.h> #include <stdlib.h> #include <sys/time.h> #include <time.h> int **genRandomMatrix(int n, int max) { int i, j; int **mat = malloc(n * sizeof(int *)); for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { mat[i] = malloc(n * sizeof(int)); for (j = 0; j < n; j++) { mat[i][j] = 1 + rand() % max; } } return mat; } void free_all(int **mat, int n) { int i; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { free(mat[i]); } free(mat); } int main(int argc, char **argv) { int i, n; int **matrix; if (argc != 2) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s <n>
", argv[0]); fprintf(stderr, "where <n> is the dimension of the matrix
"); return 1; } n = strtol(argv[1], NULL, 10); srand(time(NULL)); matrix = genRandomMatrix(n, 100); free_all(matrix, n); return 0; } 本章前面几节介绍了两个求矩阵所有元素平均值的函数。它们的唯一区别是对矩阵的下标方式： Prior sections in this chapter introduced two functions for averaging every element of a matrix. They differ only in the way they index into the matrix: float averageMat_v1(int **mat, int n) { int i, j, total = 0; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (j = 0; j < n; j++) { // Note indexing: [i][j] total += mat[i][j]; } } return (float) total / (n * n); } float averageMat_v2(int **mat, int n) { int i, j, total = 0; for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { for (j = 0; j < n; j++) { // Note indexing: [j][i] total += mat[j][i]; } } return (float) total / (n * n); } 本节使用缓存剖析工具来量化它们之间的差异。 This section uses cache profiling tools to quantify the differences between them. 11.5.1. 初步分析：理论分析与基准测试 11.5.1. A First Cut: Theoretical Analysis and Benchmarking 基于局部性和存储器层次结构的理论分析表明，由于 mat 在内存中按 行优先顺序 存放，第一个版本（对矩阵 mat ）表现出更好的空间局部性。第二种解法的空间局部性很差，因为矩阵中的每个元素是按列优先顺序被访问的。回想一下，数据是以 块 为单位加载到缓存中的。按列优先顺序遍历矩阵很可能导致更多的缓存未命中，从而性能更差。 A theoretical analysis based on locality and the memory hierarchy suggests that the first version exhibits better spatial locality (on matrix mat ) due to the fact that mat is stored in row-major order in memory. The second solution has poor spatial locality because each element in the matrix is visited in column-major order. Recall that data is loaded into a cache in blocks . Traversing the matrix in column-major order will likely lead to more cache misses, resulting in poorer performance. 我们修改 main 函数，加入对 gettimeofday 函数的调用，以准确测量两个版本之间的性能差异： Let’s modify the main function to include calls to the gettimeofday function to accurately measure the difference in performance between the two versions: int main(int argc, char** argv) { /* Validate command line parameters. */ if (argc != 2) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s <n>

In essence, the solution using row-major order is 4.61 times faster than the second one! 11.5.2. 现实中的缓存分析：Cachegrind 11.5.2. Cache Analysis in the Real World: Cachegrind 对两种解法先做理论分析、再实际运行，验证了第一个版本比第二个快。然而，这并没有证实缓存分析的细节。幸运的是，Valgrind 工具套件可以帮上忙。在本书前面，我们讨论过 Valgrind 如何帮助 查找程序中的内存泄漏 。本节介绍 Valgrind 的缓存模拟器 Cachegrind。Cachegrind 让程序员能够研究程序或某个特定函数对缓存的影响。 Theoretically analyzing the two solutions and then running them verifies that the first version is faster than the second. However, it doesn’t confirm the details of the cache analysis. Fortunately, the Valgrind suite of tools can help. Earlier in the book, we discussed how Valgrind can help find memory leaks in a program. This section describes Cachegrind, Valgrind’s cache simulator. Cachegrind enables a programmer to study how a program or particular function affects the cache. Cachegrind 模拟程序与计算机缓存层次结构之间的交互。在很多情况下，Cachegrind 能自动检测机器的缓存组织结构。在无法检测的情况下，Cachegrind 仍然会模拟第一级（L1）缓存和最后一级（LL）缓存。它假定第一级缓存有两个独立的部分：指令缓存和数据缓存。这样做的原因是，最后一级缓存对运行时间的影响最为重要。L1 缓存的相联度也最低，所以确保程序与它良好地交互很重要。这些假设符合大多数现代机器的结构。 Cachegrind simulates how a program interacts with the computer’s cache hierarchy. In many cases, Cachegrind can autodetect the cache organization of a machine. In the cases that it cannot, Cachegrind still simulates the first level (L1) cache and the last level (LL) cache. It assumes the first level cache has two independent components: the instruction cache and the data cache. The reason for this is that the last level cache has the most important implications for runtime. L1 caches also have the lowest level of associativity, so it’s important to ensure that programs interact well with it. These assumptions match the structure of most modern machines. Summary 本章探讨了计算机存储设备的特征，以及它们在访问延迟、存储容量、传输延迟和成本等关键指标上的权衡。由于各种设备体现了截然不同的设计与性能权衡，它们自然地形成了一个存储器层次结构，按照容量和访问时间排列。在层次结构的顶端，CPU 缓存和主存等主存储设备能快速地直接向 CPU 提供数据，但容量有限。在层次结构的下层，固态硬盘和硬盘等辅助存储设备以牺牲性能为代价，提供高密度的大容量存储。 This chapter explored the characteristics of computer storage devices and their trade-offs with respect to key measures like access latency, storage capacity, transfer latency, and cost. Because devices embody many disparate design and performance trade-offs, they naturally form a memory hierarchy, which arranges them according to their capacity and access time. At the top of the hierarchy, primary storage devices like CPU caches and main memory quickly provide data directly to the CPU, but their capacity is limited. Lower in the hierarchy, secondary storage devices like solid-state drives and hard disks offer dense bulk storage at the cost of performance. 由于现代系统既需要大容量又需要良好的性能，系统设计者用多种形式的存储来构建计算机。关键在于，系统必须管理每一块数据存放在哪个存储设备上。系统的目标是把正在使用的数据存放在较快的存储设备中，而把不常用的数据转移到较慢的存储设备上。 Because modern systems require both high capacity and good performance, system designers build computers with multiple forms of storage. Crucially, the system must manage which storage device holds any particular chunk of data. Systems aim to store data that’s being actively used in faster storage devices, and they relegate infrequently used data to slower storage devices. 为了确定哪些数据正在被使用，系统依赖于称为局部性的程序数据访问模式。程序表现出两种重要的局部性： To determine which data is being used, systems rely on program data access patterns known as locality. Programs exhibit two important types of locality: 时间局部性 ：程序倾向于在一段时间内反复访问同一数据。 Temporal Locality : Programs tend to access the same data repeatedly over time. 空间局部性 ：程序倾向于访问与之前访问过的数据相邻的数据。 Spatial Locality : Programs tend to access data that is nearby other, previously accessed data. 局部性是 CPU 缓存的基础，CPU 缓存在 CPU 芯片上的快速存储中存放主存的一个小子集。当程序试图访问主存时，CPU 首先在缓存中查找数据；如果在那里找到了，就可以免去一趟代价更高的主存访问。 Locality serves as the basis for CPU caches, which store a small subset of main memory in fast storage directly on the CPU chip. When a program attempts to access main memory, the CPU first checks for the data in the cache; if it finds the data there, it can avoid the more costly trip to main memory. 当程序发出读或写内存的请求时，它提供想要访问的内存位置的地址。CPU 缓存把内存地址中的位分成三段，用来识别缓存行存放的是主存的哪个子集： When a program issues a request to read or write memory, it provides the address of the memory location that it wants to access. CPU caches use three sections of the bits in a memory address to identify which subset of main memory a cache line stores: 地址中间的 索引 位把地址映射到缓存中的一个存储位置。 The middle index bits of an address map the address to a storage location in the cache. 高位的 标记 位唯一地标识该缓存位置存放的是哪个内存子集。 The high-order tag bits uniquely identify which subset of memory the cache location stores. 低位的 偏移 位确定程序想访问所存数据中的哪些字节。 The low-order offset bits identify which bytes of stored data the program wants to access. 最后，本章演示了如何用 Cachegrind 工具对运行中的程序进行缓存性能剖析。Cachegrind 模拟程序与缓存层次结构之间的交互，并收集程序使用缓存的统计信息（例如命中率和未命中率）。 Finally, this chapter concluded by demonstrating how the Cachegrind tool can enable cache performance profiling for a running program. Cachegrind simulates a program’s interaction with the cache hierarchy and collects statistics about a program’s use of the cache (for example, the hit and miss rates).
