Key Takeaways and Summary 我们这段短暂（也许有些令人沮丧）的代码优化之旅，应当向读者传达一个非常重要的信息：如果你在考虑手动优化代码，就要仔细想想哪些事情值得花时间，哪些应该交给编译器。下面是希望提升代码性能时值得考虑的几条重要建议。 Our short (and perhaps frustrating) journey into code optimization should convey one very important message to the reader: if you are thinking about manually optimizing your code, think carefully about what is worth spending your time on and what should be left to the compiler. Below are some important tips to consider when looking to improve code performance. 选择好的数据结构和算法 使用恰当的算法和数据结构是无可替代的；做不到这一点，往往是代码性能差的首要原因。例如，著名的埃拉托斯特尼筛法（Sieve of Eratosthenes）生成素数的效率，远远高于我们在 optExample 中自己设计的算法，能显著提升性能。下面的清单展示了用筛法的一种实现生成 2 到 500 万之间所有素数所需的时间： Choose Good Data Structures and Algorithms There is no substitute for using proper algorithms and data structures; failure to do so is often the top reason for poor performance in code. For example, the famous Sieve of Eratosthenes algorithm is a much more efficient way to generate prime numbers than our custom algorithm in optExample , and yields a significant improvement in performance. The following listing shows the time needed to generate all prime numbers between 2 and 5 million using an implementation of the sieve: $ gcc -o genPrimes genPrimes.c $ ./genPrimes 5000000 Found 348513 primes (0.122245 s) 筛法只需 0.12 秒就能找出 2 到 500 万之间的所有素数，而 optExample2 在打开 -O3 优化选项时生成同样的素数需要 1.46 秒（快了 12 倍）。筛法的实现留给读者作为练习；不过应该很清楚，一开始就选择更好的算法，本可以省去好几个小时繁琐的优化工作。我们的例子说明了为什么数据结构和算法知识是计算机科学家的基础。 The sieve algorithm requires only 0.12 seconds to find all the prime numbers between 2 and 5 million, compared to the 1.46 seconds it takes optExample2 to generate the same set of primes with the -O3 optimization flags turned on (12× improvement). The implementation of the sieve algorithm is left as an exercise for the reader; however, it should be clear that choosing a better algorithm up front would have saved hours of tedious optimization effort. Our example demonstrates why a knowledge of data structures and algorithms is foundational for computer scientists. 尽可能使用标准库函数 不要重新发明轮子。如果在编程过程中你需要一个做非常标准的事情的函数（例如求绝对值，或者求一组数的最大值或最小值），先停下来查一查，这个函数是否已经是高级语言标准库的一部分。标准库中的函数经过充分测试，而且往往针对性能做过优化。例如，如果读者手动实现了自己版本的 sqrt 函数，编译器可能就不知道要自动把这个函数调用替换为 fsqrt 指令。 Use Standard Library Functions Whenever Possible Don’t reinvent the wheel. If in the course of programming you need a function that should do something very standard (e.g., find the absolute value, or find the maximum or minimum of a list of numbers), stop and check to see whether the function already exists as part of the higher-level language’s standard library. Functions in the standard libraries are well tested and tend to be optimized for performance. For example, if a reader manually implements their own version of the sqrt function, the compiler may not know to automatically replace the function call with the fsqrt instruction. 根据数据而不是感觉来优化 如果在选择了最好的数据结构和算法、 并且 使用了标准库函数之后，仍然需要进一步提升性能，就借助 Valgrind 这样好的代码剖析工具。优化 绝不 应该基于直觉。把太多精力放在自己 感觉 应该优化的地方（而没有数据支持这种想法），往往只会浪费时间。 Optimize Based on Data and Not on Feelings If after choosing the best data structures and algorithms and employing standard library functions, additional improvements in performance are required, enlist the help of a good code profiler like Valgrind. Optimization should never be based on gut feelings. Concentrating too much on what one feels should be optimized (without the data to back up the thought) often leads to wasted time. 把复杂的代码拆分成多个函数 与现代编译器所能达到的效果相比，手动内联代码通常不会带来可观的性能提升。相反，要让编译器更容易帮你优化。编译器更容易优化较短的代码段。把复杂的操作拆分成多个函数，既能提高代码的可读性，又能让编译器更容易优化。查一查你的编译器是否默认尝试内联，或者是否有单独的选项来尝试内联代码。让编译器去做内联，比自己手动内联要好。 Split Complex Code into Multiple Functions Manually inlining code usually does not result in a sizable performance gain over what modern compilers can achieve. Instead, make it easier for your compiler to help optimize for you. Compilers have an easier time optimizing shorter code segments. Splitting complex operations into multiple functions simultaneously increases code readability and makes it easier for a compiler to optimize. Check to see whether your compiler attempts inlining by default or has a separate flag to attempt inlining code. It is better to let your compiler perform inlining rather than manually doing it yourself. 优先考虑代码的可读性 在如今的许多应用中，可读性是第一位的。事实上，代码被阅读的次数比被编写的次数多。许多公司花费大量时间培训软件工程师，让他们以一种非常特定的方式编写代码，以最大限度地提高可读性。如果优化代码会明显损害可读性，就要看看所获得的性能提升是否值得付出这个代价。例如，如今许多编译器都有开启循环展开的优化选项。程序员应当始终使用现成的循环展开优化选项，而不是试图手动展开循环，后者可能会严重损害代码的可读性。降低代码的可读性常常会增加无意中引入缺陷的可能性，进而可能导致安全漏洞。 Prioritize Code Readability In many applications today, readability is king. The truth is that code is read more often than it is written. Many companies spend considerable time training their software engineers to write code in a very particular way to maximize readability. If optimizing your code results in a noticeable hit to code readability, it is important to check if the performance improvement obtained is worth the hit. For example, many compilers today have optimization flags that enable loop unrolling. Programmers should always use available optimization flags for loop unrolling instead of trying to manually unroll loops, which can lead to a significant hit in code readability. Reducing code readability often increases the likelihood that bugs are inadvertently introduced into code, which can lead to security vulnerabilities. 关注内存使用 程序的内存使用对其执行时间的影响，往往比它执行的指令数更大。 循环交换的例子 就是这一点的例证。在两种情况下，循环执行的指令数相同。然而，循环的顺序对内存访问和局部性有显著影响。在尝试优化程序时，也要记得试试 massif 和 cachegrind 这样的内存剖析工具。 Pay Attention to Memory Use A program’s memory usage often has a bigger impact on the program’s execution time than the number of instructions that it executes. The loop interchange example exemplifies this point. In both cases, the loop executes the same number of instructions. However, the ordering of the loops has a significant impact on memory access and locality. Remember to also explore memory profiling tools like massif and cachegrind when attempting to optimize a program. 编译器在不断改进 编译器开发者不断更新编译器，以便安全地执行更复杂的优化。例如，GCC 从 4.0 版开始改用 静态单赋值（SSA） 形式，显著改善了它的一些优化的效果。GCC 代码库的 GRAPHITE 分支实现了 多面体模型 （polyhedral model），让编译器能够执行更复杂的循环变换。随着编译器越来越复杂，手动优化的好处会大大减少。 Compilers Are Constantly Improving Compiler writers continually update compilers to perform more sophisticated optimizations safely. For example, GCC switched to the link: static single assignment (SSA) form starting in version 4.0, which significantly improved the effects of some of its optimizations. The GRAPHITE branch of the GCC code base implements the polyhedral model , which allows the compiler to perform more complex types of loop transformations. As compilers get more sophisticated, the benefits of manual optimization significantly reduce.

The Operating System 操作系统 （operating system，OS）是一个特殊的系统软件层，它位于计算机硬件和在计算机上运行的应用程序之间（见 图 1 ）。从开机到关机，操作系统软件一直驻留在计算机上。它的主要目的是 管理 底层的硬件部件，以便高效地运行程序工作负载，并让计算机 易于使用 。 The operating system (OS) is a special system software layer that sits between the computer hardware and application programs running on the computer (see Figure 1 ). The OS software is persistent on the computer, from power-on to power-off. Its primary purpose is to manage the underlying hardware components to efficiently run program workloads and to make the computer easy to use . 图 1. 操作系统是位于用户和硬件之间的特殊系统软件。它管理计算机的硬件，并实现各种抽象，让硬件更易于使用。 Figure 1. The OS is special system software between the user and the hardware. It manages the computer’s hardware and implements abstractions to make the hardware easier to use. 操作系统让计算机硬件易于使用的方式之一，是支持在计算机上启动程序运行。考虑用户双击一个图标，或者在 shell 提示符下输入程序可执行文件的名字（例如 ./a.out ），以便在底层系统上启动一个程序时会发生什么。操作系统处理这个操作的所有细节，例如把程序从磁盘加载到 RAM 中，以及初始化 CPU 以开始执行程序的指令；操作系统向用户隐藏了在计算机上运行用户程序所必需的这类底层动作。 One of the ways in which the OS makes the computer hardware easy to use is in its support for initiating programs to run on the computer. Consider what happens when a user double-clicks an icon or types the name of a program executable at a shell prompt (e.g., ./a.out ) to start a program running on the underlying system. The OS handles all the details of this operation, such as loading the program from disk into RAM and initializing the CPU to start running the program instructions; the OS hides from users these types of low-level actions that are necessary to run the user’s program on the computer. 操作系统高效利用系统资源的一个例子是实现 多道程序设计 （multiprogramming），即允许计算机上同时运行不止一个程序。多道程序设计并不一定意味着所有程序都在计算机硬件上同时执行。事实上，系统中正在运行的程序集合通常远远多于 CPU 核心的数量。它的意思是，操作系统在系统上运行的多个程序之间共享包括 CPU 在内的硬件资源。例如，当一个程序需要当前在磁盘上的数据时，操作系统可以在第一个程序等待数据就绪期间，把另一个程序放到 CPU 上运行。如果没有多道程序设计，每当计算机上运行的程序访问较慢的硬件设备时，CPU 就会闲置。为了支持多道程序设计，操作系统需要实现一种对正在运行的程序的抽象，称为 进程 （process）。进程抽象让操作系统能够管理任一时刻在系统中运行的多个程序。 One example of how the OS makes efficient use of system resources is by implementing multiprogramming , which means allowing more than a single program to run on the computer at a time. Multiprogramming does not necessarily mean that all the programs are running simultaneously on the computer hardware. In fact, the set of running programs in the system is typically much larger than the number of CPU cores. Instead, it means that the OS shares hardware resources, including the CPU, among several programs running on the system. For example, when one program needs data that are currently on disk, the OS can put another program on the CPU while the first program waits for the data to become available. Without multiprogramming, the CPU would sit idle whenever the program running on the computer accesses slower hardware devices. To support multiprogramming, the OS needs to implement an abstraction of a running program, called a process . The process abstraction enables the OS to manage the set of multiple programs that are running in the system at any given time. 操作系统的例子包括微软的 Windows、苹果的 macOS 和 iOS、甲骨文的 Solaris，以及 OpenBSD 和 Linux 等开源的类 Unix 系统。本书使用 Linux 的例子。不过，其他这些通用操作系统都实现了类似的功能，尽管实现方式有时不同。 Some example operating systems include Microsoft’s Windows, Apple’s macOS and iOS, Oracle’s Solaris, and open-source Unix variants such as OpenBSD and Linux. We use Linux examples in this book. However, all of these other general-purpose operating systems implement similar functionality, albeit sometimes in different ways. 译注 在 Mac 上跟做本章时， fork 、 exec 、 wait 、信号、管道等 POSIX 接口都可以直接使用；但 macOS 没有 Linux 的 /proc 文件系统，书中涉及 /proc 的例子需要在 Linux 中运行。 内核 The Kernel 操作系统 这个术语常用来指一大套系统级软件，它们执行某种资源管理，并实现底层系统的「易用」抽象。在本章中，我们关注的是操作系统 内核 （kernel）；因此，当我们单独使用「操作系统」这个术语时，指的是操作系统内核。 The term operating system is often used to refer to a large set of system-level software that performs some kind of resource management and that implements “easy-to-use” abstractions of the underlying system. In this chapter, we focus on the operating system kernel ; thus, when we use the term OS alone, we mean the OS kernel. 操作系统内核实现了操作系统的核心功能，即使用系统所必需的功能。这些功能包括：管理计算机硬件层以运行程序，实现并管理向系统用户提供的操作系统抽象（例如，文件就是建立在所存储数据之上的一种操作系统抽象），以及实现面向用户应用层和硬件设备层的接口。内核实现了 机制 （mechanism），使硬件能够运行程序，并实现进程等抽象。机制是操作系统功能中「如何做」的部分。内核还实现了 策略 （policy），用于高效地管理计算机硬件和支配各种抽象。策略决定了操作系统功能中「做什么」「何时做」以及「为谁做」的部分。例如，机制负责初始化 CPU 以执行某个特定进程的指令，而策略决定下一个在 CPU 上运行的是哪个进程。 The OS kernel implements core OS functionality — the functionality necessary for any use of the system. This functionality includes managing the computer hardware layer to run programs, implementing and managing OS abstractions exported to users of the system (e.g., files are an OS abstraction on top of stored data), and implementing interfaces to the user applications layer and to the hardware device layer. The kernel implements mechanisms to enable the hardware to run programs and to implement its abstractions such as processes. Mechanisms are the “how” part of OS functionality. The kernel also implements policies for efficiently managing the computer hardware and for governing its abstractions. Policies dictate the “what,” “when,” and “to whom” part of OS functionality. For example, a mechanism implements initializing the CPU to run instructions from a particular process, and a policy decides which process gets to run next on the CPU. 内核为系统的用户实现了一个编程接口： 系统调用接口 （system call interface）。用户和程序通过系统调用接口与操作系统交互。例如，如果程序想知道当前的时间，它可以通过调用 gettimeofday 系统调用从操作系统获取这个信息。 The kernel implements a programming interface for users of the system: the system call interface . Users and programs interact with the OS through its system call interface. For example, if a program wants to know the current time of day, it can obtain that information from the OS by invoking the gettimeofday system call. 内核还提供了一个与硬件设备交互的接口（ 设备接口 ，device interface）。通常，硬盘驱动器（HDD）、键盘和固态硬盘（SSD）等 I/O 设备通过这个接口与内核交互。这些设备带有特殊的设备驱动程序软件，它们在操作系统中运行，负责与特定设备之间的数据传输。设备驱动程序软件通过操作系统的设备接口与操作系统交互；只要把按照操作系统设备接口编写的设备驱动程序代码加载到操作系统中，就可以给计算机系统添加一个新设备。CPU 和 RAM 等其他硬件设备则由内核直接管理。 图 2 展示了位于用户应用程序和计算机硬件之间的操作系统内核层，包括它面向用户的编程接口和它的硬件设备接口。 The kernel also provides an interface for interacting with hardware devices (the device interface ). Typically, I/O devices such as hard disk drives (HDDs), keyboards, and solid-state drives (SSDs) interact with the kernel through this interface. These devices come with special device driver software that runs in the OS and handles transferring data to or from a specific device. The device driver software interacts with the OS through the OS’s device interface; a new device can be added to a computer system by loading its device driver code, written to conform to the OS’s device interface, into the OS. The kernel directly manages other hardware devices, such as the CPU and RAM. Figure 2 shows the OS kernel layer between the user applications and the computer hardware, including its programming interface to users and its hardware device interface. 图 2. 操作系统内核：使用系统所必需的核心操作系统功能，并促成 I/O 设备与系统用户之间的协作 Figure 2. The OS kernel: core OS functionality necessary to use the system and facilitate cooperation between I/O devices and users of the system 在本章余下的部分，我们考察操作系统在运行程序和高效管理系统资源方面所起的作用。我们的讨论主要集中在操作系统功能的机制（「如何做」）上，以及两个主要操作系统抽象的实现： 进程 （正在运行的程序）和 虚拟内存 （一种进程内存空间的视图，它从底层 RAM 或辅助存储中的物理存储中抽象出来）。 In the rest of this chapter, we examine the role the operating system plays in running programs and in efficiently managing system resources. Our discussion is primarily focused on the mechanism (the “how”) of the OS functionality and the implementation of two primary OS abstractions: a process (a running program) and virtual memory (a view of process memory space that is abstracted from its underlying physical storage in RAM or secondary storage).

x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C13-OS/impl.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 13.1. How the OS Works and How It Runs 操作系统的一部分工作，是支持在系统上运行程序。要在计算机上启动一个程序，操作系统要为这个正在运行的程序分配一部分 RAM，把程序的二进制可执行文件从磁盘加载到 RAM 中，为与这个正在运行的程序相关的进程创建并初始化操作系统状态，并初始化 CPU 以开始执行该进程的指令（例如，操作系统需要初始化 CPU 寄存器，以便取出并执行进程的指令）。 图 1 展示了这些步骤。 Part of the job of the OS is to support programs running on the system. To start a program running on a computer, the OS allocates a portion of RAM for the running program, loads the program’s binary executable from disk into RAM, creates and initializes OS state for the process associated with this running program, and initializes the CPU to start executing the process’s instructions (e.g., the CPU registers need to be initialized by the OS to fetch and execute the process’s instructions). Figure 1 illustrates these steps. 图 1. 操作系统为在底层硬件上启动一个新程序而采取的步骤 Figure 1. Steps the OS takes to start a new program running on the underlying hardware 与用户程序一样，操作系统也是在计算机硬件上运行的软件。不过，操作系统是一种特殊的系统软件，它管理所有系统资源，并为计算机系统的用户实现接口；要使用计算机系统，就离不开它。由于操作系统是软件，它的二进制可执行代码与其他程序一样在硬件上运行：它的数据和指令存放在 RAM 中，它的指令与用户程序的指令一样，由 CPU 取出并执行。因此，要让操作系统运行起来，就需要把它的二进制可执行文件加载到 RAM 中，并初始化 CPU 以开始运行操作系统代码。然而，由于操作系统本身就负责在硬件上运行代码这项任务，它需要一些帮助才能开始运行。 Like user programs, the OS is also software that runs on the computer hardware. The OS, however, is special system software that manages all system resources and implements the interface for users of the computer system; it is necessary for using the computer system. Because the OS is software, its binary executable code runs on the hardware just like any other program: its data and instructions are stored in RAM and its instructions are fetched and executed by the CPU just like user’s program instructions are. As a result, for the OS to run, its binary executable needs to be loaded into RAM and the CPU initialized to start running OS code. However, because the OS is responsible for the task of running code on the hardware, it needs some help to get started running. 13.1.1. 操作系统的引导 13.1.1. OS Booting 操作系统在计算机上加载并初始化自身的过程称为 引导 （booting）：操作系统「拽着自己的靴带把自己提起来」，即在计算机上 引导 自己。操作系统最初需要一点帮助才能被加载到计算机上并开始运行它的引导代码。为了让操作系统代码开始运行，计算机刚加电时，会运行存放在计算机固件（硬件中的非易失性存储器）中的代码； BIOS （Basic Input/Output System，基本输入/输出系统）和 UEFI （Unified Extensible Firmware Interface，统一可扩展固件接口）就是这类固件的两个例子。加电时，BIOS 或 UEFI 运行，只做足够的硬件初始化，把操作系统的第一块内容（它的引导块）从磁盘加载到 RAM 中，并开始在 CPU 上运行引导块中的指令。一旦操作系统开始运行，它就会从磁盘加载自身的其余部分，发现并初始化硬件资源，并初始化它的数据结构和抽象，使系统为用户做好准备。 The process of the OS loading and initializing itself on the computer is known as booting — the OS “pulls itself up by its bootstraps”, or boots itself on the computer. The OS needs a little help to initially get loaded onto the computer and to begin running its boot code. To initiate the OS code to start running, code stored in computer firmware (nonvolatile memory in the hardware) runs when the computer first powers up; BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) and UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) are two examples of this type of firmware. On power-up, BIOS or UEFI runs and does just enough hardware initialization to load the first chunk of the OS (its boot block) from disk into RAM and to start running boot block instructions on the CPU. Once the OS starts running, it loads the rest of itself from disk, discovers and initializes hardware resources, and initializes its data structures and abstractions to make the system ready for users. 13.1.2. 让操作系统做事：中断与陷阱 13.1.2. Getting the OS to Do Something: Interrupts and Traps 操作系统完成引导、把系统初始化为可用状态之后，就只是等着有事可做。大多数操作系统都实现为 中断驱动的系统 （interrupt-driven system），即直到某个实体需要它做什么事情，操作系统才会运行：操作系统被唤醒（从睡眠中被中断）来处理一个请求。 After the OS finishes booting and initializing the system for use, it then just waits for something to do. Most operating systems are implemented as interrupt-driven systems , meaning that the OS doesn’t run until some entity needs it to do something — the OS is woken up (interrupted from its sleep) to handle a request. 硬件层中的设备可能需要操作系统为它们做些事情。例如， 网络接口卡 （network interface card，NIC）是计算机与网络之间的硬件接口。当 NIC 通过它的网络连接收到数据时，它会中断（即唤醒）操作系统来处理收到的数据（见 图 2 ）。例如，操作系统可能判断出 NIC 收到的数据是 Web 浏览器请求的某个网页的一部分；然后它把数据从 NIC 交给正在等待的 Web 浏览器进程。 Devices in the hardware layer may need the OS to do something for them. For example, a network interface card (NIC) is a hardware interface between a computer and a network. When the NIC receives data over its network connection, it interrupts (or wakes up) the OS to handle the received data (see Figure 2 ). For example, the OS may determine that the data received by the NIC is part of a web page that was requested by a web browser; it then delivers the data from the NIC to the waiting web browser process. 当用户应用程序需要访问受保护的资源时，也会向操作系统发出请求。例如，当应用程序想写一个文件时，它会向操作系统发出一个 系统调用 （system call），唤醒操作系统来代表它执行写操作（见 图 2 ）。操作系统通过把数据写入存放在磁盘上的文件来处理这个系统调用。 Requests to the OS also come from user applications when they need access to protected resources. For example, when an application wants to write to a file, it makes a system call to the OS, which wakes up the OS to perform the write on its behalf (see Figure 2 ). The OS handles the system call by writing the data to a file stored on disk. 图 2. 在中断驱动的系统中，用户级程序发出系统调用，硬件设备发出中断，以触发操作系统的动作。 Figure 2. In an interrupt-driven system, user-level programs make system calls, and hardware devices issue interrupts to initiate OS actions. 来自硬件层的中断，例如 NIC 从网络收到数据时产生的中断，通常称为硬件中断，或简称 中断 （interrupt）。来自软件层、由指令执行引起的中断，例如应用程序发出系统调用时产生的中断，通常称为 陷阱 （trap）。也就是说，系统调用「陷入操作系统」，由操作系统代表用户级程序处理请求。来自任一层的异常也可能中断操作系统。例如，如果因为磁盘块损坏而读取失败，硬盘驱动器可能会中断操作系统；如果应用程序执行了一条除以零的除法指令，它可能会触发一个陷入操作系统的陷阱。 Interrupts that come from the hardware layer, such as when a NIC receives data from the network, are typically referred to as hardware interrupts, or just interrupts . Interrupts that come from the software layer as the result of instruction execution, such as when an application makes a system call, are typically referred to as traps . That is, a system call “traps into the OS”, which handles the request on behalf of the user-level program. Exceptions from either layer may also interrupt the OS. For example, a hard disk drive may interrupt the OS if a read fails due to a bad disk block, and an application program may trigger a trap to the OS if it executes a divide instruction that divides by zero. 系统调用是用 CPU 指令集架构（ISA）中定义的特殊陷阱指令实现的。操作系统给它的每个系统调用分配一个唯一的标识号。当应用程序想调用某个系统调用时，它把所需调用的编号放到一个已知的位置（具体位置因 ISA 而异），然后发出一条陷阱指令来中断操作系统。陷阱指令让 CPU 停止执行应用程序的指令，开始执行处理该陷阱的操作系统指令（运行操作系统的陷阱处理程序代码）。陷阱处理程序读取用户提供的系统调用号，并执行相应的系统调用实现。 System calls are implemented using special trap instructions that are defined as part of the CPU’s instruction set architecture (ISA). The OS associates each of its system calls with a unique identification number. When an application wants to invoke a system call, it places the desired call’s number in a known location (the location varies according to the ISA) and issues a trap instruction to interrupt the OS. The trap instruction triggers the CPU to stop executing instructions from the application program and to start executing OS instructions that handle the trap (run the OS trap handler code). The trap handler reads the user-provided system call number and executes the corresponding system call implementation. 下面是在 IA32 Linux 系统上，一个 write 系统调用大致的样子： Here’s an example of what a write system call might look like on an IA32 Linux system: /* C code */ ret = write(fd, buff, size); # IA32 translation write: ... # set up state and parameters for OS to perform write movl $4, %eax # load 4 (unique ID for write) into register eax int $0x80 # trap instruction: interrupt the CPU and transition to the OS addl $8, %ebx # an example instruction after the trap instruction 第一条指令（ movl $4, %eax ）把 write 的系统调用号（4）放到寄存器 eax 中。第二条指令（ int $0x80 ）触发陷阱。操作系统的陷阱处理程序代码运行时，它用寄存器 eax 中的值（4）来判断调用的是哪个系统调用，并运行相应的处理程序代码（在这里运行的是 write 的处理代码）。操作系统处理程序运行完之后，操作系统从紧跟在陷阱指令之后的那条指令（本例中是 addl ）继续执行程序。 The first instruction ( movl $4, %eax ) puts the system call number for write (4) into register eax . The second instruction ( int $0x80 ) triggers the trap. When the OS trap handler code runs, it uses the value in register eax (4) to determine which system call is being invoked and runs the appropriate trap handler code (in this case it runs the write handler code). After the OS handler runs, the OS continues the program’s execution at the instruction right after the trap instruction ( addl in this example). 译注 · 其他体系结构上的系统调用指令 int $0x80 是 32 位 x86 的做法。按 Linux 的 syscall(2) 手册中的调用约定表：x86-64 使用专门的 syscall 指令，系统调用号放在 eax ，参数依次放在 rdi 、 rsi 、 rdx 、 r10 、 r8 、 r9 ；arm64 使用 svc #0 指令，系统调用号放在 w8 ，参数放在 x0 – x5 。不同体系结构上同一个系统调用的编号也可能不同。 与来自程序指令执行的系统调用不同，硬件中断是通过中断总线传递给 CPU 的。设备把一个信号（通常是一个表示中断类型的编号）放到 CPU 的中断总线上（见 图 3 ）。当 CPU 在中断总线上检测到这个信号时，它停止执行当前进程的指令，开始执行操作系统的中断处理程序代码。操作系统处理程序代码运行完之后，操作系统从中断发生时正在执行的那条应用程序指令处继续执行该进程。 Unlike system calls, which come from executing program instructions, hardware interrupts are delivered to the CPU on an interrupt bus. A device places a signal, typically a number indicating the type of interrupt, on the CPU’s interrupt bus (see Figure 3 ). When the CPU detects the signal on its interrupt bus, it stops executing the current process’s instructions and starts executing OS interrupt handler code. After the OS handler code runs, the OS continues the process’s execution at the application instruction that was being executed when the interrupt occurred. 图 3. 一个硬件设备（磁盘）通过中断总线向 CPU 发送信号，触发操作系统为它执行代码。 Figure 3. A hardware device (disk) sends a signal to the CPU on the interrupt bus to trigger OS execution on its behalf. 如果中断（或陷阱）发生时 CPU 上正在运行一个用户程序，CPU 就会运行操作系统的中断（或陷阱）处理程序代码。操作系统处理完中断后，从被中断的地方恢复执行该用户程序。 If a user program is running on the CPU when an interrupt (or trap) occurs, the CPU runs the OS’s interrupt (or trap) handler code. When the OS is done handling an interrupt, it resumes executing the interrupted user program at the point it was interrupted. 由于操作系统是软件，它的代码与用户程序代码一样被加载到 RAM 中并在 CPU 上运行，所以操作系统必须保护自己的代码和状态，不受系统中运行的普通进程的影响。CPU 通过定义两种执行模式来提供帮助： Because the OS is software, and its code is loaded into RAM and run on the CPU just like user program code, the OS must protect its code and state from regular processes running in the system. The CPU helps by defining two execution modes: 在 用户态 （user mode）下，CPU 只执行用户级指令，并且只访问操作系统允许它访问的内存位置。操作系统通常会阻止处于用户态的 CPU 访问操作系统的指令和数据。用户态还限制了 CPU 可以直接访问哪些硬件部件。 In user mode a CPU executes only user-level instructions and accesses only the memory locations that the operating system makes available to it. The OS typically prevents a CPU in user mode from accessing the OS’s instructions and data. User mode also restricts which hardware components the CPU can directly access. 在 内核态 （kernel mode）下，CPU 可以执行任何指令，访问任何内存位置（包括存放操作系统指令和数据的位置）。它还可以直接访问硬件部件，执行特殊指令。 In kernel mode , a CPU executes any instructions and accesses any memory location (including those that store OS instructions and data). It can also directly access hardware components and execute special instructions. 在 CPU 上运行操作系统代码时，系统运行在内核态；在 CPU 上运行用户级程序时，系统运行在用户态。如果 CPU 处于用户态时收到一个中断，CPU 就切换到内核态，取出中断处理例程，开始执行操作系统的处理程序代码。在内核态下，操作系统可以访问用户态下不允许访问的硬件和内存位置。操作系统处理完中断后，它恢复 CPU 的状态，以便从程序被中断时停下的地方继续执行用户级代码，并把 CPU 切回用户态（见 图 4 ）。 When OS code is run on the CPU, the system runs in kernel mode, and when user-level programs run on the CPU, the system runs in user mode. If the CPU is in user mode and receives an interrupt, the CPU switches to kernel mode, fetches the interrupt handler routine, and starts executing the OS handler code. In kernel mode, the OS can access hardware and memory locations that are not allowed in user mode. When the OS is done handling the interrupt, it restores the CPU state to continue executing user-level code at the point at which the program left off when interrupted and returns the CPU back to user mode (see Figure 4 ). 图 4. CPU 与中断。在 CPU 上运行的用户代码被中断（在时间线上的时刻 X），操作系统的中断处理程序代码开始运行。操作系统处理完中断后，用户代码恢复执行（在时间线上的时刻 Y）。 Figure 4. The CPU and interrupts. User code running on the CPU is interrupted (at time X on the time line), and OS interrupt handler code runs. After the OS is done handling the interrupt, user code execution is resumed (at time Y on the time line). 在中断驱动的系统中，中断随时可能发生，这意味着操作系统可能在任何一个机器周期从运行用户代码切换到运行中断处理程序代码。高效地支持这种从用户态到内核态的执行上下文切换的一种方法，是让内核在系统中每个进程的执行上下文中运行。在引导时，操作系统把它的代码加载到 RAM 中的一个固定位置，该位置被映射到每个进程地址空间的顶部（见 图 5 ），并用操作系统处理函数的起始地址初始化一个 CPU 寄存器。发生中断时，CPU 切换到内核态，执行操作系统的中断处理程序代码指令，这些指令在每个进程地址空间的顶部地址处都可以访问到。由于每个进程都把操作系统映射在其地址空间顶部的同一位置，无论中断发生时 CPU 上正在运行哪个进程，操作系统的中断处理程序代码都能在该进程的上下文中快速执行。这些操作系统代码只能在内核态下访问，从而保护操作系统不受用户态访问的影响；在常规执行期间，进程运行在用户态，不能读写映射在其地址空间顶部的操作系统地址。 In an interrupt-driven system, interrupts can happen at any time, meaning that the OS can switch from running user code to interrupt handler code at any machine cycle. One way to efficiently support this execution context switch from user mode to kernel mode, is to allow the kernel to run within the execution context of every process in the system. At boot time, the OS loads its code at a fixed location in RAM that is mapped into the top of the address space of every process (see Figure 5 ), and initializes a CPU register with the starting address of the OS handler function. On an interrupt, the CPU switches to kernel mode and executes OS interrupt handler code instructions that are accessible at the top addresses in every process’s address space. Because every process has the OS mapped to the same location at the top of its address space, the OS interrupt handler code is able to execute quickly in the context of any process that is running on the CPU when an interrupt occurs. This OS code can be accessed only in kernel mode, protecting the OS from user-mode accesses; during regular execution a process runs in user mode and cannot read or write to the OS addresses mapped into the top of its address space. 图 5. 进程地址空间：操作系统内核被映射到每个进程地址空间的顶部。 Figure 5. Process address space: the OS kernel is mapped into the top of every process’s address space. 尽管把操作系统代码映射到每个进程的地址空间中，能让内核代码在中断时快速执行，但当操作系统像这样映射到每个进程中时，许多现代处理器的某些特性会暴露出破坏内核保护的漏洞。自 2018 年 1 月 Meltdown 硬件漏洞 1 公布以来，操作系统开始以能够防御这种攻击的方式，把内核内存和用户级程序内存分离开来，但这也使得切换到内核态处理中断的效率降低了。 Although mapping the OS code into the address space of every process results in fast kernel code execution on an interrupt, many modern processors have features that expose vulnerabilities to kernel protections when the OS is mapped into every process like this. As of the January 2018 announcement of the Meltdown hardware exploit 1 , operating systems are separating kernel memory and user-level program memory in ways that protect against this exploit, but that also result in less efficient switching to kernel mode to handle interrupts. 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· Linux 的页表隔离（PTI） 原文说的「把内核内存和用户程序内存分离」，在 Linux 中就是 页表隔离 （Page Table Isolation，PTI，早期称为 KAISER），它是针对 Meltdown 这类利用共享用户/内核地址空间的攻击的对策：内核为每个进程维护两套页表，运行用户程序时使用一套专门为此创建的独立页表，通过系统调用、中断或异常进入内核时再切换到完整的「内核」页表。内核文档指出，这会带来一些开销（例如上下文切换后更多的 TLB 未命中），而支持进程上下文标识符（PCID）的 CPU 可以避免切换页表时刷新整个 TLB；PTI 可以在编译时开启，并能用 nopti 或 pti= 启动参数关闭。 Linux 内核文档：Page Table Isolation (PTI) 13.1.3. 参考文献 13.1.3. References Meltdown and Spectre. https://meltdownattack.com/

说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C13-OS/ipc_signals.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 13.4.1. Signals 信号 （signal）是一个进程通过操作系统发送给另一个进程的软件中断。当一个进程收到信号时，操作系统会中断它当前的执行点，转而运行信号处理程序代码。如果信号处理程序返回，进程就从为处理信号而被中断的地方继续执行。有时信号处理程序会使进程退出，这时它就不会从停下的地方继续执行了。 A signal is a software interrupt that is sent by one process to another process via the OS. When a process receives a signal, its current execution point is interrupted by the OS to run signal handler code. If the signal handler returns, the process’s execution continues from where it was interrupted to handle the signal. Sometimes the signal handler causes the process to exit, and thus it does not continue its execution from where it left off. 信号与硬件中断和陷阱相似，但又与两者都不同。陷阱是进程显式调用系统调用时发生的同步软件中断，而信号是异步的：进程在执行的任何时刻都可能因收到信号而被中断。信号与异步的硬件中断的不同之处在于，信号是由软件而不是硬件设备触发的。 Signals are similar to hardware interrupts and traps but are different from both. Whereas a trap is a synchronous software interrupt that occurs when a process explicitly invokes a system call, signals are asynchronous — a process may be interrupted by the receipt of a signal at any point in its execution. Signals also differ from asynchronous hardware interrupts in that they are triggered by software rather than hardware devices. 一个进程可以通过执行 kill 系统调用向另一个进程发送信号，这个系统调用请求操作系统向另一个进程投递一个信号。操作系统负责把信号投递给目标进程，并设置目标进程的执行状态，使其运行与所投递的特定信号相关联的信号处理程序代码。 A process can send another process a signal by executing the kill system call, which requests that the OS post a signal to another process. The OS handles posting the signal to the target process and setting its execution state to run the signal handler code associated with the particular posted signal. 原书注 kill 系统调用的名字可能会让人误解，而且不幸地带有暴力色彩。尽管它可以（也常常）用来传递终止信号，但它也用来向进程发送其他任何类型的信号。 The name of the kill system call is potentially misleading as well as unfortunately violent. While it can be (and often is) used to deliver a termination signal, it is also used to send any other type of signal to a process. 操作系统自己也用信号来通知进程某些事件。例如，当一个进程的某个子进程退出时，操作系统会向该进程投递一个 SIGCHLD 信号。 The OS itself also uses signals to notify processes of certain events. For example, the OS posts a SIGCHLD signal to a process when one of its child processes exits. 系统定义了固定数量的信号（例如，Linux 定义了 32 种不同的信号）。因此，与消息传递或共享内存等其他进程间通信方法相比，信号提供的进程间通信方式是有限的。 Systems define a fixed number of signals (e.g., Linux defines 32 different signals). As a result, signals provide a limited way in which processes can communicate with one another, as opposed to other interprocess communication methods such as messaging or shared memory. 译注 更准确地说，32 左右指的是 Linux 的「标准信号」（编号 1–31）。按 signal(7) 手册，Linux 内核另外还支持 33 个编号为 32 到 64 的实时信号（real-time signal），程序应使用 SIGRTMIN 、 SIGRTMAX 宏来引用它们，因为 glibc 的线程实现会占用其中几个。 表 1 列出了一些已定义的信号。更多例子请查看手册页（ man 7 signal ）。 Table 1 lists some of the defined signals. See the man page ( man 7 signal ) for additional examples. 表 1. 用于进程间通信的信号示例 Table 1. Example Signals Used for Interprocess Communication 信号名 说明 SIGSEGV 段错误（例如对空指针解引用） SIGINT 中断进程（例如在终端窗口中按 Ctrl-C 终止进程） SIGCHLD 子进程已退出（例如子进程运行 exit 后成为僵尸） SIGALRM 通知进程定时器到时（例如 alarm(2) 每 2 秒一次） SIGKILL 终止进程（例如 pkill -9 a.out ） SIGBUS 发生总线错误（例如用未对齐的内存地址访问 int 值） SIGSTOP 挂起进程，使其转入阻塞状态（例如 Ctrl-Z） SIGCONT 让阻塞的进程继续（使其转入就绪状态；例如 bg 或 fg ） Signal Name Description SIGSEGV Segmentation fault (e.g., dereferencing a null pointer) SIGINT Interrupt process (e.g., Ctrl-C in terminal window to kill process) SIGCHLD Child process has exited (e.g., a child is now a zombie after running exit ) SIGALRM Notify a process a timer goes off (e.g., alarm(2) every 2 secs) SIGKILL Terminate a process (e.g., pkill -9 a.out ) SIGBUS Bus error occurred (e.g., a misaligned memory address to access an int value) SIGSTOP Suspend a process, move to Blocked state (e.g., Ctrl-Z) SIGCONT Continue a blocked process (move it to the Ready state; e.g., bg or fg ) 译注 在终端按 Ctrl-Z 发送的其实是 SIGTSTP （「在终端键入的停止」），而不是 SIGSTOP 。两者的默认动作都是停止进程，区别在于 SIGTSTP 可以被程序捕获或忽略，而 SIGSTOP 和 SIGKILL 一样不能被捕获、阻塞或忽略（见 signal(7) ）。 当进程收到一个信号时，可能发生下面几种默认动作之一： When a process receives a signal, one of several default actions can occur: 进程终止 the process can terminate 信号被忽略 the signal can be ignored 进程被阻塞 the process can be blocked 进程被解除阻塞 the process can be unblocked 操作系统为每个信号编号定义了默认动作，并提供默认的信号处理程序代码。不过，应用程序员可以改变大多数信号的默认动作，并编写自己的信号处理程序代码。如果应用程序没有为某个信号注册自己的信号处理函数，那么进程收到该信号时，就执行操作系统的默认处理程序。对于某些信号，操作系统定义的默认动作不能被应用程序的信号处理程序代码覆盖。例如，如果进程收到 SIGKILL 信号，操作系统总会强制进程退出；收到 SIGSTOP 信号总会使进程阻塞，直到它收到让它继续（ SIGCONT ）或退出（ SIGKILL ）的信号。 The OS defines a default action and supplies the default signal handler code for every signal number. Application programmers, however, can change the default action of most signals and can write their own signal handler code. If an application program doesn’t register its own signal handler function for a particular signal, then the OS’s default handler executes when the process receives a signal. For some signals, the OS-defined default action cannot be overridden by application signal handler code. For example, if a process receives a SIGKILL signal, the OS will always force the process to exit, and receiving a SIGSTOP signal will always block the process until it receives a signal to continue ( SIGCONT ) or to exit ( SIGKILL ). Linux 支持两个不同的系统调用，可以用来改变信号的默认行为，或者为某个特定信号注册信号处理程序： sigaction 和 signal 。由于 sigaction 符合 POSIX 标准且功能更丰富，在正式的软件中应当使用它。不过，我们在示例代码中使用 signal ，因为它更容易理解。 Linux supports two different system calls that can be used to change the default behavior of a signal or to register a signal handler on a particular signal: sigaction and signal . Because sigaction is POSIX compliant and more featureful, it should be used in production software. However, we use signal in our example code because it is easier to understand. 下面是一个 示例程序 ，它用 signal 系统调用为 SIGALRM 、 SIGINT 和 SIGCONT 信号注册信号处理程序（为了可读性去掉了错误处理）： Following is an example program that registers signal handlers for SIGALRM , SIGINT , and SIGCONT signals using the signal system call (error handling is removed for readability): /* * Example of signal handlers for SIGALRM, SIGINT, and SIGCONT * * A signal handler function prototype must match: * void handler_function_name(int signum); * * Compile and run this program, then send this process signals by executing: * kill -INT pid (or Ctrl-C) will send a SIGINT * kill -CONT pid (or Ctrl-Z fg) will send a SIGCONT */ #include <stdio.h> #include <stdlib.h> #include <unistd.h> #include <signal.h> /* signal handler for SIGALRM */ void sigalarm_handler(int sig) { printf("BEEP, signal number %d
.", sig); fflush(stdout); alarm(5); /* sends another SIGALRM in 5 seconds */ } /* signal handler for SIGCONT */ void sigcont_handler(int sig) { printf("in sigcont handler function, signal number %d
.", sig); fflush(stdout); } /* signal handler for SIGINT */ void sigint_handler(int sig) { printf("in sigint handler function, signal number %d...exiting
.", sig); fflush(stdout); exit(0); } /* main: register signal handlers and repeatedly block until receive signal */ int main(void) { /* Register signal handlers. */ if (signal(SIGCONT, sigcont_handler) == SIG_ERR) { printf("Error call to signal, SIGCONT
"); exit(1); } if (signal(SIGINT, sigint_handler) == SIG_ERR) { printf("Error call to signal, SIGINT
"); exit(1); } if (signal(SIGALRM, sigalarm_handler) == SIG_ERR) { printf("Error call to signal, SIGALRM
"); exit(1); } printf("kill -CONT %d to send SIGCONT
", getpid()); alarm(5); /* sends a SIGALRM in 5 seconds */ while(1) { pause(); /* wait for a signal to happen */ } } 运行时，进程每 5 秒收到一个 SIGALRM （由于 main 和 sigalarm_handler 中对 alarm 的调用）。可以在另一个 shell 中运行 kill 或 pkill 命令来触发 SIGINT 和 SIGCONT 信号。例如，如果进程的 PID 是 1234，可执行文件是 a.out ，那么下面的 shell 命令就会向该进程发送 SIGINT 和 SIGCONT 信号，触发它们的信号处理函数运行： When run, the process receives a SIGALRM every 5 seconds (due to the call to alarm in main and sigalarm_handler ). The SIGINT and SIGCONT signals can be triggered by running the kill or pkill commands in another shell. For example, if the process’s PID is 1234 and its executable is a.out , then the following shell command sends the process SIGINT and SIGCONT signals, triggering their signal handler functions to run: pkill -INT a.out kill -INT 1234 pkill -CONT a.out kill -CONT 1234 编写 SIGCHLD 处理程序 Writing a SIGCHLD handler 回想一下，当一个进程终止时，操作系统会向它的父进程传递一个 SIGCHLD 信号。在创建子进程的程序中，父进程并不总是希望阻塞在 wait 调用上，直到子进程退出。例如，当 shell 程序在后台运行一个命令时，它与子进程并发运行，在子进程于后台运行的同时，继续在前台处理其他 shell 命令。然而，父进程需要调用 wait 来回收退出后的僵尸子进程。否则，僵尸进程永远不会消亡，会一直占用一些系统资源。在这些情况下，父进程可以为 SIGCHLD 信号注册一个信号处理程序。当父进程收到来自已退出子进程的 SIGCHLD 时，它的处理程序代码就会运行，调用 wait 来回收僵尸子进程。 Recall that when a process terminates, the OS delivers a SIGCHLD signal to its parent process. In programs that create child processes, the parent process does not always want to block on a call to wait until its child processes exit. For example, when a shell program runs a command in the background, it continues to run concurrently with its child process, handling other shell commands in the foreground as the child process runs in the background. A parent process, however, needs to call wait to reap its zombie child processes after they exit. If not, the zombie processes will never die and will continue to hold on to some system resources. In these cases, the parent process can register a signal handler on SIGCHLD signals. When the parent receives a SIGCHLD from an exited child process, its handler code runs and makes calls to wait to reap its zombie children. 下面是一个代码片段，展示了 SIGCHLD 信号处理函数的实现。这个片段还展示了 main 函数中为 SIGCHLD 信号注册该信号处理函数的部分代码（注意，这应当在任何 fork 调用之前完成）： Below is a code snippet showing the implementation of a signal handler function for SIGCHLD signals. This snippet also shows parts of a main function that register the signal handler function for the SIGCHLD signal (note that this should be done before any calls to fork ): /* * signal handler for SIGCHLD: reaps zombie children * signum: the number of the signal (will be 20 for SIGCHLD) */ void sigchld_handler(int signum) { int status; pid_t pid; /* * reap any and all exited child processes * (loop because there could be more than one) */ while( (pid = waitpid(-1, &status, WNOHANG)) > 0) { /* uncomment debug print stmt to see what is being handled printf("signal %d me:%d child: %d
", signum, getpid(), pid); */ } } int main(void) { /* register SIGCHLD handler: */ if ( signal(SIGCHLD, sigchld_handler) == SIG_ERR) { printf("ERROR signal failed
"); exit(1); } ... /* create a child process */ pid = fork(); if(pid == 0) { /* child code...maybe call execvp */ ... } /* the parent continues executing concurrently with child */ ... 上面的例子把 -1 作为 PID 传给 waitpid ，意思是「回收任何一个僵尸子进程」。它还传入了 WNOHANG 标志，表示如果没有可回收的僵尸子进程， waitpid 调用不会阻塞。还要注意， waitpid 是在一个 while 循环中调用的，只要它返回有效的 PID 值（只要它回收了一个僵尸子进程），循环就继续。信号处理函数在循环中调用 waitpid 是很重要的，因为在它运行期间，进程可能会收到来自其他已退出子进程的更多 SIGCHLD 信号。操作系统并不记录进程收到了多少个 SIGCHLD 信号，它只记下进程收到过 SIGCHLD ，并中断其执行去运行处理程序代码。因此，如果没有这个循环，信号处理程序可能会漏掉一些僵尸子进程而没有回收。 The example above passes -1 as the PID to waitpid , which means “reap any zombie child process.” It also passes the WNOHANG flag, which means that the call to waitpid does not block if there are no zombie child processes to reap. Also note that waitpid is called inside a while loop that continues as long as it returns a valid PID value (as long as it reaps a zombie child process). It is important that the signal handler function calls waitpid in a loop because as it is running, the process could receive additional SIGCHLD signals from other exited child process. The OS doesn’t keep track of the number of SIGCHLD signals a process receives, it just notes that the process received a SIGCHLD and interrupts its execution to run the handler code. As a result, without the loop, the signal handler could miss reaping some zombie children. 无论父进程是否阻塞在 wait 或 waitpid 调用上，只要父进程收到 SIGCHLD 信号，信号处理程序就会执行。如果父进程在收到 SIGCHLD 时阻塞在 wait 调用上，它会被唤醒并运行信号处理程序代码，回收一个或多个僵尸子进程。然后，它从程序中 wait 调用之后的地方继续执行（它刚刚回收了一个已退出的子进程）。然而，如果父进程阻塞在针对某个特定子进程的 waitpid 调用上，那么在它的信号处理程序代码回收了一个已退出的子进程之后，父进程可能继续阻塞，也可能不再阻塞。如果信号处理程序代码回收的正是父进程在等待的那个子进程，父进程就从 waitpid 调用之后继续执行。否则，父进程会继续阻塞在 waitpid 调用上，等待指定的子进程退出。用一个不存在的子进程（也许是之前已在信号处理程序的循环中被回收的子进程）的 PID 调用 waitpid ，不会使调用者阻塞。 The signal handler executes whenever the parent receives a SIGCHLD signal, regardless of whether the parent is blocked on a call to wait or waitpid . If the parent is blocked on a call to wait when it receives a SIGCHLD , it wakes up and runs the signal handler code to reap one or more of its zombie children. It then continues execution at the point in the program after the call to wait (it just reaped an exited child process). If, however, the parent is blocked on a call to waitpid for a specific child, then the parent may or may not continue to block after its signal handler code runs to reap an exited child. The parent process continues execution after its call to waitpid if the signal handler code reaped the child for which it was waiting. Otherwise, the parent continues to block on the call to waitpid to wait for the specified child to exit. A call to waitpid with a PID of a non existent child process (perhaps one that was previously reaped in the signal handler loop) does not block the caller.

Interprocess Communication 进程是操作系统实现的主要抽象之一。私有的虚拟地址空间是多道程序设计系统中的一个重要抽象，也是操作系统防止进程干扰彼此执行状态的方式之一。然而，有时用户或程序员可能希望自己的应用进程在运行时能够相互通信（或者共享一部分执行状态）。 Processes are one of the primary abstractions implemented by the OS. Private virtual address spaces are an important abstraction in multiprogrammed systems, and are one way in which the OS prevents processes from interfering with one another’s execution state. However, sometimes a user or programmer may want their application processes to communicate with one another (or to share some of their execution state) as they run. 操作系统通常支持几种进程间通信（interprocess communication，IPC）方式，即进程之间相互通信或共享执行状态的方式。 信号 （signal）是一种非常受限的进程间通信形式，一个进程可以通过它向另一个进程发送信号，通知其发生了某个事件。进程还可以通过 消息传递 （message passing）进行通信，操作系统为此实现了一种消息通信信道的抽象，进程用它与另一个进程交换消息。最后，操作系统还可能通过 共享内存 （shared memory）支持进程间通信，允许一个进程与其他进程共享其全部或部分虚拟地址空间。拥有共享内存的进程可以通过读写共享空间中的地址来相互通信。 Operating systems typically implement support for several types of interprocess communication, or ways in which processes can communicate or share their execution state. Signals are a very restricted form of interprocess communication by which one process can send a signal to another process to notify it of some event. Processes can also communicate using message passing , in which the OS implements an abstraction of a message communication channel that is used by a process to exchange messages with another process. Finally, the OS may support interprocess communication through shared memory that allows a process to share all or part of its virtual address space with other processes. Processes with shared memory can read or write to addresses in shared space to communicate with one another.

Message Passing 拥有私有虚拟地址空间的进程之间相互通信的一种方式是 消息传递 （message passing），即相互发送和接收消息。消息传递让程序可以交换任意数据，而不仅仅是信号所支持的那一小组预定义的消息。操作系统通常会实现几种不同类型的消息传递抽象，供进程用来通信。 One way in which processes with private virtual address spaces can communicate is through message passing — by sending and receiving messages to one another. Message passing allows programs to exchange arbitrary data rather than just a small set of predefined messages like those supported by signals. And operating systems typically implement a few different types of message passing abstractions that processes can use to communicate. 消息传递式的进程间通信模型由三部分组成： The message passing interprocess communication model consists of three parts: 进程从操作系统分配某种类型的消息信道。消息信道的类型包括用于单向通信的 管道 （pipe）和用于双向通信的 套接字 （socket）等。进程可能还需要采取另外一些建立连接的步骤来配置消息信道。 Processes allocate some type of message channel from the OS. Example message channel types include pipes for one-way communication, and sockets for two-way communication. There may be additional connection setup steps that processes need to take to configure the message channel. 进程使用消息信道相互发送和接收消息。 Processes use the message channel to send and receive messages to one another. 进程用完消息信道后，关闭自己那一端。 Processes close their end of the message channel when they are done using it. 管道 （pipe）是运行在同一台机器上的两个进程之间的单向通信信道。单向是指管道的一端只能用来发送消息（即写入），另一端只能用来接收消息（即读取）。在 shell 命令中，管道常用来把一个进程的输出送到另一个进程的输入。 A pipe is a one-way communication channel for two processes running on the same machine. One-way means that one end of the pipe is for sending messages (or writing to) only, and the other end of the pipe is for receiving messages (or for reading from) only. Pipes are commonly used in shell commands to send the output from one process to the input of another process. 例如，考虑在 bash shell 提示符下输入的下面这条命令，它在两个进程之间创建一个管道（ cat 进程输出文件 foo.c 的内容，管道（ | ）把这个输出重定向到 grep 命令的输入， grep 在它的输入中查找字符串「factorial」）： For example, consider the following command entered at a bash shell prompt that creates a pipe between two processes (the cat process outputs the contents of file foo.c and the pipe ( | ) redirects that output to the input of the grep command that searches for the string “factorial” in its input): $ cat foo.c | grep factorial 为了执行这条命令，bash shell 进程调用 pipe 系统调用，请求操作系统创建一个管道通信。这个管道将由 shell 的两个子进程（ cat 和 grep ）使用。shell 程序把 cat 进程的 stdout 设置为写入管道的写端，把 grep 进程的 stdin 设置为从管道的读端读取，这样当子进程被创建并运行时， cat 进程的输出就会作为输入发送给 grep 进程（见 图 1 ）。 To execute this command, the bash shell process calls the pipe system call to request that the OS creates a pipe communication. The shell program sets up the cat process’s stdout to write to the write end of the pipe and the grep process’s stdin to read from the read end of the pipe, so that when the child processes are created and run, the cat process’s output will be sent as input to the grep process (see Figure 1 ). 图 1. 管道是同一系统上的进程之间的单向通信信道。在这个例子中，cat 进程通过向管道的写端写入来向 grep 进程发送信息，grep 进程通过从管道的读端读取来接收这些信息。 Figure 1. A socket is a two-way communication channel, which means that each end of a socket can be used for both sending and receiving messages. Sockets can be used by communicating processes running on the same computer or running on different computers connected by a network (see Figure 2 ). The computers could be connected by a local area network (LAN), which connects computers in a small area, such as a network in a university computer science department. The communicating processes could also be on different LANs, connected to the internet. As long as there exists some path through network connections between the two machines, the processes can use sockets to communicate. 图 2. 套接字是双向通信信道，可以供通过网络相连的不同机器上的进程通信使用。 Figure 2. Sockets are bidirectional communication channels that can be used by communicating processes on different machines connected by a network. 由于每台计算机都是一个独立的系统（硬件和操作系统），而一个系统上的操作系统并不了解、也不管理另一个系统上的资源，所以消息传递是不同计算机上的进程相互通信的唯一方式。为了支持这类通信，操作系统需要实现一种通用的消息传递协议，用于在网络上发送和接收消息。TCP/IP 就是可以用来在互联网上发送消息的一种消息协议。当一个进程想向另一个进程发送消息时，它发出一个 send 系统调用，把想要用来传输的套接字、消息缓冲区，以及可能还有关于消息或其预期接收者的其他信息交给操作系统。操作系统负责把消息缓冲区中的消息打包，并通过网络发送到另一台机器。当操作系统从网络上收到一条消息时，它把消息解包，并交给本系统上请求接收该消息的进程。这个进程可能正处于阻塞状态，等待消息到来。在这种情况下，消息的到达会让该进程再次进入就绪状态。 Because each individual computer is its own system (hardware and OS), and because the OS on one system does not know about or manage resources on the other system, message passing is the only way in which processes on different computers can communicate. To support this type of communication, operating systems need to implement a common message passing protocol for sending and receiving messages over a network. In the Parallel Systems Chapter , we discuss message passing and the abstractions built atop it in more detail.

Processes 操作系统实现的主要抽象之一是 进程 （process）。进程代表在系统中运行的一个程序实例，它包括程序的二进制可执行代码、数据和执行 上下文 （context）。上下文通过维护程序的寄存器值、栈的位置以及当前正在执行的指令，来跟踪程序的执行。 One of the main abstractions implemented by the operating system is a process . A process represents an instance of a program running in the system, which includes the program’s binary executable code, data, and execution context . The context tracks the program’s execution by maintaining its register values, stack location, and the instruction it is currently executing. 在支持多个进程同时存在于系统中的 多道程序设计 系统中，进程是必不可少的抽象。操作系统用进程抽象来跟踪系统中运行的各个程序实例，并管理它们对系统资源的使用。 Processes are necessary abstractions in multiprogramming systems, which support multiple processes existing in the system at the same time. The process abstraction is used by the OS to keep track of individual instances of programs running in the system, and to manage their use of system resources. 操作系统为每个进程提供一种「独占视图」的系统抽象。也就是说，操作系统把进程彼此隔离开来，给每个进程一种它在控制整台机器的错觉。实际上，操作系统支持许多活动的进程，并管理它们之间的资源共享。操作系统向用户隐藏了共享和访问系统资源的细节，并保护进程不受系统中其他运行进程行为的影响。 The OS provides each process with a “lone view” abstraction of the system. That is, the OS isolates processes from one another and gives each process the illusion that it’s controlling the entire machine. In reality, the OS supports many active processes and manages resource sharing among them. The OS hides the details of sharing and accessing system resources from the user, and the OS protects processes from the actions of other processes running in the system. 例如，用户可能在一个计算机系统上同时运行两个 Unix shell 程序实例和一个 Web 浏览器。操作系统为这三个正在运行的程序创建三个相应的进程：Unix shell 程序的每次单独执行各一个进程，Web 浏览器一个进程。操作系统负责在 CPU 上运行的这三个进程之间切换，并确保一个进程在 CPU 上运行时，只能访问分配给该进程的执行状态和系统资源。 For example, a user may simultaneously run two instances of a Unix shell program along with a web browser on a computer system. The OS creates three processes associated with these three running programs: one process for each separate execution of the Unix shell program, and one process for the web browser. The OS handles switching between these three processes running on the CPU, and it ensures that as a process runs on the CPU, only the execution state and system resources allocated to the process can be accessed. 13.2.1. 多道程序设计与上下文切换 13.2.1. Multiprogramming and Context Switching 多道程序设计让操作系统能够高效地利用硬件资源。例如，当在 CPU 上运行的进程需要访问当前在磁盘上的数据时，操作系统不必让 CPU 闲着等数据读入内存，而是可以把 CPU 交给另一个进程运行，同时由磁盘处理原进程的读操作。通过多道程序设计，操作系统可以在一些进程等待访问存储器层次结构较低层中的数据时，让 CPU 忙于执行另一些进程，从而缓解存储器层次结构对其程序工作负载的一些影响。 Multiprogramming enables the OS to make efficient use of hardware resources. For example, when a process running on the CPU needs to access data that are currently on disk, rather than have the CPU sit idle waiting for the data to be read into memory, the OS can give the CPU to another process and let it run while the read operation for the original process is being handled by the disk. By using multiprogramming, the OS can mitigate some of the effects of the memory hierarchy on its program workload by keeping the CPU busy executing some processes while other processes are waiting to access data in the lower levels of the memory hierarchy. 通用操作系统常常实现 分时 （timesharing），这是一种多道程序设计，操作系统调度各个进程轮流在 CPU 上执行一小段时间（称为 时间片 ，time slice 或 quantum）。当一个进程用完它在 CPU 上的时间片时，操作系统把它从 CPU 上移下来，让另一个进程运行。大多数系统把时间片定为几毫秒（10 -3 秒），以 CPU 周期计这是很长的时间，但人察觉不到。 General-purpose operating systems often implement timesharing , which is multiprogramming wherein the OS schedules each process to take turns executing on the CPU for short time durations (known as a time slice or quantum ). When a process completes its time slice on the CPU, the OS removes the process from the CPU and lets another run. Most systems define time slices to be a few milliseconds (10 -3 seconds), which is a long time in terms of CPU cycles but is not noticeable to a human. 分时系统进一步支持了计算机系统对用户的「独占视图」；由于每个进程都频繁地在 CPU 上执行一小段时间，用户通常察觉不到它们在共享 CPU。只有在系统负载非常重时，用户才可能注意到系统中其他进程的影响。Unix 命令 ps -A 列出系统中运行的所有进程，你可能会对进程之多感到吃惊。 top 命令也很有用，它显示当前使用系统资源（例如 CPU 时间和内存空间）最多的那些进程，让你在系统运行时查看其状态。 Timesharing systems further support the “lone view” of the computer system to the user; because each process frequently executes on the CPU for short bursts of time, the fact that they are all sharing the CPU is usually imperceptible to the user. Only when the system is very heavily loaded might a user notice the effects of other processes in the system. The Unix command ps -A lists all the processes running in the system — you may be surprised by how many there are. The top command is also useful for seeing the state of the system as it runs by displaying the set of processes that currently use the most system resources (such as CPU time and memory space). 在多道程序设计和分时系统中，进程是 并发 （concurrently）运行的，即它们的执行在时间上有重叠。例如，操作系统可能先在 CPU 上运行进程 A，然后切换去运行进程 B 一段时间，之后再切换回来继续运行进程 A。在这种情况下，进程 A 和 B 是并发运行的，因为操作系统在两者之间切换，使它们在 CPU 上的执行有重叠。 In multiprogrammed and timeshared systems, processes run concurrently , meaning that their executions overlap in time. For example, the OS may start running process A on the CPU, and then switch to running process B for a while, and later switch back to running process A some more. In this scenario, processes A and B run concurrently because their execution on the CPU overlaps due to the OS switching between the two. 上下文切换 Context Switching 多道程序设计背后的 机制 决定了操作系统如何把在 CPU 上运行的一个进程换成另一个。多道程序设计的 策略 方面则支配着 CPU 调度，即从一组候选进程中挑选哪个进程下一个使用 CPU，以及使用多长时间。我们主要关注实现多道程序设计的机制。操作系统教材会更详细地介绍调度策略。 The mechanism behind multiprogramming determines how the OS swaps one process running on the CPU with another. The policy aspect of multiprogramming governs scheduling the CPU, or picking which process from a set of candidate processes gets to use the CPU next and for how long. We focus primarily on the mechanism of implementing multiprogramming. Operating systems textbooks cover scheduling policies in more detail. 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· Linux 换了新的进程调度器 本书只讲调度的机制，不讲策略。值得一提的是，2023 年 10 月 29 日发布的 Linux 6.6 用一个名为 EEVDF （Earliest Eligible Virtual Deadline First，最早合格虚拟截止时间优先）的新调度器取代了自 2.6.23 版起使用多年的 CFS（完全公平调度器），Kernel Newbies 的版本说明称它总体上应能提供更好的延迟。 Kernel Newbies：Linux 6.6 操作系统执行 上下文切换 （context switching），即在 CPU 上交换进程状态，这是多道程序设计（以及分时）背后的主要机制。执行一次 CPU 上下文切换有两个主要步骤： The OS performs context switching , or swapping process state on the CPU, as the primary mechanism behind multiprogramming (and timesharing). There are two main steps to performing a CPU context switch: 操作系统保存当前在 CPU 上运行的进程的上下文，包括它所有的寄存器值（PC、栈指针、通用寄存器、条件码等）、它的内存状态，以及其他一些状态（例如它所使用的系统资源的状态，比如打开的文件）。 The OS saves the context of the current process running on the CPU, including all of its register values (PC, stack pointers, general-purpose register, condition codes, etc.), its memory state, and some other state (for example the state of system resources it uses, like open files). 操作系统在 CPU 上恢复另一个进程已保存的上下文，并让 CPU 开始运行这个进程，从它上次停下的那条指令继续执行。 The OS restores the saved context from another process on the CPU and starts the CPU running this other process, continuing its execution from the instruction where it left off. 上下文切换中有一部分看起来似乎不可能做到：实现上下文切换的操作系统代码，必须在把进程的执行上下文从 CPU 保存出来（或恢复到 CPU 上）的同时，在 CPU 上运行；上下文切换代码的指令需要用 CPU 硬件寄存器来执行，但被换下 CPU 的那个进程的寄存器值又需要由上下文切换代码来保存。计算机硬件提供了一些帮助，使这成为可能。 One part of context switching that may seem impossible to accomplish is that the OS’s code that implements context switching must run on the CPU while it saves (restores) a process’s execution contexts from (to) the CPU; the instructions of the context switching code need to use CPU hardware registers to execute, but the register values from the process being context switched off the CPU need to be saved by the context switching code. Computer hardware provides some help to make this possible. 在引导时，操作系统初始化了硬件，包括初始化 CPU 状态，使得 CPU 在中断时切换到内核态后，操作系统的中断处理程序代码开始执行，而被中断进程的执行状态不受这次执行的影响。计算机硬件和操作系统一起完成对用户级执行上下文最初的一部分保存工作，足以让操作系统代码在 CPU 上运行而不会丢失被中断进程的执行状态。例如，被中断进程的寄存器值需要保存下来，这样当该进程再次在 CPU 上运行时，就能用它的寄存器值从它停下的地方继续执行。根据硬件支持的不同，保存用户级进程寄存器值的工作可能完全由硬件完成，也可能几乎完全由软件完成，作为内核中断处理代码的第一部分。至少，进程的程序计数器（PC）的值需要保存下来，这样在把内核中断处理程序的地址加载到 PC 时，它的值才不会丢失。 At boot time, the OS initialized the hardware, including initializing the CPU state, so that when the CPU switches to kernel mode on an interrupt, the OS interrupt handler code starts executing and the interrupted process’s execution state is protected from this execution. Together, the computer hardware and OS perform some of the initial saving of the user-level execution context, enough that the OS code can run on the CPU without losing the execution state of the interrupted process. For example, register values of the interrupted process need to be saved so that when the process runs again on the CPU, the process can continue from the point at which it left off, using its register values. Depending on the hardware support, saving the user-level process’s register values may be done entirely by the hardware or may be done almost entirely in software as the first part of the kernel’s interrupt handling code. At a minimum, the process’s program counter (PC) value needs to be saved so that its value is not lost when the kernel interrupt handler address is loaded into the PC. 一旦操作系统开始运行，它就执行完整的进程上下文切换代码，保存正在 CPU 上运行的进程的完整执行状态，并把另一个进程已保存的执行状态恢复到 CPU 上。由于操作系统运行在内核态，它能访问计算机内存的任何部分，能执行特权指令，能访问任何硬件寄存器。因此，它的上下文切换代码能够访问任何进程的 CPU 执行状态并把它保存到内存中，也能把任何进程的执行状态从内存恢复到 CPU 上。操作系统的上下文切换代码最后设置好 CPU，以执行恢复后的进程的执行状态，并把 CPU 切换到用户态。切换到用户态后，CPU 执行的指令和使用的执行状态，就都来自操作系统切换到 CPU 上的那个进程了。 Once the OS starts running, it executes its full process context switching code, saving the full execution state of the process running on the CPU and restoring the saved execution state of another process onto the CPU. Because the OS runs in kernel mode it is able to access any parts of computer memory and can execute privileged instructions and access any hardware registers. As a result, its context switching code is able to access and save the CPU execution state of any process to memory, and it is able to restore from memory the execution state of any process to the CPU. OS context switching code completes by setting up the CPU to execute the restored process’s execution state and by switching the CPU to user mode. Once switched to user mode, the CPU executes instructions, and uses execution state, from the process that the OS context switched onto the CPU. 13.2.2. 进程状态 13.2.2. Process State 在多道程序设计系统中，操作系统必须跟踪和管理任一时刻存在于系统中的多个进程。操作系统为每个进程维护的信息包括： In multiprogrammed systems, the OS must track and manage the multiple processes existing in the system at any given time. The OS maintains information about each process, including: 进程 ID （process id，PID），即进程的唯一标识符。 ps 命令列出系统中进程的信息，包括它们的 PID 值。 A process id (PID), which is a unique identifier for a process. The ps command lists information about processes in the system, including their PID values. 进程的地址空间信息。 The address space information for the process. 进程的执行状态（例如 CPU 寄存器值、栈的位置）。 The execution state of the process (e.g., CPU register values, stack location). 分配给进程的资源集合（例如打开的文件）。 The set of resources allocated to the process (e.g., open files). 当前的 进程状态 （process state），这个值决定了它是否有资格在 CPU 上执行。 The current process state , which is a value that determines its eligibility for execution on the CPU. 在生命周期中，进程会经历几种状态，这些状态对应于进程执行资格的不同类别。操作系统使用进程状态的一种方式，是确定哪些进程是可以被调度到 CPU 上的候选者。 Over the course of its lifetime, a process moves through several states, which correspond to different categories of process execution eligibility. One way that the OS uses process state is to identify the set of processes that are candidates for being scheduled on the CPU. 进程的执行状态包括： The set of process execution states are: 就绪 （Ready）：进程可以在 CPU 上运行，但当前没有被调度（它是被上下文切换到 CPU 上的候选者）。新进程被操作系统创建并初始化后，就进入就绪状态（它已准备好让 CPU 开始执行它的第一条指令）。在分时系统中，如果一个进程因为时间片用完而被上下文切换下 CPU，它也会被置于 就绪 状态（它已准备好让 CPU 执行它的下一条指令，但它用完了时间片，必须等待轮到它再次被调度到 CPU 上）。 Ready : The process could run on the CPU but is not currently scheduled (it is a candidate for being context switched on to the CPU). Once a new process is created and initialized by the OS, it enters the ready state (it is ready for the CPU to start executing its first instruction). In a timesharing system, if a process is context switched off the CPU because its time slice is up, it is also placed in the ready state (it is ready for the CPU to execute its next instruction, but it used up its time slice and has to wait its turn to get scheduled again on the CPU). 运行 （Running）：进程被调度到 CPU 上，正在执行指令。 Running : The process is scheduled on the CPU and is actively executing instructions. 阻塞 （Blocked）：进程在等待某个事件，然后才能继续执行。例如，进程在等待从磁盘读入一些数据。阻塞的进程不是被调度到 CPU 上的候选者。等到使进程阻塞的事件发生后，进程就转到 就绪 状态（它已准备好再次运行）。 Blocked : The process is waiting for some event before it can continue being executed. For example, the process is waiting for some data to be read in from disk. Blocked processes are not candidates for being scheduled on the CPU. After the event on which the process is blocked occurs, the process moves to the ready state (it is ready to run again). 退出 （Exited）：进程已经退出，但仍需要从系统中彻底清除。进程退出的原因可能是它执行完了程序的指令，也可能是因错误而退出（例如它试图除以零），还可能是收到了来自另一个进程的终止请求。退出的进程永远不会再运行，但在与其执行状态相关的最后清理工作完成之前，它仍然留在系统中。 Exited : The process has exited but still needs to be completely removed from the system. A process exits due to its completing the execution of its program instructions, or by exiting with an error (e.g., it tries to divide by zero), or by receiving a termination request from another process. An exited process will never run again, but it remains in the system until final clean-up associated with its execution state is complete. 图 1 展示了一个进程在系统中的生命周期，说明了它如何在不同状态之间转换。注意从一个状态到另一个状态的转换（箭头）。例如，进程可以通过三种方式之一进入 就绪 状态：第一，它是操作系统新创建的；第二，它原本因等待某个事件而阻塞，而该事件发生了；第三，它原本在 CPU 上运行，时间片用完了，操作系统把它上下文切换下来，让另一个 就绪 进程轮到使用 CPU。 Figure 1 shows the lifetime of a process in the system, illustrating how it moves between different states. Note the transitions (arrows) from one state to another. For example, a process can enter the Ready state in one of three ways: first, if it is newly created by the OS; second, if it was blocked waiting for some event and the event occurs; and third, if it was running on the CPU and its time slice is over and the OS context switches it off to give another Ready process its turn on the CPU. 图 1. 进程在其生命周期中的各种状态 Figure 1. The states of a process during its lifetime 原书旁注 · 进程运行时间（Process Runtime） 程序员常常用进程的完成时间作为评估其性能的指标。对于非交互式程序，运行时间越短，通常表示实现越好、越优化。例如，比较两个计算大数质因数的程序时，能更快地正确完成任务的那个更可取。 进程的运行时间有两种不同的度量。第一种是总的 挂钟时间 （wall time 或 wall-clock time）。挂钟时间是进程从开始到完成之间的时长，即用挂在墙上的钟测得的、从进程开始到结束所经过的时间。挂钟时间包括进程处于运行状态、在 CPU 上执行的时间，也包括进程处于阻塞状态、等待 I/O 等事件的时间，还包括进程处于就绪状态、等待轮到它被调度到 CPU 上运行的时间。在多道程序设计和分时系统中，进程的挂钟时间可能会因为系统上并发运行、共享系统资源的其他进程而变长。 进程运行时间的第二种度量是总的 CPU 时间 （CPU time，或进程时间）。CPU 时间只度量进程处于运行状态、在 CPU 上执行其指令的时间。CPU 时间不包括进程处于阻塞或就绪状态的时间。因此，进程的总 CPU 时间不受系统上并发运行的其他进程的影响。 Programmers often use a process’s completion time as a metric to evaluate its performance. For noninteractive programs, a faster runtime typically indicates a better, or more optimal, implementation. For example, in comparing two programs that compute the prime factors of a large number, the one that correctly completes the task faster is preferable. There are two different measures of the runtime of a process. The first is total wall time (or wall-clock time). Wall time is the duration between the start and completion of a process it is the elapsed time from the process’s start to finish as measured by a clock hanging on a wall. Wall time includes the time that the process is in the Running state executing on the CPU, as well as time that the process is in the Blocked state waiting for an event like I/O, as well as time that the process spends in the Ready state waiting for its turn to be scheduled to run on the CPU. In multiprogrammed and timeshared systems, the wall time of a process can slow down due to other processes running concurrently on the system and sharing system resources. The second measure of process runtime is total CPU time (or process time). CPU time measures just the amount of time the process spends in the Running state executing its instructions on the CPU. CPU time does not include the time the process spends in the Blocked or Ready states. As a result, a process’s total CPU time is not affected by other processes concurrently running on the system. 译注 在 shell 中用 time ./a.out 运行程序，可以同时看到这两种时间： real 是挂钟时间， user 和 sys 分别是在用户态和内核态下消耗的 CPU 时间。 13.2.3. 进程的创建（与销毁） 13.2.3. Creating (and Destroying) Processes 当一个现有进程发出系统调用请求操作系统创建新进程时，操作系统就创建一个新进程。在 Unix 中， fork 系统调用创建一个新进程。调用 fork 的进程是 父 进程，它创建的新进程是它的 子 进程。例如，如果你在 shell 中运行 a.out ，shell 进程就会调用 fork 系统调用，请求操作系统创建一个新的子进程，用来运行 a.out 程序。另一个例子是 Web 浏览器进程，它调用 fork 创建子进程来处理不同的浏览事件。当用户加载一个网页时，Web 浏览器可能会创建一个子进程来处理与 Web 服务器的通信。它可能再创建一个进程来处理用户的鼠标输入，还会创建其他进程来处理单独的浏览器窗口或标签页。像这样的多进程 Web 浏览器，能够通过它的一些子进程继续处理用户请求，同时它的另一些子进程可能正因等待远程 Web 服务器的响应或用户的鼠标点击而阻塞。 An OS creates a new process when an existing process makes a system call requesting it to do so. In Unix, the fork system call creates a new process. The process calling fork is the parent process and the new process it creates is its child process. For example, if you run a.out in a shell, the shell process calls the fork system call to request that the OS create a new child process that will be used to run the a.out program. Another example is a web browser process that calls fork to create child processes to handle different browsing events. A web browser may create a child process to handle communication with a web server when a user loads a web page. It may create another process to handle user mouse input, and other processes to handle separate browser windows or tabs. A multiple-process web browser like this is able to continue handling user requests through some of its child browser processes, while at the same time some of its other child browser processes may be blocked waiting for remote web server responses or for user mouse clicks. 系统中活动的进程之间存在由父子关系构成的 进程层次结构 （process hierarchy）。例如，如果进程 A 调用两次 fork ，就会创建两个新的子进程 B 和 C 。如果进程 C 接着调用 fork ，就会再创建一个新进程 D 。进程 C 是 A 的子进程，也是 D 的父进程。进程 B 和 C 是兄弟（它们有共同的父进程 A ）。进程 A 是 B 、 C 和 D 的祖先。 图 2 展示了这个例子。 A process hierarchy of parent-child relationships exists between the set of processes active in the system. For example, if process A makes two calls to fork , two new child processes are created, B and C_. If process C then calls fork , another new process, D , will be created. Process C is the child of A , and the parent of D . Processes B and C are siblings (they share a common parent process, process A ). Process A is the ancestor of B , C , and D . This example is illustrated in Figure 2 . 图 2. 一个进程层次结构的例子：父进程（A）调用两次 fork，创建两个子进程（B 和 C）。C 调用 fork 创建它的子进程 D。在 Linux 系统上，要列出进程层次结构，可以运行 pstree 或 ps -Aef --forest 。 Figure 2. An example process hierarchy created by a parent process (A) calling fork twice to create two child processes (B and C). C’s call to fork creates its child process, D. To list the process hierarchy on Linux systems, run pstree , or ps -Aef --forest . 由于是现有进程触发进程的创建，系统至少需要一个进程才能创建任何新进程。在引导时，操作系统创建系统中第一个用户级进程。这个特殊的进程名为 init ，它位于进程层次结构的最顶端，是系统中所有其他进程的祖先。 Since existing processes trigger process creation, a system needs at least one process to create any new processes. At boot time, the OS creates the first user-level process in the system. This special process, named init , sits at the very top of the process hierarchy as the ancestor of all other processes in the system. 译注 如今大多数 Linux 发行版中，作为第一个进程（PID 1）运行的 init 程序是 systemd：按其手册，systemd 作为引导时的第一个进程运行时，充当 init 系统，负责启动和维护用户空间的各项服务（ systemd(1) ）。在 macOS 上，PID 1 是 launchd ，译者在 Mac 上运行 ps -p 1 -o pid=,comm= 得到的正是 /sbin/launchd 。 fork fork fork 系统调用用于创建进程。在 fork 的那一刻，子进程从父进程那里继承执行状态。操作系统为调用者（父）进程在调用 fork 那一刻的执行状态创建一个 副本 。这个执行状态包括父进程地址空间的内容、CPU 寄存器的值，以及它已分配的任何系统资源（例如打开的文件）。操作系统还会创建一个新的 进程控制结构 （process control struct），即用来管理子进程的操作系统数据结构，并给子进程分配一个唯一的 PID。操作系统创建并初始化新进程之后，子进程和父进程就是并发的：它们都继续运行，随着操作系统把它们上下文切换上

Summary and Other OS Functionality 在本章中，我们考察了操作系统是什么、它如何工作，以及它在计算机上运行应用程序时所起的作用。作为位于计算机硬件和应用程序之间的系统软件层，操作系统高效地管理计算机硬件，并实现让计算机更易于使用的各种抽象。操作系统实现了进程和虚拟内存这两个抽象，以支持多道程序设计（允许计算机系统上同时运行不止一个程序）。操作系统跟踪系统中所有的进程及其状态，并实现 CPU 核心上运行的进程之间的上下文切换。操作系统还为进程提供了创建新进程、退出以及相互通信的方式。通过虚拟内存，操作系统为每个进程实现了私有虚拟内存空间的抽象。虚拟内存抽象使进程看不到共享计算机物理内存空间的其他进程的影响。分页是虚拟内存的一种实现，它把每个进程虚拟地址空间中的各个页映射到物理 RAM 空间的页框上。虚拟内存也是操作系统更高效地利用 RAM 的一种方式：通过把 RAM 当作磁盘的缓存，它允许虚拟内存空间的页存放在 RAM 中或磁盘上。 In this chapter, we examined what an operating system is, how it works, and the role it plays in running application programs on the computer. As the system software layer between the computer hardware and application programs, the OS efficiently manages the computer hardware and implements abstractions that make the computer easier to use. Operating systems implement two abstractions, processes and virtual memory, to support multiprogramming (allowing more than one program running on the computer system at a time). The OS keeps track of all the processes in the system and their state, and it implements context switching of processes running on the CPU cores. The OS also provides a way for processes to create new processes, to exit, and to communicate with one another. Through virtual memory, the OS implements the abstraction of a private virtual memory space for each process. The virtual memory abstraction protects processes from seeing the effects of other processes sharing the computer’s physical memory space. Paging is one implementation of virtual memory that maps individual pages of each process’s virtual address space to frames of physical RAM space. Virtual memory is also a way in which the OS makes more efficient use of RAM; by treating RAM as a cache for disk, it allows pages of virtual memory space to be stored in RAM or on disk. 本章关注的是操作系统在运行程序中所起的作用，包括它为高效运行程序而实现的抽象和机制，但这绝不是全部。关于进程和进程管理、虚拟内存和内存管理，还有许多其他的实现选择、细节和策略问题。此外，操作系统还实现了许多其他重要的抽象、功能和策略，用于管理和使用计算机。例如，操作系统实现了用于访问存储数据的文件系统抽象、保护用户和系统的保护机制和安全策略，以及针对各种操作系统和硬件资源的调度策略。 Our focus in this chapter on the operating system’s role in running a program, including the abstractions and mechanisms it implements to efficiently run programs, is in no way complete. There are many other implementation options and details and policy issues related to processes and process management, and to virtual memory and memory management. Additionally, operating systems implement many other important abstractions, functionality, and policies for managing and using the computer. For example, the OS implements filesystem abstractions for accessing stored data, protection mechanisms and security policies to protect users and the system, and scheduling policies for different OS and hardware resources. 现代操作系统还实现了对进程间通信、网络以及并行和分布式计算的支持。此外，大多数操作系统都包含对 虚拟机管理程序 （hypervisor）的支持，它把系统硬件虚拟化，允许宿主操作系统运行多个虚拟的客户操作系统。虚拟化让管理计算机硬件的宿主操作系统能够在自身之上引导和运行多个其他操作系统，每个操作系统都有自己对底层硬件的私有虚拟化视图。宿主操作系统的虚拟机管理程序支持负责管理虚拟化，包括在各客户操作系统之间保护和共享底层的物理资源。 Modern operating systems also implement support for interprocess communication, networking, and parallel and distributed computing. In addition, most operating systems include hypervisor support, which virtualizes the system hardware and allows the host OS to run multiple virtual guest operating systems. Virtualization supports the host OS that manages the computer hardware in booting and running multiple other operating systems on top of itself, each with its own private virtualized view of the underlying hardware. The host operating system’s hypervisor support manages the virtualization, including protection and sharing of the underlying physical resources among the guest operating systems. 最后，大多数操作系统都提供了一定程度的可扩展性，让用户（通常是系统管理员）可以调优操作系统。例如，大多数类 Unix 系统允许用户（通常需要 root 即超级用户权限）改变操作系统缓冲区、缓存和交换分区的大小，并为操作系统子系统和硬件设备从一组不同的调度策略中进行选择。通过这些修改，用户可以针对自己运行的应用程序工作负载类型对系统进行调优。这类操作系统常常支持 可加载内核模块 （loadable kernel module），即可以加载到内核中、在内核态下运行的可执行代码。可加载内核模块常用来向内核添加额外的抽象或功能，也用来把用于管理特定硬件设备的设备驱动程序代码加载到内核中。 Finally, most operating systems provide some degree of extensibility by which a user (often a system administrator) can tune the OS. For example, most Unix-like systems allow users (usually requiring root, or superuser, privileges) to change sizes of OS buffers, caches, swap partitions, and to select from a set of different scheduling policies in OS subsystems and hardware devices. Through these modifications, a user can tune the system for the type of application workloads they run. These types of operating systems often support loadable kernel modules , which are executable code that can be loaded into the kernel and run in kernel mode. Loadable kernel modules are often used to add additional abstractions or functionality into the kernel as well as for loading device driver code into the kernel that is used to handle managing a particular hardware device. 要更广泛、更深入地了解操作系统，我们推荐阅读一本操作系统教材，例如《Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces》 1 。 For more breadth and depth of coverage of operating systems, we recommend reading an operating systems textbook, such as “Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces” 1 . 译注 这本书常简称 OSTEP，可在作者网站上免费阅读，中译本名为《操作系统导论》。 13.5.1. 参考文献 13.5.1.
