Virtual Memory 操作系统的进程抽象为每个进程提供了一个虚拟内存空间。 虚拟内存 （virtual memory）是一种抽象，它给每个进程一个私有的逻辑地址空间，用来存放进程的指令和数据。每个进程的虚拟地址空间可以看作一个可寻址字节的数组，地址从 0 一直到某个最大地址。例如，在 32 位系统上，最大地址是 2 32 -1。进程不能访问彼此地址空间中的内容。进程虚拟地址空间中的某些部分来自它所运行的二进制可执行文件（例如， 代码段 （text）包含来自 a.out 文件的程序指令）。进程虚拟地址空间的其他部分则是在运行时创建的（例如 栈 ）。 The OS’s process abstraction provides each process with a virtual memory space. Virtual memory is an abstraction that gives each process its own private, logical address space in which its instructions and data are stored. Each process’s virtual address space can be thought of as an array of addressable bytes, from address 0 up to some maximum address. For example, on 32-bit systems the maximum address is 2 32 -1. Processes cannot access the contents of one another’s address spaces. Some parts of a process’s virtual address space come from the binary executable file it’s running (e.g., the text portion contains program instructions from the a.out file). Other parts of a process’s virtual address space are created at runtime (e.g., the stack ). 操作系统把虚拟内存作为进程 独占视图 抽象的一部分来实现。也就是说，每个进程只以自己的虚拟地址空间的形式与内存交互，而不必面对许多进程同时共享计算机物理内存（RAM）这一现实。操作系统还利用其虚拟内存实现，保护进程不能访问彼此的内存空间。举个例子，考虑下面这个简单的 C 程序： Operating systems implement virtual memory as part of the lone view abstraction of processes. That is, each process only interacts with memory in terms of its own virtual address space rather than the reality of many processes simultaneously sharing the computer’s physical memory (RAM). The OS also uses its virtual memory implementation to protect processes from accessing one another’s memory spaces. As an example, consider the following simple C program: /* a simple program */ #include <stdio.h> int main(int argc, char* argv[]) { int x, y; printf("enter a value: "); scanf("%d", &y); if (y > 10) { x = y; } else { x = 6; } printf("x is %d\n", x); return 0; } 如果两个进程同时执行这个程序，它们各自都会得到一份栈内存的副本，作为各自独立的虚拟地址空间的一部分。因此，如果一个进程执行 x = 6 ，对另一个进程中 x 的值不会有任何影响：每个进程在自己私有的虚拟地址空间中都有一份 x 的副本，如 图 1 所示。 If two processes simultaneously execute this program, they each get their own copy of stack memory as part of their separate virtual address spaces. As a result, if one process executes x = 6 it will have no effect on the value of x in the other process — each process has its own copy of x , in its private virtual address space, as shown in Figure 1 . 图 1. 执行两次 a.out 会产生两个进程，各自运行 a.out 程序的一个相互隔离的实例。每个进程都有自己私有的虚拟地址空间，其中包含它自己的程序指令、全局变量以及栈和堆内存空间的副本。例如，每个进程在其虚拟地址空间的栈部分中都可能有一个局部变量 x。 Figure 1. Two executions of a.out results in two processes, each running isolated instances of the a.out program. Each process has its own private virtual address space, containing its copies of program instructions, global variables, and stack and heap memory space. For example, each may have a local variable x in the stack portion of their virtual address spaces. 进程的虚拟地址空间被划分为几个区段，每个区段存放进程内存的不同部分。顶部（位于最低地址处）保留给操作系统，只能在内核态下访问。进程虚拟地址空间中的代码段和数据段由程序的可执行文件（ a.out ）初始化。代码段包含程序指令，数据段包含全局变量（数据部分实际上又分为两部分，一部分用于已初始化的全局变量，另一部分用于未初始化的全局变量）。 A process’s virtual address space is divided into several sections, each of which stores a different part of the process’s memory. The top part (at the lowest addresses) is reserved for the OS and can only be accessed in kernel mode. The text and data parts of a process’s virtual address space are initialized from the program executable file ( a.out ). The text section contains the program instructions, and the data section contains global variables (the data portion is actually divided into two parts, one for initialized global variables and the other for uninitialized globals). 译注 本书的地址空间示意图把低地址画在上方、高地址画在下方，所以文中说操作系统在「顶部（最低地址处）」，栈在「底部（接近最大地址处）」并「向上」朝低地址增长。这与 13.1 节图 5 一致，但有些教材的画法正好上下颠倒，读图时注意方向。 进程虚拟地址空间中的栈和堆区段会随着进程的运行而改变大小。栈空间随着进程进行函数调用而增长，随着它从函数返回而收缩。堆空间在进程动态分配内存空间时（通过调用 malloc ）增长，在进程释放动态分配的内存空间时（通过调用 free ）收缩。进程内存中的堆和栈部分在其地址空间中通常相距很远，以使两者能使用的空间都尽可能大。通常，栈位于进程地址空间的底部（接近最大地址处），随着函数调用把栈帧加到栈顶，栈向上朝较低的地址增长。 The stack and heap sections of a process’s virtual address space vary in size as the process runs. Stack space grows in response to the process making function calls, and shrinks as it returns from functions. Heap space grows when the process dynamically allocates memory space (via calls to malloc ), and shrinks when the process frees dynamically allocated memory space (via calls to free ). The heap and stack portions of a process’s memory are typically located far apart in its address space to maximize the amount of space either can use. Typically, the stack is located at the bottom of a process’s address space (near the maximum address), and grows upward into lower addresses as stack frames are added to the top of the stack in response to a function call. 原书旁注 · 关于堆内存和栈内存（About Heap and Stack Memory） 堆内存和栈内存空间的实际总容量，通常并不会在每次调用 malloc 和 free 时改变，也不会在每次函数调用和返回时改变。这些动作常常只改变进程正在使用的、当前已分配的那部分堆和栈虚拟内存空间的多少。不过，有时这些动作确实会导致堆或栈空间总容量的变化。 操作系统负责管理进程的虚拟地址空间，包括改变堆和栈空间的总容量。可以用 brk 、 sbrk 或 mmap 系统调用请求操作系统改变堆内存的总容量。C 程序员通常不直接调用这些系统调用，而是调用标准 C 库函数 malloc （和 free ）来分配（和释放）堆内存空间。在内部，标准 C 库的用户级堆管理器可能会调用这些系统调用之一，请求操作系统改变堆内存空间的大小，以满足 malloc 请求。 The actual total capacity of heap and stack memory space does not typically change on every call to malloc and free , nor on every function call and return. Instead, these actions often only make changes to how much of the currently allocated heap and stack parts of the virtual memory space are actively being used by the process. Sometimes, however, these actions do result in changes to the total capacity of the heap or stack space. The operating system is responsible for managing a process’s virtual address space, including changing the total capacity of heap and stack space. The system calls brk , sbrk , or mmap can be used to request that the OS change the total capacity of heap memory. C programmers do not usually invoke these system calls directly. Instead, C programmers call the standard C library function malloc (and free ) to allocate (and free) heap memory space. Internally, the standard C library’s user-level heap manager may invoke one of these system calls to request that the OS change the size of heap memory space to satisfy a malloc request. 13.3.1. 内存地址 13.3.1. Memory Addresses 由于进程在各自的虚拟地址空间中运行，操作系统必须对两种内存地址做出重要的区分。 虚拟地址 （virtual address）指进程虚拟地址空间中的存储位置， 物理地址 （physical address）指物理内存（RAM）中的存储位置。 Because processes operate within their own virtual address spaces, operating systems must make an important distinction between two types of memory addresses. Virtual addresses refer to storage locations in a process’s virtual address space, and physical addresses refer to storage locations in physical memory (RAM). 物理内存（RAM）与物理内存地址 Physical Memory (RAM) and Physical Memory Addresses 从 存储与存储器层次结构一章 我们知道，物理内存（RAM）可以看作一个可寻址字节的数组，地址范围从 0 到某个由 RAM 总大小决定的最大地址值。例如，在有 2 GB RAM 的系统中，物理内存地址的范围是 0 到 2 31 -1（1 GB 是 2 30 字节，所以 2 GB 是 2 31 字节）。 From the Storage and Memory Hierarchy Chapter , we know that physical memory (RAM) can be viewed as an array of addressable bytes in which addresses range from 0 to a maximum address value based on the total size of RAM. For example, in a system with 2 gigabytes (GB) of RAM, physical memory addresses range from 0 to 2 31 -1 (1 GB is 2 30 bytes, so 2 GB is 2 31 bytes). 要让 CPU 运行一个程序，程序的指令和数据必须由操作系统加载到 RAM 中；CPU 不能直接访问其他存储设备（例如磁盘）。操作系统管理 RAM，并决定 RAM 中的哪些位置用来存放进程虚拟地址空间的内容。例如，如果两个进程 P1 和 P2 运行上面列出的 示例程序 ，那么 P1 和 P2 各有一份独立的 x 变量副本，分别存放在 RAM 中的不同位置。也就是说，P1 的 x 和 P2 的 x 有不同的物理地址。如果操作系统给 P1 和 P2 的 x 变量分配同一个物理地址，那么 P1 把 x 设为 6 也会修改 P2 的 x 值，从而违背了每个进程拥有私有虚拟地址空间的原则。 In order for the CPU to run a program, the program’s instructions and data must be loaded into RAM by the OS; the CPU cannot directly access other storage devices (e.g., disks). The OS manages RAM and determines which locations in RAM should store the virtual address space contents of a process. For example, if two processes, P1 and P2, run the example program listed above, then P1 and P2 have separate copies of the x variable, each stored at a different location in RAM. That is, P1’s x and P2’s x have different physical addresses. If the OS gave P1 and P2 the same physical address for their x variables, then P1 setting x to 6 would also modify P2’s value of x , violating the per-process private virtual address space. 在任一时刻，操作系统都在 RAM 中存放着许多进程的地址空间内容，以及它可能映射到每个进程虚拟地址空间中的操作系统代码（操作系统代码通常从 RAM 的地址 0x0 处开始加载）。 图 2 展示了操作系统和三个进程（P1、P2 和 P3）被加载到 RAM 中的一个例子。每个进程的地址空间内容都有自己独立的物理存储位置（例如，即使 P1 和 P2 运行的是同一个程序，它们的变量 x 也有各自独立的物理存储位置）。 At any point in time, the OS stores in RAM the address space contents from many processes as well as OS code that it may map into every process’s virtual address space (OS code is typically loaded starting at address 0x0 of RAM). Figure 2 shows an example of the OS and three processes (P1, P2, and P3) loaded into RAM. Each process gets its own separate physical storage locations for its address space contents (e.g., even if P1 and P2 run the same program, they get separate physical storage locations for their variable x ). 图 2. RAM 内容示例：操作系统加载在地址 0x0 处，各进程加载在 RAM 中不同的物理内存地址处。如果 P1 和 P2 运行的是同一个 a.out，P1 中 x 的物理地址也与 P2 中 x 的物理地址不同。 Figure 2. Example RAM contents showing OS loaded at address 0x0, and processes loaded at different physical memory addresses in RAM. If P1 and P2 are running the same a.out, P1’s physical address for x is different from P2’s physical address for x. 虚拟内存与虚拟地址 Virtual Memory and Virtual Addresses 虚拟内存是每个进程对自己内存空间的视图， 虚拟地址 是进程视图中的内存地址。如果两个进程运行同一个二进制可执行文件，它们地址空间中函数代码和全局变量的虚拟地址完全相同（堆内存中动态分配空间的虚拟地址和栈上局部变量的虚拟地址，可能由于两次独立执行在运行时的差异而在两个进程之间略有不同）。换句话说，两个进程中 main 函数所在位置的虚拟地址相同，全局变量 x 在它们地址空间中所在位置的虚拟地址也相同，如 图 3 所示。 Virtual memory is the per-process view of its memory space, and virtual addresses are addresses in the process’s view of its memory. If two process run the same binary executable, they have exactly the same virtual addresses for function code and for global variables in their address spaces (the virtual addresses of dynamically allocated space in heap memory and of local variables on the stack may vary slightly between the two processes due to runtime differences in their two separate executions). In other words, both processes will have the same virtual addresses for the location of their main function, and the same virtual address for the location of a global variable x in their address spaces, as shown in Figure 3 . 译注 这是在不考虑地址空间布局随机化（ASLR）的情况下说的。现代系统默认启用 ASLR，若程序编译为位置无关可执行文件（PIE），同一程序两次运行时代码和全局变量的虚拟地址通常也不同（参见第 7 章缓冲区溢出一节的译注）；不过「两个进程的虚拟地址各自独立、互不相干」这一要点不变。 图 3. 运行同一个 a.out 文件的两个进程的虚拟内存内容示例。P1 和 P2 中全局变量 x 的虚拟地址相同。 Figure 3. Example virtual memory contents for two processes running the same a.out file. P1 and P2 have the same virtual address for global variable x. 13.3.2. 虚拟地址到物理地址的转换 13.3.2. Virtual Address to Physical Address Translation 程序的汇编指令和机器码指令引用的是虚拟地址。因此，如果两个进程执行同一个 a.out 程序，CPU 就会执行带有相同虚拟地址的指令，去访问它们两个独立虚拟地址空间中的对应部分。例如，假设 x 位于虚拟地址 0x24100，那么把 x 设为 6 的汇编指令可能是这样的： A program’s assembly and machine code instructions refer to virtual addresses. As a result, if two processes execute the same a.out program, the CPU executes instructions with identical virtual addresses to access corresponding parts of their two separate virtual address spaces. For example, suppose that x is at virtual address 0x24100, then assembly instructions to set x to 6 might look like this: movl $0x24100, %eax # load 0x24100 into register eax movl $6, (%eax) # store 6 at memory address 0x24100 在运行时，操作系统把每个进程的 x 变量加载到不同的物理内存地址（RAM 中的不同位置）。这意味着，每当 CPU 执行一条指定了虚拟地址的内存加载或存储指令时，都必须先把来自 CPU 的虚拟地址转换为 RAM 中对应的物理地址，然后才能从 RAM 中读写字节。 At runtime the OS loads each of the processes’ x variables at different physical memory addresses (at different locations in RAM). This means that whenever the CPU executes a load or store instruction to memory that specify virtual addresses, the virtual address from the CPU must be translated to its corresponding physical address in RAM before reading or writing the bytes from RAM. 由于虚拟内存是操作系统实现的一个重要的核心抽象，处理器通常会为虚拟内存提供一些硬件支持。操作系统可以利用这种硬件级的虚拟内存支持来快速完成虚拟地址到物理地址的转换，避免每次地址转换都要陷入操作系统处理。具体的操作系统自行选择在实现虚拟内存时使用多少分页方面的硬件支持。在选择用硬件实现还是用软件实现某个功能时，常常要在速度和灵活性之间权衡。 Because virtual memory is an important and core abstraction implemented by operating systems, processors generally provide some hardware support for virtual memory. An OS can make use of this hardware-level virtual memory support to perform virtual to physical address translations quickly, avoiding having to trap to the OS to handle every address translation. A particular OS chooses how much of the hardware support for paging it uses in its implementation of virtual memory. There is often a trade-off in speed versus flexibility when choosing a hardware-implemented feature versus a software-implemented feature. 内存管理单元 （memory management unit，MMU）是计算机硬件中实现地址转换的部分。当应用程序访问内存时，MMU 硬件和操作系统一起把虚拟地址转换为物理地址。硬件和软件之间具体如何分工，取决于硬件和操作系统的具体组合。在最完备的情况下，MMU 硬件完成全部转换：它从 CPU 获取虚拟地址，把它转换为用来寻址 RAM 的物理地址（如 图 4 所示）。无论硬件对虚拟内存的支持程度如何，总会有一些虚拟到物理的转换需要由操作系统来处理。在讨论虚拟内存时，我们假设 MMU 比较完备，使地址转换所需的操作系统参与降到最低。 The memory management unit (MMU) is the part of the computer hardware that implements address translation. Together, the MMU hardware and the OS translate virtual to physical addresses when applications access memory. The particular hardware/software split depends on the specific combination of hardware and OS. At its most complete, MMU hardware performs the full translation: it takes a virtual address from the CPU and translates it to a physical address that is used to address RAM (as shown in Figure 4 ). Regardless of the extent of hardware support for virtual memory, there will be some virtual-to-physical translations that the OS has to handle. Leveraging Shared Memory in the Multicore Era 世界已经改变。 The world is changed. 我在硅中感觉到了。 I feel it in the silica. 我在晶体管中感觉到了。 I feel it in the transistor. 我在核心中看到了。 I see it in the core. ——向凯兰崔尔致歉（《 指环王：护戒同盟 》） ~ With apologies to Galadriel ( Lord of the Rings: Fellowship of the Ring ) 到目前为止，我们对体系结构的讨论都集中在纯粹的单 CPU 世界中。但世界已经改变。如今的 CPU 有多个 核心 （core），即计算单元。在本章中，我们讨论多核体系结构，以及如何利用它们来加快程序的执行。 Until now, our discussion of architecture has focused on a purely single-CPU world. But the world has changed. Today’s CPUs have multiple cores , or compute units. In this chapter, we discuss multicore architectures, and how to leverage them to speed up the execution of programs. 原书注 · CPU、处理器与核心（CPUs, Processors, and Cores） 在本章的许多地方， 处理器 和 CPU 这两个术语是混用的。从根本上说， 处理器 （processor）是对外部数据执行某种计算的任何电路。按照这个定义， 中央处理器 （central processing unit，CPU）就是处理器的一个例子。带有多个计算核心的处理器或 CPU 称为 多核处理器 （multicore processor）或 多核 CPU 。 核心 （core）是一个计算单元，它包含构成经典 CPU 的许多部件：ALU、寄存器和一点缓存。尽管 核心 与处理器不同，但在文献中看到这两个术语混用并不罕见（特别是那些写于多核处理器还被视为新鲜事物的年代的文献）。 In many instances in this chapter, the terms processor and CPU are used interchangeably. At a fundamental level, a processor is any circuit that performs some computation on external data. Based on this definition, the central processing unit (CPU) is an example of a processor. A processor or a CPU with multiple compute cores is referred to as a multicore processor or a multicore CPU . A core is a compute unit that contains many of the components that make up the classical CPU: an ALU, registers, and a bit of cache. Although a core is different from a processor, it is not unusual to see these terms used interchangeably in the literature (especially if the literature originated at a time when multicore processors were still considered novel). 1965 年，英特尔创始人戈登·摩尔（Gordon Moore）估计，集成电路中的晶体管数量每年会翻一番。他的预测如今被称为 摩尔定律 （Moore’s Law），后来被修正为晶体管数量每 两 年翻一番。尽管电子开关已经从巴丁（Bardeen）的晶体管演变成如今现代计算机中使用的微小芯片晶体管，摩尔定律在过去 50 年里一直成立。然而，世纪之交时，处理器设计撞上了几道关键的性能壁垒： In 1965, the founder of Intel, Gordon Moore, estimated that the number of transistors in an integrated circuit would double every year. His prediction, now known as Moore’s Law , was later revised to transistor counts doubling every two years. Despite the evolution of electronic switches from Bardeen’s transistor to the tiny chip transistors that are currently used in modern computers, Moore’s Law has held true for the past 50 years. However, the turn of the millennium saw processor design hit several critical performance walls: 内存墙 （memory wall）：内存技术的进步跟不上时钟速度的提升，使内存成为性能的瓶颈。因此，持续加快 CPU 的执行速度，已不能再提高系统的整体性能。 The memory wall : Improvements in memory technology did not keep pace with improvements in clock speed, resulting in memory becoming a bottleneck to performance. As a result, continuously speeding up the execution of a CPU no longer improves its overall system performance. 功耗墙 （power wall）：增加处理器上的晶体管数量，必然会提高处理器的温度和功耗，进而增加为系统供电和散热所需的成本。随着多核系统的普及，功耗如今已成为计算机系统设计中最主要的考虑因素。 The power wall : Increasing the number of transistors on a processor necessarily increases that processor’s temperature and power consumption, which in turn increases the required cost to power and cool the system. With the proliferation of multicore systems, power is now the dominant concern in computer system design. 功耗墙和内存墙迫使计算机体系结构设计者改变了设计处理器的方式。设计者不再通过增加晶体管来提高 CPU 执行单个指令流的速度，而是开始在一个 CPU 上加入多个 计算核心 （compute core）。计算核心是简化了的处理单元，它们包含的晶体管比传统 CPU 少，通常也更容易制造。在一个 CPU 上组合多个核心，使 CPU 能够同时执行 多个 独立的指令流。 The power and memory walls caused computer architects to change the way they designed processors. Instead of adding more transistors to increase the speed at which a CPU executes a single stream of instructions, architects began adding multiple compute cores to a CPU. Compute cores are simplified processing units that contain fewer transistors than traditional CPUs and are generally easier to create. Combining multiple cores on one CPU allows the CPU to execute multiple independent streams of instructions at once. 原书警示 · 核心多 != 更好（More cores != better） 人们很容易认为所有核心都是一样的，计算机的核心越多就越好。事实并非一定如此！例如， 图形处理器 （graphics processing unit，GPU）的核心比 CPU 核心包含的晶体管还要少，并且专门用于涉及向量的特定任务。一个典型的 GPU 可能有 5,000 个甚至更多的 GPU 核心。然而，GPU 核心能执行的操作类型有限，并不总是像 CPU 核心那样适合通用计算。用 GPU 进行计算称为 众核 （manycore）计算。本章集中讨论 多核 （multicore）计算。关于众核计算的讨论，见 第 15 章 。 It may be tempting to assume that all cores are equal and that the more cores a computer has, the better it is. This is not necessarily the case! For example, graphics processing unit (GPU) cores have even fewer transistors than CPU cores, and are specialized for particular tasks involving vectors. A typical GPU can have 5,000 or more GPU cores. However, GPU cores are limited in the types of operations that they can perform and are not always suitable for general-purpose computing like the CPU core. Computing with GPUs is known as manycore computing. In this chapter, we concentrate on multicore computing. See Chapter 15 for a discussion of manycore computing. 仔细看看：有多少个核心？ Taking a Closer Look: How Many Cores? 几乎所有现代计算机系统都有多个核心，包括 树莓派 这样的小型设备。确定系统上的核心数，对于准确测量多核程序的性能至关重要。在 Linux 和 macOS 计算机上， lscpu 命令可以给出系统体系结构的概要。在下面的例子中，我们展示了在一台示例机器上运行 lscpu 命令的输出（省略了部分输出，以突出关键特征）： Almost all modern computer systems have multiple cores, including small devices like the Raspberry Pi . Identifying the number of cores on a system is critical for accurately measuring the performance of multicore programs. On Linux and macOS computers, the lscpu command provides a summary of a system’s architecture. In the following example, we show the output of the lscpu command when run on a sample machine (some output is omitted to emphasize the key features): 译注 · macOS 上没有 lscpu 原文说 macOS 上也有 lscpu ，但译者的 Mac 上并没有这个命令（ which lscpu 找不到）。在 macOS 上可以用 sysctl 查询：在 Apple M1 Pro 上， sysctl hw.physicalcpu hw.logicalcpu 都是 8（没有超线程）， hw.perflevel0.physicalcpu 为 6、 hw.perflevel1.physicalcpu 为 2，即 6 个性能核加 2 个能效核，正是下文「性能核与能效核」旁注所说的异构设计。 $ lscpu Architecture: x86_64 CPU op-mode(s): 32-bit, 64-bit Byte Order: Little Endian CPU(s): 8 On-line CPU(s) list: 0-7 Thread(s) per core: 2 Core(s) per socket: 4 Socket(s): 1 Model name: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-3770 CPU @ 3.40GHz CPU MHz: 1607.562 CPU max MHz: 3900.0000 CPU min MHz: 1600.0000 L1d cache: 32K L1i cache: 32K L2 cache: 256K L3 cache: 8192K ... lscpu 命令给出了许多有用的信息，包括处理器的类型、核心速度和核心数。要计算系统上 物理 （实际）核心的数目，就把插槽（socket）数乘以每个插槽的核心数。上面的 lscpu 示例输出表明，该系统有一个插槽，每个插槽四个核心，即总共四个物理核心。 The lscpu command gives a lot of useful information, including the type of processors, the core speed, and the number of cores. To calculate the number of physical (or actual) cores on a system, multiply the number of sockets by the number of cores per socket. The sample lscpu output shown above shows that the system has one socket with four cores per socket, or four physical cores in total. 原书旁注 · 超线程（Hyperthreading） 乍一看，上例中的系统似乎总共有八个核心。毕竟，「CPU(s)」字段似乎就是这个意思。然而，这个字段实际表示的是 超线程 （hyperthreaded，即逻辑）核心的数目，而不是物理核心的数目。超线程，即同时多线程（simultaneous multithreading，SMT），能够在单个核心上高效地处理多个线程。尽管超线程可以缩短程序的整体运行时间，但在超线程核心上，性能的扩展速度不如在物理核心上。不过，如果一个任务空闲下来（例如由于 控制冒险 ），另一个任务仍然可以利用这个核心。简而言之，引入超线程是为了提高 进程吞吐量 （衡量单位时间内完成的进程数），而不是 进程加速比 （衡量单个进程运行时间的改善程度）。在接下来的一章中，我们对性能的讨论将主要关注加速比。 At first glance, it may appear that the system in the previous example has eight cores in total. After all, this is what the “CPU(s)” field seems to imply. However, that field actually indicates the number of hyperthreaded (logical) cores, not the number of physical cores. Hyperthreading, or simultaneous multithreading (SMT), enables the efficient processing of multiple threads on a single core. Although hyperthreading can decrease the overall runtime of a program, performance on hyperthreaded cores does not scale at the same rate as on physical cores. However, if one task idles (e.g., due to a control hazard ), another task can still utilize the core. In short, hyperthreading was introduced to improve process throughput (which measures the number of processes that complete in a given unit of time) rather than process speedup (which measures the amount of runtime improvement of an individual process). Much of our discussion of performance in the coming chapter will focus on speedup. 原书旁注 · 性能核与能效核（Performance Cores and Efficiency Cores） 在一些较新的体系结构上（例如英特尔第 12 代及更新的处理器），把插槽数乘以核心数和硬件线程数，得到的数字与「CPU(s)」字段中显示的不同（通常更小）。这是怎么回事？答案在于芯片制造商正在开发的新型异构体系结构。例如，从第 12 代处理器开始，英特尔引入了一种由「性能」核心（ P 核 ，P-core）和「能效」核心（ E 核 ，E-core）混合组成的体系结构。这种混合设计的目标，是把较小的后台任务交给较小的、省电的 E 核，让较大的、耗电的 P 核腾出来处理计算密集型任务。Arm 早先推出的 big.LITTLE 移动体系结构，其设计也出自类似的原理。在异构体系结构上， lscpu 的默认输出只显示可用的 P 核；E 核的数目通常可以用「CPU(s)」字段中显示的总核心数减去 P 核数算出。使用 --all 和 --extended 选项调用 lscpu 命令，会显示系统上 P 核和 E 核的完整对应关系，其中 E 核可以通过较低的处理器速度识别出来。 On some newer architectures (such as Intel’s 12th generation processors and newer), multiplying the number of sockets by the numbers of cores and hardware threads yields a different (usually smaller) number than what is shown in the “CPU(s)” field. What’s going on here? The answer lies in the new heterogeneous architectures being developed by chip makers. For example, starting with its 12th generation processors, Intel has introduced an architecture that consists of a mixture of “Performance” cores ( P-cores ) and “Efficiency” cores ( E-cores ). The goal of this hybrid design is to delegate smaller background tasks to the smaller power-sipping E-cores, freeing the larger power-hungry P-cores for compute-intensive tasks. A similar principle drives the design of the earlier big.LITTLE mobile architecture introduced by Arm. On heterogeneous architectures, the default output of lscpu only displays the available P-cores; the number of E-cores can typically be computed by subtracting the number of P-cores from the total cores shown in the “CPU(s)” field. Invoking the lscpu command with its --all and --extended flags will display a full mapping of the P-cores and E-cores on a system, with the E-core identifiable by their lower processor speeds.

x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C14-SharedMemory/multicore.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 14.1. Programming Multicore Systems 如今程序员熟悉的大多数常用语言都诞生于多核时代之前。因此，许多语言无法 隐式地 （即自动地）利用多核处理器来加快程序的执行。程序员必须专门编写软件，来利用系统上的多个核心。 Most of the common languages that programmers know today were created prior to the multicore age. As a result, many languages cannot implicitly (or automatically) employ multicore processors to speed up the execution of a program. Instead, programmers must specifically write software to leverage the multiple cores on a system. 14.1.1. 多核系统对进程执行的影响 14.1.1. The Impact of Multicore Systems on Process Execution 回想一下， 进程 可以看作正在运行的程序的抽象。每个进程都在自己的虚拟地址空间中执行。操作系统（OS）调度进程在 CPU 上执行；当 CPU 改变它当前执行的进程时，就发生了 上下文切换 （context switch）。 Recall that a process can be thought of as an abstraction of a running program. Each process executes in its own virtual address space. The operating system (OS) schedules processes for execution on the CPU; a context switch occurs when the CPU changes which process it currently executes. 图 1 展示了五个示例进程可能如何在单核 CPU 上执行。 Figure 1 illustrates how five example processes may execute on a single-core CPU. 图 1. 五个进程共享单个 CPU 核心时的执行时间序列 Figure 1. An execution time sequence for five processes as they share a single CPU core 横轴是时间，每个时间片占一个时间单位。方框表示某个进程正在使用这个单核 CPU。假设每个进程执行完整的一个时间片之后才发生上下文切换。所以，进程 1 在时间步 T1 和 T3 使用 CPU。 The horizontal axis is time, with each time slice taking one unit of time. A box indicates when a process is using the single-core CPU. Assume that each process executes for one full time slice before a context switch occurs. So, Process 1 uses the CPU during time steps T1 and T3. 在这个例子中，进程的执行顺序是 P1、P2、P1、P2、P4、P2、P3、P4、P5、P3、P5。这里我们花点时间区分两种时间度量。 CPU 时间 度量一个进程在 CPU 上执行所用的时间。与之不同， 挂钟时间 （wall-clock time）度量的是人所感知到的进程完成所用的时间。由于上下文切换，挂钟时间常常比 CPU 时间长得多。例如，进程 1 的 CPU 时间是两个时间单位，而它的挂钟时间是三个时间单位。 In this example, the order of process execution is P1, P2, P1, P2, P4, P2, P3, P4, P5, P3, P5. We take a moment here to distinguish between two measures of time. The CPU time measures the amount of time a process takes to execute on a CPU. In contrast, the wall-clock time measures the amount of time a human perceives a process takes to complete. The wall-clock time is often significantly longer than the CPU time, due to context switches. For example, Process 1’s CPU time requires two time units, whereas its wall-clock time is three time units. 当一个进程的总执行时间与另一个进程的相重叠时，这两个进程就是 并发 （concurrently）运行的。在单核时代，操作系统利用并发营造出计算机能同时做许多事情的错觉（例如，你可以同时打开计算器程序、Web 浏览器和文字处理文档）。实际上，每个进程都是串行执行的，由操作系统决定 进程执行和完成的顺序 （而且这个顺序在后续运行中常常不同）。 When the total execution time of one process overlaps with another, the processes are running concurrently with each other. Operating systems employed concurrency in the single-core era to give the illusion that a computer can execute many things at once (e.g., you can have a calculator program, a web browser, and a word processing document all open at the same time). In truth, each process executes serially and the operating system determines the order in which processes execute and complete (which often differs in subsequent runs). 回到这个例子，可以看到进程 1 和进程 2 是彼此并发运行的，因为它们的执行在时间点 T2–T4 上有重叠。同样，进程 2 与进程 4 并发运行，因为它们的执行在时间点 T4–T6 上有重叠。与之不同，进程 2 与进程 3 不是 并发运行的，因为它们的执行没有任何重叠；进程 3 从时间 T7 才开始运行，而进程 2 在时间 T6 就完成了。 Returning to the example, observe that Process 1 and Process 2 run concurrently with each other, since their executions overlap at time points T2-T4. Likewise, Process 2 runs concurrently with Process 4, as their executions overlap at time points T4-T6. In contrast, Process 2 does not run concurrently with Process 3, because they share no overlap in their execution; Process 3 only starts running at time T7, whereas Process 2 completes at time T6. 多核 CPU 让操作系统能够把不同的进程调度到各个可用的核心上，使进程能够 同时 执行。来自运行在多个核心上的进程的指令同时执行，称为 并行执行 （parallel execution）。 图 2 展示了我们的示例进程可能如何在双核系统上执行。 A multicore CPU enables the OS to schedule a different process to each available core, allowing processes to execute simultaneously . The simultaneous execution of instructions from processes running on multiple cores is referred to as parallel execution . Figure 2 shows how our example processes might execute on a dual-core system. 图 2. 五个进程的执行时间序列，扩展为包含两个 CPU 核心（一个为深蓝色，另一个为浅绿色）。 Figure 2. An execution time sequence for five processes, extended to include two CPU cores (one in dark blue, the other in light green). 在这个例子中，两个 CPU 核心用不同的颜色表示。假设进程的执行顺序仍然是 P1、P2、P1、P2、P4、P2、P3、P4、P5、P3、P5。多个核心的存在让某些进程能够 更早 执行。例如，在时间单位 T1 内，第一个核心执行进程 1，同时第二个核心执行进程 2。在时间 T2，第一个核心执行进程 2，第二个核心执行进程 1。因此，进程 1 在时间 T2 之后就执行完了，而进程 2 在时间 T3 执行完。 In this example, the two CPU cores are colored differently. Suppose that the process execution order is again P1, P2, P1, P2, P4, P2, P3, P4, P5, P3, P5. The presence of multiple cores enables certain processes to execute sooner . For example, during time unit T1, the first core executes Process 1 while the second core executes Process 2. At time T2, the first core executes Process 2 while the second executes Process 1. Thus, Process 1 finishes executing after time T2, whereas Process 2 finishes executing at time T3. 注意，多个进程的并行执行只是增加了任一时刻正在执行的进程数。在 图 2 中，所有进程在时间单位 T7 之前都执行完了。然而，每个单独的进程完成所需的 CPU 时间仍然与 图 1 中所示的相同。例如，无论在单核还是多核系统上执行，进程 2 都需要三个时间单位（即它的 CPU 时间 保持不变）。多核处理器提高的是进程执行的 吞吐量 （throughput），即在给定时间段内能够完成的进程数。因此，尽管单个进程的 CPU 时间保持不变，它的挂钟时间却可能减少。 Note that the parallel execution of multiple processes increases just the number of processes that execute at any one time. In Figure 2 , all the processes complete execution by time unit T7. However, each individual process still requires the same amount of CPU time to complete as shown in Figure 1 . For example, Process 2 requires three time units regardless of execution on a single or multicore system (i.e., its CPU time remains the same). A multicore processor increases the throughput of process execution, or the number of processes that can complete in a given period of time. Thus, while the CPU time of an individual process remains unchanged, its wall-clock time may decrease. 14.1.2. 用线程加快进程执行 14.1.2. Expediting Process Execution with Threads 加快单个进程执行的一种方式，是把它分解成称为 线程 （thread）的轻量级的独立执行流。 图 3 展示了一个进程被多线程化为两个线程时，其虚拟地址空间如何变化。每个线程都有自己私有的调用栈内存，而所有线程 共享 分配给这个多线程进程的程序数据、指令和堆。 One way to speed up the execution of a single process is to decompose it into lightweight, independent execution flows called threads . Figure 3 shows how a process’s virtual address space changes when it is multithreaded with two threads. While each thread has its own private allocation of call stack memory, all threads share the program data, instructions, and the heap allocated to the multithreaded process. 图 3. 比较单线程进程与有两个线程的多线程进程的虚拟地址空间 Figure 3. Comparing the virtual address space of a single-threaded and a multithreaded process with two threads 操作系统调度线程的方式与调度进程的方式相同。在多核处理器上，操作系统可以把不同的线程调度到不同的核心上运行，从而加快多线程程序的执行。能够并行执行的线程数的最大值等于系统上物理核心的数目。如果线程数超过了物理核心数，其余的线程就必须等待轮到它们执行（类似于进程在单核上的执行方式）。 The operating system schedules threads in the same manner as it schedules processes. On a multicore processor, the OS can speed up the execution of a multithreaded program by scheduling the different threads to run on separate cores. The maximum number of threads that can execute in parallel is equal to the number of physical cores on the system. If the number of threads exceeds the number of physical cores, the remaining threads must wait their turn to execute (similar to how processes execute on a single core). 一个例子：标量乘法 An Example: Scalar Multiplication 作为如何用多线程加速应用程序的第一个例子，考虑对数组 array 和某个整数 s 执行标量乘法的问题。在标量乘法中，数组中的每个元素都通过与 s 相乘而被缩放。 As an initial example of how to use multithreading to speed up an application, consider the problem of performing scalar multiplication of an array array and some integer s . In scalar multiplication, each element in the array is scaled by multiplying the element with s . 下面是标量乘法函数的一个串行实现： A serial implementation of a scalar multiplication function follows: void scalar_multiply(int * array, long length, int s) { int i; for (i = 0; i < length; i++) { array[i] = array[i] * s; } } 假设 array 总共有 N 个元素。要用 t 个线程创建这个应用程序的多线程版本，需要： Suppose that array has N total elements. To create a multithreaded version of this application with t threads, it is necessary to: 创建 t 个线程。 Create t threads. 给每个线程分配输入数组的一个子集（即 N / t 个元素）。 Assign each thread a subset of the input array (i.e., N / t elements). 让每个线程把它所分到的数组子集中的元素乘以 s 。 Instruct each thread to multiply the elements in its array subset by s . 假设 scalar_multiply 的串行实现乘一个有 1 亿个元素的输入数组需要 60 秒。为了构建一个用 t = 4 个线程执行的版本，我们给每个线程分配整个输入数组的四分之一（2500 万个元素）。 Suppose that the serial implementation of scalar_multiply spends 60 seconds multiplying an input array of 100 million elements. To build a version that executes with t = 4 threads, we assign each thread one fourth of the total input array (25 million elements). 图 4 展示了在单个核心上运行四个线程时会发生什么。和之前一样，执行顺序由操作系统决定。在这个场景中，假设线程的执行顺序是线程 1、线程 3、线程 2、线程 4。在单核处理器上（用方框表示），每个线程依次执行。因此，在一个核心上运行的这个多线程进程仍然需要 60 秒（考虑到创建线程的开销，也许还要稍长一点）。 Figure 4 shows what happens when we run four threads on a single core. As before, the execution order is left to the operating system. In this scenario, assume that the thread execution order is Thread 1, Thread 3, Thread 2, Thread 4. On a single-core processor (represented by the squares), each thread executes sequentially. Thus, the multithreaded process running on one core will still take 60 seconds to run (perhaps a little longer, given the overhead of creating threads). 图 4. 在单核 CPU 上运行四个线程 Figure 4. Running four threads on a single-core CPU 现在假设我们在双核系统上运行这个多线程进程。 图 5 展示了结果。同样假设 t = 4 个线程，线程的执行顺序是线程 1、线程 3、线程 2、线程 4。两个核心用带阴影的方框表示。由于系统是双核的，线程 1 和线程 3 在时间步 T1 并行执行。然后线程 2 和线程 4 在时间步 T2 并行执行。因此，原本需要 60 秒运行的多线程进程，现在只需 30 秒。 Now suppose that we run our multithreaded process on a dual-core system. Figure 5 shows the result. Again, assume t = 4 threads, and that the thread execution order is Thread 1, Thread 3, Thread 2, Thread 4. Our two cores are represented by shaded squares. Since the system is dual-core, Thread 1 and Thread 3 execute in parallel during time step T1. Threads 2 and 4 then execute in parallel during time step T2. Thus, the multithreaded process that originally took 60 seconds to run now runs in 30 seconds. 图 5. 在双核 CPU 上运行四个线程 Figure 5. Running four threads on a dual-core CPU 最后，假设这个多线程进程（ t = 4）在四核 CPU 上运行。 图 6 展示了这样的一个执行序列。 图 6 中的四个核心各用不同的阴影表示。在四核系统上，每个线程都在时间片 T1 内并行执行。因此，在四核 CPU 上，原本需要 60 秒的多线程进程现在只需 15 秒。 Finally, suppose that the multithreaded process ( t = 4) is run on a quad-core CPU. Figure 6 shows one such execution sequence. Each of the four cores in Figure 6 is shaded differently. On the quad-core system, each thread executes in parallel during time slice T1. Thus, on a quad-core CPU, the multithreaded process that originally took 60 seconds now runs in 15 seconds. 图 6. 在四核 CPU 上运行四个线程 Figure 6. Running four threads on a quad-core CPU 一般来说，如果线程数与核心数（ c ）相同，并且操作系统把每个线程调度到不同的核心上并行运行，那么多线程进程的运行时间应该大约是原来的 1/ c 。这样的线性加速比是理想情况，在实践中并不常见。例如，如果有许多其他进程（或多线程进程）在等待使用 CPU，它们会争夺数量有限的核心，导致进程之间的 资源争用 （resource contention）。如果指定的线程数超过了 CPU 核心数，每个线程都必须等待轮到它运行。我们会在 本章后面 探讨其他经常妨碍线性加速的因素。 In general, if the number of threads matches the number of cores ( c ) and the operating system schedules each thread to run on a separate core in parallel, then the multithreaded process should run in approximately 1/ c of the time. Such linear speedup is ideal, but not frequently observed in practice. For example, if there are many other processes (or multithreaded processes) waiting to use the CPU, they will all compete for the limited number of cores, resulting in resource contention among the processes. If the number of specified threads exceeds the number of CPU cores, each thread must wait its turn to run. We explore other factors that often prevent linear speedup later in this chapter .

说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C14-SharedMemory/posix.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 14.2. Hello Threading! Writing Your First Multithreaded Program 在本节中，我们考察无处不在的 POSIX 线程库 Pthreads 。POSIX 是 Portable Operating System Interface（可移植操作系统接口）的缩写。它是一项 IEEE 标准，规定了 UNIX 系统的外观、行为和使用感受。POSIX 线程 API 在几乎所有类 UNIX 操作系统上都可以使用，这些系统要么完全符合该标准，要么在很大程度上符合。所以，如果你在一台 Linux 机器上用 POSIX 线程编写并行代码，它肯定能在其他 Linux 机器上运行，并且很可能也能在运行 macOS 或其他 UNIX 变体的机器上运行。 In this section, we examine the ubiquitous POSIX thread library Pthreads . POSIX is an acronym for Portable Operating System Interface. It is an IEEE standard that specifies how UNIX systems look, act, and feel. The POSIX threads API is available on almost all UNIX-like operating systems, each of which meets the standard in its entirety or to some great degree. So, if you write parallel code using POSIX threads on a Linux machine, it will certainly work on other Linux machines, and it will likely work on machines running macOS or other UNIX variants. 我们先来分析一个「Hello World」Pthreads 示例程序（ hellothreads.c ）。为简洁起见，清单中省略了错误处理，不过 可下载的版本 中包含错误处理的示例。 Let’s begin by analyzing an example “Hello World” Pthreads program ( hellothreads.c ). For brevity, we have excluded error handling in the listing, though the downloadable version contains sample error handling. #include <stdio.h> #include <stdlib.h> #include <pthread.h> /* The "thread function" passed to pthread_create. Each thread executes this * function and terminates when it returns from this function. */ void *HelloWorld(void *id) { /* We know the argument is a pointer to a long, so we cast it from a * generic (void *) to a (long *). */ long *myid = (long *) id; printf("Hello world! I am thread %ld
", *myid); return NULL; // We don't need our threads to return anything. } int main(int argc, char **argv) { int i; int nthreads; //number of threads pthread_t *thread_array; //pointer to future thread array long *thread_ids; // Read the number of threads to create from the command line. if (argc !=2) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s <n>
", argv[0]); fprintf(stderr, "where <n> is the number of threads
"); return 1; } nthreads = strtol(argv[1], NULL, 10); // Allocate space for thread structs and identifiers. thread_array = malloc(nthreads * sizeof(pthread_t)); thread_ids = malloc(nthreads * sizeof(long)); // Assign each thread an ID and create all the threads. for (i = 0; i < nthreads; i++) { thread_ids[i] = i; pthread_create(&thread_array[i], NULL, HelloWorld, &thread_ids[i]); } /* Join all the threads. Main will pause in this loop until all threads * have returned from the thread function. */ for (i = 0; i < nthreads; i++) { pthread_join(thread_array[i], NULL); } free(thread_array); free(thread_ids); return 0; } 我们把这个程序拆成小块来考察。 Let’s examine this program in smaller components. 注意其中包含了 pthread.h 头文件，它声明了 pthread 的类型和函数。 Notice the inclusion of the pthread.h header file, which declares pthread types and functions. 接下来， HelloWorld 函数定义了 线程函数 （thread function），我们稍后会把它传给 pthread_create 。线程函数相当于工作线程（被创建的线程）的 main 函数：线程从线程函数的开头开始执行，到达线程函数的末尾时终止。每个线程都使用自己私有的执行状态（即它自己的栈内存和寄存器值）来执行线程函数。还要注意，线程函数的类型是 void* 。在这里使用 匿名指针 ，让程序员能编写处理不同类型参数和返回值的线程函数。 Next, the HelloWorld function defines the thread function that we later pass to pthread_create . A thread function is analogous to a main function for a worker (created) thread — a thread begins execution at the start of its thread function and terminates when it reaches the end. Each thread executes the thread function using its private execution state (i.e., its own stack memory and register values). Note also that the thread function is of type void* . Specifying an anonymous pointer in this context allows programmers to write thread functions that deal with arguments and return values of different types. 最后，在 main 函数中，主线程先初始化程序状态，然后创建并合并（join）工作线程。 Lastly, in the main function, the main thread initializes the program state before creating and joining the worker threads. 14.2.1. 创建与合并线程 14.2.1. Creating and Joining Threads 程序一开始是一个单线程进程。执行 main 函数时，它读取要创建的线程数，并为两个数组分配内存： thread_array 和 thread_ids 。 thread_array 数组存放所创建的每个线程的地址集合。 thread_ids 数组存放传给每个线程的参数集合。在这个例子中，传给每个线程的是它的序号（rank，即 ID，用 thread_ids[i] 表示）的地址。 The program first starts as a single-threaded process. As it executes the main function, it reads the number of threads to create, and it allocates memory for two arrays: thread_array and thread_ids . The thread_array array contains the set of addresses for each thread created. The thread_ids array stores the set of arguments that each thread is passed. Mutual Exclusion 互斥锁是什么？答案就在那里，它在寻找你，只要你愿意，它就会找到你。 What is the mutex? The answer is out there, and it’s looking for you, and it will find you if you want it to. ——崔妮蒂向尼奥解释互斥锁（向《 黑客帝国 》致歉） ~Trinity, explaining mutexes to Neo (Apologies to The Matrix ) 为了修正数据竞争，我们来使用一种称为互斥锁（mutual exclusion lock，简称 mutex ）的同步结构。互斥锁是一种同步原语，它确保在任一时刻只有一个线程能进入并执行临界区中的代码。 To fix the data race, let’s use a synchronization construct known as a mutual exclusion lock, or mutex . Mutual exclusion locks are a type of synchronization primitive that ensures that only one thread enters and executes the code inside the critical section at any given time. 在使用互斥锁之前，程序必须先： Before using a mutex, a program must first: 在线程共享的内存中声明互斥锁（通常作为全局变量）。 Declare the mutex in memory that’s shared by threads (often as a global variable). 在线程需要使用互斥锁之前初始化它（通常在 main 函数中）。 Initialize the mutex before the threads need to use it (typically in the main function). Pthreads 库为互斥锁定义了 pthread_mutex_t 类型。要声明一个互斥锁变量，添加这一行： The Pthreads library defines a pthread_mutex_t type for mutexes. To declare a mutex variable, add this line: pthread_mutex_t mutex; 要初始化互斥锁，使用 pthread_mutex_init 函数，它接收一个互斥锁的地址和一个属性结构（通常设为 NULL ）： To initialize the mutex use the pthread_mutex_init function, which takes the address of a mutex and an attribute structure, typically set to NULL : pthread_mutex_init(&mutex, NULL); 当不再需要互斥锁时（通常在 main 函数末尾、 pthread_join 之后），程序应当调用 pthread_mutex_destroy 函数来释放互斥锁结构： When the mutex is no longer needed (typically at the end of the main function, after pthread_join ), a program should release the mutex structure by invoking the pthread_mutex_destroy function: pthread_mutex_destroy(&mutex); 互斥锁：上膛 The Mutex: Locked and Loaded 互斥锁的初始状态是未加锁的，即任何线程都可以立即使用它。要进入临界区，线程必须先获得锁。这是通过调用 pthread_mutex_lock 函数来完成的。一个线程持有锁之后，在持锁线程释放锁之前，其他任何线程都不能进入临界区。如果另一个线程调用 pthread_mutex_lock 时互斥锁已经被锁住，该线程就会 阻塞 （block，即等待），直到互斥锁变为可用。回想一下， 阻塞 意味着该线程不会被调度 使用 CPU，直到它所等待的条件（互斥锁可用）成立为止。 The initial state of a mutex is unlocked, meaning it’s immediately usable by any thread. To enter a critical section, a thread must first acquire a lock. This is accomplished with a call to the pthread_mutex_lock function. After a thread has the lock, no other thread can enter the critical section until the thread with the lock releases it. Semaphores 信号量（semaphore）常用于操作系统和并发程序中，目的是管理对一个资源池的并发访问。使用信号量时，关注的不是 谁 拥有什么，而是还有 多少 资源可用。信号量与互斥锁在几个方面有所不同： Semaphores are commonly used in operating systems and concurrent programs where the goal is to manage concurrent access to a pool of resources. When using a semaphore, the goal isn’t who owns what, but how many resources are still available. Semaphores are different from mutexes in several ways: 信号量不一定只有二元（加锁或未加锁）的状态。一种称为 计数信号量 （counting semaphore）的特殊信号量，其值的范围可以从 0 到某个 r ，其中 r 是可能的资源数。每当生产出一个资源，信号量就加一。每当一个资源被使用，信号量就减一。当计数信号量的值为 0 时，表示没有可用的资源，任何其他试图获取资源的线程都必须等待（即阻塞）。 Semaphores need not be in a binary (locked or unlocked) state. A special type of semaphore called a counting semaphore can range in value from 0 to some r , where r is the number of possible resources. Any time a resource is produced, the semaphore is incremented. Any time a resource is being used, the semaphore is decremented. When a counting semaphore has a value of 0, it means that no resources are available, and any other threads that attempt to acquire a resource must wait (e.g., block). 信号量可以默认处于加锁状态。 Semaphores can be locked by default. 尽管互斥锁和条件变量可以模拟信号量的功能，但在某些情况下，使用信号量可能更简单、更高效。信号量还有一个优点： 任何 线程都可以给信号量解锁（与之相对，互斥锁必须由加锁的线程来解锁）。 While a mutex and condition variables can simulate the functionality of a semaphore, using a semaphore may be simpler and more efficient in some cases. Semaphores also have the advantage that any thread can unlock the semaphore (in contrast to a mutex, where the calling thread must unlock it). 信号量不属于 Pthreads 库，但这并不意味着你不能使用它们。在 Linux 和 macOS 系统上，可以通过 semaphore.h 使用信号量原语，这个头文件通常位于 /usr/include 中。由于没有统一的标准，不同系统上的函数调用可能有所不同。尽管如此，信号量库的声明与互斥锁的类似： Semaphores are not part of the Pthreads library, but that does not mean that you cannot use them. On Linux and macOS systems, semaphore primitives can be accessed from semaphore.h , typically located in /usr/include . Since there is no standard, the function calls may differ on different systems. That said, the semaphore library has similar declarations to those of mutexes: 译注 说「没有标准」并不准确：按 sem_init(3) 手册， sem_init 等函数属于 POSIX 标准（POSIX.1-2001 起，现为 POSIX.1-2008），在 Linux 上由 POSIX 线程库提供。各系统的差异主要在于实现的完整程度，见下面关于 macOS 的译注。 声明一个信号量（类型为 sem_t ，例如 sem_t semaphore ）。 Declare a semaphore (type sem_t , e.g., sem_t semaphore ). 用 sem_init 初始化信号量（通常在 main 中）。 sem_init 函数有三个参数：第一个是信号量的地址，第二个是它的初始状态（加锁或未加锁），第三个参数表示信号量是在一个进程的各线程之间共享（例如取值 0），还是在进程之间共享（例如取值 1）。这很有用，因为信号量常用于进程同步。例如，用调用 sem_init(&semaphore, 1, 0) 初始化信号量，表示我们的信号量初始时是加锁的（第二个参数为 1），并且要在同一个进程的各线程之间共享（第三个参数为 0）。与之不同，互斥锁总是以未加锁状态开始。需要注意的是，在 macOS 中，等价的函数是 sem_open 。 Initialize a semaphore using sem_init (usually in main ). The sem_init function has three parameters: the first is the address of a semaphore, the second is its initial state (locked or unlocked), and the third parameter indicates whether the semaphore should be shared with the threads of a process (e.g., with value 0) or between processes (e.g., with value 1). This is useful because semaphores are commonly used for process synchronization. For example, initializing a semaphore with the call sem_init(&semaphore, 1, 0) indicates that our semaphore is initially locked (the second parameter is 1), and is to be shared among the threads of a common process (the third parameter is 0). In contrast, mutexes always start out unlocked. It is important to note that in macOS, the equivalent function is sem_open . 译注 · 参数顺序写反了 按 sem_init(3) 手册，原型是 int sem_init(sem_t *sem, int pshared, unsigned int value); ： 第二个 参数 pshared 决定共享范围（0 表示在一个进程的各线程间共享，非 0 表示在进程间共享）， 第三个 参数 value 是信号量的初始值（0 即「加锁」，没有可用资源）。所以 sem_init(&semaphore, 1, 0) 实际表示「初始值为 0、在进程间共享」；本章这类多线程用法应写成 sem_init(&semaphore, 0, 0) 。 另外，在 macOS 上 sem_init 并不能用：译者在 Mac 上编译调用 sem_init(&s, 0, 1) 的程序，Clang 给出「’sem_init’ is deprecated」警告，运行时它返回 -1， errno 为「Function not implemented」。因此在 Mac 上要么改用有名信号量 sem_open ，要么在 Linux 中运行本节的例子。 用 sem_destroy 销毁信号量（通常在 main 中）。这个函数只接收一个指向信号量的指针（ sem_destroy(&semaphore) ）。注意，在 macOS 中，等价的函数可能是 sem_unlink 或 sem_close 。 Destroy a semaphore using sem_destroy (usually in main ). This function only takes a pointer to the semaphore ( sem_destroy(&semaphore) ). Note that in macOS, the equivalent function may be sem_unlink or sem_close . sem_wait 函数表示一个资源正在被使用，并把信号量减一。如果信号量的值大于 0（表示仍有可用的资源），函数会立即返回，线程可以继续执行。如果信号量的值已经是 0，线程就会阻塞，直到有资源可用（即信号量的值为正）。对 sem_wait 的调用通常写作 sem_wait(&semaphore) 。 The sem_wait function indicates that a resource is being used, and decrements the semaphore. If the semaphore’s value is greater than 0 (indicating there are still resources available), the function will immediately return, and the thread is allowed to proceed. If the semaphore’s value is already 0, the thread will block until a resource becomes available (i.e., the semaphore has a positive value). A call to sem_wait typically looks like sem_wait(&semaphore) . sem_post 函数表示一个资源正在被释放，并把信号量加一。这个函数会立即返回。如果有线程在等待这个信号量（即信号量之前的值为 0），那么那个线程将取得被释放资源的所有权。对 sem_post 的调用写作 sem_post(&semaphore) 。 The sem_post function indicates that a resource is being freed, and increments the semaphore. This function returns immediately. If there is a thread waiting on the semaphore (i.e., the semaphore’s value was previously 0), then the other thread will take ownership of the freed resource. A call to sem_post looks like sem_post(&semaphore) .

Other Synchronization Constructs 互斥锁和信号量并不是多线程程序中仅有的同步结构。在本小节中，我们简要讨论屏障和条件变量这两种同步结构，它们都是 Pthreads 库的一部分。 Mutexes and semaphores are not the only example of synchronization constructs that can be used in the context of multithreaded programs. In this subsection we will briefly discuss the barrier and condition variable synchronization constructs, which are both part of the Pthreads library. 屏障 Barriers 屏障 （barrier）是一种同步结构，它强制 所有 线程到达执行中的一个公共点，然后再放行这些线程继续并发执行。Pthreads 提供了屏障同步原语。要使用 Pthreads 屏障，需要做以下几件事： A barrier is a type of synchronization construct that forces all threads to reach a common point in execution before releasing the threads to continue executing concurrently. Pthreads offers a barrier synchronization primitive. To use Pthreads barriers, it is necessary to do the following: 声明一个屏障全局变量（例如 pthread_barrier_t barrier ） Declare a barrier global variable (e.g., pthread_barrier_t barrier ) 在 main 中初始化屏障（ pthread_barrier_init(&barrier) ） Initialize the barrier in main ( pthread_barrier_init(&barrier) ) 译注 pthread_barrier_init 实际上有三个参数：屏障的地址、属性（通常为 NULL ）以及必须到达屏障的线程数，例如 pthread_barrier_init(&barrier, NULL, nthreads) 。另外，macOS 没有实现 POSIX 屏障：译者在 Mac 上编译使用 pthread_barrier_t 的代码，Clang 报错「unknown type name ‘pthread_barrier_t’」。在 Mac 上可以用本节后面介绍的「条件变量 + 广播」自己实现屏障，或者在 Linux 中运行这个例子。 使用后在 main 中销毁屏障（ pthread_barrier_destroy(&barrier) ） Destroy the barrier in main after use ( pthread_barrier_destroy(&barrier) ) 用 pthread_barrier_wait 函数创建一个同步点。 Use the pthread_barrier_wait function to create a synchronization point. 下面的程序展示了在一个名为 threadEx 的函数中使用屏障： The following program shows the use of a barrier in a function called threadEx : void *threadEx(void *args){ //parse args //... long myid = myargs->id; int nthreads = myargs->numthreads; int *array = myargs->array printf("Thread %ld starting thread work!
", myid); pthread_barrier_wait(&barrier); //forced synchronization point printf("All threads have reached the barrier!
"); for (i = start; i < end; i++) { array[i] = array[i] * 2; } printf("Thread %ld done with work!
", myid); return NULL; } 在这个例子中，在 每个 线程都打印出它们开始工作的消息之前，没有哪个线程能开始处理分配给它的那部分数组。如果没有屏障，就可能出现一个线程在其他线程打印出开始工作的消息之前就已经完成了工作！注意， 仍然 可能出现一个线程在另一个线程完成之前就打印出它已完成工作的情况。 In this example, no thread can start processing its assigned portion of the array until every thread has printed out the message that they are starting work. Without the barrier, it is possible for one thread to have finished work before the other threads have printed their starting work message! Notice that it is still possible for one thread to print that it is done doing work before another thread finishes. 条件变量 Condition Variables 条件变量（condition variable）强制线程阻塞，直到达到某个特定的条件。在线程做某些工作之前必须满足某个条件的场景中，这种结构很有用。如果没有条件变量，线程就不得不反复检查条件是否满足，持续占用 CPU。条件变量总是与互斥锁一起使用。在这种同步结构中，互斥锁实施互斥，而条件变量确保在线程获得互斥锁之前满足特定的条件。 Condition variables force a thread to block until a particular condition is reached. This construct is useful for scenarios in which a condition must be met before the thread does some work. In the absence of condition variables, a thread would have to repeatedly check to see whether the condition is met, continuously utilizing the CPU. Condition variables are always used in conjunction with a mutex. In this type of synchronization construct, the mutex enforces mutual exclusion, whereas the condition variable ensures that particular conditions are met before a thread acquires the mutex. POSIX 条件变量的类型是 pthread_cond_t 。与互斥锁和屏障结构一样，条件变量必须在使用前初始化，在使用后销毁。 POSIX condition variables have the type pthread_cond_t . Like the mutex and barrier constructs, condition variables must be initialized prior to use and destroyed after use. 要初始化条件变量，使用 pthread_cond_init 函数。要销毁条件变量，使用 pthread_cond_destroy 函数。 To initialize a condition variable, use the pthread_cond_init function. To destroy a condition variable, use the pthread_cond_destroy function. 使用条件变量时，常调用的两个函数是 pthread_cond_wait 和 pthread_cond_signal 。这两个函数除了需要条件变量的地址之外，还需要一个互斥锁的地址： The two functions commonly invoked when using condition variables are pthread_cond_wait and pthread_cond_signal . Both functions require the address of a mutex in addition to the address of the condition variable: pthread_cond_wait(&cond, &mutex) 函数接收条件变量 cond 和互斥锁 mutex 的地址作为参数。它使调用线程阻塞在条件变量 cond 上，直到另一个线程向它发出信号（即「唤醒」它）。 The pthread_cond_wait(&cond, &mutex) function takes the addresses of a condition variable cond and a mutex mutex as its arguments. It causes the calling thread to block on the condition variable cond until another thread signals it (or “wakes” it up). 译注 · wait 会暂时释放互斥锁 上一段说两个函数都需要互斥锁，其实只有 pthread_cond_wait 需要； pthread_cond_signal(&cond) 只接收条件变量（下一条也是这么写的）。调用 pthread_cond_wait 时，调用线程必须已经持有 mutex ；按 POSIX 手册，该函数会 原子地释放 mutex 并让调用线程阻塞在 cond 上，被唤醒、成功返回时， mutex 又会被调用线程重新持有。正因为等待期间锁被释放了，其他线程（例如下面例子中的「母鸡」）才能获得锁去修改共享变量。 pthread_cond_wait(3p) pthread_cond_signal(&cond) 函数使调用线程解除另一个等待在条件变量 cond 上的线程的阻塞（即向它发出信号）（依据调度优先级）。如果当前没有线程阻塞在该条件上，这个函数就没有任何作用。与 pthread_cond_wait 不同，无论调用 pthread_cond_signal 的线程是否持有调用 pthread_cond_wait 时使用的那个互斥锁，都可以调用这个函数。 The pthread_cond_signal(&cond) function causes the calling thread to unblock (or signal) another thread that is waiting on the condition variable cond (based on scheduling priority). If no threads are currently blocked on the condition, then the function has no effect. Unlike pthread_cond_wait , the pthread_cond_signal function can be called by a thread regardless of whether or not it owns the mutex in which pthread_cond_wait is called. 条件变量示例 Condition Variable Example 传统上，当一部分线程在等待另一组线程完成某个动作时，条件变量最为有用。在下面的例子中，我们用多个线程模拟一群农夫从一群母鸡那里收集鸡蛋。「Chicken」（母鸡）和「Farmer」（农夫）代表两类不同的线程。这个程序的完整源代码可以下载（ layeggs.c ）。注意，为简洁起见，清单中省略了许多注释和错误处理。 Traditionally, condition variables are most useful when a subset of threads are waiting on another set to complete some action. In the following example, we use multiple threads to simulate a set of farmers collecting eggs from a set of chickens. “Chicken” and “Farmer” represent two separate classes of threads. The full source of this program can be downloaded ( layeggs.c ). Note that the listing excludes many comments/error handling for brevity. main 函数创建了一个共享变量 num_eggs （表示任一时刻可用的鸡蛋总数）、一个共享的 mutex （每当线程访问 num_eggs 时使用）和一个共享的条件变量 eggs 。然后它创建两个母鸡线程和两个农夫线程： The main function creates a shared variable num_eggs (which indicates the total number of eggs available at any given time), a shared mutex (which is used whenever a thread accesses num_eggs ), and a shared condition variable eggs . It then creates two Chicken and two Farmer threads: int main(int argc, char **argv){ //... declarations omitted for brevity // these will be shared by all threads via pointer fields in t_args int num_eggs; // number of eggs ready to collect pthread_mutex_t mutex; // mutex associated with cond variable pthread_cond_t eggs; // used to block/wake-up farmer waiting for eggs //... args parsing removed for brevity num_eggs = 0; // number of eggs ready to collect ret = pthread_mutex_init(&mutex, NULL); //initialize the mutex pthread_cond_init(&eggs, NULL); //initialize the condition variable //... thread_array and thread_args creation/filling omitted for brevity // create some chicken and farmer threads for (i = 0; i < (2 * nthreads); i++) { if ( (i % 2) == 0 ) { ret = pthread_create(&thread_array[i], NULL, chicken, &thread_args[i]); } else { ret = pthread_create(&thread_array[i], NULL, farmer, &thread_args[i] ); } } // wait for chicken and farmer threads to exit for (i = 0; i < (2 * nthreads); i++) { ret = pthread_join(thread_array[i], NULL); } // clean-up program state pthread_mutex_destroy(&mutex); //destroy the mutex pthread_cond_destroy(&eggs); //destroy the cond var return 0; } 每个母鸡线程负责下一定数量的蛋： Each Chicken thread is responsible for laying a certain number of eggs: void *chicken(void *args ) { struct t_arg *myargs = (struct t_arg *)args; int *num_eggs, i, num; num_eggs = myargs->num_eggs; i = 0; // lay some eggs for (i = 0; i < myargs->total_eggs; i++) { usleep(EGGTIME); //chicken sleeps pthread_mutex_lock(myargs->mutex); *num_eggs = *num_eggs + 1; // update number of eggs num = *num_eggs; pthread_cond_signal(myargs->eggs); // wake a sleeping farmer (squawk) pthread_mutex_unlock(myargs->mutex); printf("chicken %d created egg %d available %d
",myargs->id,i,num); } return NULL; } 为了下一个蛋，母鸡线程先睡一会儿，然后获得互斥锁，把可用鸡蛋的总数加一。在释放互斥锁之前，母鸡线程「唤醒」一个正在睡觉的农夫（大概是靠咯咯叫）。母鸡线程重复这个循环，直到下完了它打算下的所有蛋（ total_eggs ）。 To lay an egg, a Chicken thread sleeps for a while, acquires the mutex and updates the total number of available eggs by one. Prior to releasing the mutex, the Chicken thread “wakes up” a sleeping Farmer (presumably by squawking). The Chicken thread repeats the cycle until it has laid all the eggs it intends to ( total_eggs ). 每个农夫线程负责从这群母鸡那里收集 total_eggs 个鸡蛋（大概是当早饭）： Each Farmer thread is responsible for collecting total_eggs eggs from the set of chickens (presumably for their breakfast): void *farmer(void *args ) { struct t_arg * myargs = (struct t_arg *)args; int *num_eggs, i, num; num_eggs = myargs->num_eggs; i = 0; for (i = 0; i < myargs->total_eggs; i++) { pthread_mutex_lock(myargs->mutex); while (*num_eggs == 0 ) { // no eggs to collect // wait for a chicken to lay an egg pthread_cond_wait(myargs->eggs, myargs->mutex); } // we hold mutex lock here and num_eggs > 0 num = *num_eggs; *num_eggs = *num_eggs - 1; pthread_mutex_unlock(myargs->mutex); printf("farmer %d gathered egg %d available %d
",myargs->id,i,num); } return NULL; } 每个农夫线程在检查共享变量 num_eggs 、看是否有可用的鸡蛋（ *num_eggs == 0 ）之前，都要先获得互斥锁。当没有可用的鸡蛋时，农夫线程就阻塞（即打个盹）。 Each Farmer thread acquires the mutex prior to checking the shared num_eggs variable to see whether any eggs are available ( *num_eggs == 0 ). While there aren’t any eggs available, the Farmer thread blocks (i.e., takes a nap). 农夫线程因母鸡线程发出的信号而「醒来」后，会检查是否仍有鸡蛋可用（可能另一个农夫先拿走了），如果有，农夫就「收集」一个鸡蛋（把 num_eggs 减一）并释放互斥锁。 After the Farmer thread “wakes up” due to a signal from a Chicken thread, it checks to see that an egg is still available (another Farmer could have grabbed it first) and if so, the Farmer “collects” an egg (decrementing num_eggs by one) and releases the mutex. 就这样，母鸡和农夫协同工作，下蛋/收蛋。条件变量确保在母鸡线程下蛋之前，没有哪个农夫线程会去收蛋。 In this manner, the Chicken and Farmer work in concert to lay/collect eggs. Condition variables ensure that no Farmer thread collects an egg until it is laid by a Chicken thread. 广播 Broadcasting 与条件变量一起使用的另一个函数是 pthread_cond_broadcast ，当多个线程阻塞在某个特定条件上时，它很有用。调用 pthread_cond_broadcast(&cond) 会唤醒阻塞在条件 cond 上的 所有 线程。在下一个例子中，我们展示如何用条件变量实现前面讨论过的屏障结构： Another function used with condition variables is pthread_cond_broadcast , which is useful when multiple threads are blocked on a particular condition. Calling pthread_cond_broadcast(&cond) wakes up all threads that are blocked on condition cond . In this next example, we show how condition variables can implement the barrier construct discussed previously: // mutex (initialized in main) pthread_mutex_t mutex; // condition variable signifying the barrier (initialized in main) pthread_cond_t barrier; void *threadEx_v2(void *args){ // parse args // ... long myid = myargs->id; int nthreads = myargs->numthreads; int *array = myargs->array // counter denoting the number of threads that reached the barrier int *n_reached = myargs->n_reached; // start barrier code pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex); *n_reached++; printf("Thread %ld starting work!
", myid) // if some threads have not reached the barrier while (*n_reached < nthreads) { pthread_cond_wait(&barrier, &mutex); } // all threads have reached the barrier printf("all threads have reached the barrier!
"); pthread_cond_broadcast(&barrier); pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex); // end barrier code // normal thread work for (i = start; i < end; i++) { array[i] = array[i] * 2; } printf("Thread %ld done with work!
", myid); return NULL; } 函数 threadEx_v2 的功能与 threadEx 完全相同。在这个例子中，条件变量名为 barrier 。每个线程获得锁之后，把 n_reached （已到达该点的线程数）加一。当到达屏障的线程数少于线程总数时，线程就在条件变量 barrier 和互斥锁 mutex 上等待。 The function threadEx_v2 has identical functionality to threadEx . In this example, the condition variable is named barrier . As each thread acquires the lock, it increments n_reached , the number of threads that have reached that point. While the number of threads that have reached the barrier is less than the total number of threads, the thread waits on the condition variable barrier and mutex mutex . 然而，当最后一个线程到达屏障时，它调用 pthread_cond_broadcast(&barrier) ，释放等待在条件变量 barrier 上的 所有 其他线程，使它们能够继续执行。 However, when the last thread reaches the barrier, it calls pthread_cond_broadcast(&barrier) , which releases all the other threads that are waiting on the condition variable barrier , enabling them to continue execution. 这个例子很适合用来说明 pthread_cond_broadcast 函数；不过，只要程序中需要屏障，最好还是使用 Pthreads 的屏障原语。 This example is useful for illustrating the pthread_cond_broadcast function; however, it is best to use the Pthreads barrier primitive whenever barriers are necessary in a program. 学生们常问的一个问题是： farmer 和 threadEx_v2 代码中围绕 pthread_cond_wait 调用的 while 循环，能否换成 if 语句？实际上，这个 while 循环是绝对必要的，主要有两个原因。第一，在被唤醒的线程回来继续执行之前，条件可能已经改变了。 while 循环强制最后再检测一次条件。第二， pthread_cond_wait 函数可能出现 虚假唤醒 （spurious wakeup），即线程在条件可能并未满足的情况下被错误地唤醒。这个 while 循环实际上是 谓词循环 （predicate loop）的一个例子，它强制在释放互斥锁之前对条件做最后一次检查。因此，使用条件变量时，使用谓词循环是正确的做法。 One question that students tend to ask is if the while loop around the call to pthread_cond_wait in the farmer and threadEx_v2 code can be replaced with an if statement. This while loop is in fact absolutely necessary for two main reasons. First, the condition may change prior to the woken thread arriving to continue execution. The while loop enforces that the condition be retested one last time. Second, the pthread_cond_wait function is vulnerable to spurious wakeups , in which a thread is erroneously woken up even though the condition may not be met. The while loop is in fact an example of a predicate loop , which forces a final check of the condition variable before releasing the mutex. The use of predicate loops is therefore correct practice when using condition variables.

Measuring the Performance of Parallel Programs 到目前为止，我们一直用 gettimeofday 函数来测量程序执行所用的时间。在本节中，我们讨论如何衡量一个并行程序相对于串行程序的表现，以及与测量并行程序性能相关的其他话题。 So far, we have used the gettimeofday function to measure the amount of time it takes for programs to execute. In this section, we discuss how to measure how well a parallel program performs in comparison to a serial program as well as other topics related to measuring the performance of parallel programs. 我们首先介绍与并行性能相关的一些基础知识： We first cover some basics related to parallel performance: 加速比 Speedup 效率 Efficiency 阿姆达尔定律 Amdahl’s Law 尽管阿姆达尔定律和加速比是与性能相关的两个非常重要的概念，但对下面这些话题有良好的理解，能让读者对性能的理解更加全面： While Amdahl’s Law and speedup are two very important concepts related to performance, having a good understanding of the following topics will round out a reader’s understanding of performance: 古斯塔夫森-巴西斯定律 Gustafson-Barsis Law 可扩展性 Scalability 具体来说，古斯塔夫森-巴西斯定律让我们更好地理解阿姆达尔定律的局限。 Specifically, the Gustafson-Barsis Law gives a better understanding of the limits of Amdahl’s Law.

Advanced Topics 古斯塔夫森-巴西斯定律 Gustafson-Barsis Law 1988 年，桑迪亚国家实验室的计算机科学家和研究员约翰·L·古斯塔夫森（John L. Gustafson）写了一篇题为《重新评估阿姆达尔定律》（Reevaluating Amdahl’s Law 1 ）的论文。在这篇论文中，古斯塔夫森指出了关于并行程序执行的一个关键假设，而这个假设并不总是成立。 In 1988, John L. Gustafson, a computer scientist and researcher at Sandia National Labs, wrote a paper called “Reevaluating Amdahl’s Law 1 “. In this paper, Gustafson calls to light a critical assumption that was made about the execution of a parallel program that is not always true. 具体来说，阿姆达尔定律隐含了一个前提：计算核心数 c 与程序中可并行的比例 P 彼此独立。古斯塔夫森指出，这「 几乎从来不是事实 」 1 。尽管在一组固定的数据上改变核心数来测试程序的性能是一项有用的学术练习，但在现实世界中，人们是随着问题规模变大才增加更多的核心（或者处理器，正如我们在讨论分布式内存时所考察的那样）。古斯塔夫森写道 1 ：「 假定运行时间而不是问题规模保持不变，可能是最符合实际的 。」 Specifically, Amdahl’s law implies that the number of compute cores c and the fraction of a program that is parallelizable P are independent of each other. Gustafson notes that this “ is virtually never the case .” 1 While benchmarking a program’s performance by varying the number of cores on a fixed set of data is a useful academic exercise, in the real world, more cores (or processors, as examined in our discussion of distributed memory) are added as the problem grows large. “ It may be most realistic ,” Gustafson writes 1 , “ to assume run time, not problem size, is constant .” 因此，按照古斯塔夫森的说法，最准确的说法是：「 可以并行完成的工作量随处理器数线性变化 。」 1 Thus, according to Gustafson, it is most accurate to say that “ The amount of work that can be done in parallel varies linearly with the number of processors .” 1 考虑一个 并行 程序，它在有 c 个核心的系统上运行需要 T c 的时间。设 S 表示程序执行中必然串行的那部分所占的比例，它需要 S × T c 的时间运行。于是，程序执行中可并行的那部分 P = 1 - S ，在 c 个核心上需要 P × T c 的时间运行。 Consider a parallel program that takes time T c to run on a system with c cores. Let S represent the fraction of the program execution that is necessarily serial and takes S × T c time to run. Thus, the parallelizable fraction of the program execution, P = 1 - S , takes P × T c time to run on c cores. 当同一个程序只在一个核心上运行时，代码的串行部分仍然需要 S × T c 的时间（假设其他条件相同）。然而，可并行的部分（原本分给了 c 个核心）现在必须由一个核心串行执行，需要 P × T c × c 的时间。换句话说，在单核系统上，并行部分要花 c 倍的时间。由此可得，按比例扩展的加速比（scaled speedup）为： When the same program is run on just one core, the serial fraction of the code still takes S x T c (assuming all other conditions are equal). However, the parallelizable fraction (which was divided between c cores) now has to be executed by just one core to run serially and takes P × T c × c time. In other words, the parallel component will take c times as long on a single-core system. It follows that the scaled speedup would be: 这表明，按比例扩展的加速比随计算单元的数目线性增长。 This shows that the scaled speedup increases linearly with the number of compute units. 译注 上图的公式即：按比例扩展的加速比 = ( S × T c + P × T c × c ) / T c = S + P × c 。 考虑我们之前那个程序的 99% 可并行（即 P = 0.99）的例子。应用按比例扩展的加速比公式，在 100 个处理器上的理论加速比将是 99.01。在 1,000 个处理器上，它将是 990.01。注意，效率保持在 P 不变。 Consider our prior example in which 99% of a program is parallelizable (i.e., P = 0.99). Applying the scaled speedup equation, the theoretical speedup on 100 processors would be 99.01. On 1,000 processors, it would be 990.01. Notice that the efficiency stays constant at P . 正如古斯塔夫森所总结的：「 衡量加速比时，应当让问题规模随处理器数按比例扩展，而不是固定问题规模 。」 1 古斯塔夫森的结论之所以引人注目，是因为它表明，通过增加处理器数获得越来越大的加速比是可能的。作为一名在国家超级计算机构工作的研究员，古斯塔夫森更关心的是在固定的时间内完成 更多的工作 。在一些科学领域中，能够分析更多的数据通常会带来更高的精度或保真度。古斯塔夫森的工作表明，在大量处理器上获得很大的加速比是可能的，这重新激起了人们对并行处理的兴趣 2 。 As Gustafson concludes, “ speedup should be measured by scaling the problem to the number of processors, not by fixing a problem size .” 1 Gustafson’s result is notable because it shows that it is possible to get increasing speedup by updating the number of processors. As a researcher working in a national supercomputing facility, Gustafson was more interested in doing more work in a constant amount of time. In several scientific fields, the ability to analyze more data usually leads to higher accuracy or fidelity of results. Gustafson’s work showed that it was possible to get large speedups on large numbers of processors, and revived interest in parallel processing 2 . 可扩展性 Scalability 如果在增加资源（核心、处理器）数量或问题规模时，程序的性能有所提高（或保持不变），我们就说这个程序是 可扩展的 （scalable）。两个相关的概念是 强扩展 （strong scaling）和 弱扩展 （weak scaling）。重要的是要注意，这里的「弱」和「强」并不表示程序可扩展性的 好坏 ，而只是衡量可扩展性的不同方式。 We describe a program as scalable if we see improving (or constant) performance as we increase the number of resources (cores, processors) or the problem size. Two related concepts are strong scaling and weak scaling . It is important to note that “weak” and “strong” in this context do not indicate the quality of a program’s scalability, but are simply different ways to measure scalability. 如果在问题规模 固定 的情况下，增加核心/处理单元的数量能提高性能，我们就说这个程序是 强可扩展的 （strongly scalable）。如果程序在 n 个核心上运行时加速比也是 n ，就说它表现出强线性可扩展性。当然，阿姆达尔定律保证了过了某个点之后，再增加核心就没有什么意义了。 We say that a program is strongly scalable if increasing the number of cores/processing units on a fixed problem size yields an improvement in performance. A program displays strong linear scalability if, when run on n cores, the speedup is also n . Of course, Amdahl’s Law guarantees that after some point, adding additional cores makes little sense. 如果以与核心数相同的速率增大数据规模（即每个核心/处理器分到的数据量固定）时，性能保持不变或有所提高，我们就说这个程序是 弱可扩展的 （weakly scalable）。如果每个核心的工作量扩大 n 倍时，我们看到 n 倍的改进，就说这个程序表现出弱线性可扩展性。 We say that a program is weakly scalable if increasing the size of the data at the same rate as the number of cores (i.e., if there is a fixed data size per core/processor) results in constant or an improvement in performance. We say a program displays weak linear scalability if we see an improvement of n if the work per core is scaled up by a factor of n . 关于测量性能的一般建议 General Advice Regarding Measuring Performance 最后，我们就基准测试以及超线程核心上的性能给出一些说明，结束对性能的讨论。 We conclude our discussion on performance with some notes about benchmarking and performance on hyperthreaded cores. 做基准测试时要多次运行程序。 在本书迄今展示的许多例子中，我们只运行一次程序来大致了解它的运行时间。然而，对于正式的基准测试来说，这是不够的。只运行一次程序 绝不 是对程序真实运行时间的准确度量！上下文切换和其他正在运行的进程可能会暂时导致运行时间剧烈波动。因此，最好总是多次运行程序，报告平均运行时间，并给出尽可能多的细节，包括运行次数、观察到的测量波动（例如误差棒、最小值、最大值、中位数、标准差）以及测量时的条件。 Run a program multiple times when benchmarking. In many of the examples shown thus far in this book, we run a program only once to get a sense of its runtime. However, this is not sufficient for formal benchmarks. Running a program once is never an accurate measure of a program’s true runtime! Context switches and other running processes can temporarily cause the runtime to radically fluctuate. Therefore, it is always best to run a program several times and report an average runtime together with as many details as feasible, including number of runs, observed variability of the measurements (e.g., error bars, minimum, maximum, median, standard deviation) and conditions under which the measurements were taken. 注意在哪里计时。 gettimeofday 函数有助于准确测量程序运行所用的时间。然而，它也可能被滥用。尽管可能很想只把 gettimeofday 调用放在 main 中线程创建和合并那部分的周围，但重要的是要想清楚你到底要测量什么。例如，如果程序在执行中必须读入一个外部数据文件，那么读取文件的时间很可能应当计入程序的计时中。 Be careful where you measure timing. The gettimeofday function is useful in helping to accurately measure the time a program takes to run. However, it can also be abused. Even though it may be tempting to place the gettimeofday call around only the thread creation and joining component in main , it is important to consider what exactly you are trying to time. For example, if a program reads in an external data file as a necessary part of its execution, the time for file reading should likely be included in the program’s timing. 留意超线程核心的影响。 正如 本章引言 和 硬件多线程一节 所讨论的，超线程（逻辑）核心能够在单个核心上执行多个线程。在一个每个核心有两个逻辑线程的四核系统上，我们说系统上有八个超线程核心。在许多情况下，在八个逻辑核心上并行运行程序，比在四个核心上运行能得到更好的挂钟时间。然而，由于超线程核心通常会发生资源争用，你可能会看到核心效率下降，加速比也不是线性的。 Be aware of the impact of hyperthreaded cores. As discussed in the introduction to this chapter and hardware multithreading section , hyper-threaded (logical) cores are capable of executing multiple threads on a single core. In a quad-core system with two logical threads per core, we say there are eight hyperthreaded cores on the system. Running a program in parallel on eight logical cores in many cases yields better wall time than running a program on four cores. However, due to the resource contention that usually occurs with hyperthreaded cores, you may see a dip in core efficiency and nonlinear speedup. 译注 在 Apple Silicon Mac 这类混合了性能核与能效核的机器上（见本章引言的译注），还要注意线程可能被调度到能效核上运行，这也会让测得的加速比偏离线性。 当心资源争用。 做基准测试时，始终要考虑系统上还有哪些 其他 进程和多线程应用程序在运行。如果你的性能结果看起来有点奇怪，值得快速运行一下 top ，看看是否有其他用户也在同一系统上运行资源密集型的任务。如果有，试着换一个系统做基准测试（或者等到系统不那么繁忙时再测）。 Beware of resource contention. When benchmarking, it’s always important to consider what other processes and threaded applications are running on the system. If your performance results ever look a bit strange, it is worth quickly running top to see whether there are any other users also running resource-intensive tasks on the same system. If so, try using a different system to benchmark (or wait until the system is not so heavily used). 参考文献 References John Gustafson. “Reevaluating Amdahl’s law”. Parallel Performance Basics 加速比 Speedup 假设一个程序在 c 个核心上执行需要 T c 的时间。那么，这个程序的串行版本需要 T 1 的时间。 Suppose that a program takes T c time to execute on c cores. Thus, the serial version of the program would take T 1 time. 于是，程序在 c 个核心上的加速比（speedup）由下面的公式表示： The speedup of the program on c cores is then expressed by the equation: 如果一个串行程序执行需要 60 秒，而它的并行版本在 2 个核心上需要 30 秒，对应的加速比就是 2。同样，如果这个程序在 4 个核心上需要 15 秒，加速比就是 4。在理想情况下，一个在 n 个核心上用总共 n 个线程运行的程序，加速比为 n 。 If a serial program takes 60 seconds to execute, while its parallel version takes 30 seconds on 2 cores, the corresponding speedup is 2. Likewise if that program takes 15 seconds on 4 cores, the speedup is 4. In an ideal scenario, a program running on n cores with n total threads has a speedup of n . 译注 上图的公式即：加速比 = T 1 / T c 。 如果程序的加速比大于 1，说明并行化带来了一些改进。如果加速比小于 1，那么并行解法实际上比串行解法还慢。程序的加速比也可能大于 n （例如，作为额外的缓存减少了内存访问的副作用）。这种情况称为 超线性加速 （superlinear speedup）。 If the speedup of a program is greater than 1, it indicates that the parallelization yielded some improvement. If the speedup is less than 1, then the parallel solution is in fact slower than the serial solution. It is possible for a program to have a speedup greater than n (for example, as a side effect of additional caches reducing accesses to memory). Such cases are referred to as superlinear speedup . 效率 Efficiency 加速比没有把核心数考虑进去，它只是串行时间与并行时间之比。例如，如果一个串行程序需要 60 秒，而一个并行程序在四个核心上需要 30 秒，它的加速比仍然是 2。然而，这个指标并没有反映出它是在四个核心上运行的这一事实。 Speedup doesn’t factor in the number of cores — it is simply the ratio of the serial time to the parallel time. For example, if a serial program takes 60 seconds, but a parallel program takes 30 seconds on four cores, it still gets a speedup of 2. However, that metric doesn’t capture the fact that it ran on four cores. 要度量每个核心的加速比，就用效率（efficiency）： To measure the speedup per core, use efficiency: 效率通常在 0 到 1 之间变化。效率为 1 表示核心得到了完美的利用。如果效率接近 0，说明并行几乎没有带来好处，因为额外的核心并没有提高性能。如果效率大于 1，说明出现了超线性加速。 Efficiency typically varies from 0 to 1. An efficiency of 1 indicates that the cores are being used perfectly. If efficiency is close to 0, then there is little to no benefit to parallelism, as the additional cores do not improve performance. If efficiency is greater than 1, it indicates superlinear speedup. 译注 上图的公式即：效率 = 加速比 / c = T 1 / ( c × T c )。 我们再看前面那个串行程序需要 60 秒的例子。如果并行版本在两个核心上需要 30 秒，那么它的效率是 1（即 100%）。如果程序在四个核心上需要 30 秒，那么效率就降到 0.5（即 50%）。 Let’s revisit the previous example, in which a serial program takes 60 seconds. If the parallel version takes 30 seconds on two cores, then its efficiency is 1 (or 100%). If instead the program takes 30 seconds on four cores, then the efficiency drops to 0.5 (or 50%). 现实世界中的并行性能 Parallel Performance in the Real World 在理想的世界里，加速比是线性的。每增加一个计算单元，并行程序都应该获得相应的加速。然而，这种情形在现实世界中很少出现。大多数程序都包含一个必然串行的部分，它源于代码中固有的依赖关系。程序中最长的依赖链称为它的 关键路径 （critical path）。缩短程序的关键路径，是并行化的重要第一步。线程同步点以及（对于在多个计算节点上运行的程序而言）进程之间的通信开销，是代码中可能限制程序并行性能的其他因素。 In an ideal world, speedup is linear. For each additional compute unit, a parallel program should achieve a commensurate amount of speedup. However, this scenario rarely occurs in the real world. Most programs contain a necessarily serial component that exists due to inherent dependencies in the code. The longest set of dependencies in a program is referred to as its critical path . Reducing the length of a program’s critical path is an important first step in its parallelization. Thread synchronization points and (for programs running on multiple compute nodes) communication overhead between processes are other components in the code that can limit a program’s parallel performance. 原书警示 · 并非所有程序都适合并行化！（Not all programs are good candidates for parallelism!） 关键路径的长度可能使某些程序 极难 并行化。举个例子，考虑生成第 n 个斐波那契数的问题。由于每个斐波那契数都依赖于它前面的两个数，要高效地并行化这个程序是非常困难的！ The length of the critical path can make some programs downright hard to parallelize. As an example, consider the problem of generating the _n_th Fibonacci number. Since every Fibonacci number is dependent on the two before it, parallelizing this program efficiently is very difficult! 考虑本章前面计数排序算法中 countElems 函数的并行化。在理想的世界里，我们会预期程序的加速比随核心数线性增长。然而，我们来测量一下它的运行时间（这里是在一个有八个逻辑线程的四核系统上运行）： Consider the parallelization of the countElems function of the CountSort algorithm from earlier in this chapter. In an ideal world, we would expect the speedup of the program to be linear with respect to the number of cores. Performance Benchmarks 线程数 2 4 8 加速比 1.68 2.36 3.08 效率 0.84 0.59 0.39 Number of threads 2 4 8 Speedup 1.68 2.36 3.08 Efficiency 0.84 0.59 0.39 两个核心时我们有 84% 的效率，而八个核心时核心效率降到了 39%。注意，没有达到理想的加速比 8。一个原因是，在线程数较多时，给线程分配工作的开销以及对 counts 数组的串行更新开始主导性能。第二，八个线程之间的资源争用（记住这是一个四核处理器）降低了核心效率。 While we have 84% efficiency with two cores, the core efficiency falls to 39% with eight cores. Notice that the ideal speedup of 8 was not met. One reason for this is that the overhead of assigning work to threads and the serial update to the counts array starts dominating performance at higher numbers of threads. Second, resource contention by the eight threads (remember this is a quad-core processor) reduces core efficiency. 阿姆达尔定律 Amdahl’s Law 1967 年，IBM 的杰出计算机体系结构设计师吉恩·阿姆达尔（Gene Amdahl）预言，计算机程序能够达到的最大加速比受限于其必然串行部分的大小（这一点如今称为阿姆达尔定律，Amdahl’s Law）。更一般地说，阿姆达尔定律指出，每个程序都有一个可以加速的部分（即程序中可以被优化或并行化的那部分所占的比例，记为 P ），以及一个 不能 加速的部分（即程序中固有串行的那部分所占的比例，记为 S ）。即使执行可优化或可并行化部分 P 所需的时间减少到零，串行部分 S 仍然存在，并最终会主导性能。由于 S 和 P 都是比例，注意 S + P = 1。 In 1967, Gene Amdahl, a leading computer architect at IBM, predicted that the maximum speedup that a computer program can achieve is limited by the size of its necessarily serial component (now referred to as Amdahl’s Law). More generally, Amdahl’s Law states that for every program, there is a component that can be sped up (i.e., the fraction of a program that can be optimized or parallelized, P ), and a component that cannot be sped up (i.e., the fraction of a program that is inherently serial, or S ). Even if the time needed to execute the optimizable or parallelizable component P is reduced to zero, the serial component S will exist, and will come to eventually dominate performance. Since S and P are fractions, note that S + P = 1. 考虑一个在一个核心上执行需要 T 1 时间的程序。那么，程序执行中必然串行的那部分需要 S × T 1 的时间运行，而可并行的那部分（ P = 1 - S ）需要 P × T 1 的时间运行。 Consider a program that executes on one core in time T 1 .
