Thus, the maximum improvement for the parallel processor with c cores to run the same job is: 随着 c 的增大，并行处理器上的执行时间会被程序的串行部分所主导。 As c increases, the execution time on the parallel processor becomes dominated by the serial fraction of the program. 译注 上图的公式即：T c = S × T 1 + ( P × T 1 ) / c 。 为了理解阿姆达尔定律的影响，考虑一个 90% 可并行、在 1 个核心上执行需要 10 秒的程序。在我们的公式中，可并行部分（ P ）是 0.9，串行部分（ S ）是 0.1。 表 2 描绘了根据阿姆达尔定律，在 c 个核心上对应的总时间（T c ）以及相应的加速比。 To understand the impact of Amdahl’s law, consider a program that is 90% parallelizable and executes in 10 seconds on 1 core. In our equation, the parallelizable component ( P ) is 0.9, while the serial component ( S ) is 0.1. Table 2 depicts the corresponding total time on c cores (T c ) according to Amdahl’s Law, and the associated speedup. 表 2. 阿姆达尔定律对一个 90% 可并行的 10 秒程序的影响 Table 2. The Effect of Amdahl’s Law on a 10-Second Program that is 90% Parallelizable 核心数 串行时间（秒） 并行时间（秒） 总时间（T c ，秒） 加速比（相对于一个核心） 1 1 9 10 1 10 1 0.9 1.9 5.26 100 1 0.09 1.09 9.17 1000 1 0.009 1.009 9.91 Number of cores Serial time (s) Parallel time (s) Total Time (T c s) Speedup (over one core) 1 1 9 10 1 10 1 0.9 1.9 5.26 100 1 0.09 1.09 9.17 1000 1 0.009 1.009 9.91 可以看到，随着核心数的增加，程序的串行部分开始占主导地位，再增加越来越多的核心似乎几乎没有任何效果。 Observe that, over time, the serial component of the program begins to dominate, and the effect of adding more and more cores seems to have little to no effect. 更形式化的分析方法是，把阿姆达尔对 T c 的计算代入加速比的公式： A more formal way to look at this requires incorporating Amdahl’s calculation for T c into the equation for speedup: 对这个公式取极限可以看出，当核心数（ c ）趋于无穷时，加速比趋近于 1/ S 。在 表 2 所示的例子中，加速比趋近于 1/0.1，即 10。 Taking the limit of this equation shows that as the number of cores ( c ) approaches infinity, speedup approaches 1/ S . In the example shown in Table 2 , speedup approaches 1/0.1, or 10. 译注 上图的公式即：加速比 = T 1 / T c = 1 / ( S + P / c )。当 c → ∞ 时， P / c → 0，所以加速比 → 1/ S 。 再举一个例子，考虑一个 P = 0.99 的程序。换句话说，程序的 99% 是可并行的。当 c 趋于无穷时，串行时间开始主导性能（在这个例子中， S = 0.01）。因此，加速比趋近于 1/0.01，即 100。换句话说，即使有一百万个核心，这个程序能达到的最大加速比也只有 100。 As another example, consider a program where P = 0.99. In other words, 99% of the program is parallelizable. As c approaches infinity, the serial time starts to dominate the performance (in this example, S = 0.01). Thus, speedup approaches 1/0.01 or 100. In other words, even with a million cores, the maximum speedup achievable by this program is only 100. 原书旁注 · 并非全无希望：阿姆达尔定律的局限（All is not lost: The limits of Amdahl’s Law） 在学习阿姆达尔定律时，重要的是要考虑它的提出者吉恩·阿姆达尔的 本意 。用他自己的话说，这个定律的提出是为了论证「 单处理器方法的持续有效性，以及多处理器方法在应用于实际问题及其伴随的不规则性时的弱点 1 」。在他 1967 年的论文中，阿姆达尔进一步阐述了这个观点，写道：「 十多年来，一些预言家一直声称，单台计算机的组织结构已经达到了极限，只有把多台计算机互连起来、使之能够协作求解，才能取得真正重大的进展 1 。 」 后来的研究对阿姆达尔所做的一些关键假设提出了挑战。关于阿姆达尔定律的局限，以及关于如何看待并行之好处的另一种论证，请阅读 古斯塔夫森-巴西斯定律 。 When learning about Amdahl’s Law, it’s important to consider the intentions of its originator, Gene Amdahl. In his own words, the law was proposed to demonstrate “ the continued validity of the single processor approach, and the weakness of the multiple processor approach in terms of application to real problems and their attendant irregularities 1 .” In his 1967 paper Amdahl expanded on this concept, writing: “ For over a decade prophets have voiced the contention that the organization of a single computer has reached its limits, and that truly significant advances can be made only by interconnection of a multiplicity of computers in such a manner as to permit cooperative solution 1 . “ Subsequent work challenged some of the key assumptions made by Amdahl. Cache Coherence and False Sharing 多核缓存可能对多线程程序的性能产生深远的影响。不过，我们先快速回顾一下 与缓存设计有关的一些基本概念 ： Multicore caches can have profound implications on a multithreaded program’s performance. First, however, let’s quickly review some of the basic concepts related to cache design : 数据/指令不是 单个 地传送到缓存中的，而是以 块 为单位传送，并且在存储器层次结构中越往下，块往往越大。 Data/instructions are not transported individually to the cache. Instead, data is transferred in blocks , and block sizes tend to get larger at lower levels of the memory hierarchy. 每个缓存被组织成一系列组，每个组有若干行。每一行存放一个数据块。 Each cache is organized into a series of sets, with each set having a number of lines. Each line holds a single block of data. 内存地址的各个位用来确定一个数据块要写入缓存的哪个组、标记是什么以及块内偏移是多少。 The individual bits of a memory address are used to determine which set, tag, and block offset of the cache to which to write a block of data. 当所需的数据块存在于缓存中时，发生 缓存命中 （cache hit）。否则，发生 缓存未命中 （cache miss），并在存储器层次结构的下一层（可能是缓存，也可能是主存）进行查找。 A cache hit occurs when the desired data block exists in the cache. Otherwise, a cache miss occurs, and a lookup is performed on the next lower level of the memory hierarchy (which can be cache or main memory). 有效位 （valid bit）表示缓存中某一行的块是否可以安全使用。如果有效位为 0，该行的数据块就不能使用（例如，这个块可能包含来自一个已退出进程的数据）。 The valid bit indicates if a block at a particular line in the cache is safe to use. If the valid bit is set to 0, the data block at that line cannot be used (e.g., the block could contain data from an exited process). 信息写入缓存/内存主要有两种策略。在 写直达 （write-through）策略中，数据同时写入缓存和主存。在 写回 （write-back）策略中，数据只写入缓存，在块被驱逐出缓存之后才写到层次结构的较低层。 Information is written to cache/memory based on two main strategies. In the write-through strategy, the data is written to cache and main memory simultaneously. In the write-back strategy, data is written only to cache and gets written to lower levels in the hierarchy after the block is evicted from the cache. 14.5.1. 多核系统上的缓存 14.5.1. The repeated invalidation and overwriting of lines from the L1 cache is an example of thrashing , where repeated conflicts in the cache cause a series of misses. 加入更多的核心会让问题更加严重，因为现在有更多的 L1 缓存在使该行失效。因此，尽管每个线程访问的是 counts 数组中不同的元素，增加线程反而拖慢了运行时间！这就是 伪共享 （false sharing）的一个例子，即一种多个核心在共享各个元素的假象。在前面的例子中，看起来所有核心都在访问 counts 中相同的元素，尽管事实并非如此。 The addition of more cores makes the problem worse, given that now more L1 caches are invalidating the line. As a result, adding additional threads slows down the runtime, despite the fact that each thread is accessing different elements of the counts array! This is an example of false sharing , or the illusion that individual elements are being shared by multiple cores. In the previous example, it appears that all the cores are accessing the same elements of counts , even though this is not the case. 14.5.3. 修正伪共享 14.5.3. Fixing False Sharing 修正伪共享的一种方法，是给数组（在我们的例子中是 counts ）填充额外的元素，使它不能放在单个缓存行中。然而，填充会浪费内存，而且可能无法在所有体系结构上都消除这个问题（考虑两台不同的机器 L1 缓存大小不同的情形）。在大多数情况下，为了支持不同的缓存大小而编写代码，通常不值得为此付出性能上的收益。 One way to fix an instance of false sharing is to pad the array (in our case counts ) with additional elements so that it doesn’t fit in a single cache line. Local storage in this context refers to memory that is local to a thread. The following solution reduces false sharing by choosing to perform updates to a locally declared version of counts called local_counts . 我们再来看 countElems 函数的最终版本（转引自 countElems_p_v3.c ）： Let’s revisit the final version of our countElems function (reproduced from countElems_p_v3.c ): /*parallel version of CountSort algorithm step 1 (final attempt with mutexes): * extracts arguments from args value * calculates the portion of the array this thread is responsible for counting * computes the frequency of all the elements in assigned component and stores * the associated counts of each element in counts array */ void *countElems( void *args ){ //extract arguments //omitted for brevity int *array = myargs->ap; long *counts = myargs->countp; long local_counts[MAX] = {0}; //local declaration of counts array //assign work to the thread //compute chunk, start, and end values (omitted for brevity) long i; //heart of the program for (i = start; i < end; i++){ val = array[i]; local_counts[val] = local_counts[val] + 1; //update local counts array } //update to global counts array pthread_mutex_lock(&mutex); //acquire the mutex lock for (i = 0; i < MAX; i++){ counts[i] += local_counts[i]; } pthread_mutex_unlock(&mutex); //release the mutex lock return NULL; } 在这个例子中，使用 local_counts 代替 counts 来累计频次，是减少伪共享的主要原因： The use of local_counts to accumulate frequencies in lieu of counts is the major source of reduction of false sharing in this example: for (i = start; i < end; i++){ val = array[i]; local_counts[val] = local_counts[val] + 1; //updates local counts array } 由于缓存一致性的目的是维持共享内存的一致视图，所以只有对内存中 共享值 的 写 操作才会触发失效。由于 local_counts 不在不同线程之间共享，写它不会使它所在的缓存行失效。 Since cache coherence is meant to maintain a consistent view of shared memory, the invalidations trigger only on writes to shared values in memory. The difference is that the penalty here is at most MAX × t writes vs. n writes, where n is the length of our input array, and t is the number of threads employed.

Summary 本章概述了多核处理器以及如何为它们编程。具体来说，我们介绍了 POSIX 线程（即 Pthreads）库，以及如何用它编写正确的多线程程序来加快单线程程序的性能。POSIX 和 OpenMP 这样的库采用 共享内存 （shared memory）通信模型，因为线程在一个公共的内存空间中共享数据。 This chapter provided an overview of multicore processors and how to program them. Specifically, we cover the POSIX threads (or Pthreads) library and how to use it to create correct multithreaded programs that speed up a single-threaded program’s performance. Libraries like POSIX and OpenMP utilize the shared memory model of communication, as threads share data in a common memory space. 要点 Key Takeaways 线程是并发程序的基本单位 为了并行化一个串行程序，程序员使用称为 线程 的轻量级结构。对于一个特定的多线程进程，每个线程都有自己的栈内存，但共享进程的程序数据、堆和指令。与进程一样，线程在 CPU 上的运行是 不确定的 （nondeterministic，即执行顺序每次运行都会变化，哪个线程被分配到哪个核心由操作系统决定）。 Threads are the fundamental unit of concurrent programs To parallelize a serial program, programmers utilize lightweight constructs known as threads . For a particular multithreaded process, each thread has its own allocation of stack memory, but shares the program data, heap and instructions of the process. Like processes, threads run nondeterministically on the CPU (i.e., the order of execution changes between runs, and which thread is assigned to which core is left up to the operating system). 同步结构确保程序正确运行 共享内存的一个后果是，线程可能无意中覆盖驻留在共享内存中的数据。每当两个操作错误地更新一个共享值时，就可能发生 竞态条件 。当这个共享值是数据时，就可能出现一种特殊的竞态条件，称为 数据竞争 。同步结构（互斥锁、信号量等）通过确保线程在更新共享变量时一次一个地执行，来帮助保证程序的正确性。 Synchronization constructs ensure that programs work correctly A consequence of shared memory is that threads can accidentally overwrite data residing in shared memory. A race condition can occur whenever two operations incorrectly update a shared value. When that shared value is data, a special type of race condition called a data race can arise. Synchronization constructs (mutexes, semaphores, etc.) help to guarantee program correctness by ensuring that threads execute one at a time when updating shared variables. 使用同步结构时要谨慎 同步本质上会在原本并行的程序中引入串行计算的点。因此，重要的是要清楚 如何 使用同步概念。必须原子地运行的那组操作称为 临界区 。如果临界区太大，线程就会串行执行，运行时间得不到任何改善。同步结构用得马虎，就可能无意中出现 死锁 之类的情况。一个好的策略是让线程尽可能使用局部变量，只在必要时才更新共享变量。 Be mindful when using synchronization constructs Synchronization inherently introduces points of serial computation in an otherwise parallel program. It is therefore important to be aware of how one uses synchronization concepts. The set of operations that must run atomically is referred to as a critical section . If a critical section is too big, the threads will execute serially, yielding no improvement in runtime. Use synchronization constructs sloppily, and situations like deadlock may inadvertently arise. A good strategy is to have threads employ local variables as much as possible and update shared variables only when necessary. 并非程序的所有部分都可以并行化 有些程序必然包含很大的串行部分，这可能会妨碍多线程程序在多个核心上的性能（例如 阿姆达尔定律 ）。即使程序中可并行的比例很高，加速比也很少是线性的。在确定程序的性能时，我们也鼓励读者考察效率和可扩展性等其他指标。 Not all components of a program are parallelizable Some programs necessarily have large serial components that can hinder a multithreaded program’s performance on multiple cores (e.g., Amdahl’s Law ). Even when a high percentage of a program is parallelizable, speedup is rarely linear. Readers are also encouraged to look at other metrics such as efficiency and scalability when ascertaining the performance of their programs. 延伸阅读 Further Reading 本章旨在让读者初步领略关于线程的并发话题，绝不是面面俱到的。要进一步学习用 POSIX 线程和 OpenMP 编程，请查看劳伦斯·利弗莫尔国家实验室的 Blaise Barney 编写的优秀的 Pthreads 和 OpenMP 教程。关于调试并行程序的自动化工具，我们鼓励读者看看 Valgrind 中的 Helgrind 和 DRD 工具。 This chapter is meant to give a taste of concurrency topics with threads; it is by no means exhaustive. To learn more about programming with POSIX threads and OpenMP, check out the excellent tutorials on Pthreads and OpenMP by Blaise Barney from Lawrence Livermore National Labs. For automated tools for debugging parallel programs, readers are encouraged to check out the Helgrind and DRD Valgrind tools. 译注 Valgrind 不能在 Apple Silicon Mac 上运行，但 Clang 自带的 ThreadSanitizer 可以直接使用。译者在 Mac 上写了一个两个线程不加锁地递增 counts[i % 10] 的程序，用 clang -g -O1 -fsanitize=thread 编译后运行，输出了「WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race」，并指出了发生竞争的源代码行。 在本书的 最后一章 中，我们会从较高的层次概述其他常见的并行体系结构以及如何为它们编程。 继续阅读以了解更多 。 In the final chapter of the book, we give a high-level overview of other common parallel architectures and how to program them. x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C15-Parallel/index.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 15. Looking Ahead: Other Parallel Systems and Parallel Programming Models 在 上一章 中，我们讨论了共享内存并行与多线程编程。本章将介绍面向不同类别体系结构的其他并行编程模型与语言。具体来说：以 CUDA 为例，介绍面向硬件加速器的并行，重点是图形处理器（GPU）以及在 GPU 上进行的通用计算（GPGPU 计算）；以 MPI 为例，介绍分布式内存系统与消息传递；以 MapReduce 和 Apache Spark 为例，介绍云计算。 In the previous chapter , we discussed shared memory parallelism and multithreaded programming. In this chapter, we introduce other parallel programming models and languages for different classes of architecture. Namely, we introduce parallelism for hardware accelerators focusing on graphics processing units (GPUs) and general-purpose computing on GPUs (GPGPU computing), using CUDA as an example; distributed memory systems and message passing, using MPI as an example; and cloud computing, using MapReduce and Apache Spark as examples. 全新的世界：弗林体系结构分类法 A Whole New World: Flynn’s Taxonomy of Architecture 弗林分类法 （Flynn’s taxonomy）常被用来描述现代计算体系结构的整体版图（ 图 1 ）。 Flynn’s taxonomy is commonly used to describe the ecosystem of modern computing architecture ( Figure 1 ). 译注 该分类由 Michael J. Flynn 于 1966 年提出（1972 年的论文做了扩展）。它只看”指令流”和”数据流”各是一条还是多条，不涉及内存组织方式；所以后面 15.2 节还要再引入”共享内存 vs. 分布式内存”这条正交的维度。 图 1. 弗林分类法根据处理器执行指令的方式对其进行分类。 Figure 1. Flynn’s taxonomy classifies the ways in which a processor applies instructions. 译注 · 图中标签 横轴 Data Stream＝数据流，纵轴 Instruction Stream＝指令流；Single＝单，Multiple＝多。四格依次为 SISD（单指令单数据）、SIMD（单指令多数据）、MISD（多指令单数据）、MIMD（多指令多数据）。 横轴表示数据流，纵轴表示指令流。这里的 流 （stream）指的是数据或指令的流动。 单一流 每个时间单位发出一个元素，类似于一个队列；相比之下， 多重流 通常每个时间单位发出多个元素（可以想象成多个队列）。因此，单指令流（SI）每个时间单位发出一条指令，而多指令流（MI）每个时间单位发出多条指令。同样，单数据流（SD）每个时间单位发出一个数据元素，而多数据流（MD）每个时间单位发出多个数据元素。 The horizontal axis refers to the data stream, whereas the vertical axis refers to the instruction stream. A stream in this context is a flow of data or instructions. A single stream issues one element per time unit, similar to a queue. In contrast, multiple streams typically issue many elements per time unit (think of multiple queues). Thus, a single instruction stream (SI) issues a single instruction per time unit, whereas a multiple instruction stream (MI) issues many instructions per time unit. Likewise, a single data stream (SD) issues one data element per time unit, whereas a multiple data stream (MD) issues many data elements per time unit. 根据所使用的流的类型，处理器可以归入以下四类之一： A processor can be classified into one of four categories based on the types of streams it employs: SISD ：单指令流/单数据流系统只有一个控制单元，处理单一的指令流，因此一次只能执行一条指令。同样，处理器也只能处理单一的数据流，即一次处理一个数据单元。2000 年代中期以前，大多数商用处理器都是 SISD 机器。 SISD : Single instruction/single data systems have a single control unit processing a single stream of instructions, allowing it to execute only one instruction at a time. Likewise, the processor can process only a single stream of data or process one data unit at a time. Most commercially available processors prior to the mid-2000s were SISD machines. 译注 严格来说，2000 年代中期以前的商用 CPU 也并非”纯” SISD：x86 早在 1997 年就有了 MMX、1999 年有了 SSE 这类 SIMD 扩展指令。这里的”SISD”应理解为”单核、单指令流”。另外，单核时代的性能提升主要来自流水线、超标量、乱序执行等 指令级并行 （ILP），这些对程序员是透明的；而本章讨论的都是需要程序员显式表达的并行。 MISD ：多指令流/单数据流系统由多个指令单元作用于同一条数据流。MISD 系统通常用于为关键任务系统提供容错能力，例如 NASA 航天飞机的飞行控制程序。话虽如此，MISD 机器如今在实践中已很少使用。 MISD : Multiple instruction/single data systems have multiple instruction units performing on a single data stream. MISD systems were typically designed for incorporating fault tolerance in mission-critical systems, such as the flight control programs for NASA shuttles. That said, MISD machines are rarely used in practice anymore. 译注 航天飞机的例子是”多台计算机用同样的输入各自计算、再投票表决”的冗余设计。也有教材把 脉动阵列 （systolic array，如 Google TPU 的矩阵乘法单元：同一份数据在一串处理单元之间逐级流动、被多个单元依次使用）归为类 MISD 结构，但这种归类有争议（每个单元执行的其实是同样的乘加运算），了解即可。 SIMD ：单指令流/多数据流系统以”锁步”（lockstep）方式，同时在多个数据上执行 同一条 指令。在”锁步”执行过程中，所有指令被放入一个队列，而数据被分发到不同的计算单元。执行时，每个计算单元同时执行队列中的第一条指令，然后再同时执行队列中的下一条指令，依此类推。SIMD 体系结构最著名的例子是图形处理器（GPU）。早期的超级计算机也采用 SIMD 体系结构。我们将在 下一节 进一步讨论 GPU。 SIMD : Single instruction/multiple data systems execute the same instruction on multiple data simultaneously and in lockstep fashion. During “lockstep” execution, all instructions are placed into a queue, while data is distributed among different compute units. During execution, each compute unit executes the first instruction in the queue simultaneously, before simultaneously executing the next instruction in the queue, and then the next, and so forth. The most well-known example of the SIMD architecture is the graphics processing unit. Early supercomputers also followed the SIMD architecture. We discuss GPUs more in the next section . 译注 今天最常见的 SIMD 其实就在你的 CPU 核内部：x86 的 SSE/AVX/AVX-512，Arm 的 NEON/SVE，RISC-V 的 V 扩展（RVV），一条指令同时处理一个向量寄存器里的多个元素。编译器的”自动向量化”就是把普通循环翻译成这类指令。GPU 严格说是 SIMT（下一节会讲），它是 SIMD 的变体。”早期超级计算机”指 ILLIAC IV、Thinking Machines CM-1/CM-2 这类阵列处理机，以及 Cray-1 这类向量机。 MIMD ：多指令流/多数据流系统是使用最广泛的体系结构类别。它们极其灵活，能够同时处理多条指令流或多条数据流。由于几乎所有现代计算机都使用多核 CPU，大多数计算机都属于 MIMD 机器。我们将在 15.2 节 中讨论另一类 MIMD 系统——分布式内存系统。 MIMD : Multiple instruction/multiple data systems represent the most widely used architecture class. They are extremely flexible and have the ability to work on multiple instructions or multiple data streams. Since nearly all modern computers use multicore CPUs, most are classified as MIMD machines. We discuss another class of MIMD systems, distributed memory systems, in Section 15.2 . 译注 现代机器往往是”多层嵌套”的：一台服务器在多个核之间是 MIMD，每个核内部的向量单元是 SIMD，插在上面的 GPU 是 SIMT，多台服务器组成集群又是分布式内存的 MIMD。还有一个常用的编程层面的说法： SPMD （单程序多数据）——所有进程/线程运行同一份程序、处理不同数据，CUDA 核函数和 MPI 程序基本都是这种写法（见 15.1、15.2 节）。 现代更新（截至 2026-11） · SIMD、加速器与矩阵单元 CPU 内的 SIMD 仍在演进 ：Intel 于 2023 年提出 AVX10（融合向量指令集），让未来所有 Intel 处理器支持同一套以 AVX-512 为基础的向量指令；2025 年 3 月的 3.0 版文档删去了早期”最大 256 位”的限制表述。 Intel AVX10 技术文档 异构已成主流 ：2026 年 6 月 TOP500 中，500 台超算有 276 台使用加速器（107 台 NVIDIA Hopper、62 台 Ampere、32 台 AMD Instinct）。 TOP500 2026-06 GPU 里的矩阵单元 ：H100 每个 SM 有 4 个第四代 Tensor Core，一条指令完成一小块矩阵乘加，可看作 SIMD 在矩阵维度上的延伸。 NVIDIA Hopper 架构详解

说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C14-SharedMemory/openmp.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 14.7. Implicit Threading with OpenMP 到目前为止，我们介绍的都是用 POSIX 线程进行共享内存编程。尽管 Pthreads 很适合简单的应用程序，但随着程序本身越来越复杂，它也变得越来越难用。POSIX 线程是线程 显式并行编程 （explicit parallel programming）的一个例子，它要求程序员准确指定每个线程需要做什么，以及每个线程应当何时开始、何时停止。 Thus far, we have presented shared memory programming using POSIX threads. Although Pthreads are great for simple applications, they become increasingly difficult to use as programs themselves become more complex. POSIX threads are an example of explicit parallel programming of threads, requiring a programmer to specify exactly what each thread is required to do and when each thread should start and stop. 使用 Pthreads 时，要给现有的顺序程序 逐步地 加入并行也可能很困难。也就是说，程序员常常必须完全重写程序才能使用线程，而在试图并行化一个大型的现有代码库时，这往往是不可取的。 With Pthreads, it can also be challenging to incrementally add parallelism to an existing sequential program. That is, one must often rewrite the program entirely to use threads, which is often not desirable when attempting to parallelize a large, existing codebase. 开放多处理（Open Multiprocessing，OpenMP）库实现了 Pthreads 的一种 隐式 替代方案。OpenMP 内置于 GCC 以及 LLVM 和 Clang 等其他流行的编译器中，可以与 C、C++ 和 Fortran 编程语言一起使用。OpenMP 的一个主要优点是，它让程序员只需在代码的某些部分加入 编译指示 （pragma，即特殊的编译器指令），就能并行化现有的顺序 C 代码中的组成部分。OpenMP 专用的编译指示以 #pragma omp 开头。 The Open Multiprocessing (OpenMP) library implements an implicit alternative to Pthreads. OpenMP is built into GCC and other popular compilers such as LLVM and Clang, and can be used with the C, C++, and Fortran programming languages. A key advantage of OpenMP is that it enables programmers to parallelize components of existing, sequential C code by adding pragmas (special compiler directives) to parts of the code. Pragmas specific to OpenMP begin with #pragma omp . 译注 · Mac 上的 OpenMP macOS 自带的 Apple Clang 不直接支持 OpenMP：译者在 Mac 上用 clang -fopenmp 编译一个带 #pragma omp parallel 的程序，得到「unsupported option ‘-fopenmp’」错误。要在 Mac 上跟做本节，需要另外安装 OpenMP 运行时库（例如通过 Homebrew 安装 libomp ）并相应调整编译选项，或者安装 GCC / 上游 LLVM，也可以直接在 Linux 中运行。 对 OpenMP 的详细介绍超出了本书的范围，不过我们会介绍一些常用的编译指示，并展示如何在一些示例应用程序中使用其中的几个。 Detailed coverage of OpenMP is outside the scope of this book, but we cover some common pragmas, and show how several can be used in the context of some sample applications. 14.7.1. 常用的编译指示 14.7.1. Common Pragmas 下面是 OpenMP 程序中最常用的一些编译指示： Here are some of the most commonly used pragmas in OpenMP programs: #pragma omp parallel 这个编译指示创建一组线程，让每个线程运行其作用域中的代码（通常是一个函数调用）。调用这个编译指示通常相当于调用 我们最初讨论 Pthreads 时 介绍的 pthread_create 和 pthread_join 函数对。这个编译指示可以带若干子句，包括： num_threads 指定要创建的线程数。 private 是一个变量列表，列出对每个线程来说应当是私有（或局部）的变量。对线程私有的变量也可以在编译指示的作用域内声明（例子见下文）。每个线程都会得到每个这类变量的一份副本。 shared 是一个变量列表，列出应当在线程之间共享的变量。这类变量只有一份副本，由所有线程共享。 default 表示是否由编译器决定哪些变量应当共享。在大多数情况下，我们希望使用 default(none) ，并显式指定哪些变量应当共享、哪些应当私有。 #pragma omp parallel This pragma creates a team of threads and has each thread run the code in its scope (usually a function call) on each thread. An invocation of this pragma is usually equivalent to an invocation of the pthread_create and pthread_join function pairing discussed in our original discussion on Pthreads . The pragma may have a number of clauses, including the following: num_threads specifies the number of threads to create. private is a list of variables that should be private (or local) to each thread. Variables that should be private to a thread can also be declared within the scope of the pragma (see below for an example). Each thread gets its own copy of each variable. shared is a listing of variables that should be shared amongst the threads. There is one copy of the variable that is shared amongst all threads. default indicates whether the determination of which variables should be shared is left up to the compiler. In most cases, we want to use default(none) and specify explicitly which variables should be shared, and which should be private. #pragma omp for 指定每个线程执行 for 循环迭代的一个子集。尽管循环的调度由系统决定，但默认通常是在 标量乘法的例子 中首次讨论的「分块」方法。这是一种 静态 的调度形式：每个线程得到一个分配好的块，然后处理块中的迭代。不过，OpenMP 也让 动态 调度变得很容易。在动态调度中，每个线程得到若干次迭代，处理完之后再请求一组新的迭代。调度策略可以用下面的子句来设置： schedule(dynamic) ：指定应当使用 动态 形式的调度。尽管在某些情况下这样做有好处，但静态（默认）形式的调度通常更快。 #pragma omp for Specifies that each thread execute a subset of iterations of a for loop. Although the scheduling of the loops is up to the system, the default is usually the “chunking” method first discussed in the scalar multiplication example . This is a static form of scheduling: each thread gets an assigned chunk, and then processes the iterations in its chunk. However, OpenMP also makes dynamic scheduling easy. In dynamic scheduling, each thread gets a number of iterations, and requests a new set upon completing processing their iteration. The scheduling policy can be set using the following clause: schedule(dynamic) : specifies that a dynamic form of scheduling should be used. While this is advantageous in some cases, the static (default) form of scheduling is usually faster. #pragma omp parallel for 这个编译指示是 omp parallel 和 omp for 编译指示的组合。与 omp for 编译指示不同， omp parallel for 编译指示还会先生成一组线程，然后再给每个线程分配循环迭代的一个集合。 #pragma omp parallel for This pragma is a combination of the omp parallel and the omp for pragmas. Unlike the omp for pragma, the omp parallel for pragma also generates a team of threads before assigning each thread a set of iterations of the loop. #pragma omp critical 这个编译指示用来指定其作用域下的代码应当被视为 临界区 ，即一次只能有一个线程执行这段代码，以确保正确的行为。 #pragma omp critical This pragma is used to specify that the code under its scope should be treated as a critical section — that is, only one thread should execute the section of code at a time to ensure correct behavior. 还有几个线程可以调用的 函数 ，在执行中常常很有用。例如： There are also several functions that a thread can access that are often useful for execution. For example: omp_get_num_threads 返回当前正在执行的线程组中的线程数。 omp_get_num_threads returns the number of threads in the current team that is being executed. omp_set_num_threads 设置一个线程组应当拥有的线程数。 omp_set_num_threads sets the number of threads that a team should have. omp_get_thread_num 返回调用线程的标识符。 omp_get_thread_num returns the identifier of the calling thread. 原书警示 · omp parallel for 指令只适用于 for 循环！（The omp parallel for directive works only with for loops!） 记住， omp parallel for 编译指示 只 适用于 for 循环。其他类型的循环，例如 while 循环和 do - while 循环，都不受支持。 Keep in mind that the omp parallel for pragma works only with for loops. Other types of loops, such as while loops and do - while loops, are not supported. 14.7.2. 你好，线程：OpenMP 风味 14.7.2. Hello Threading: OpenMP flavored 我们再来看「Hello World」（ hellothreads.c ）程序，这次用 OpenMP 而不是 Pthreads 来写： Let’s revisit our “Hello World” ( hellothreads.c ) program, now using OpenMP instead of Pthreads: #include <stdio.h> #include <stdlib.h> #include <omp.h> void HelloWorld( void ) { long myid = omp_get_thread_num(); printf( "Hello world! I am thread %ld
", myid ); } int main( int argc, char** argv ) { long nthreads; if (argc !=2) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s <n>
", argv[0]); fprintf(stderr, "where <n> is the number of threads
"); return 1; } nthreads = strtol( argv[1], NULL, 10 ); #pragma omp parallel num_threads(nthreads) HelloWorld(); return 0; } 注意，OpenMP 程序比 Pthreads 版本 短得多 。为了使用 OpenMP 库函数，我们包含头文件 omp.h 。 main 中的 omp parallel num_threads(nthreads) 编译指示创建一组线程，每个线程都调用 HelloWorld 函数。子句 num_threads(nthreads) 指定总共应当生成 nthreads 个线程。这个编译指示还会把每个创建的线程合并回单线程进程。换句话说，创建和合并线程的所有底层工作都对程序员 抽象 掉了，只需加入一个编译指示就能完成。因此，OpenMP 被认为是一种 隐式多线程 （implicit threading）库。 Note that the OpenMP program is much shorter than the Pthreads version. To access the OpenMP library functions, we include the header file omp.h . The omp parallel num_threads(nthreads) pragma in main creates a set of threads, where each thread calls the HelloWorld function. The clause num_threads(nthreads) specifies that a total of nthreads should be generated. The pragma also joins each created thread back to a single-threaded process. In other words, all the low-level work of creating and joining threads is abstracted away from the programmer and is accomplished with the inclusion of just one pragma. For this reason, OpenMP is considered an implicit threading library. OpenMP 还省去了显式管理线程 ID 的需要。在 HelloWorld 中， omp_get_thread_num 函数取出运行它的那个线程的唯一 ID。 OpenMP also abstracts away the need to explicitly manage thread IDs. In the context of HelloWorld , the omp_get_thread_num function extracts the unique ID associated with the thread that is running it. 编译代码 Compiling the code 我们给编译器传入 -fopenmp 选项来编译并运行这个程序，这个选项表示我们是在用 OpenMP 进行编译： Let’s compile and run this program by passing the -fopenmp flag to the compiler, which signals that we’re compiling with OpenMP: $ gcc -o hello_mp hello_mp.c -fopenmp $ ./hello_mp 4 Hello world! I am thread 2 Hello world! I am thread 3 Hello world! I am thread 0 Hello world! I am thread 1 由于线程的执行在后续运行中可能变化，重新运行这个程序会得到不同顺序的消息： Since the execution of threads can change with subsequent runs, rerunning this program results in a different sequence of messages: $ ./hello_mp 4 Hello world! I am thread 3 Hello world! I am thread 2 Hello world! I am thread 1 Hello world! I am thread 0 这种行为与我们 用 Pthreads 编写的例子 是一致的。 This behavior is consistent with our example with Pthreads . 14.7.3. 一个更复杂的例子：OpenMP 版计数排序 14.7.3. A More Complex Example: CountSort in OpenMP OpenMP 的一个强大优势在于，它让程序员能够逐步地并行化自己的代码。为了实际看一看，我们来并行化本章前面讨论过的、更复杂的计数排序算法（串行代码在这里： countSort.c ）。回想一下，这个算法对只包含少量取值的数组进行排序。串行程序的 main 函数如下： A powerful advantage of OpenMP is that it enables programmers to incrementally parallelize their code. To see this in action, let’s parallelize the more complex CountSort algorithm discussed earlier in this chapter (the serial code is located here: countSort.c ). Recall that this algorithm sorts arrays containing a small range of values. The main function of the serial program looks like the following: int main( int argc, char **argv ) { //parse args (omitted for brevity) srand(10); //use of static seed ensures the output is the same every run //generate random array of elements of specified length //(omitted for brevity) //allocate counts array and initializes all elements to zero. int counts[MAX] = {0}; countElems(counts, array, length); //calls step 1 writeArray(counts, array); //calls step2 free(array); //free memory return 0; } main 函数在做了一些命令行解析并生成一个随机数组之后，先调用 countsElems 函数，再调用 writeArray 函数。 The main function, after doing some command line parsing and generating a random array, calls the countsElems function followed by the writeArray function. 用 OpenMP 并行化 CountElems Parallelizing CountElems Using OpenMP 并行化前面的程序有好几种方法。一种方法（如下面的例子所示）是在 countElems 和 writeArray 函数中使用 omp parallel 编译指示。这样，就不需要对 main 函数做任何改动。程序的完整版本见： countSort_mp.c 。 There are several ways to parallelize the preceding program. One way (shown in the example that follows) uses the omp parallel pragma in the context of the countElems and writeArray functions. As a result, no changes need to be made to the main function. A full version of the program is available at: countSort_mp.c . 首先，我们来看如何用 OpenMP 并行化 countElems 函数： First, let’s examine how to parallelize the countElems function using OpenMP: void countElems(int *counts, int *array, long length) { #pragma omp parallel default(none) shared(counts, array, length) { int val, i, local[MAX] = {0}; #pragma omp for for (i = 0; i < length; i++) { val = array[i]; local[val]++; } #pragma omp critical { for (i = 0; i < MAX; i++) { counts[i] += local[i]; } } } } 在这个版本的代码中，使用了三个编译指示： In this version of the code, three pragmas are employed: #pragma omp parallel 编译指示表示应当创建一组线程。 main 中的 omp_set_num_threads(nthreads) 这一行把线程组的默认大小设为 nthreads 。如果没有使用 omp_set_num_threads 函数，分配的线程数将等于系统中的核心数。提醒一下， omp parallel 编译指示在块的开头隐式地创建线程，在块的末尾合并它们。花括号（ {} ）用来指定作用域。 shared 子句声明变量 counts 、 array 和 length 在所有线程之间共享（全局的）。因此，变量 val 、 i 和 local[MAX] 在每个线程中都是 局部 声明的。 The #pragma omp parallel pragma indicates that a team of threads should be created. The omp_set_num_threads(nthreads) line in main sets the default size of the thread team to be nthreads . If the omp_set_num_threads function is not used, then the number of threads assigned will equal the number of cores in the system. As a reminder, the omp parallel pragma implicitly creates threads at the beginning of the block and joins them at the end of the block. Braces ( {} ) are used to specify scope. The shared clause declares that the variables counts , array , and length are shared (global) among all the threads. Thus, the variables val , i , and local[MAX] are declared locally in each thread. 下一个编译指示是 #pragma omp for ，它并行化 for 循环，把迭代次数分给各个线程。OpenMP 会计算如何最好地划分循环的迭代。如前所述，默认策略通常是分块方法，让每个线程计算大致相同数量的迭代。因此，每个线程读取共享数组 array 的一部分，并在它的局部数组 local 中累计计数。 The next pragma is #pragma omp for , which parallelizes the for loop, splitting the number of iterations among the number of threads. OpenMP calculates how best to split up the iterations of the loop. As previously mentioned, the default strategy is usually a chunking method, wherein each thread gets roughly the same number of iterations to compute. Thus, each thread reads a component of the shared array array , and accumulates its counts in its local array local . #pragma omp critical 编译指示表示临界区作用域中的代码一次只能由一个线程执行。这相当于这个程序的 Pthreads 版本中使用的互斥锁。在这里，每个线程依次递增共享的 counts 数组。 The #pragma omp critical pragma indicates that the code in the scope of the critical section should be executed by exactly one thread at a time. This is equivalent to the mutex that was employed in the Pthreads version of this program. Here, each thread increments the shared counts array one at a time. 我们用 1 亿个元素运行这个函数，来感受一下它的性能： Let’s get a sense of the performance of this function by running it with 100 million elements: $ ./countElems_mp 100000000 1 Run Time for Phase 1 is 0.249893 $ ./countElems_mp 100000000 2 Run Time for Phase 1 is 0.124462 $ ./countElems_mp 100000000 4 Run Time for Phase 1 is 0.068749 这是非常出色的性能：我们的函数在两个线程上得到了 2 的加速比，在四个线程上得到了 3.63 的加速比。性能甚至比 Pthreads 的实现还要好！ This is excellent performance, with our function getting a speedup of 2 on two threads, and a speedup of 3.63 on four threads. We get even better performance than the Pthreads implementation! OpenMP 中的 writeArray 函数 The writeArray Function in OpenMP 并行化 writeArray 函数要 难得多 。下面的代码展示了一种可能的解决方案： Parallelizing the writeArray function is much harder. The following code shows one possible solution: void writeArray(int *counts, int *array) { int i; //assumed the number of threads is no more than MAX #pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic) for (i = 0; i < MAX; i++) { int j = 0, amt, start = 0; for (j = 0; j < i; j++) { //calculate the "true" start position start += counts[j]; } amt = counts[i]; //the number of array positions to fill //overwrite amt elements with value i, starting at position start for (j = start; j < start + amt; j++) { array[j] = i; } } } 在并行化之前，我们对这个函数做了一处修改，因为 旧版本 的 writeArray 使 j 依赖于循环的前几次迭代。在这个版本中，每个线程根据 counts 中前面所有元素之和，算出自己唯一的 start 值。 Prior to parallelizing, we made a change to this function, because the old version of writeArray caused j to have a dependency on the previous iterations of the loop. In this version, each thread calculates its unique start value based on the sum of all the previous elements in counts . 去掉这个依赖之后，并行化就相当直接了。 #pragma omp parallel for 编译指示生成一组线程，并通过给每个线程分配循环迭代的一个子集来并行化 for 循环。提醒一下，这个编译指示是 omp parallel 和 omp for 编译指示（在并行化 countElems 时用过）的组合。 When this dependency is removed, the parallelization is pretty straightforward. The #pragma omp parallel for pragma generates a team of threads and parallelizes the for loop by assigning each thread a subset of the iterations of the loop. As a reminder, this pragma is a combination of the omp parallel and the omp for pragmas (which were used in the parallelization of countElems ). 分块的线程调度方法（如前面的 countElems 函数中所示）在这里并不合适，因为 counts 中各个元素的频次可能相差悬殊。因此，各线程的工作量不会相等，导致一些线程分到的工作比其他线程多。所以这里使用了 schedule(dynamic) 子句，让每个线程完成分配给它的迭代后，再向线程管理器请求新的迭代。 A chunking approach to scheduling threads (as shown in the earlier countElems function) is not appropriate here, because it is possible that each element in counts has a radically different frequency. Therefore, the threads will not have equal work, resulting in some threads being assigned more work than others. Therefore, the schedule(dynamic) clause is employed, so that each thread completes the iteration it is assigned before requesting a new iteration from the thread manager. 由于每个线程写的是数组中不同的位置，这个函数不需要互斥。 Since each thread is writing to distinct array locations, mutual exclusion is not needed for this function. 注意，OpenMP 代码比 POSIX 线程的实现简洁得多。代码非常易读，而且只需要很少的修改。这就是 抽象 （abstraction）的威力之一：实现细节对程序员隐藏了起来。 Notice how much cleaner the OpenMP code is than the POSIX thread implementation. The code is very readable, and required very little modification. This is one of the powers of abstraction , in which the implementation details are hidden from the programmer. 然而，抽象必然要以控制力为代价。程序员假定编译器足够「聪明」，能处理并行化的种种细节，因而能更轻松地并行化自己的应用程序。但是，程序员不再对并行化的细节做出具体的决定。如果不清楚 OpenMP 编译指示在底层是如何执行的，就可能很难调试 OpenMP 应用程序，也很难知道在某个时候使用哪个编译指示最合适。 However, a necessary trade-off for abstraction is control. The programmer assumes that the compiler is “smart” enough to take care of the particulars of parallelization and thus has an easier time parallelizing their application. However, the programmer no longer makes detailed decisions about the particulars of that parallelization. Without a clear idea of how OpenMP pragmas execute under the hood, it can be difficult to debug an OpenMP application or know which pragma is the most appropriate to use at a given time. 14.7.4. 进一步学习 OpenMP 14.7.4. Learning More about OpenMP 对 OpenMP 更深入的讨论超出了本书的范围，不过有一些学习 OpenMP 的免费资源 1,2 很有用。 A deeper discussion of OpenMP is beyond the scope of this book, but there are useful free resources 1,2 for learning OpenMP. 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· OpenMP 6.0 2024 年 11 月 14 日，OpenMP 架构审查委员会（ARB）在 SC24 大会上发布了 OpenMP 6.0 规范。按官方新闻稿，主要新增内容包括：简化任务（task）编程，例如允许不属于任何线程组的「自由代理线程」（free-agent thread）执行任务、可以录制任务图以便高效重放；增强加速器设备支持；完整支持 C23、C++23 和 Fortran 2023 等最新语言标准；以及让用户更细致地控制存储资源和内存空间。本节介绍的 parallel 、 for 、 critical 等基本编译指示在新版本中依然适用。 Business Wire：OpenMP ARB Releases OpenMP 6.0 for Easier Programming 参考文献 References: Blaise Barney. “OpenMP”. https://hpc.llnl.gov/tuts/openMP/ Richard Brown and Libby Shoop. “Multicore Programming with OpenMP”. Heterogeneous Computing: Hardware Accelerators, GPGPU Computing, and CUDA 异构计算 （heterogeneous computing）是指利用计算机中多种不同的处理单元进行计算。这些处理单元往往具有不同的指令集架构（ISA），其中一些由操作系统管理，另一些则不由操作系统管理。通常，异构计算指的是同时利用计算机的 CPU 核心和一个或多个加速单元——例如 图形处理器 （GPU）或 现场可编程门阵列 （FPGA）——来支持并行计算 1 。 Heterogeneous computing is computing using multiple, different processing units found in a computer. These processing units often have different ISAs, some managed by the OS, and others not. Typically, heterogeneous computing means support for parallel computing using the computer’s CPU cores and one or more of its accelerator units such as graphics processing units (GPUs) or field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) 1 . 针对大规模的数据密集型和计算密集型问题，开发者越来越多地采用异构计算方案。这类问题在科学计算中无处不在，也广泛出现在大数据处理、分析与信息提取等更多样的应用中。通过同时利用计算机上 CPU 和加速单元的处理能力，程序员可以提高应用程序的并行执行程度，从而获得更好的性能和可扩展性。 It is increasingly common for developers to implement heterogeneous computing solutions to large, data-intensive and computation-intensive problems. These types of problems are pervasive in scientific computing, as well as in a more diverse range of applications to Big Data processing, analysis, and information extraction. By making use of the processing capabilities of both the CPU and the accelerator units that are available on a computer, a programmer can increase the degree of parallel execution in their application, resulting in improved performance and scalability. 本节介绍如何利用硬件加速器进行异构计算，以支持通用并行计算。我们重点讨论 GPU 和 CUDA 编程语言。 In this section, we introduce heterogeneous computing using hardware accelerators to support general-purpose parallel computing. We focus on GPUs and the CUDA programming language. 15.1.1. 硬件加速器 15.1.1. Hardware Accelerators 除了 CPU 之外，计算机中还有其他为执行特定任务而设计的处理单元。它们不像 CPU 那样是通用处理单元，而是专用硬件：经过优化，用来实现某些设备特有的功能，或在系统中执行特定类型的处理。FPGA、Cell 处理器和 GPU 就是这类处理单元的三个例子。 In addition to the CPU, computers have other processing units that are designed to perform specific tasks. These units are not general-purpose processing units like the CPU, but are special-purpose hardware that is optimized to implement functionality that is specific to certain devices or that is used to perform specialized types of processing in the system. FPGAs, Cell processors, and GPUs are three examples of these types of processing units. FPGA FPGAs FPGA 是一种由逻辑门、存储器和互连部件组成的集成电路。它是可重新编程的，也就是说可以被重新配置，从而在硬件中实现特定的功能；FPGA 常被用来为专用集成电路（ASIC）做原型验证。FPGA 运行所需的功耗通常低于一颗完整的 CPU，因此能效较高。FPGA 集成到计算机系统中的方式举例来说包括：用作设备控制器、处理传感器数据、执行密码运算，以及测试新的硬件设计（由于可重编程，设计可以在 FPGA 上实现、调试和测试）。FPGA 可以被设计成包含大量简单处理单元的电路。FPGA 还是低延迟器件，可以直接连接到系统总线上。因此，人们用它来实现非常快速的并行计算，这类计算的特点是：在多个数据输入通道上进行规则的、相互独立的并行处理。不过，对 FPGA 重新编程需要很长时间，因此它的用途仅限于加速并行工作负载中的某些特定部分，或运行固定不变的程序负载 2 。 An FPGA is an integrated circuit that consists of gates, memory, and interconnection components. They are reprogrammable, meaning that they can be reconfigured to implement specific functionality in hardware, and they are often used to prototype application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs). FPGAs typically require less power to run than a full CPU, resulting in energy-efficient operation. Some example ways in which FPGAs are integrated into a computer system include as device controllers, for sensor data processing, for cryptography, and for testing new hardware designs (because they are reprogrammable, designs can be implemented, debugged, and tested on an FPGA). FPGAs can be designed as a circuit with a high number of simple processing units. FPGAs are also low-latency devices that can be directly connected to system buses. As a result, they have been used to implement very fast parallel computation that consists of regular patterns of independent parallel processing on several data input channels. However, reprogramming FPGAs takes a long time, and their use is limited to supporting fast execution of specific parts of parallel workloads or for running a fixed program workload 2 . 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· FPGA 厂商格局 AMD 于 2022-02-14 完成对 Xilinx 的收购（2020-10-27 宣布） AMD 公告 ；Intel 于 2025 年 9 月把 Altera 51% 股权售予 Silver Lake（Intel 保留 49%），Altera 成为独立的 FPGA 公司 Altera 公告 。两大 FPGA 厂商一家并入 CPU/GPU 厂商、一家独立。 GPU 与 Cell 处理器 GPUs and Cell Processors Cell 处理器是一种多核处理器，由一个通用处理器和多个协处理器组成，这些协处理器专门用于加速某一类计算，例如多媒体处理。索尼 PlayStation 3 游戏机是第一个采用 Cell 架构的系统，它利用 Cell 协处理器实现快速图形处理。 A Cell processor is a multicore processor consisting of one general-purpose processor and multiple co-processors that are specialized to accelerate a specific type of computation, such as multimedia processing. The Sony PlayStation 3 gaming system was the first Cell architecture, using the Cell coprocessors for fast graphics. 译注 补充两点背景：① PS3 其实另有一颗 NVIDIA 设计的 RSX 图形芯片负责主要的图形渲染，Cell 的 8 个 SPE 协处理器更多用于物理、音频、视频解码等计算，也可以辅助图形处理。② Cell 后来还被 IBM 用在 Roadrunner 超级计算机上，它在 2008 年成为世界上第一台持续性能突破 1 PetaFLOPS（每秒千万亿次浮点运算）的机器。Cell 架构之后没有后续产品，但”一个通用核 + 多个专用核”的思路在今天的手机/笔记本 SoC 里随处可见。 GPU 负责计算机图形计算——它们对图像数据进行运算，以实现高速图形渲染和图像处理。GPU 将计算结果写入帧缓冲区（frame buffer），再由帧缓冲区把数据送到计算机的显示器上。在电脑游戏应用的推动下，如今台式机和笔记本电脑都标配了复杂的 GPU。 GPUs perform computer graphics computations — they operate on image data to enable high-speed graphics rendering and image processing. A GPU writes its results to a frame buffer, which delivers the data to the computer’s display. Driven by computer gaming applications, today sophisticated GPUs come standard in desktop and laptop systems. 在 2000 年代中期，并行计算研究者认识到，将加速器与计算机的 CPU 核心结合使用来支持通用并行计算具有很大潜力。 In the mid 2000s, parallel computing researchers recognized the potential of using accelerators in combination with a computer’s CPU cores to support general-purpose parallel computing. 15.1.2. GPU 体系结构概览 15.1.2. GPU architecture overview GPU 硬件是为计算机图形和图像处理而设计的。从历史上看，GPU 的发展一直由电子游戏产业推动。为了支持更精细的画面和更快的帧渲染，一块 GPU 设备包含数千个专用处理器，它们专门被设计用来高效地并行处理图像数据，例如二维图像中各个像素的值。 GPU hardware is designed for computer graphics and image processing. Historically, GPU development has been driven by the video game industry. To support more detailed graphics and faster frame rendering, a GPU device consists of thousands of special-purpose processors, specifically designed to efficiently manipulate image data, such as the individual pixel values of a two-dimensional image, in parallel. GPU 所实现的硬件执行模型是 单指令多线程 （single instruction/multiple thread，SIMT），它是 SIMD 的一种变体。SIMT 类似于多线程版的 SIMD：同一条指令由运行在各个处理单元上的多个线程以锁步方式执行。在 SIMT 中，线程总数可以多于处理单元总数，因此需要把多组线程调度到处理器上，去执行同一段指令序列。 The hardware execution model implemented by GPUs is single instruction/multiple thread (SIMT), a variation of SIMD. SIMT is like multithreaded SIMD, where a single instruction is executed in lockstep by multiple threads running on the processing units. In SIMT, the total number of threads can be larger than the total number of processing units, requiring the scheduling of multiple groups of threads on the processors to execute the same sequence of instructions. 译注 · SIMT 与 SIMD 的区别 对程序员来说，最大的区别是：SIMD 要你 显式 操作向量寄存器（比如用 AVX intrinsics 一次算 8 个 float）；SIMT 让你写 普通的标量代码 ，按”一个线程处理一个元素”来思考，硬件再把 32 个线程打包成一个 warp 去执行。当一个 warp 内的线程走进 if/else 的不同分支时，硬件会把两个分支依次执行、并屏蔽掉不该执行的线程，这叫 分支发散 （warp divergence），会降低效率——这是写 GPU 代码时要注意的第一个性能陷阱。 举个例子，NVIDIA 的 GPU 由若干个流式多处理器（streaming multiprocessor，SM）组成，每个 SM 都有自己的执行控制单元和存储空间（寄存器、L1 缓存和共享内存）。每个 SM 包含若干个标量处理器（scalar processor，SP）核心。SM 中有一个线程束调度器（warp scheduler），负责调度 warp （线程束，即一组应用程序线程），让它们在 SP 核心上以锁步方式执行。在锁步执行中，一个 warp 中的每个线程在每个周期都执行同一条指令，但处理的数据不同。例如，如果应用程序要把一张彩色图像转换为灰度图，那么 warp 中的每个线程会同时执行同一段指令序列，把一个像素的 RGB 值设置成对应的灰度值。warp 中的每个线程在不同的像素数据上执行这些指令，于是图像中的多个像素被并行地更新。由于线程是以锁步方式执行的，处理器的设计可以得到简化，让多个核心共享同一套指令控制单元。每个单元都包含缓存和多个寄存器，用来存放由这些并行处理核心以锁步方式处理的数据。 As an example, NVIDIA GPUs consist of several streaming multiprocessors (SMs), each of which has its own execution control units and memory space (registers, L1 cache, and shared memory). Each SM consists of several scalar processor (SP) cores. The SM includes a warp scheduler that schedules warps , or sets of application threads, to execute in lockstep on its SP cores. In lockstep execution, each thread in a warp executes the same instruction each cycle but on different data. For example, if an application is changing a color image to grayscale, each thread in a warp executes the same sequence of instructions at the same time to set a pixel’s RGB value to its grayscale equivalent. Each thread in the warp executes these instructions on a different pixel data value, resulting in multiple pixels of the image being updated in parallel. Because the threads are executed in lockstep, the processor design can be simplified so that multiple cores share the same instruction control units. Each unit contains cache memory and multiple registers that it uses to hold data as it’s manipulated in lockstep by the parallel processing cores. 译注 原书的 SP 核心，就是 NVIDIA 文档中常说的 CUDA Core （例如 H100 的每个 SM 有 128 个 FP32 CUDA Core，见 NVIDIA Hopper 架构详解 ）。 迄今为止，NVIDIA GPU 的 warp 大小一直是 32 个线程 （AMD GPU 对应的概念叫 wavefront，传统上是 64，RDNA 架构起支持 32）。代码里不要写死，可以用内置变量 warpSize 。 这里说的”共享内存”（shared memory）是 SM 内部一块由程序员显式管理的片上高速存储（类似软件管理的缓存），只在同一个线程块内共享，和第 14 章”共享内存多线程”里的共享内存不是一回事，注意区分。 图 1 展示了一个简化的 GPU 体系结构，其中包括其中一个 SM 单元的详细视图。每个 SM 由多个 SP 核心、一个线程束调度器、一个执行控制单元、一个 L1 缓存和一块共享内存空间组成。 Figure 1 shows a simplified GPU architecture that includes a detailed view of one of its SM units. Each SM consists of multiple SP cores, a warp scheduler, an execution control unit, an L1 cache, and shared memory space. 图 1. 一个简化的 GPU 体系结构示例，共有 2,048 个核心。图中 GPU 被划分为 64 个 SM 单元，并展示了其中一个 SM 的细节，它由 32 个 SP 核心组成。SM 的线程束调度器把线程 warp 调度到它的 SP 上执行。一个 warp 中的线程在 SP 核心上以锁步方式执行。 Figure 1. An example of a simplified GPU architecture with 2,048 cores. This shows the GPU divided into 64 SM units, and the details of one SM consisting of 32 SP cores. The SM’s warp scheduler schedules thread warps on its SPs. A warp of threads executes in lockstep on the SP cores. 译注 · 图中标签 GPU Global Memory＝GPU 全局内存（即显存）；L2 Cache＝所有 SM 共享的二级缓存；Interface to Host＝与主机（CPU）的接口（通常是 PCIe）；右侧放大的 SM 中：Warp Scheduler & Execution Cntrl＝线程束调度器与执行控制，Register File＝寄存器文件，L1 Cache＝一级缓存，Shared Memory＝共享内存。图中 4 组 × 16 个 SM ＝ 64 个 SM，每个 SM 32 个 SP，共 2,048 个核心。 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· 真实 GPU 的规模 本图示意 NVIDIA H100 SXM5（2022） SM 数 64 132（完整芯片 144） 每 SM 的 FP32 核 32 128 FP32 核总数 2,048 16,896 显存 — 80 GB HBM3，> 3 TB/s；L2 50 MB 来源： NVIDIA Hopper 架构详解 。下一代 Blackwell 有 2,080 亿晶体管，由两颗裸片经 10 TB/s 互连组成一颗 GPU，支持 FP4，第五代 NVLink 最多连 576 颗 GPU。 NVIDIA Blackwell 15.1.3. GPGPU 计算 15.1.3. GPGPU Computing 通用 GPU （General Purpose GPU，GPGPU）计算是指把专用的 GPU 处理器用于通用的并行计算任务。GPGPU 计算把主机（host）CPU 核心上的计算与 GPU 处理器上的 SIMT 计算结合起来。GPGPU 计算最适合这样的并行应用（或应用中的某些部分）：它们可以被构造成在多维数据网格上进行的流式处理（stream processing）计算。 General Purpose GPU (GPGPU) computing applies special-purpose GPU processors to general-purpose parallel computing tasks. GPGPU computing combines computation on the host CPU cores with SIMT computation on the GPU processors. GPGPU computing performs best on parallel applications (or parts of applications) that can be constructed as a stream processing computation on a grid of multidimensional data. 主机操作系统并不管理 GPU 的处理器和内存。因此，程序员需要自己在 GPU 上为程序数据分配空间，并在主机内存与 GPU 内存之间复制数据。GPGPU 编程语言和库通常会提供访问 GPU 内存的编程接口，向程序员隐藏显式管理 GPU 内存的部分甚至全部难度。例如在 CUDA 中，程序员可以调用 CUDA 库函数，显式地在 GPU 上分配 CUDA 内存，并在 GPU 上的 CUDA 内存与主机内存之间复制数据。CUDA 程序员也可以使用 CUDA 统一内存（unified memory），它是 CUDA 在主机内存和 GPU 内存之上抽象出的单一内存空间。CUDA 统一内存向 CUDA 程序员隐藏了 GPU 内存与主机内存相互分离这一事实，以及两者之间的内存复制。 The host operating system does not manage the GPU’s processors or memory. As a result, space for program data needs to be allocated on the GPU and the data copied between the host memory and the GPU memory by the programmer. GPGPU programming languages and libraries typically provide programming interfaces to GPU memory that hide some or all of the difficulty of explicitly managing GPU memory from the programmer. For example, in CUDA a programmer can include calls to CUDA library functions to explicitly allocate CUDA memory on the GPU and to copy data between CUDA memory on the GPU and host memory. A CUDA programmer can also use CUDA unified memory, which is CUDA’s abstraction of a single memory space on top of host and GPU memory. CUDA unified memory hides the separate GPU and host memory, and the memory copies between the two, from the CUDA programmer. 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· 统一内存走向硬件 NVIDIA Grace Hopper（GH200） ：72 核 Arm CPU 与 Hopper GPU 之间用 NVLink-C2C 相连，带宽 900 GB/s（约 PCIe Gen5 x16 的 7 倍）， 硬件保证一致性 ，CPU 和 GPU 线程可同时透明访问对方内存并做原子操作。 NVIDIA 博客 AMD Instinct MI300A （2023-12 发布）：Zen 4 CPU 与 CDNA3 GPU 封装在一起， 共用 128 GB HBM3 （5.3 TB/s） AMD 产品页 ；AMD 文档称其为带硬件缓存一致性的完全统一内存架构 AMD MI300A 概览 。超算 El Capitan 就用它。 GPU 对线程同步的支持也很有限，这意味着 GPGPU 并行计算尤其适合这样的并行应用：要么是易并行（embarrassingly parallel）的，要么包含大量相互独立、基于流的并行计算且同步点很少。GPU 是大规模并行处理器，任何对数据执行长串相互独立、相同（或基本相同）计算步骤的程序，都可能非常适合作为 GPGPU 并行应用。当主机内存与设备内存之间的内存复制较少时，GPGPU 计算的表现也会更好。如果 GPU 与 CPU 之间的数据传输占据了大部分执行时间，或者应用需要细粒度的同步，那么 GPGPU 计算的表现可能不佳，与程序的 CPU 多线程版本相比几乎没有提升，甚至毫无提升。 GPUs also provide limited support for thread synchronization, which means that GPGPU parallel computing performs particularly well for parallel applications that are either embarrassingly parallel or have large extents of independent parallel stream-based computation with very few synchronization points. GPUs are massively parallel processors, and any program that performs long sequences of independent identical (or mostly identical) computation steps on data may perform well as a GPGPU parallel application. GPGPU computing also performs well when there are few memory copies between host and device memory. If GPU-CPU data transfer dominates execution time, or if an application requires fine-grained synchronization, GPGPU computing may not perform well or provide much, if any, gain over a multithreaded CPU version of the program. 译注 · 判断”值不值得上 GPU”的粗略算法 一个常用的思考工具是 算术强度 （arithmetic intensity）＝ 每从内存搬运 1 字节数据所做的浮点运算次数，以及据此画出的 Roofline 模型 。本节后面的例子”向量乘一个标量”每读写 8 字节只做 1 次乘法，算术强度极低，在真实机器上几乎一定是被内存带宽（以及 CPU↔GPU 的 PCIe 传输）卡住的——它适合用来学习 CUDA 语法，但不是 GPU 能体现优势的场景。矩阵乘法、卷积这类每个数据被反复使用的计算才是 GPU 的主场，这也是深度学习和 GPU 绑定在一起的根本原因。 15.1.4. CUDA 15.1.4. CUDA CUDA（Compute Unified Device Architecture，统一计算设备架构） 3 是 NVIDIA 为在其图形设备上进行 GPGPU 计算而提供的编程接口。CUDA 是为异构计算而设计的：程序中的一些函数运行在主机 CPU 上，另一些运行在 GPU 设备上。程序员通常用 C 或 C++ 编写 CUDA 程序，用注解（annotation）标明哪些是 CUDA 核函数，并调用 CUDA 库函数来管理 GPU 设备内存。CUDA 核函数 （kernel function）是在 GPU 上执行的函数，而 CUDA 线程 是 CUDA 程序中最基本的执行单位。CUDA 线程以 warp 为单位进行调度，在 GPU 的 SM 上以锁步方式执行，各自在 GPU 内存中属于自己的那部分数据上执行 CUDA 核函数代码。核函数用 global 注解，以区别于主机函数。CUDA device 函数是可以从 CUDA 核函数中调用的辅助函数。 CUDA (Compute Unified Device Architecture) 3 is NVIDIA’s programming interface for GPGPU computing on its graphics devices. CUDA is designed for heterogeneous computing in which some program functions run on the host CPU, and others run on the GPU device. Programmers typically write CUDA programs in C or C++ with annotations that specify CUDA kernel functions, and they make calls to CUDA library functions to manage GPU device memory. A CUDA kernel function is a function that is executed on the GPU, and a CUDA thread is the basic unit of execution in a CUDA program. CUDA threads are scheduled in warps that execute in lockstep on the GPU’s SMs, executing CUDA kernel code on their part of data stored in GPU memory. Kernel functions are annotated with global to distinguish them from host functions. CUDA device functions are helper functions that can be called from a CUDA kernel function. 译注 · 原文排版问题 原网页这里显示成斜体的 global / device ，实际应为带双下划线的限定符 __global__ 和 ** __device__ **（AsciiDoc 把成对的下划线当成了斜体标记）。后面的代码清单，以及原书附带的完整代码 scalar_multiply_cuda.cu ，写的都是 __global__ void scalar_multiply(...) 。此外还有 __host__ （默认，可省略）， __host__ __device__ 可同时为两端编译。 CUDA 程序的内存空间分为主机内存和 GPU 内存两部分。程序必须显式地分配和释放 GPU 内存空间，用来存放由 CUDA 核函数处理的程序数据。CUDA 程序员要么显式地在主机内存与 GPU 内存之间来回复制数据，要么使用 CUDA 统一内存——它提供了一个由 GPU 和主机直接共享的内存空间视图。下面是 CUDA 基本的内存分配、内存释放以及显式内存复制函数的示例： The memory space of a CUDA program is separated into host and GPU memory. The program must explicitly allocate and free GPU memory space to store program data manipulated by CUDA kernels. The CUDA programmer must either explicitly copy data to and from the host and GPU memory, or use CUDA unified memory that presents a view of memory space that is directly shared by the GPU and host. Here is an example of CUDA’s basic memory allocation, memory deallocation, and explicit memory copy functions: /* "returns" through pass-by-pointer param dev_ptr GPU memory of size bytes * returns cudaSuccess or a cudaError value on error */ cudaMalloc(void **dev_ptr, size_t size); /* free GPU memory * returns cudaSuccess or cudaErrorInvalidValue on error */ cudaFree(void *data); /* copies data from src to dst, direction is based on value of kind * kind: cudaMemcpyHosttoDevice is copy from cpu to gpu memory * kind: cudaMemcpyDevicetoHost is copy from gpu to cpu memory * returns cudaSuccess or a cudaError value on error */ cudaMemcpy(void *dst, const void *src, size_t count, cudaMemcpyKind kind); 译注 注释中的枚举值大小写不准确，真正的名字是 cudaMemcpyHostToDevice / cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost （主机→设备 / 设备→主机），下面的完整程序里写的是对的。 这里列出的是 函数原型 而不是调用。所有这些函数都返回 cudaError_t ，真实代码应该检查返回值，常见写法是包一个宏： #define CHECK(x) do { cudaError_t e = (x); if (e != cudaSuccess) { fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", cudaGetErrorString(e)); exit(1); } } while (0) 。 使用统一内存时，把 cudaMalloc 换成 cudaMallocManaged(&ptr, size) ，CPU 和 GPU 就可以用同一个指针访问，不再需要手写 cudaMemcpy （但别忘了在 CPU 读结果前 cudaDeviceSynchronize() ）。 CUDA 线程被组织成 线程块 （block），线程块又被组织成 网格 （grid）。网格可以把线程块组织成一维、二维或三维的形式；同样，线程块也可以把线程组织成一维、二维或三维的形式。每个线程由两部分唯一确定：它在所属线程块中的 ( x , y , z ) 位置，以及该线程块在网格中的 ( x , y , z ) 位置。例如，程序员可以像下面这样定义二维的线程块和网格维度： CUDA threads are organized into blocks , and the blocks are organized into a grid . Grids can be organized into one-, two-, or three-dimensional groupings of blocks. Blocks, likewise, can be organized into one-, two-, or three-dimensional groupings of threads. Each thread is uniquely identified by its thread ( x , y , z ) position in its containing block’s ( x , y , z ) position in the grid. For example, a programmer could define two-dimensional block and grid dimensions as the following: dim3 blockDim(16,16); // 256 threads per block, in a 16x16 2D arrangement dim3 gridDim(20,20); // 400 blocks per grid, in a 20x20 2D arrangement 译注 注释的意思：每个线程块 256 个线程，按 16×16 的二维排列；每个网格 400 个线程块，按 20×20 的二维排列。另外要注意，CUDA 里 gridDim 和 blockDim 也是核函数内部可用的 内置变量名 ，这里在主机代码里用同名变量只是为了好理解，实际工程中通常起别的名字（如 grid 、 block ）以免混淆。 调用核函数时，要在调用中指定”网格中的线程块”布局和”线程块中的线程”布局。例如，下面调用一个名为 do_something 的核函数，用上面定义的 gridDim 和 blockDim 指定网格和线程块的布局（并传入参数 dev_array 和 100）： When a kernel is invoked, its blocks/grid and thread/block layout is specified in the call. For example, here is a call to a kernel function named do_something specifying the grid and block layout using gridDim and blockDim defined above (and passing parameters dev_array and 100): ret = do_something<<<gridDim,blockDim>>>(dev_array, 100); 译注 这行是示意写法，实际上 核函数的返回类型必须是 void ， ret = ...<<<...>>>(...) 无法通过编译。核函数调用是 异步 的：CPU 发起调用后立刻返回，错误要用 cudaGetLastError() （检查启动参数错误）和 cudaDeviceSynchronize() （等待执行完并取得运行时错误）来获取。 <<<...>>> 里还可以写第 3、4 个参数：动态共享内存大小和 CUDA 流（stream）。 图 2 展示了线程块二维排列的一个例子。在这个例子中，网格是一个 3 × 2 的线程块数组，每个线程块是一个 4 × 3 的线程数组。 Figure 2 shows an example of a two-dimensional arrangement of thread blocks. In this example, the grid is a 3 × 2 array of blocks, and each block is a 4 × 3 array of threads. 图 2. CUDA 线程模型。由线程块组成的网格，线程块由线程组成。线程块和线程都可以组织成一维、二维或三维的布局。本例展示了一个由二维线程块组成的网格，每个网格有 3 × 2 个线程块，每个线程块中有一组二维排列的线程，每块 4 × 3 个线程。 Figure 2. The CUDA thread model. A grid of blocks of threads. Blocks and threads can be organized into one-, two-, or three-dimensional layouts. This example shows a grid of two-dimensional blocks, 3 × 2 blocks per grid, and each block has a two-dimensional set of threads, 4 × 3 threads per block). 译注 · 用图做一道练习 图中 Block (x,y) 即 blockIdx ，Thread(x,y) 即块内的 threadIdx ；这里 blockDim = (4, 3)。以放大的 Block (2,1) 中的 Thread(1,2) 为例，代入下文的公式：row = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y = 1×3+2 = 5 ，col = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x = 2×4+1 = 9 。整个网格共 (3×4) 列 × (2×3) 行 = 12 × 6 个线程。 线程在这个布局中的位置

A Deeper Dive into C Programming 上一章已经介绍了 C 语言编程的许多基础知识，现在我们更深入地探究 C 的细节。本章会重新讨论上一章中的许多主题，如数组、字符串和结构体，并更详细地展开。我们还会介绍 C 的指针变量和动态内存分配。 指针 （pointer）为访问程序状态提供了一层间接性，而 动态内存分配 （dynamic memory allocation）让程序在运行时能够适应大小和空间需求的变化：需要时分配更多空间，不再需要时释放空间。理解了如何以及何时使用指针变量和动态内存分配，C 程序员就能设计出既强大又高效的程序。 With many of the basics of C programming covered in the previous chapter, we now dive deeper into the details of C. As the chapter progresses, we cover C file I/O and some advanced C topics including library linking and compiling to assembly code.

Parts of Program Memory and Scope 下面的 C 程序展示了函数、参数、局部变量和全局变量的例子（为缩短代码清单，省略了函数注释）： The following C program shows examples of functions, parameters, and local and global variables (function comments are omitted to shorten this code listing): /* An example C program with local and global variables */ #include <stdio.h> int max(int n1, int n2); /* function prototypes */ int change(int amt); int g_x; /* global variable: declared outside function bodies */ int main(void) { int x, result; /* local variables: declared inside function bodies */ printf("Enter a value: "); scanf("%d", &x); g_x = 10; /* global variables can be accessed in any function */ result = max(g_x, x); printf("%d is the largest of %d and %d\n", result, g_x, x); result = change(10); printf("g_x's value was %d and now is %d\n", result, g_x); return 0; } int max(int n1, int n2) { /* function with two parameters */ int val; /* local variable */ val = n1; if ( n2 > n1 ) { val = n2; } return val; } int change(int amt) { int val; val = g_x; /* global variables can be accessed in any function */ g_x += amt; return val; } 这个例子展示了作用域各不相同的程序变量。变量的 作用域 （scope）决定了它的名字在什么时候有意义。换句话说，作用域定义了一组程序代码块：在这些代码块中，变量被绑定到（关联到）某个程序内存位置，并且可以被程序代码使用。 This example shows program variables with different scope. A variable’s scope defines when its name has meaning. In other words, scope defines the set of program code blocks in which a variable is bound to (associated with) a program memory location and can be used by program code. 在任何函数体之外声明变量，就创建了一个 全局变量 （global variable）。全局变量永远处于作用域内，程序中的任何代码都可以使用它，因为它始终绑定在一个特定的内存位置上。每个全局变量都必须有唯一的名字——在程序的整个运行期间，它的名字唯一地标识程序内存中的一个特定存储位置。 Declaring a variable outside of any function body creates a global variable . Global variables remain permanently in scope and can be used by any code in the program because they’re always bound to one specific memory location. Every global variable must have a unique name — its name uniquely identifies a specific storage location in program memory for the entire duration of the program. 局部变量和参数 只在定义它们的函数内部处于作用域内。例如，参数 amt 只在 change 函数内部处于作用域内。这意味着只有 change 函数体内的语句才能访问参数 amt ，而且 amt 参数的一个实例只在函数的某一次具体执行期间才被绑定到一个特定的内存存储位置。存放参数值的空间在函数被调用时在栈上分配，在函数返回时从栈上释放。函数的每一次活动（activation）都有自己的一套参数和局部变量绑定。因此，对于递归函数调用，每次调用（或活动）都会得到一个独立的栈帧，其中包含存放其参数和局部变量的空间。 Local variables and parameters are only in scope inside the function in which they are defined. For example, the amt parameter is in scope only inside the change function. This means that only statements within the change function body can access the amt parameter, and an instance of the amt parameter is bound to a specific memory storage location only within a specific active execution of the function. Space to store a parameter’s value is allocated on the stack when the function gets called, and it is deallocated from the stack when the function returns. Each activation of a function gets its own bindings for its parameters and local variables. Thus, for recursive function calls, each call (or activation) gets a separate stack frame containing space for its parameters and local variables. 由于参数和局部变量只在定义它们的函数内部处于作用域内，不同的函数可以为局部变量和参数使用相同的名字。例如， change 和 max 函数都有一个名为 val 的局部变量。当 max 函数中的代码引用 val 时，它引用的是自己的局部变量 val ，而不是 change 函数的局部变量 val （后者在 max 函数内部不在作用域内）。 Because parameters and local variables are only in scope inside the function that defines them, different functions can use the same names for local variables and parameters. For example, both the change and the max functions have a local variable named val . When code in the max function refers to val it refers to its local variable val and not to the change function’s local variable val (which is not in scope inside the max function.) 虽然偶尔有必要在 C 程序中使用全局变量，但我们强烈建议你 尽可能避免用全局变量编程 。只使用局部变量和参数，写出的代码更模块化、更通用，也更容易调试。此外，由于函数的参数和局部变量只在函数处于活动状态时才在程序内存中分配，这样的程序可能更节省空间。 While there may occasionally be times when using global variables in C programs is necessary, we strongly recommend that you avoid programming with global variables whenever possible . Using only local variables and parameters yields code that’s more modular, more general-purpose, and easier to debug. Also, because a function’s parameters and local variables are only allocated in program memory when the function is active, they may result in more space-efficient programs. 启动一个新程序时，操作系统会为这个新程序分配地址空间。程序的 地址空间 （address space，或称内存空间）代表程序执行所需的一切的存储位置，也就是存放其指令和数据的存储空间。可以把程序的地址空间看作一个由可寻址字节组成的数组；程序地址空间中每个被使用的地址，存放着某条程序指令或某个数据值的全部或一部分（或者程序执行所需的其他一些状态）。 Upon launching a new program, the operating system allocates the new program’s address space. A program’s address space (or memory space) represents storage locations for everything it needs in its execution, namely storage for its instructions and data. A program’s address space can be thought of as an array of addressable bytes; each used address in the program’s address space stores all or part of a program instruction or data value (or some additional state necessary for the program’s execution). 程序的内存空间被划分为几个部分，每个部分用来存放进程地址空间中不同种类的实体。 图 1 展示了程序内存空间的各个组成部分。 A program’s memory space is divided into several parts, each of which is used to store a different kind of entity in the process’s address space. Figure 1 illustrates the parts of a program’s memory space. 图 1. 程序地址空间的组成部分 Figure 1. The parts of a program’s address space. 译注 · 图中内容与真实布局 图的顶部是地址较小（接近 0）的一端，依次是操作系统、代码（指令）、数据（全局变量）和堆（动态分配的内存）；另一端（最大地址处）是存放局部变量和函数参数的栈。 这是一张教学用的简化图。以 x86_64 Linux 为例，真实的划分是：用户程序使用低端约 128 TB 的虚拟地址（ 0000000000000000 – 00007fffffffffff ），内核位于高端（以 ffff8... 开头）的地址范围；地址 0 附近的一小段通常故意不映射，好让空指针解引用立刻触发段错误。 Linux 内核文档：x86_64 内存映射 程序内存的顶部保留给操作系统使用，其余部分可供正在运行的程序使用。程序的指令存放在内存的 代码 段（code section）中。例如，上面列出的程序把 main 、 max 和 change 函数的指令存放在这一内存区域。 The top of a program’s memory is reserved for use by the operating system, but the remaining parts are usable by the running program. The program’s instructions are stored in the code section of the memory. For example, the program listed above stores instructions for the main , max , and change functions in this region of memory. 局部变量和参数位于内存中 栈 （stack）所在的部分。由于栈空间的大小会随着函数的调用和返回在程序执行过程中增长和收缩，栈所在的内存部分通常被分配在内存底部附近（即最高的内存地址处），为它的变化留出空间。局部变量和参数的栈存储空间只在函数处于活动状态时才存在（位于该次函数活动在栈上的栈帧中）。 Local variables and parameters reside in the portion of memory for the stack . Because the amount of stack space grows and shrinks over the program’s execution as functions are called and returned from, the stack part of memory is typically allocated near the bottom of memory (at the highest memory addresses) to leave space for it to change. Stack storage space for local variables and parameters exists only when the function is active (within the stack frame for the function’s activation on the stack.) 全局变量存放在 数据 段（data section）中。与栈不同，数据区不会增长或收缩——全局变量的存储空间在程序的整个运行期间一直存在。 Global variables are stored in the data section. Unlike the stack, the data region does not grow or shrink — storage space for globals persists for the entire run of the program. 最后，内存中的 堆 （heap）部分是程序地址空间中与动态内存分配相关的部分。堆通常位于离栈内存很远的地方，随着运行中的程序动态分配更多空间，它会向更高的地址增长。 Finally, the heap portion of memory is the part of a program’s address space associated with dynamic memory allocation. The heap is typically located far from stack memory, and grows into higher addresses as more space is dynamically allocated by the running program.

To Exascale and Beyond: Cloud Computing, Big Data, and the Future of Computing 译注 Exascale （百亿亿次，也称 E 级）指每秒 10¹⁸ 次浮点运算（1 ExaFLOPS）。数量级依次是：Giga（10⁹）→ Tera（10¹²）→ Peta（10¹⁵，千万亿次）→ Exa（10¹⁸）。 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· E 级已经实现 2026 年 6 月第 67 期 TOP500 前五名全部 ≥ 1 ExaFLOPS（HPL，64 位浮点）： 排名 系统 所在地 ExaFLOPS 功耗 MW 1 LineShine 中国深圳 2.198 42.2 2 El Capitan 美国 LLNL 1.809 29.7 3 Frontier 美国 ORNL 1.353 24.6 4 Aurora 美国 ANL 1.012 38.7 5 JUPITER Booster 德国于利希（欧洲首台 E 级） 1.000 15.8 来源： TOP500 2026-06 Highlights 、 TOP500 榜单 技术的进步让人类能够以前所未有的速度产生数据。望远镜、生物测序仪和各类传感器等科学仪器，能以低成本产生高保真度的科学数据。在科学家们努力分析这场”数据洪流”的过程中，他们越来越依赖复杂的多节点超级计算机，而超级计算机正是 高性能计算 （high-performance computing，HPC）的基础。 Advances in technology have made it possible for humanity to produce data at a rate never seen before. Scientific instruments such as telescopes, biological sequencers, and sensors produce high-fidelity scientific data at low cost. As scientists struggle to analyze this “data deluge”, they increasingly rely on sophisticated multinode supercomputers, which form the foundation of high-performance computing (HPC). HPC 应用通常用 C、C++ 或 Fortran 等语言编写，并借助 POSIX 线程 、 OpenMP 和 MPI 等库来实现 多线程 和 消息传递 。到目前为止，本书的绝大部分内容所介绍的，都是 HPC 系统上常用的体系结构特性、语言和库。致力于推动科学进步的公司、国家实验室和其他机构通常使用 HPC 系统，它们构成了计算科学生态系统的核心。 HPC applications are typically written in languages like C, C++, or Fortran, with multithreading and message passing enabled with libraries such as POSIX threads , OpenMP , and MPI . Thus far, the vast majority of this book has described architectural features, languages, and libraries commonly leveraged on HPC systems. Companies, national laboratories, and other organizations interested in advancing science typically use HPC systems and form the core of the computational science ecosystem. 与此同时，联网设备的普及和社交媒体的无处不在，使人类毫不费力地产生了海量的在线多媒体内容，包括网页、图片、视频、推文和社交媒体帖子。据估计，所有在线数据中有 90% 是在过去两年内产生的，而且整个社会每秒产生 30 TB 的用户数据（即每天 2.5 EB）。 用户数据 的洪流为公司和机构提供了关于其用户习惯、兴趣和行为的丰富信息，也便于它们构建数据丰富的客户画像，从而更好地定制商业产品和服务。为了分析用户数据，公司通常依赖多节点的数据中心，这些数据中心与典型的超级计算机共享许多硬件体系结构组件。然而，数据中心依赖的是另一套专为互联网数据设计的软件栈。用于存储和分析大规模互联网数据的计算机系统，有时被称为 高端数据分析 （high-end data analysis，HDA）系统。Amazon、Google、Microsoft 和 Facebook 等公司在互联网数据分析方面有切身利益，它们构成了数据分析生态系统的核心。HDA 和数据分析革命大约始于 2010 年，如今已成为云计算研究的主导领域。 Meanwhile, the proliferation of internet-enabled devices and the ubiquity of social media have caused humanity to effortlessly produce large volumes of online multimedia, in the form of web pages, pictures, videos, tweets, and social media posts. It is estimated that 90% of all online data was produced in the past two years, and that society produces 30 terabytes of user data per second (or 2.5 exabytes per day). The deluge of user data offers companies and organizations a wealth of information about the habits, interests, and behavior of its users, and it facilitates the construction of data-rich customer profiles to better tailor commercial products and services. To analyze user data, companies typically rely on multinode data centers that share many of the hardware architecture components of typical supercomputers. However, these data centers rely on a different software stack designed specifically for internet-based data. The computer systems used for the storage and analysis of large-scale internet-based data are sometimes referred to as high-end data analysis (HDA) systems. Companies like Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Facebook have a vested interest in the analysis of internet data, and form the core of the data analytics ecosystem. The HDA and data analytics revolution started around 2010, and now is a dominant area of cloud computing research. 现代更新 · Facebook 更名与旧数据统计 Facebook 公司已于 2021 年 10 月更名为 Meta。 Meta 公告 本段关于 90% 数据产生于近两年、每天 2.5 EB 的数字是较早的统计口径，本次未找到可核实的最新替代数字，引用时请查阅 IDC 等机构的最新原始报告。 图 1 突出展示了 HDA 社区和 HPC 社区在所用软件上的主要差异。注意，两个社区使用的集群硬件很相似，都遵循 分布式内存 模型：每个计算节点通常有一个或多个 多核 处理器，并且常常配有 GPU 。集群硬件通常还包括一个 分布式文件系统 ，让用户和应用能够共同访问分散存放在集群多个节点本地的文件。 Figure 1 highlights the key differences in software utilized by the HDA and HPC communities. Note that both communities use similar cluster hardware that follows a distributed memory model, where each compute node typically has one or more multicore processors and frequently a GPU . The cluster hardware typically includes a distributed filesystem that allows users and applications common access to files that reside locally on multiple nodes in the cluster. 图 1. At a software level, data centers typically employ virtual machines, large distributed databases, and frameworks that enable high-throughput analysis of internet data. The term cloud refers to the data storage and computing power components of HDA data centers. 本节我们简要介绍云计算、一些常用于支撑云计算的软件（具体来说是 MapReduce），以及未来面临的一些挑战。请注意，本节并不打算深入探讨这些概念；我们鼓励感兴趣的读者阅读所引用的资料以了解更多细节。 In this section, we take a brief look at cloud computing, some of the software commonly used to enable cloud computing (specifically MapReduce), and some challenges for the future. Please note that this section is not meant to be an in-depth look at these concepts; we encourage interested readers to explore the referenced sources for greater detail. 15.3.1. 云计算 15.3.1. Cloud Computing 云计算 （cloud computing）是指为获取各种服务而使用或租用云。云计算让计算基础设施能够像”公用事业”（utility）一样运作：少数几家集中的提供商通过互联网，向用户和机构提供（看似无限的）计算能力，用户和机构按需选择用多少，并按使用量付费。云计算有三大支柱：软件即服务（SaaS）、基础设施即服务（IaaS）和平台即服务（PaaS） 1 。 Cloud computing is the use or lease of the cloud for a variety of services. Cloud computing enables computing infrastructure to act as a “utility”: a few central providers give users and organizations access to (a seemingly infinite amount of) compute power through the internet, with users and organizations choosing to use as much as they want and paying according to their level of use. Cloud computing has three main pillars: software as a service (SaaS), infrastructure as a service (IaaS), and platform as a service (PaaS) 1 . 软件即服务（SaaS） Software as a Service 软件即服务 （software as a service，SaaS）是指通过云直接提供给用户的软件。大多数人都在使用云计算的这一支柱，甚至没有意识到这一点。许多人每天使用的应用（例如网页邮箱、社交媒体和视频流媒体）都依赖于云基础设施。以网页邮箱这个经典应用为例：用户可以从任何设备登录并访问自己的网页邮箱，收发邮件，而且似乎永远不会用完存储空间。感兴趣的机构也可以反过来”租用”云邮件服务，为自己的客户和员工提供电子邮件，而无需承担自己运行该服务的硬件和维护成本。SaaS 支柱中的服务完全由云提供商管理；机构和用户（除了也许配置几项设置之外）不需要管理应用、数据、软件或硬件基础设施的任何部分——如果它们想在自己的硬件上搭建这个服务，这些都是必不可少的。在云计算出现之前，想为用户提供网页邮箱的机构需要有自己的基础设施，以及专门维护它的 IT 支持人员。SaaS 提供商的常见例子包括 Google 的 G Suite 和 Microsoft 的 Office 365。 Software as a service (SaaS) refers to software provided directly to users through the cloud. Most people utilize this pillar of cloud computing without even realizing it. Applications that many people use daily (e.g., web mail, social media, and video streaming) depend upon cloud infrastructure. Consider the classic application of web mail. Users are able to log on and access their web mail from any device, send and receive mail, and seemingly never run out of storage space. Interested organizations can in turn “rent” cloud email services to provide email to their own clients and employees, without incurring the hardware and maintenance cost of running the service themselves. Services in the SaaS pillar are managed completely by cloud providers; organizations and users do not (beyond configuring a few settings, perhaps) manage any part of the application, data, software, or hardware infrastructure, all which would be necessary if they were trying to set up the service on their own hardware. Prior to the advent of cloud computing, organizations interested in providing web mail for their users would need their own infrastructure and dedicated IT support staff to maintain it. MapReduce 云系统上最著名的编程范式，大概要数 MapReduce 3 。虽然 MapReduce 起源于函数式编程中的 Map 和 Reduce 操作，但 Google 是第一个把这个概念用于分析海量 Web 数据的。MapReduce 让 Google 处理 Web 查询的速度比竞争对手更快，助力 Google 迅速崛起，成为人们首选的 Web 服务提供商，以及今天的互联网巨头。 Perhaps the most famous programming paradigm used on cloud systems is MapReduce 3 . Although MapReduce’s origins lay in functional programming’s Map and Reduce operations, Google was the first to apply the concept to analyzing large quantities of web data. MapReduce enabled Google to perform web queries faster than its competitors, and enabled Google’s meteoric rise as the go-to web service provider and internet giant it is today. 译注 准确地说，MapReduce 在 Google 内部主要用于 离线批处理 ——例如构建网页索引（ 2004 年的论文 提到，Google 用 MapReduce 重写了生产环境的索引系统）——而不是直接响应用户的实时搜索查询。原书”perform web queries faster”的说法是一种简化。 理解 Map 与 Reduce 操作 Understanding Map and Reduce Operations MapReduce 范式中的 map 和 reduce 函数，源自函数式编程中 Map 和 Reduce 这两种数学运算。本节通过回顾本书前面出现过的一些例子，简要讨论这些数学运算是如何工作的。 The map and reduce functions in the MapReduce paradigm are based on the mathematical operations of Map and Reduce from functional programming. In this section, we briefly discuss how these mathematical operations work by revisiting some examples presented earlier in the book. Map 操作通常把同一个函数应用于集合中的所有元素。熟悉 Python 的读者可能最容易从 Python 的列表推导式（list comprehension）功能中认出这种功能。例如， 表 1 中的两段代码都在 Python 中实现了标量乘法： The Map operation typically applies the same function to all the elements in a collection. Readers familiar with Python may recognize this functionality most readily in the list comprehension feature in Python. For example, the following two code snippets in Table 1 perform scalar multiplication in Python: 表 1. 使用循环与使用列表推导式的标量乘法对比。 Table 1. Comparison scalar multiplication using loop and list comprehension. 常规的标量乘法 （Regular scalar multiply） ''' The typical way to perform scalar multiplication ''' # array is an array of numbers # s is an integer def scalarMultiply(array, s): for i in range(len(array)): array[i] = array[i] * s return array # call the scalarMultiply function: myArray = [1, 3, 5, 7, 9] result = scalarMultiply(myArray, 2) #prints [2, 6, 10, 14, 18] print(result) 译注 代码注释：执行标量乘法的常规方式；array 是一个数字数组，s 是一个整数；调用 scalarMultiply 函数；输出 [2, 6, 10, 14, 18]。 使用列表推导式的标量乘法 （Scalar multiply with list comprehension） ''' Equivalent program that performs scalar multiplication with list comprehension ''' # multiplies two numbers together def multiply(num1, num2): return num1 * num2 # array is an array of numbers # s is an integer def scalarMultiply(array, s): # using list comprehension return [multiply(x, s) for x in array] # call the scalarMultiply function: myArray = [1, 3, 5, 7, 9] result = scalarMultiply(myArray, 2) # prints [2, 6, 10, 14, 18] print(result) 译注 代码注释：用列表推导式实现标量乘法的等价程序；把两个数相乘。Python 里也有直接对应 Map / Reduce 的内置函数： list(map(lambda x: x * s, array)) ，以及 functools.reduce(lambda a, b: a + b, result) 。 列表推导式把同一个函数（在本例中，是把数组元素与标量值 s 相乘）应用到 array 中的每一个元素 x 上。 The list comprehension applies the same function (in this case, multiplying an array element with scalar value s ) to every element x in array . 一次 Reduce 操作接受一个元素集合，并用某个共同的函数把它们组合成单个值。例如，Python 的 sum 函数的行为就类似于 Reduce 操作：它接受一个集合（通常是 Python 列表），并用加法把所有元素组合在一起。例如，对 表 1 中 scalarMultiply 函数返回的 result 数组的所有元素应用加法，得到的总和是 50。 A single Reduce operation takes a collection of elements and combines them together into a single value using some common function. For example, the Python function sum acts similarly to a Reduce operation, as it takes a collection (typically a Python list) and combines all the elements together using addition. So, for example, applying addition to all the elements in the result array returned from the scalarMultiply function in Table 1 yields a combined sum of 50. MapReduce 编程模型 The MapReduce Programming Model MapReduce 的一个关键特性是它简化的编程模型。开发者只需要实现两类函数： map 和 reduce ；其余的工作都由底层的 MapReduce 框架自动完成。 A key feature of MapReduce is its simplified programming model. Developers need to implement only two types of functions, map and reduce ; the underlying MapReduce framework automates the rest of the work. 由程序员编写的 map 函数接受一个输入 ( key , value ) 对，输出一系列中间 ( key , value ) 对，这些中间结果被写入一个由所有节点共享的分布式文件系统。然后，一个通常由 MapReduce 框架定义的合并器（combiner）按 key 对这些 ( key , value ) 对进行聚合，生成 ( key ,list( value )) 对，并传给程序员定义的 reduce 函数。 reduce 函数以一个 ( key ,list( value )) 对作为输入，通过某种由程序员定义的操作把所有的值组合在一起，形成最终的 ( key , value )，其中输出的 value 就是归约操作的结果。 reduce 函数的输出被写入分布式文件系统，通常也会输出给用户。 The programmer-written map function takes an input ( key , value ) pair and outputs a series of intermediate ( key , value ) pairs that are written to a distributed filesystem shared among all the nodes. A combiner that is typically defined by the MapReduce framework then aggregates ( key , value ) pairs by key, to produce ( key ,list( value )) pairs that are passed to the programmer-defined reduce function. The reduce function then takes as input a ( key ,list( value )) pair and combines all the values together through some programmer-defined operation to form a final ( key , value ), where the value in this output corresponds to the result of the reduction operation. The output from the reduce function is written to the distributed filesystem and usually output to the user. 译注 · 与原论文的术语差异（重要） 对照 Dean & Ghemawat 2004 年的 原论文 （第 3.1 节执行流程、第 4.3 节 Combiner Function），这一段有两处与通行说法不同，读其他资料时容易混淆： 按 key 把中间结果分组、排序并送到对应 reducer 的过程，通常叫 shuffle（洗牌）/ sort 阶段，由框架完成。论文中的 combiner 是另一个东西：一个 可选的、由用户提供 的函数，在 map 端先做一次局部归约（比如把同一台机器上的 1000 个 (the, 1) 先合并成 (the, 1000) ），以减少网络传输量。 在原论文的实现中，map 输出的中间结果写在 map 工作节点的本地磁盘 上，reduce 任务再通过远程读取把它们拉过来；只有 reduce 的 最终输出 才写入分布式文件系统（GFS）。 为了说明如何用 MapReduce 模型把程序并行化，我们来讨论词频统计（Word Frequency）程序。词频统计的目标是确定一个大型文本语料库中每个单词出现的频率。 To illustrate how to use the MapReduce model to parallelize a program, we discuss the Word Frequency program. The goal of Word Frequency is to determine the frequency of each word in a large text corpus. Distributed Memory Systems, Message Passing, and MPI 第 14 章介绍了 Pthreads 和 OpenMP 等机制，程序可以借助它们在 共享内存系统 上利用多个 CPU 核心。在这类系统中，所有核心共享同一套物理内存硬件，因此它们可以通过读写共享的内存地址来交换数据、同步各自的行为。虽然共享内存系统让通信变得相对容易，但其可扩展性受限于系统中 CPU 核心的数量。 Chapter 14 describes mechanisms like Pthreads and OpenMP that programs use to take advantage of multiple CPU cores on a shared memory system . In such systems, each core shares the same physical memory hardware, allowing them to communicate data and synchronize their behavior by reading from and writing to shared memory addresses. Although shared memory systems make communication relatively easy, their scalability is limited by the number of CPU cores in the system. 截至 2019 年，高端商用服务器 CPU 一般最多提供 64 个核心。然而对于某些任务来说，即便有几百个 CPU 核心也远远不够。例如，设想模拟地球海洋的流体动力学，或者为整个万维网的内容建立索引以构建一个搜索应用。这类庞大的任务所需的物理内存和处理器数量，超出了任何一台计算机所能提供的范围。因此，需要大量 CPU 核心的应用会运行在放弃了共享内存的系统上：它们运行在由多台计算机组成的系统中，每台计算机都有自己的 CPU 和内存，彼此通过网络通信来协调行为。 As of 2019, high-end commercial server CPUs generally provide a maximum of 64 cores. For some tasks, though, even a few hundred CPU cores isn’t close enough. For example, imagine trying to simulate the fluid dynamics of the Earth’s oceans or index the entire contents of the World Wide Web to build a search application. Such massive tasks require more physical memory and processors than any single computer can provide. Thus, applications that require a large number of CPU cores run on systems that forego shared memory.
