Debugging Assembly Code 除了在 C 和 C++ 高级语言层面调试之外，GDB 还可以在汇编代码层面调试程序。这样，GDB 可以列出函数反汇编后的代码序列、在汇编指令级别设置断点、一次一条汇编指令地单步执行程序，以及在运行时检查机器寄存器和栈、堆内存地址中存放的值。本节以 IA32 作为示例汇编语言，但这里介绍的 GDB 命令适用于 GCC 支持的任何汇编语言。需要说明的是，读者可能要在后面的章节中进一步了解汇编代码之后，才会觉得这一小节最有用。 In addition to high-level C and C++ debugging, GDB can debug a program at its assembly code level. Doing so enables GDB to list disassembled code sequences from functions, set breakpoints at the assembly instruction level, step through program execution one assembly instruction at a time, and examine the values stored in machine registers and in stack and heap memory addresses at runtime. We use IA32 as the example assembly language in this section, but the GDB commands presented here apply to any assembly language that GCC supports. We note that readers may find this subsection most useful after reading more about assembly code in later chapters. 我们用下面这个简短的 C 程序作为例子： We use the following short C program as an example: int main(void) { int x, y; x = 1; x = x + 2; x = x - 14; y = x * 100; x = x + y * 6; return 0; } 要编译成 IA32 可执行文件，使用 -m32 标志： To compile to an IA32 executable, use the -m32 flag: $ gcc -m32 -o simpleops simpleops.c 也可以选择用 gcc 的 -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables 命令行选项编译，这样生成的 IA32 代码对程序员来说更容易阅读和理解： Optionally, compiling with gcc ‘s -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables command line option generates IA32 code that’s a bit easier for the programmer to read and understand: $ gcc -m32 -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -o simpleops simpleops.c 3.5.1. 用 GDB 检查二进制代码 3.5.1. Using GDB to Examine Binary Code 本节给出一些在汇编代码层面调试这个简短 C 程序的 GDB 命令示例。下表总结了本节将演示的许多命令： In this section we show some example GDB commands to debug the short C program at the assembly code level. The following table summarizes many of the commands this section demonstrates: GDB 命令 说明 break sum 在函数 sum 的开头设置断点 break *0x0804851a 在内存地址 0x0804851a 处设置断点 disass main 反汇编 main 函数 ni 执行下一条指令 si 进入函数调用（单步执行指令） info registers 列出寄存器的内容 p $eax 打印寄存器 %eax 中存放的值 p *(int *)($ebp+8) 打印某个地址（%ebp+8）处的 int 值 x/d $ebp+8 检查某个地址处的内存内容 GDB command Description break sum Set a breakpoint at the beginning of the function sum break *0x0804851a Set a breakpoint at memory address 0x0804851a disass main Disassemble the main function ni Execute the next instruction si Step into a function call (step instruction) info registers List the register contents p $eax Print the value stored in register %eax p *(int *)($ebp+8) Print out the value of an int at an address (%ebp+8) x/d $ebp+8 Examine the contents of memory at an address 首先，编译成 IA32 汇编，并对 IA32 可执行程序 simpleops 运行 GDB： First, compile to IA32 assembly and run GDB on the IA32 executable program simpleops : $ gcc -m32 -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -o simpleops simpleops.c $ gdb ./simpleops 然后，在 main 中设置断点，再用 run 命令开始运行程序： Then, set a breakpoint in main , and then start running the program with the run command: (gdb) break main (gdb) run disass 命令反汇编程序的某些部分（列出与之对应的汇编代码）。例如，查看 main 函数的汇编指令： The disass command disassembles (lists the assembly code associated with) parts of the program. For example, to view the assembly instructions of the main function: (gdb) disass main # Disassemble the main function GDB 允许程序员在单条汇编指令处设置断点，方法是对指令的内存地址解引用： GDB allows a programmer to set breakpoints at individual assembly instructions by dereferencing the memory address of the instruction: (gdb) break *0x080483c1 # Set breakpoint at instruction at 0x080483c1 可以用 si 或 ni 一次一条汇编指令地执行程序，分别是进入下一条指令或执行下一条指令： The program’s execution can be executed one assembly instruction at a time using si or ni to step into or execute the next instruction: (gdb) ni # Execute the next instruction (gdb) si # Execute next instruction; if it is a call instruction, # then step into the function si 命令会进入函数调用，即 GDB 会让程序暂停在被调用函数的第一条指令处。 ni 命令则跳过函数调用，即 GDB 会让程序暂停在 call 指令之后的下一条指令处（在函数执行完并返回调用者之后）。 The si command steps into function calls, meaning that GDB will pause the program at the first instruction of the called function. The ni command skips over them, meaning that GDB will pause the program at the next instruction following the call instruction (after the function executes and returns to the caller). 程序员可以用 print 命令加上以 $ 为前缀的寄存器名，打印机器寄存器中存放的值： The programmer can print values stored in machine registers using the print command and the name of the register prefixed by $ : (gdb) print $eax # print the value stored in register eax display 命令会在到达断点时自动显示值： The display command automatically displays values upon reaching a breakpoint: (gdb) display $eax (gdb) display $edx info registers 命令显示所有机器寄存器中存放的值： The info registers command shows all of the values stored in the machine registers: (gdb) info registers 3.5.2. 用 DDD 在汇编层面调试 3.5.2. Using DDD to Debug at the Assembly Level DDD 调试器在另一个调试器（这里是 GDB）之上提供了图形界面。它为显示汇编代码、查看寄存器和单步执行 IA32 指令提供了很好的界面。由于 DDD 有分别显示反汇编代码、寄存器值和 GDB 命令提示符的独立窗口，在汇编代码层面调试时，它往往比 GDB 更好用。 The DDD debugger provides a graphical interface on top of another debugger (GDB in this case). It provides a nice interface for displaying assembly code, viewing registers, and stepping through IA32 instruction execution. Because DDD has separate windows for displaying disassembled code, register values, and the GDB command prompt, it’s often easier to use than GDB when debugging at the assembly code level. 要用 DDD 调试，把 gdb 换成 ddd 即可： To debug with DDD, substitute ddd for gdb : $ ddd ./simpleops GDB 提示符出现在底部窗口中，在那里可以输入 GDB 命令。虽然 DDD 为一些 GDB 命令提供了菜单选项和按钮，但使用底部的 GDB 提示符往往更方便。 The GDB prompt appears in the bottom window, where it accepts GDB commands at the prompt. Although it provides menu options and buttons for some GDB commands, often the GDB prompt at the bottom is easier to use. 选择 View → Machine Code Window 菜单选项，DDD 就会显示程序的汇编代码视图。这个选项会新建一个子窗口，列出程序的汇编代码（你可能会想把这个窗口拉大一些）。 DDD displays the assembly code view of a program by selecting the View → Machine Code Window menu option. That option creates a new subwindow with a listing of the program’s assembly code (you will likely want to resize this window to make it larger). 要在单独的窗口中查看程序所有寄存器的值，启用 Status → Registers 菜单选项。 To view all of the program’s register values in a separate window, enable the Status → Registers menu option. 3.5.3. GDB 汇编代码调试命令与示例 3.5.3. GDB Assembly Code Debugging Commands and Examples 下面是一些在汇编代码层面调试时有用的 GDB 命令的细节和示例（关于其中一些命令，特别是 print 和 x 的格式选项的更多细节，请参见 常用 GDB 命令 一节）： Here are some details and examples of GDB commands that are useful for debugging at the assembly code level (see the Common GDB Commands section for more details about some of these commands, particularly for the print and x formatting options): disass ：反汇编某个函数或某个地址范围内的代码。 disass <func_name> # Lists assembly code for function disass <start> <end> # Lists assembly instructions between start & end address disass main # Disassemble main function disass 0x1234 0x1248 # Disassemble instructions between addr 0x1234 & 0x1248 disass : Disassemble code for a function or range of addresses. disass <func_name> # Lists assembly code for function disass <start> <end> # Lists assembly instructions between start & end address disass main # Disassemble main function disass 0x1234 0x1248 # Disassemble instructions between addr 0x1234 & 0x1248 译注 按 GDB 手册，指定地址范围时两个参数之间要用 逗号 隔开： disass 0x1234,0x1248 （结束地址不包含在内），或者 disass 0x1234,+20 表示从起始地址开始的 20 个字节。上面代码中用空格分隔的写法 GDB 不认。 GDB 手册：Machine Code break ：在某个指令地址处设置断点。 break *0x80dbef10 # Sets breakpoint at the instruction at address 0x80dbef10 break : Set a breakpoint at an instruction address. break *0x80dbef10 # Sets breakpoint at the instruction at address 0x80dbef10 stepi （ si ）、 nexti （ ni ）： stepi, si # Execute next machine code instruction, # stepping into function call if it is a call instr nexti, ni # Execute next machine code instruction, # treating function call as a single instruction stepi ( si ), nexti ( ni ) : stepi, si # Execute next machine code instruction, # stepping into function call if it is a call instr nexti, ni # Execute next machine code instruction, # treating function call as a single instruction info registers ：列出所有寄存器的值。 info registers : Lists all the register values. print ：显示一个表达式的值。 print $eax # Print the value stored in the eax register print *(int *)0x8ff4bc10 # Print int value stored at memory addr 0x8ff4bc10 print : Display the value of an expression. print $eax # Print the value stored in the eax register print *(int *)0x8ff4bc10 # Print int value stored at memory addr 0x8ff4bc10 x ：给定一个地址，显示该内存位置的内容。记住 x 的格式是粘性的，所以需要显式地改变它。 (gdb) x $ebp-4 # Examine memory at address: (contents of register ebp)-4 # if the location stores an address x/a, an int x/wd, ... (gdb) x/s 0x40062d # Examine the memory location 0x40062d as a string 0x40062d "Hello There" (gdb) x/4c 0x40062d # Examine the first 4 char memory locations # starting at address 0x40062d 0x40062d 72 'H' 101 'e' 108 'l' 108 'l' (gdb) x/d 0x40062d # Examine the memory location 0x40062d in decimal 0x40062d 72 # NOTE: units is 1 byte, set by previous x/4c command (gdb) x/wd 0x400000 # Examine memory location 0x400000 as 4 bytes in decimal 0x400000 100 # NOTE: units was 1 byte set, need to reset to w x Display the contents of the memory location given an address. Remember that the format of x is sticky, so it needs to be explicitly changed. (gdb) x $ebp-4 # Examine memory at address: (contents of register ebp)-4 # if the location stores an address x/a, an int x/wd, ... (gdb) x/s 0x40062d # Examine the memory location 0x40062d as a string 0x40062d "Hello There" (gdb) x/4c 0x40062d # Examine the first 4 char memory locations # starting at address 0x40062d 0x40062d 72 'H' 101 'e' 108 'l' 108 'l' (gdb) x/d 0x40062d # Examine the memory location 0x40062d in decimal 0x40062d 72 # NOTE: units is 1 byte, set by previous x/4c command (gdb) x/wd 0x400000 # Examine memory location 0x400000 as 4 bytes in decimal 0x400000 100 # NOTE: units was 1 byte set, need to reset to w set ：设置内存位置和寄存器的内容。 set $eax = 10 Set the value of register eax to 10 set $esp = $esp + 4 Pop a 4-byte value off the stack set *(int *)0x8ff4bc10 = 44 Store 44 at address 0x8ff4bc10 set : Set the contents of memory locations and registers. set $eax = 10 Set the value of register eax to 10 set $esp = $esp + 4 Pop a 4-byte value off the stack set *(int *)0x8ff4bc10 = 44 Store 44 at address 0x8ff4bc10 display ：每次遇到断点时打印一个表达式。 display $eax Display value of register eax display : Print an expression each time a breakpoint is hit. display $eax Display value of register eax 3.5.4. 汇编调试常用命令速查 3.5.4. Quick Summary of Common Commands for Assembly Debugging $ ddd ./a.out (gdb) break main (gdb) run (gdb) disass main # Disassemble the main function (gdb) break sum # Set a breakpoint at the beginning of a function (gdb) cont # Continue execution of the program (gdb) break *0x0804851a # Set a breakpoint at memory address 0x0804851a (gdb) ni # Execute the next instruction (gdb) si # Step into a function call (step instruction) (gdb) info registers # List the register contents (gdb) p $eax # Print the value stored in register %eax (gdb) p *(int *)($ebp+8) # Print out value of an int at addr (%ebp+8) (gdb) x/d $ebp+8 # Examine the contents of memory at the given # address (/d: prints the value as an int) (gdb) x/s 0x0800004 # Examine contents of memory at address as a string (gdb) x/wd 0xff5634 # After x/s, the unit size is 1 byte, so if want # to examine as an int specify both the width w & d

说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C3-C_debug/gdb_pthreads.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 3.6. Debugging Multithreaded Programs with GDB 由于存在多条执行流，以及并发执行的线程之间的相互作用，调试多线程程序可能很棘手。一般来说，下面这些做法能让调试多线程程序稍微容易一些： Debugging multithreaded programs can be tricky due to the multiple streams of execution and due to interactions between the concurrently executing threads. In general, here are some things to make debugging multithreaded programs a bit easier: 尽可能调试线程数尽量少的程序版本。 When possible, try to debug a version of the program with as few threads as possible. 在代码中加入调试用的 printf 语句时，打印出正在执行的线程的 ID，以便识别是哪个线程在打印，并以 
 结束这一行。 When adding debugging printf statements to the code, print out the executing thread’s ID to identify which thread is printing and end the line with a 
 . 只让其中一个线程打印它自己的信息和公共信息，以限制调试输出的数量。例如，如果每个线程都把自己的逻辑 ID 存放在名为 my_tid 的局部变量中，就可以对 my_tid 的值加一个条件判断，把调试输出限制在一个线程上，如下例所示： Limit the amount of debug output by having only one of the threads print its information and common information. For example, if each thread stores its logical ID in a local variable named my_tid , a conditional statement on the value of my_tid can be used to limit printing debug output to one thread, as illustrated in the following example: if (my_tid == 1) { printf("Tid:%d: value of count is %d and my i is %d
", my_tid, count, i); fflush(stdout); } 3.6.1. GDB 与 Pthreads 3.6.1. GDB and Pthreads GDB 调试器对调试多线程程序有专门的支持，包括为单个线程设置断点、检查单个线程的栈。在 GDB 中调试 Pthreads 程序时要注意，每个线程至少有三种标识符： The GDB debugger has specific support for debugging threaded programs, including setting breakpoints for individual threads and examining the stacks of individual threads. One thing to note when debugging Pthreads programs in GDB is that there are at least three identifiers for each thread: Pthreads 库为线程分配的 ID（它的 pthread_t 值）。 The Pthreads library’s ID for the thread (its pthread_t value). 操作系统为线程分配的轻量级进程（lightweight process，LWP）ID。操作系统部分地用这个 ID 来跟踪该线程，以便进行调度。 The operating system’s lightweight process (LWP) ID value for the thread. This ID is used in part for the OS to keep track of this thread for scheduling purposes. GDB 为线程分配的 ID。在 GDB 命令中指定某个线程时用的就是这个 ID。 The GDB ID for the thread. This is the ID to use when specifying a specific thread in GDB commands. 这几种线程 ID 之间的具体关系，因操作系统和 Pthreads 库实现的不同而有所差异，但在大多数系统上，Pthreads ID、LWP ID 和 GDB 线程 ID 之间是一一对应的。 The specific relationship between thread IDs can differ from one OS and Pthreads library implementation to another, but on most systems there is a one-to-one-to-one correspondence between a Pthreads ID, an LWP ID, and a GDB thread ID. 我们介绍在 GDB 中调试多线程程序的一些基础知识。关于 在 GDB 中调试多线程程序 的更多信息，请参见该链接。 We present a few GDB basics for debugging threaded programs in GDB. See the following for more information about debugging threaded programs in GDB . 3.6.2. GDB 中与线程相关的命令： 3.6.2. GDB Thread-Specific Commands: 开启线程启动和退出事件的打印： set print thread-events Enable printing thread start and exit events: set print thread-events 列出程序中现有的所有线程（列出的第一个值是 GDB 线程编号，遇到断点的那个线程用 * 标出）： info threads List all existing threads in the program (the GDB thread number is the first value listed and the thread that hit the breakpoint is denoted with an * ): info threads 切换到某个特定线程的执行上下文（例如，以便执行 where 查看它的栈），用线程 ID 指定线程： thread <threadno> thread 12 # Switch to thread 12's execution context where # Thread 12's stack trace Switch to a specific thread’s execution context (for example, to examine its stack when executing where ), specify the thread by its thread ID: thread <threadno> thread 12 # Switch to thread 12's execution context where # Thread 12's stack trace 只为某个特定线程设置断点。在设置断点的代码位置执行的其他线程，不会触发这个断点使程序暂停并打印 GDB 提示符： break <where> thread <threadno> break foo thread 12 # Break when thread 12 executes function foo Set a breakpoint for just a particular thread. Other threads executing at the point in the code where the breakpoint is set will not trigger the breakpoint to pause the program and print the GDB prompt: break <where> thread <threadno> break foo thread 12 # Break when thread 12 executes function foo 要把某条 GDB 命令应用到所有线程或部分线程，可以在 GDB 命令前加上前缀 thread apply <threadno | all> ，其中 threadno 指 GDB 线程 ID： thread apply <threadno|all> command 这并不适用于所有 GDB 命令，尤其是设置断点，所以设置线程专属的断点时要改用下面的语法： break <where> thread <threadno> To apply a specific GDB command to all or to a subset of threads, by adding the prefix thread apply <threadno | all> to a GDB command, where threadno refers to the GDB thread ID: thread apply <threadno|all> command This doesn’t work for every GDB command, setting breakpoints in particular, so use this syntax instead for setting thread-specific breakpoints: break <where> thread <threadno> 默认情况下，到达断点时，GDB 会暂停所有线程，直到用户输入 cont 。用户可以改变这一行为，要求 GDB 只暂停遇到断点的那些线程，让其他线程继续执行。 Upon reaching a breakpoint, by default, GDB pauses all threads until the user types cont . The user can change the behavior to request that GDB only pause the threads that hit a breakpoint, allowing other threads to continue executing. 译注 这种模式在 GDB 中叫 不停止模式 （non-stop mode），用 set non-stop on 开启（需要在程序开始运行之前设置）；默认的「一停全停」叫 all-stop 模式。 GDB 手册：Non-Stop Mode 3.6.3. 示例： 3.6.3. Examples: 下面展示一些 GDB 命令，以及在由 racecond.c 文件编译出的多线程可执行文件上运行 GDB 时的输出。 We show some GDB commands and output from a GDB run on a multithreaded executable compiled from the file racecond.c . 这个有缺陷的程序在访问共享变量 count 时缺少同步。因此，程序的不同次运行会得出不同的 count 最终值，这表明存在竞态条件。例如，下面是用五个线程运行程序两次、得出不同结果的情形： This errant program lacks synchronization around accesses to the shared variable count . As a result, different runs of the program produce different final values for count , indicating a race condition. For example, here are two runs of the program with five threads that produce different results: ./a.out 5 hello I'm thread 0 with pthread_id 139673141077760 hello I'm thread 3 with pthread_id 139673115899648 hello I'm thread 4 with pthread_id 139673107506944 hello I'm thread 1 with pthread_id 139673132685056 hello I'm thread 2 with pthread_id 139673124292352 count = 159276966 ./a.out 5 hello I'm thread 0 with pthread_id 140580986918656 hello I'm thread 1 with pthread_id 140580978525952 hello I'm thread 3 with pthread_id 140580961740544 hello I'm thread 2 with pthread_id 140580970133248 hello I'm thread 4 with pthread_id 140580953347840 count = 132356636 修复方法是用一个 pthread_mutex_t 变量，把对 count 的访问放进临界区。如果用户仅凭查看 C 代码看不出这个修复方法，那么在 GDB 中运行并在访问 count 变量的位置附近设置断点，也许能帮助程序员发现问题。 The fix is to put accesses to count inside a critical section, using a pthread_mutex_t variable. Summary 本章结束了我们对 C 语言的介绍。与其他高级编程语言相比，C 是一门相对小巧的语言，程序员用为数不多的几种基本构造来搭建自己的程序。由于 C 语言的抽象更接近计算机执行的底层机器码，C 程序员写出的代码可以比用其他编程语言提供的更高级抽象写成的等价代码运行得高效得多。尤其是，C 程序员对程序如何使用内存有更多的控制，而这会对程序的性能产生重大影响。在底层控制和效率至关重要的计算机系统编程领域，C 就是那门语言。 This chapter concludes our coverage of the C programming language. Compared to other high-level programming languages, C is a relatively small programming language with a few basic constructs from which a programmer builds their program. Because C language abstractions are closer to the underlying machine code executed by the computer, a C programmer can write code that runs much more efficiently than equivalent code written using the higher-level abstractions provided by other programming languages. In particular, a C programmer has much more control over how their program uses memory, which can have a significant impact on the program’s performance. C is the language of computer systems programming where low-level control and efficiency are crucial. 在后续章节中，我们会用 C 示例来说明计算机系统是如何设计来运行程序的。 In subsequent chapters we use C examples to illustrate how a computer system is designed to run a program.

Binary and Data Representation 从简陋的石板和洞穴壁画，到书面文字和留声机唱片的纹槽，人类一直在设法记录和保存信息。本章我们将刻画人类在存储方面最新的重大突破——数字计算——是如何表示信息的，并说明如何从数字数据中解读出含义。 From simple stone tablets and cave paintings to written words and phonograph grooves, humans have perpetually sought to record and store information. In this chapter, we’ll characterize how the latest of humanity’s big storage breakthroughs, digital computing, represents information. We also illustrate how to interpret meaning from digital data. 现代计算机使用多种介质存储信息（例如磁盘、光盘、闪存、磁带和简单的电路）。我们会在后面的 第 11 章 中刻画存储设备；不过就本章的讨论而言，介质基本无关紧要——无论是激光扫描 DVD 的表面，还是磁头掠过磁盘盘片，存储设备的输出最终都是一串电信号。为了简化电路，每个信号都是 二进制 （binary）的，即只能取两种状态之一：没有电压（解释为零）和有电压（解释为一）。本章探讨系统如何把信息编码为二进制，而不管原始的存储介质是什么。 Modern computers utilize a variety of media for storing information (e.g., magnetic disks, optical discs, flash memory, tapes, and simple electrical circuits). We characterize storage devices later in Chapter 11 ; however, for this discussion, the medium is largely irrelevant — whether there’s a laser scanning the surface of a DVD or a disk head gliding over a magnetic platter, the output from the storage device is ultimately a sequence of electrical signals. To simplify the circuitry, each signal is binary , meaning it can take only one of two states: the absence of a voltage (interpreted as zero) and the presence of a voltage (one). This chapter explores how systems encode information into binary, regardless of the original storage medium. 在二进制中，每个信号对应一 位 （bit，即 binary digit，二进制数字）信息：0 或 1。所有数据都能只用 0 和 1 表示，这也许让人惊讶。当然，信息越复杂，表示它所需的位数也越多。幸运的是，位序列每增加一位，能表示的不同值的个数就翻一倍，因此一个 N 位的序列可以表示 2 N 个不同的值。 In binary, each signal corresponds to one bit (binary digit) of information: a zero or a one. It may be surprising that all data can be represented using just zeros and ones. Of course, as the complexity of information increases, so does the number of bits needed to represent it. Luckily, the number of unique values doubles for each additional bit in a bit sequence, so a sequence of N bits can represent 2 N unique values. 图 1 展示了随着位序列长度的增加，可表示值的个数如何增长。一位可以表示 两 个值：0 和 1。两位可以表示 四 个值：在两个一位值前面加上 0（00 和 01），以及在两个一位值前面加上 1（10 和 11）。任何一个扩展已有位序列的新位都遵循同样的模式：新位可以是 0 或 1，无论哪种情况，其余各位表示的值的范围都与加入新位之前相同。因此，增加位数会使新序列能表示的值的个数呈指数增长。 Figure 1 illustrates the growth in the number of representable values as the length of a bit sequence increases. A single bit can represent two values: 0 and 1. Two bits can represent four values: both of the one-bit values with a leading 0 (00 and 01), and both of the one-bit values with a leading 1 (10 and 11). The same pattern applies for any additional bit that extends an existing bit sequence: the new bit can be a 0 or 1, and in either case, the remaining bits represent the same range of values they did prior to the new bit being added. Thus, adding additional bits exponentially increases the number of values the new sequence can represent. 图 1. 用一到四位能表示的值。带下划线的位对应来自上一行的前缀。 Figure 1. The values that can be represented with one to four bits. The underlined bits correspond to the prefix coming from the row above. 由于单个位表示不了多少信息，存储系统通常把位组成更长的序列，来存储更有意义的值。最普遍的分组是 字节 （byte），即八位的集合。一个字节可以表示 2 8 = 256 个不同的值（0–255）——足以列举英语的字母和常用标点符号。字节是计算机系统中可寻址内存的最小单位，也就是说，程序不能申请少于八位的空间来存储变量。 Because a single bit doesn’t represent much information, storage systems commonly group bits into longer sequences for storing more interesting values. The most ubiquitous grouping is a byte , which is a collection of eight bits. One byte represents 2 8 = 256 unique values (0-255) — enough to enumerate the letters and common punctuation symbols of the English language. Bytes are the smallest unit of addressable memory in a computer system, meaning a program can’t ask for fewer than eight bits to store a variable. 现代 CPU 通常还把 字 （word）定义为 32 位或 64 位，取决于硬件的设计。字的大小决定了系统硬件在组件之间（例如在内存和寄存器之间）移动数据时使用的「默认」大小。存储数字需要这些更长的序列，因为程序常常需要数到比 256 更大的数！ Modern CPUs also typically define a word as either 32 bits or 64 bits, depending on the design of the hardware. The size of a word determines the “default” size a system’s hardware uses to move data from one component to another (e.g., between memory and registers). These larger sequences are necessary for storing numbers, since programs often need to count higher than 256! 如果你用 C 编过程序，就知道必须 先声明变量再使用 。这样的声明会告诉 C 编译器变量二进制表示的两个重要属性：要为它分配多少位，以及程序打算如何解释这些位。从概念上讲，位数很简单，编译器只需查一下 所声明类型对应多少位 （例如 char 是一个字节），并把这么多内存与该变量关联起来。而对一串位的解释在概念上则有趣得多。计算机内存中的所有数据都以位的形式存储，但位本身并没有 固有的 含义。例如，即使只有一位，也可以用许多不同的方式解释它的两个值：上和下、黑和白、是和否、开和关，等等。 If you’ve programmed in C, you know that you must declare a variable before using it . Such declarations inform the C compiler of two important properties regarding the variable’s binary representation: the number of bits to allocate for it, and the way in which the program intends to interpret those bits. Conceptually, the number of bits is straightforward, as the compiler simply looks up how many bits are associated with the declared type (e.g., a char is one byte) and associates that amount of memory with the variable. The interpretation of a sequence of bits is much more conceptually interesting. All data in a computer’s memory is stored as bits, but bits have no inherent meaning. For example, even with just a single bit, you could interpret the bit’s two values in many different ways: up and down, black and white, yes and no, on and off, etc. 增加位序列的长度会扩大它的解释范围。例如， char 变量使用美国信息交换标准代码（American Standard Code for Information Interchange，ASCII）编码标准，它定义了八位二进制值与英文字母和标点符号之间的对应关系。 表 1 列出了 ASCII 标准的一小部分（完整的参考可以在命令行运行 man ascii 查看）。字符 'X' 对应 01011000 并没有什么特别的原因，所以不必费力去记这张表。重要的是，每个存储字母的程序对位序列的解释必须一致，这正是 ASCII 由一个标准委员会来定义的原因。 Extending the length of a bit sequence expands the range of its interpretations. For example, a char variable uses the American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII) encoding standard, which defines how an eight-bit binary value corresponds to English letters and punctuation symbols. Table 1 shows a small subset of the ASCII standard (for a full reference, run man ascii on the command line). There’s no special reason why the character 'X' needs to correspond to 01011000, so don’t bother memorizing the table. What matters is that every program storing letters agrees on their bit sequence interpretation, which is why ASCII is defined by a standards committee. 译注 严格说 ASCII 是 7 位 编码（0–127），存在 8 位的 char 中时最高位为 0；表题中的「八位 ASCII」是一种宽松的说法。0–127 以外的值在不同的扩展编码中含义不同，这正是后来统一到 Unicode/UTF-8 的原因。 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· 今天的文本几乎都是 UTF-8 ASCII 只覆盖英文字母和常用符号。如今的文本普遍采用 Unicode 的 UTF-8 编码：它对 ASCII 范围内的字符仍用单字节、编码与 ASCII 完全相同，其他字符（包括汉字）用 2–4 个字节表示。根据 W3Techs 2026 年 11 月的统计，在已知字符编码的网站中，99.1% 使用 UTF-8。因此在 C 中处理中文时要记住：一个汉字通常占 3 个 char ， strlen 返回的是字节数而不是字符数。 W3Techs：网站字符编码统计 表 1. 八位 ASCII 字符编码标准的一小段 Table 1. For example, suppose that an image encoding scheme defines 00, 01, 10, and 11 to correspond to the colors white, orange, blue, and black. Parts b and c show the corresponding binary encoding as two-bit and byte sequences, respectively. Although this example encoding scheme is simplified for learning purposes, the general idea is similar to what real graphics systems use, albeit with many more bits for a wider range of colors. 图 2. 一幅简单的鱼图像的 (a) 图像表示、(b) 两位格子表示和 (c) 字节表示。 Figure 2. The (a) image representation, (b) two-bit cell representation, and (c) byte representation of a simple fish image. 译注 · 图中内容 鱼的背景是蓝色（10），眼白是白色（00），瞳孔是黑色（11），身体是橙色（01）。 我们刚刚介绍了两种编码方案，同一个位序列 01011010，对文本编辑器来说可能表示字符 'Z' ，而图形程序可能把它解释为鱼尾鳍的一部分。哪种解释正确取决于上下文。尽管底层的位相同，人们往往觉得某些解释比另一些容易理解得多（例如，把鱼看成彩色格子，要比看成一张字节表容易）。 Having just introduced two encoding schemes, the same bit sequence, 01011010, might mean the character 'Z' to a text editor, whereas a graphics program might interpret it as part of a fish’s tail fin. Which interpretation is correct depends on the context. Despite the underlying bits being the same, humans often find some interpretations much easier to comprehend than others (e.g., perceiving the fish as colored cells rather than a table of bytes). 本章其余部分主要讨论二进制数的表示和运算，但总体的要点值得再强调一遍：所有信息都以 0 和 1 的形式存储在计算机内存中，这些位的含义由程序或运行程序的人来解释。 The remainder of this chapter largely deals with representing and manipulating binary numbers, but the overall point bears repeating: all information is stored in a computer’s memory as 0’s and 1’s, and it’s up to programs or the people running them to interpret the meaning of those bits.

That leaves 133 - 128 = 5. 64 does not fit into 5, so d 6 should be a 0. 32 does not fit into 5, so d 5 should be a 0. 16 does not fit into 5, so d 4 should be a 0. 8 does not fit into 5, so d 3 should be a 0. 4 fits into 5, so d 2 should be a 1. That leaves 6 - 5 = 1. 2 fits does not fit into 1, so d 1 should be a 0. 1 fits into 1, so d 0 should be a 1. That leaves 1 - 1 = 0. Thus, decimal 389 corresponds to 0b110000101 . Using repeated division: 389 is odd, so d 0 should be a 1. 389 / 2 = 194, which is even, so d 1 should be a 0. 194 / 2 = 97, which is odd, so d 2 should be a 1. 97 / 2 = 48, which is even, so d 3 should be a 0. 48 / 2 = 24, which is even, so d 4 should be a 0. 24 / 2 = 12, which is even, so d 5 should be a 0. 12 / 2 = 6, which is even, so d 6 should be a 0. 6 / 2 = 3, which is odd, so d 7 should be a 1. 3 / 2 = 1, which is odd, so d 8 should be a 1. 1 / 2 = 0, so any digit numbered nine or above will be 0. Thus, decimal 389 corresponds to 0b110000101 . Number Bases and Unsigned Integers 我们已经看到， 二进制序列可以用各种非数值的方式来解释 ，现在把注意力转向数。具体来说，我们从 无符号 （unsigned）数开始，它可以解释为零或正数，但永远不会是负数（它们没有 符号 ）。 Having seen that binary sequences can be interpreted in all sorts of nonnumerical ways , let’s turn our attention to numbers. Specifically, we’ll start with unsigned numbers, which can be interpreted as zero or positive, but they can never be negative (they have no sign ). 4.1.1. 十进制数 4.1.1. Decimal Numbers 我们不从二进制开始，而是先看一看我们已经用惯了的数制—— 十进制数制 （decimal number system），它的 基数 （base）是 10。 以 10 为基数 意味着在解释和表示十进制值时有两个重要性质。 Rather than starting with binary, let’s first examine a number system we’re already comfortable using, the decimal number system , which uses a base of 10. Base 10 implies two important properties for the interpretation and representation of decimal values. 十进制数中的任何一位数字都存储 10 个不同值（0–9）之一。要存储大于 9 的值，就必须向左边多出来的一位 进位 （carry）。例如，如果某一位从它的最大值（9）开始，再加 1，结果就需要两位数字（9 + 1 = 10）。无论这一位在数中的什么位置，都遵循同样的模式（例如 50 8 0 + 2 0 = 5 10 0）。 Any individual digit in a base 10 number stores one of 10 unique values (0-9). To store a value larger than 9, the value must carry to an additional digit to the left. For example, if one digit starts at its maximum value (9) and we add 1 to it, the result requires two digits (9 + 1 = 10). The same pattern holds for any digit, regardless of its position within a number (e.g., 50 8 0 + 2 0 = 5 10 0). 数中每一位数字的位置决定了这位数字对整个数值的重要程度。把各位数字 从右到左 标记为 d 0 、d 1 、d 2 等，每往左一位，贡献就比右边那一位大 10 倍。例如，看看数值 8425（ 图 1 ）。 The position of each digit in the number determines how important that digit is to the overall value of the number. Labeling the digits from right to left as d 0 , d 1 , d 2 , etc., each successive digit contributes a factor of ten more than the next. For example, take the value 8425 ( Figure 1 ). 图 1. 十进制数中每一位数字的重要程度，用的是你在小学时可能用过的各位名称。 Figure 1. The importance of each digit in a base 10 number, using names that you may have given to each digit in grade school. 译注 · 图中内容 对于数 8425，第 0 位是 5，在「个位」；第 1 位是 2，在「十位」；第 2 位是 4，在「百位」；第 3 位是 8，在「千位」。 对于示例值 8425，「个」位上的 5 贡献 5（5 × 10 0 ），「十」位上的 2 贡献 20（2 × 10 1 ），「百」位上的 4 贡献 400（4 × 10 2 ），最后，「千」位上的 8 贡献 8000（8 × 10 3 ）。更正式地说，8425 可以表示为 For the example value 8425, the 5 in the “ones” place contributes 5 (5 × 10 0 ). The 2 in the “tens” place contributes 20 (2 × 10 1 ). The 4 in the “hundreds” place contributes 400 (4 × 10 2 ), and, finally, the 8 in the “thousands” place contributes 8000 (8 × 10 3 ). More formally, one could express 8425 as 原书旁注 (8 × 10 3 ) + (4 × 10 2 ) + (2 × 10 1 ) + (5 × 10 0 ) 这种对底数 10 施加递增指数的模式，正是它被称为 十进制 （base 10）数制的原因。从右到左给各位数字指定位置编号、从 d 0 开始，意味着每一位数字 d i 对总值的贡献为 10 i （的倍数）。因此，任何 N 位十进制数的总值都可以表示为： This pattern of increasing exponents applied to a base of 10 is the reason why it’s called a base 10 number system. Assigning position numbers to digits from right to left starting with d 0 implies that each digit d i contributes 10 i to the overall value. Thus, the overall value of any N -digit decimal number can be expressed as: 原书旁注 (d N-1 × 10 N-1 ) + (d N-2 × 10 N-2 ) + …​ + (d 2 × 10 2 ) + (d 1 × 10 1 ) + (d 0 × 10 0 ) 幸运的是，我们很快会看到，其他数制也适用非常相似的模式。 Fortunately, as we’ll soon see, a very similar pattern applies to other number systems. 原书注 · 区分数的进制（Distinguishing Number Bases） 既然我们即将介绍第二种数制，一个潜在的问题是如何解释一个数可能不够清楚。例如，看看数值 1000。它应当被解释为十进制值（即一千），还是二进制值（即八，原因稍后解释），一时并不明显。为了表达清楚，本章其余部分会给所有非十进制的数显式地加上前缀。我们很快会介绍二进制，它的前缀是 0b ；还有十六进制，它用前缀 0x 。 因此，如果你看到 1000，应当认为它是十进制的「一千」；如果你看到 0b1000，应当把它解释为二进制数，这里的值是「八」。 Now that we’re about to introduce a second number system, one potential problem is a lack of clarity regarding how to interpret a number. For example, consider the value 1000. It’s not immediately obvious whether you should interpret that number as a decimal value (i.e., one thousand) or a binary value (i.e., eight, for reasons explained soon). To help clarify, the remainder of this chapter will explicitly attach a prefix to all nondecimal numbers. We’ll soon introduce binary, for which the prefix is 0b , and hexadecimal, which uses a prefix of 0x . Therefore, if you see 1000, you should assume it’s a decimal “one thousand”, and if you see 0b1000, you should interpret it as a binary number, in this case the value “eight”. 4.1.2. 无符号二进制数 4.1.2. Unsigned Binary Numbers 你也许从未想过用 10 的幂来描述十进制数的具体公式，但{ 个 、 十 、 百 …… }位的概念应该很熟悉。幸运的是，类似的术语也适用于二进制等其他数制。当然，其他数制的基数不同，所以每个数位对数值的贡献也不同。 While you may never have considered the specific formula describing decimal numbers as powers of 10, the concept of { ones , tens , hundreds , etc. } places should hopefully feel comfortable. Luckily, similar terminology applies to other number systems, like binary. Of course, the base is different in other number systems, so each digit position contributes a different amount to its numerical value. 二进制数制 （binary number system）的基数是 2，而不是十进制的 10。用刚才分析十进制的方法来分析它，会发现几处相似之处（只是把 10 换成了 2）： A binary number system uses a base of 2 instead of decimal’s 10. Analyzing it the same way that we just did for decimal reveals several parallels (with 2 substituted for 10): 以 2 为基数的数中，任何一位都存储两个不同值（0 或 1）之一。要存储大于 1 的值，二进制编码就必须向左边多出来的一位 进位 。例如，如果某一位从它的最大值（1）开始，再加 1，结果就需要两位（1 + 1 = 0b10）。无论这一位在数中的什么位置，都遵循同样的模式（例如 0b100 1 00 + 0b 1 00 = 0b10 10 00）。 Any individual bit in a base 2 number stores one of two unique values (0 or 1). To store a value larger than 1, the binary encoding must carry to an additional bit to the left. For example, if one bit starts at its maximum value (1) and we add 1 to it, the result requires two bits (1 + 1 = 0b10). The same pattern holds for any bit, regardless of its position within a number (e.g., 0b100 1 00 + 0b 1 00 = 0b10 10 00). 数中每一位的位置决定了这一位对数值的重要程度。把各位 从右到左 标记为 d 0 、d 1 、d 2 等，每往左一位，贡献就比右边那一位大 两 倍。 The position of each bit in the number determines how important that bit is to the numerical value of the number. Labeling the digits from right to left as d 0 , d 1 , d 2 , etc., each successive bit contributes a factor of two more than the next. 第一点意味着二进制计数与十进制遵循同样的模式：只需依次列举各个值，并按需增加数位（位）。由于本节关注的是 无符号 数（只有零和正数），从零开始数是很自然的。 表 1 展示了如何用二进制数出前几个自然数。从表中可以看出，用二进制计数时位数增长得很快。直观上，这种增长是合理的，因为每个二进制数位（两个可能的值）所表示的信息比一个十进制数位（10 个可能的值）少。 The first point implies that counting in binary follows the same pattern as decimal: by simply enumerating the values and adding digits (bits). Because this section focuses on unsigned numbers (zero and positives only), it’s natural to start counting from zero. Table 1 shows how to count the first few natural numbers in binary. As you can see from the table, counting in binary quickly increases the number of digits. Intuitively, this growth makes sense, since each binary digit (two possible values) represents less information than a decimal digit (10 possible values). 表 1. 二进制计数与十进制计数的对比 Table 1. A Comparison of Counting in Binary versus Decimal 二进制值 十进制值 0 0 1 1 10 2 11 3 100 4 101 5 … … Binary value Decimal value 0 0 1 1 10 2 11 3 100 4 101 5 …​ …​ 关于标记数位的第二点看起来非常眼熟！事实上，它与十进制太相似了，以至于得出了几乎完全相同的二进制数解释公式。只需把每个指数的底数 10 换成 2： The second point about labeling digits looks really familiar! In fact, it’s so similar to decimal that it leads to a nearly identical formula for interpreting a binary number. Simply replace the 10 at the base of each exponent with a 2: 原书旁注 (d N-1 × 2 N-1 ) + (d N-2 × 2 N-2 ) + …​ + (d 2 × 2 2 ) + (d 1 × 2 1 ) + (d 0 × 2 0 ) 应用这个公式，就能得到任何二进制数的 无符号 解释。例如，看看 0b1000： Applying this formula yields the unsigned interpretation of any binary number. For example, take 0b1000: 原书旁注 (1 × 2 3 ) + (0 × 2 2 ) + (0 × 2 1 ) + (0 × 2 0 ) = 8 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 8 下面是一个更长的单字节例子，0b10110100： Here’s a longer one-byte example, 0b10110100: 原书旁注 (1 × 2 7 ) + (0 × 2 6 ) + (1 × 2 5 ) + (1 × 2 4 ) + (0 × 2 3 ) + (1 × 2 2 ) + (0 × 2 1 ) + (0 × 2 0 ) = 128 + 0 + 32 + 16 + 0 + 4 + 0 + 0 = 180 4.1.3. 十六进制 4.1.3. Hexadecimal 到目前为止，我们考察了两种数制：十进制和二进制。十进制之所以重要，是因为它对人类来说用着顺手；而二进制则与硬件中存储数据的方式相吻合。要注意，两者的表达能力是等价的，也就是说，能用其中一种数制表示的数，都能用另一种表示。既然两者等价，我们还要再讨论一种数制——以 16 为基数的 十六进制 （hexadecimal）——这可能会让你感到意外。 Thus far, we’ve examined two number systems, decimal and binary. Decimal is notable due to its comfort for humans, whereas binary matches the way data is stored in hardware. It’s important to note that they are equivalent in their expressive power. That is, there’s no number you can represent in one system that you can’t represent in the other. Given their equivalence, it may surprise you that we’re going to discuss one more number system: the base 16 hexadecimal system. 已经有了两种完全够用的数制，你可能会问为什么还需要另一种。答案主要是为了方便。如 表 1 所示，二进制位序列的位数增长得很快。人们往往很难理解只含 0 和 1 的长序列。而十进制虽然更紧凑，但它的基数 10 与二进制的基数 2 不匹配。 With two perfectly good number systems, you may wonder why we need another. The answer is primarily convenience. As shown in Table 1 , binary bit sequences quickly grow to a large number of digits. Humans tend to have a tough time making sense of long sequences containing only 0’s and 1’s. And whereas decimal is more compact, its base of 10 is a mismatch with binary’s base 2. 十进制不容易体现出固定位数所能表示的范围。例如，假设一台老式计算机使用 16 位内存地址，它的有效地址范围是 0b0000000000000000 到 0b1111111111111111。用十进制表示，地址范围是 0 到 65535。显然，十进制表示比长长的二进制序列更紧凑，但除非你记住它们之间的换算，否则用十进制数来推理会更困难。在使用 32 位或 64 位地址的现代设备上，这两个问题都只会更糟！ Decimal doesn’t easily capture the range that can be expressed using a fixed number of bits. For example, suppose that an old computer uses 16-bit memory addresses. Its valid addresses range from 0b0000000000000000 to 0b1111111111111111. Represented in decimal, the addresses range from 0 to 65535. Clearly, the decimal representations are more compact than the long binary sequences, but unless you memorize their conversions, it’s more difficult to reason about the decimal numbers. Both problems only get worse on modern devices, which use 32- or 64-bit addresses! 面对这些长长的位序列，正是十六进制的基数 16 大显身手的时候。较大的基数让每一位数字能表示足够多的信息，使十六进制数很紧凑。此外，由于基数本身是 2 的幂（2 4 = 16），十六进制与二进制之间的相互转换很容易。为完整起见，我们用分析十进制和二进制的方法来分析十六进制： These long bit sequences are where hexadecimal’s base 16 shines. The large base allows each digit to represent enough information for hexadecimal numbers to be compact. Furthermore, because the base is itself a power of two (2 4 = 16), it’s easy to map hexadecimal to binary, and vice versa. For the sake of completeness, let’s analyze hexadecimal in the same way as decimal and binary: 以 16 为基数的数中，任何一位数字都存储 16 个不同值之一。超过 10 个值给十六进制带来了一个新问题——传统的十进制数字最大只到 9。按照惯例，十六进制用字母表示大于 9 的值：A 表示 10，B 表示 11，一直到 F 表示 15。和其他数制一样，要存储大于 15 的值，就必须向左边多出来的一位 进位 。例如，如果某一位从它的最大值（F）开始，再加 1，结果就需要两位数字（0xF + 0x1 = 0x10；注意我们用 0x 表示十六进制数）。 Any individual digit in a base 16 number stores one of 16 unique values. Having more than 10 values presents a new challenge for hexadecimal — traditional base 10 digits stop at a maximum value of 9. By convention, hexadecimal uses letters to represent values larger than 9, with A for 10, B for 11, up to F for 15. Like the other systems, to store a value larger than 15, the number must carry to an additional digit to the left. For example, if one digit starts at its maximum value (F) and we add 1 to it, the result requires two digits (0xF + 0x1 = 0x10; note that we use 0x to indicate hexadecimal numbers). 数中每一位数字的位置决定了这位数字对数值的重要程度。把各位数字 从右到左 标记为 d 0 、d 1 、d 2 等，每往左一位，贡献就比右边那一位大 16 倍。 The position of each digit in the number determines how important that digit is to the numerical value of the number. Labeling the digits from right to left as d 0 , d 1 , d 2 , etc., each successive digit contributes a factor of 16 more than the next. 毫不意外，那个可靠的解释公式同样适用于十六进制，只是基数换成了 16： Unsurprisingly, the same trusty formula for interpreting a number applies to hexadecimal, with 16 as the base: 原书旁注 (d N-1 × 16 N-1 ) + (d N-2 × 16 N-2 ) + …​ + (d 2 × 16 2 ) + (d 1 × 16 1 ) + (d 0 × 16 0 ) 例如，求 0x23C8 的十进制值： For example, to determine the decimal value of 0x23C8: 原书旁注 (2 × 16 3 ) + (3 × 16 2 ) + (C × 16 1 ) + (8 × 16 0 ) = (2 × 16 3 ) + (3 × 16 2 ) + (12 × 16 1 ) + (8 × 16 0 ) = (2 × 4096) + (3 × 256) + (12 × 16) + (8 × 1) = 8192 + 768 + 192 + 8 = 9160 原书警示 · 关于十六进制的误解（Hexadecimal Misconception） 刚开始学习系统编程时，你可能不会经常遇到十六进制数。实际上，你最可能见到它们的场合是表示内存地址。例如，如果用 printf 的 %p （指针）格式码打印变量的地址，得到的就是十六进制输出。 很多学生常常开始把内存地址（例如 C 指针变量）等同于十六进制。虽然你可能会习惯于看到以这种方式表示的地址，但要记住， 它们在硬件中仍然以二进制存储 ，和所有其他数据一样！ You may not encounter hexadecimal numbers frequently as you’re first learning about systems programming. In fact, the only context where you’re likely to find them is in representing memory addresses. For example, if you print the address of a variable using the %p (pointer) format code for printf , you’ll get hexadecimal output. Many students often begin to equate memory addresses (e.g., C pointer variables) with hexadecimal. While you may get used to seeing addresses represented that way, keep in mind that they are still stored using binary in the hardware , just like all other data! 4.1.4. 存储的限制 4.1.4. Storage Limitations 从概念上讲，无符号整数有无穷多个。实际上，出于多种原因，程序员必须 在存储一个值之前 就选定要为变量分配多少位： Conceptually, there are infinitely many unsigned integers. In practice, a programmer must choose how many bits to dedicate to a variable prior to storing it , for a variety of reasons: 在存储一个值之前，程序必须为它分配存储空间。在 C 中，声明一个变量就是根据它的类型告诉编译器它需要 多少内存 。 Before storing a value, a program must allocate storage space for it. In C, declaring a variable tells the compiler how much memory it needs based on its type. 硬件存储设备的容量是有限的。系统的主存通常很大，不太可能成为限制因素，但 CPU 内部用作临时「草稿空间」的存储位置（即 寄存器 ）就受限得多。CPU 使用的寄存器大小受限于它的字长（通常是 32 或 64 位，取决于 CPU 体系结构）。 Hardware storage devices have finite capacity. Whereas a system’s main memory is typically large and unlikely to be a limiting factor, storage locations inside the CPU that are used as temporary “scratch space” (i.e., registers ) are more constrained. A CPU uses registers that are limited to its word size (typically 32 or 64 bits, depending on the CPU architecture). 程序经常把数据从一个存储设备移到另一个（例如在 CPU 寄存器和主存之间）。值越大，存储设备之间就需要越多的导线来传递信号。因此，扩大存储会增加硬件的复杂度，并给其他部件留下更少的物理空间。 Programs often move data from one storage device to another (e.g., between CPU registers and main memory). As values get larger, storage devices need more wires to communicate signals between them. Hence, expanding storage increases the complexity of the hardware and leaves less physical space for other components. 存储一个整数所用的位数决定了它可表示值的范围。 图 2 描绘了我们可以如何理解无限的和有限的无符号整数存储空间。 The number of bits used to store an integer dictates the range of its representable values. Figure 2 depicts how we might conceptualize infinite and finite unsigned integer storage spaces. 图 2. (a) 无限的无符号数轴和 (b) 有限的无符号数轴示意图。后者在两端都会「回绕」（溢出）。 Figure 2. Illustrations of (a) an infinite unsigned number line and (b) a finite unsigned number line. The latter “wraps around” at either endpoint (overflow). 试图把大于变量大小所允许范围的值存入变量，称为 整数溢出 （integer overflow）。本章把溢出的细节留到 后面的一节 。目前，可以把它想象成汽车的里程表：当它试图超过最大值时，就会「翻转」回零。类似地，零减一会得到最大值。 Attempting to store a larger value to a variable than the variable’s size allows is known as integer overflow . This chapter defers the details of overflow to a later section . For now, think of it like a car’s odometer that “rolls over” back to zero if it attempts to increase beyond its maximum value. Similarly, subtracting one from zero yields the maximum value. 到这里，关于无符号二进制数，一个自然的问题是：「 N 位能存储的最大正数是多少？ 」换句话说，给定一个全为 1 的 N 位序列，这个序列表示什么值？非正式地推理一下这个问题： 上一节 的分析表明， N 位可以产生 2 N 个不同的位序列。由于其中一个序列必须表示数 0，剩下的 2 N - 1 个序列表示从 1 到 2 N - 1 的正值。因此， N 位无符号二进制数的最大值必然是 2 N - 1。 At this point, a natural question to ask about unsigned binary is “ What’s the largest positive value that N bits can store? “ In other words, given a sequence of N bits that are all 1, what value does the sequence represent? Reasoning about this question informally, the analysis in the previous section shows that N bits yield 2 N unique bit sequences. Since one of those sequences must represent the number 0, that leaves 2 N - 1 positive values ranging from 1 to 2 N - 1. Thus, the maximum value for an unsigned binary number of N bits must be 2 N - 1. 例如，8 位提供 2 8 = 256 个不同的序列。其中一个序列 0b00000000 留给 0，剩下 255 个序列用于存储正值。因此，一个 8 位变量可以表示 1 到 255 的正值，其中最大的是 255。 For example, 8 bits provide 2 8 = 256 unique sequences. One of those sequences, 0b00000000, is reserved for 0, leaving 255 sequences for storing positive values. Therefore, an 8-bit variable represents the positive values 1 through 255, the largest of which is 255.

In other words, subtracting 7 - 3 is equivalent to expressing the operation as 7 + (-3). This portrayal of subtraction aligns well with how the hardware behaves — a CPU already contains circuits for negation and addition, so it makes sense to reuse those circuits rather than build an entirely new subtractor. Recall that a simple procedure to negate a binary number is to flip the bits and add one . 来看 0b0111（7）- 0b0011（3）这个例子，它先把 3 送进一个翻转各位的电路。为了得到「加一」，它利用了加法器电路的 进位输入 。也就是说，减法不是从一位向另一位进位，而是向加法器的 d 0 送入一个 进位输入 。把进位输入设为 1，会使结果的「个位」值加一，这正是取负中「加一」那部分所需要的。综合起来，这个例子如下： Consider the example 0b0111 (7) - 0b0011 (3), which starts by sending the 3 to a bit-flipping circuit. Rounding Consequences 虽然舍入不太可能毁掉你写的大多数程序，但实数的舍入误差偶尔也会导致一些引人注目的系统故障。1991 年海湾战争期间，一个舍入误差导致美国的一个爱国者导弹连 未能拦截一枚伊拉克导弹 。这枚导弹造成 28 名士兵死亡，多人受伤。1996 年，欧洲航天局 Ariane 5 火箭的首次发射在 起飞 39 秒后爆炸 。这枚火箭沿用了 Ariane 4 的大部分代码，在试图把一个浮点值转换为整数值时触发了溢出。 While rounding isn’t likely to ruin most of the programs you write, real number rounding errors have occasionally caused some high-profile system failures. The rocket, which borrowed much of its code from the Ariane 4, triggered an overflow when attempting to convert a floating-point value into an integer value.

Because the operands have the same sign and it doesn’t match the result’s sign, this operation overflows . 4.5.3. 溢出小结 4.5.3. Overflow Summary 一般来说，当算术运算在其结果所能表示的最小值和最大值之间穿越时，就会发生整数溢出。如果你对有符号与无符号溢出的规则拿不准，可以想一想 N 位序列的最小值和最大值： In general, integer overflow occurs when an arithmetic operation moves between the minimum and maximum values that its result can represent. If you’re ever in doubt about the rules for signed versus unsigned overflow, consider the minimum and maximum values of an N-bit sequence: 无符号 的最小值是 0（因为无符号编码不能表示负数），最大值是 2 N -1（因为有一个位序列留给了零）。因此不连续处位于 2 N -1 和 0 之间。 The minimum unsigned value is 0 (because unsigned encodings can’t represent negative numbers) and the maximum unsigned value is 2 N -1 (because one bit sequence is reserved for zero). Therefore the discontinuity is between 2 N -1 and 0. 有符号 的最小值是 -2 N-1 （因为一半的序列留给了负值），最大值是 2 N-1 -1（因为在另一半中，有一个值留给了零）。因此，不连续处位于 2 N-1 -1 和 -2 N-1 之间。 The minimum signed value is -2 N-1 (because half of the sequences are reserved for negative values) and the maximum is 2 N-1 -1 (because in the other half, one value is reserved for zero). Therefore, the discontinuity is between 2 N-1 -1 and -2 N-1 . 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· 在 C 里安全地检测溢出 在 C 中，无符号整数的运算按模 2 N 回绕，行为是确定的；而 有符号整数溢出是未定义行为 ，编译器可以假定它不会发生并据此优化，所以不能靠「算完再检查符号」来判断溢出。C23 为此新增了头文件 <stdckdint.h> ，提供 ckd_add 、 ckd_sub 、 ckd_mul 三个带检查的运算：它们把结果写入第一个参数，返回值为 true 表示发生了溢出。译者在 macOS 上用 gcc -std=c23 编译 ckd_add(&r, INT_MAX, 1) ，返回 1（溢出）， r 为回绕后的 -2147483648。 cppreference：<stdckdint.h> · cppreference：Arithmetic operators 4.5.4. 溢出的后果 4.5.4. Overflow Consequences 虽然你可能不会经常遇到整数溢出，但溢出有可能以引人注目（甚至可能是毁灭性）的方式破坏程序。 While you may not run into integer overflow frequently, overflows have the potential to break programs in notable (and potentially devastating) ways. 例如，2014 年，PSY 大热的音乐视频《 江南 Style 》的播放量眼看就要让 YouTube 用来统计视频播放次数的 32 位计数器溢出。于是，YouTube 改用了 64 位计数器。 For example, in 2014, PSY’s popular Gangnam Style music video threatened to overflow the 32-bit counter that YouTube used to track video hits. As a result, YouTube switched to using a 64-bit counter. 另一个相对无害的例子出现在 1980 年的街机游戏《吃豆人》（ Pac-Man ）中。游戏的开发者用一个无符号的八位值来记录玩家在游戏关卡中的进度。结果，如果高手玩家打过了第 255 关（八位无符号整数的最大值），游戏画面有一半就会出现严重的错乱，如 图 5 所示。 Another relatively harmless example shows up in the 1980 arcade game Pac-Man . The game’s developers used an unsigned eight-bit value to track the player’s progress through the game’s levels. As a result, if an expert player makes it beyond level 255 (the maximum value of an eight-bit unsigned integer), half of the board ends up glitching significantly, as shown in Figure 5 . 图 5. Pac-Man 的游戏画面在到达第 256 关时「抓狂」 Figure 5. The Pac-Man game board “freaks out” upon reaching level 256 译注 · 图中内容 游戏画面的右半边完全被乱码破坏。 一个悲惨得多的溢出例子，出现在 1980 年代中期 Therac-25 放射治疗机的历史中。Therac-25 存在多个设计问题，其中之一是对一个表示真值的标志变量做递增，而不是把它设为一个常量。使用次数足够多之后，这个标志就会溢出，错误地翻转为零（假），从而绕过安全机制。Therac-25 最终对六名患者造成了严重伤害（其中一些患者因此死亡）。 A much more tragic example of overflow appears in the history of the Therac-25 radiation therapy machine of the mid 1980s. The Therac-25 suffered from several design problems, including one that incremented a truth flag variable rather than setting it to a constant. After enough uses, the flag overflowed, causing it to erroneously roll over to zero (false) and bypass safety mechanisms. The Therac-25 ultimately caused serious harm to (and in some cases killed) six patients.

b: Dive Into Systems 中英对照
x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C5-Arch/index.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 5. What von Neumann Knew: Computer Architecture 计算机体系结构 （computer architecture）这个术语可以指计算机的整个硬件层面。不过它更常用来指计算机硬件中数字处理器部分的设计与实现，本章关注的就是计算机处理器的体系结构。 The term computer architecture may refer to the entire hardware level of the computer. However, it is often used to refer to the design and implementation of the digital processor part of the computer hardware, and we focus on the computer processor architecture in this chapter. 中央处理器 （central processing unit，CPU，或称处理器）是计算机中在程序数据上执行程序指令的部件。程序指令和数据存放在计算机的随机存取存储器（RAM）中。一个具体的数字处理器实现了某种特定的 指令集架构 （instruction set architecture，ISA），ISA 定义了指令集合及其二进制编码、CPU 寄存器的集合，以及执行指令对处理器状态的影响。ISA 有很多种，包括 SPARC、IA32、MIPS、ARM、ARC、PowerPC 和 x86（后者包括 IA32 和 x86-64）。 微体系结构 （microarchitecture）定义了某种特定 ISA 的一种实现的电路。同一种 ISA 的不同微体系结构实现可以各不相同，只要它们都实现了 ISA 的定义即可。例如，Intel 和 AMD 生产了 IA32 ISA 的不同微处理器实现。 The central processing unit (CPU, or processor) is the part of the computer that executes program instructions on program data. Program instructions and data are stored in the computer’s random access memory (RAM). A particular digital processor implements a specific instruction set architecture (ISA), which defines the set of instructions and their binary encoding, the set of CPU registers, and the effects of executing instructions on the state of the processor. There are many different ISAs, including SPARC, IA32, MIPS, ARM, ARC, PowerPC, and x86 (the latter including IA32 and x86-64). A microarchitecture defines the circuitry of an implementation of a specific ISA. Microarchitecture implementations of the same ISA can differ as long as they implement the ISA definition. For example, Intel and AMD produce different microprocessor implementations of IA32 ISA. 有些 ISA 定义的是 精简指令集计算机 （reduced instruction set computer，RISC），另一些定义的是 复杂指令集计算机 （complex instruction set computer，CISC）。RISC ISA 只有一小组基本指令，每条指令都执行得很快；每条指令大约在一个处理器时钟周期内完成，编译器把若干条基本 RISC 指令组合成序列来实现更高层的功能。相比之下，CISC ISA 的指令提供比 RISC 指令更高层的功能。CISC 体系结构还定义了比 RISC 更大的指令集合，支持更复杂的寻址模式（表示程序数据内存位置的方式），并支持变长指令。一条 CISC 指令可能执行一连串底层操作，可能需要好几个处理器时钟周期才能执行完。同样的功能在 RISC 体系结构上则需要多条指令。 Some ISAs define a reduced instruction set computer (RISC), and others define a complex instruction set computer (CISC). RISC ISAs have a small set of basic instructions that each execute quickly; each instruction executes in about a single processor clock cycle, and compilers combine sequences of several basic RISC instructions to implement higher-level functionality. In contrast, a CISC ISA’s instructions provide higher-level functionality than RISC instructions. CISC architectures also define a larger set of instructions than RISC, support more complicated addressing modes (ways to express the memory locations of program data), and support variable-length instructions. A single CISC instruction may perform a sequence of low-level functionality and may take several processor clock cycles to execute. This same functionality would require multiple instructions on a RISC architecture. 原书旁注 · RISC 与 CISC 的历史（The History of RISC versus CISC） 1980 年代初，伯克利大学和斯坦福大学的研究人员通过伯克利 RISC 项目和斯坦福 MIPS 项目开发了 RISC。伯克利的 David Patterson 和斯坦福的 John Hennessy 因开发 RISC 体系结构的工作，获得了 2017 年度的图灵奖 1 （计算机领域的最高奖项）。 在 RISC 诞生的年代，它与当时普遍认为 ISA 必须越来越复杂才能获得高性能的观点截然不同。「RISC 方法与当时盛行的复杂指令集计算机（CISC）不同，它只需要一小组简单而通用的指令（计算机必须执行的功能），所需的晶体管比复杂指令集更少，也减少了计算机必须完成的工作量。」 2 CISC ISA 用比 RISC 更少的指令来表达程序，因而可执行文件往往更小。在主存较小的系统上，可执行文件的大小是影响程序性能的重要因素，因为可执行文件越大，留给运行中程序内存空间其他部分的 RAM 就越少。基于 CISC 的微体系结构通常也经过专门设计，以高效执行 CISC 的变长、高功能指令。用于执行更复杂指令的专用电路，可以更高效地执行特定的高层功能，但代价是所有指令的执行都需要更复杂的电路。 比较 RISC 和 CISC：RISC 程序要执行的指令总数更多，但每条指令的执行效率远高于大多数 CISC 指令，而且 RISC 允许比 CISC 更简单的微体系结构设计。CISC 程序的指令更少，CISC 微体系结构被设计成能高效执行更复杂的指令，但它们需要更复杂的微体系结构设计和更高的时钟频率。总的来说，RISC 处理器带来更高效的设计和更好的性能。随着计算机内存容量的不断增长，可执行文件的大小对程序性能的影响已经不那么重要了。然而，CISC 一直是占主导地位的 ISA，这在很大程度上是因为它得到了产业界的实现和支持。 今天，CISC 仍然是台式机和许多服务器级计算机的主流 ISA。例如，Intel 的 x86 ISA 就是基于 CISC 的。RISC ISA 更常见于高端服务器（例如 SPARC）和移动设备（例如 ARM），因为它们功耗低。某种 RISC 或 CISC ISA 的具体微体系结构实现，在内部可能同时融合了 RISC 和 CISC 的设计。例如，大多数 CISC 处理器使用微码（microcode），把一些 CISC 指令编码为一种更像 RISC 的指令集，交由底层处理器执行；而一些现代 RISC 指令集也包含了比最初的 MIPS 和伯克利 RISC 指令集多一些的复杂指令或寻址模式。 In the early 1980s, researchers at Berkeley and Stanford universities developed RISC through the Berkeley RISC project and the Stanford MIPS project. David Patterson of Berkeley and John Hennessy of Stanford won the 2017 Turing Award 1 (the highest award in computing) for their work developing RISC architectures. At the time of its development, the RISC architecture was a radical departure from the commonly held view that ISAs needed to be increasingly complex to achieve high performance. “The RISC approach differed from the prevailing complex instruction set computer (CISC) computers of the time in that it required a small set of simple and general instructions (functions a computer must perform), requiring fewer transistors than complex instruction sets and reducing the amount of work a computer must perform.” 2 CISC ISAs express programs in fewer instructions than RISC, often resulting in smaller program executables. On systems with small main memory, the size of the program executable is an important factor in the program’s performance, since a large executable leaves less RAM space available for other parts of a running program’s memory space. Microarchitectures based on CISC are also typically specialized to efficiently execute the CISC variable-length and higher-functionality instructions. Specialized circuitry for executing more complex instructions may result in more efficient execution of specific higher-level functionality, but at the cost of requiring more complexity for all instruction execution. In comparing RISC to CISC, RISC programs contain more total instructions to execute, but each instruction executes much more efficiently than most CISC instructions, and RISCs allow for simpler microarchitecture designs than CISC. CISC programs contain fewer instructions, and CISC microarchitectures are designed to execute more complicated instructions efficiently, but they require more complex microarchitecture designs and faster clock rates. In general, RISC processors result in more efficient design and better performance. As computer memory sizes have increased over time, the size of the program executable is less important to a program’s performance. CISC, however, has been the dominant ISA due in large part to it being implemented by and supported by industry. Today, CISC remains the dominant ISA for desktop and many server-class computers. For example, Intel’s x86 ISAs are CISC-based. RISC ISAs are more commonly seen in high-end servers (e.g. SPARC) and in mobile devices (e.g. ARM) due to their low power requirements. A particular microarchitecture implementation of a RISC or CISC ISA may incorporate both RISC and CISC design under the covers. For example, most CISC processors use microcode to encode some CISC instructions in a more RISC-like instruction set that the underlying processor executes, and some modern RISC instruction sets contain a few more complex instructions or addressing modes than the initial MIPS and Berkeley RISC instruction sets. 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· RISC 进入个人电脑 原书说「CISC 仍是台式机的主流 ISA」，这一格局已经松动。2020 年 11 月，Apple 发布了第一款为 Mac 设计的自研芯片 M1（ARM 架构），并宣布用大约两年时间把整个 Mac 产品线从 Intel x86 处理器迁移到 Apple Silicon，如今在售的 Mac 全部采用 ARM 芯片。 Apple Newsroom：Apple unleashes M1 所有现代处理器，无论采用什么 ISA，都遵循冯·诺依曼体系结构模型。冯·诺依曼体系结构的通用设计使它能执行任何类型的程序。它采用存储程序模型，也就是说，程序指令与程序数据一起存放在计算机内存中，两者都是处理器的输入。 All modern processors, regardless of their ISA, adhere to the von Neumann architecture model. The general-purpose design of the von Neumann architecture allows it to execute any type of program. It uses a stored-program model, meaning that the program instructions reside in computer memory along with program data, and both are inputs to the processor. 本章介绍冯·诺依曼体系结构，以及支撑现代计算机体系结构的历史渊源和组成部分。我们会基于冯·诺依曼体系结构模型构建一个示例数字处理器（CPU）：用以逻辑门为构件搭建的数字电路设计一个 CPU，并演示 CPU 如何执行程序指令。 This chapter introduces the von Neumann architecture and the ancestry and components that underpin modern computer architecture. We build an example digital processor (CPU) based on the von Neumann architecture model, design a CPU from digital circuits that are constructed from logic gate building blocks, and demonstrate how the CPU executes program instructions. 参考文献 References ACM A. M. Turing Award Winners. https://amturing.acm.org/ “Pioneers of Modern Computer Architecture Receive ACM A.M. Turing Award”, ACM Media Center Notice, March 2018. https://www.acm.org/media-center/2018/march/turing-award-2017

Summary 本章介绍了计算机的体系结构，重点是处理器（CPU）的设计与实现，以便理解它如何运行程序。如今的现代处理器都基于冯·诺依曼体系结构，它定义了一种存储程序的通用计算机。冯·诺依曼体系结构的通用设计使它能执行任何类型的程序。 In this chapter, we presented the computer’s architecture, focusing on its processor (CPU) design and implementation in order to understand how it runs a program. Today’s modern processors are based on the von Neumann architecture, which defines a stored-program, universal computer. The general-purpose design of the von Neumann architecture allows it to execute any type of program. 为了理解 CPU 如何执行程序指令，我们构建了一个示例 CPU：从基本的逻辑门构件开始，搭建出共同实现一个数字处理器的各种电路。数字处理器的功能由控制电路、存储电路和算术/逻辑电路组合而成，并由一个时钟电路驱动其执行程序指令的取指、译码、执行和写回各个阶段。 To understand how the CPU executes program instructions, we built an example CPU, starting with basic logic-gate building blocks to create circuits that together implement a digital processor. A digital processor’s functionality is built by combining control, storage, and arithmetic/logic circuits, and is run by a clock circuit that drives the Fetch, Decode, Execute, and WriteBack phases of its execution of program instructions. 所有处理器体系结构都实现了某种指令集架构（ISA），ISA 定义了 CPU 指令集合、CPU 寄存器集合，以及执行指令对处理器状态的影响。ISA 有很多种，一种 ISA 也常常有多种不同的微处理器实现。如今的微处理器还采用多种技术来提升处理器性能，包括流水线执行、指令级并行和多核设计。 All processor architectures implement an instruction set architecture (ISA) that defines the set of CPU instructions, the set of CPU registers, and the effects of executing instructions on the state of the processor. There are many different ISAs, and there are often different microprocessor implementations of a given ISA. Today’s microprocessors also use a variety of techniques to improve processor performance, including pipelined execution, instruction-level parallelism, and multicore design. 想更广、更深地了解计算机体系结构，我们推荐阅读一本计算机体系结构教材 1 。 For more breadth and depth of coverage on computer architecture, we recommend reading a computer architecture textbook 1 . 脚注 Footnotes 推荐一本：David A. Patterson 和 John L. Hennessy 合著的《Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware and Software Interface》（中译本《计算机组成与设计：硬件/软件接口》）。 One suggestion is “Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware and Software Interface”, by David A. Patterson and John L. Hennessy.

The Origin of Modern Computing Architectures 追溯现代计算机体系结构的渊源时，人们很容易认为现代计算机是一条线性演变链条中的一环，每台机器只是对前一台的改进。虽然这种「继承式改进」的看法对某些类别的体系结构可能成立（想想从最初的 iPhone 到 iPhone X 的逐代改进），但体系结构这棵树的根源远没有那么清晰。 When tracing the ancestry of modern computing architecture, it is tempting to consider that modern computers are part of a linear chain of successive transmutations, with each machine simply an improvement of the one that previously existed. While this view of inherited improvements in computer design may hold true for certain classes of architecture (consider the iterative improvements of the iPhone X from the original iPhone), the root of the architectural tree is much less defined. 从 18 世纪到 20 世纪初，数学家充当了最早的 人类 计算机，为科学和工程应用进行相关计算 1 。「computer」一词最初指的是「从事计算的人」。女性数学家常常担任计算员的角色。事实上，雇用女性作为人类计算员的做法如此普遍，以至于计算量曾用「千女孩」（kilo-girls）来衡量，即一千名人类计算员一小时能完成的工作量 2 。当时人们普遍认为女性比男性更擅长数学计算，因为她们往往更有条理。女性不能担任工程师的职位，因此她们被分派去做更「琐碎」的工作，比如进行复杂的计算。 From the 1700s until the early 1900s, mathematicians served as the first human computers for calculations related to applications of science and engineering 1 . The word “computer” originally referred to “one who computes”. Women mathematicians often served in the role of computer. In fact, the use of women as human computers was so pervasive that computational complexity was measured in “kilo-girls”, or the amount of work a thousand human computers could complete in one hour 2 . Women were widely considered to be better at doing mathematical calculations than men, as they tended to be more methodical. Women were not allowed to hold the position of engineer. As such, they were relegated to more “menial” work, such as computing complex calculations. 第一台通用数字计算机—— 分析机 （Analytical Engine）——是由英国数学家查尔斯·巴贝奇（Charles Babbage）设计的，一些人把他誉为计算机之父。分析机是他最初的发明——差分机（Difference Engine）——的扩展，差分机是一台能计算多项式函数的机械计算器。阿达·洛芙莱斯（Ada Lovelace）或许应当被称为计算之母，她是第一个编写计算机程序的人，也是第一个发表可以用查尔斯·巴贝奇的分析机来计算的算法的人。她在笔记中认识到了分析机的通用性：「分析机根本不会自己创造任何东西。它能做的，是我们知道如何命令它去做的任何事情。 3 」然而，与现代计算机不同，分析机是一台机械装置，而且只建造了一部分。后来成为现代计算机直接前身的那些机器，它们的大多数设计者在开发自己的机器时，并不知道巴贝奇和洛芙莱斯的工作。 The first general-purpose digital computer, the Analytical Engine , was designed by British mathematician Charles Babbage, who is credited by some as the father of the computer. The Analytical Engine was an extension of his original invention, the Difference Engine, a mechanical calculator that was capable of calculating polynomial functions. Ada Lovelace, who perhaps should be known as the mother of computing, was the very first person to develop a computer program and the first to publish an algorithm that could be computed using Charles Babbage’s Analytical Engine. In her notes is included her recognition of the general-purpose nature of the Analytical Engine: “[t]he Analytical Engine has no pretensions whatever to originate anything. It can do whatever we know how to order it to perform. 3 “ However, unlike modern computers, the Analytical Engine was a mechanical device and was only partially built. Most of the designers of what became the direct forerunners to the modern computer were unaware of the work of Babbage and Lovelace when they developed their own machines. 因此，更准确的说法也许是：现代计算机体系结构是从 1930 年代和 1940 年代涌现出的一锅思想与创新的「原始汤」中诞生的。例如，1937 年，MIT 的学生克劳德·香农（Claude Shannon）写出了可能是有史以来最有影响力的硕士论文。香农借鉴了乔治·布尔（George Boole，创立布尔代数的数学家）的工作，证明了布尔逻辑可以应用于电路，可以用来设计电气开关。这将促成二进制计算系统的发展，以及后来大部分的数字电路设计。尽管许多早期的电子计算机由男性设计，但女性（她们不被允许成为工程师）成为了编程的先驱，主导了许多早期软件创新的设计与开发，比如编程语言、编译器、算法和操作系统。 Thus, it is perhaps more accurate to think about modern computer architecture rising out of a primordial soup of ideas and innovations that arose in the 1930s and 1940s. For example, in 1937, Claude Shannon, a student at MIT, wrote what would go on to be perhaps the most influential masters thesis of all time. Drawing upon the work of George Boole (the mathematician who developed Boolean algebra), Shannon showed that Boolean logic could be applied to circuits and could be used to develop electrical switches. This would lead to the development of the binary computing system, and much of future digital circuit design. While men would design many early electronic computers, women (who were not allowed to be engineers) became programming pioneers, leading the design and development of many early software innovations, such as programming languages, compilers, algorithms, and operating systems. 本书无法全面讨论计算机体系结构的兴起（更详细的介绍请参见乔治·戴森（George Dyson）的《图灵的大教堂》（ Turing’s Cathedral ） 4 和沃尔特·艾萨克森（Walter Isaacson）的《创新者》（ The Innovators ） 6 ）；不过，我们简要列举 1930 年代和 1940 年代出现的、对现代计算机体系结构的兴起起了关键作用的几项重要创新。 A comprehensive discussion of the rise of computer architecture is not possible in this book (see Turing’s Cathedral 4 by George Dyson and The Innovators 6 by Walter Isaacson for more detailed coverage); however, we briefly enumerate several significant innovations that occurred in the 1930s and 1940s that were instrumental in the rise of modern computer architecture. 5.1.1. 图灵机 5.1.1. The Turing Machine 1937 年，英国数学家艾伦·图灵（Alan Turing）提出了 7 一种理论计算机——「逻辑计算机器」（Logical Computing Machine）。图灵用这台机器证明了数学家戴维·希尔伯特（David Hilbert）和威廉·阿克曼（Wilhelm Ackermann）在 1928 年提出的判定问题（德语为 Entscheidungsproblem ）不存在解。判定问题要求的是一个算法：它以一个陈述为输入，判断该陈述是否普遍有效。图灵通过证明 停机问题 （机器 X 在输入 y 上会停机吗？）对于图灵的机器是不可判定的，证明了这样的算法不存在。作为这一证明的一部分，图灵描述了一种能执行任何其他计算机器所能执行的任务的通用机器。图灵在普林斯顿大学的博士导师阿隆佐·丘奇（Alonzo Church）首先把 逻辑计算机器 称为 图灵机 （Turing machine），并把它的通用形式称为 通用图灵机 （universal Turing machine）。 In 1937, British mathematician Alan Turing proposed 7 the “Logical Computing Machine”, a theoretical computer. Turing used this machine to prove that there exists no solution to the decision problem (in German, the Entscheidungsproblem ), posed by the mathematicians David Hilbert and Wilhelm Ackermann in 1928. The decision problem is an algorithm that takes a statement as input and determines whether the statement is universally valid. Turing proved that no such algorithm exists by showing that the halting problem (will machine X halt on input y ?) was undecidable for Turing’s machine. As part of this proof, Turing described a universal machine that is capable of performing the tasks of any other computing machine. Alonzo Church, Turing’s dissertation advisor at Princeton University, was the first to refer to the logical computing machine as the Turing machine , and its universal form as the universal Turing machine . 图灵后来回到英国，在第二次世界大战期间作为布莱切利园（Bletchley Park）密码破译小组的成员为国效力。他在设计和建造 Bombe 的过程中发挥了关键作用，这是一种机电装置，帮助破译了恩尼格玛（Enigma）密码机产生的密码，纳粹德国在第二次世界大战期间普遍用这种机器保护敏感通信。 Turing later returned to England and served his country as part of the code breaking unit in Bletchley Park during World War II. He was instrumental in the design and construction of the Bombe , an electromechanical device that helped break the cipher produced by the Enigma machine, which was commonly used by Nazi Germany to protect sensitive communication during World War II. 战后，图灵设计了 自动计算机 （automatic computing engine，ACE）。ACE 是一台存储程序计算机，也就是说，程序指令和数据都被加载到计算机的内存中，由这台通用计算机来运行。他在 1946 年发表的论文，可能是对这种计算机最详细的描述 8 。 After the war, Turing designed the automatic computing engine (ACE). The ACE was a stored-program computer, meaning that both the program instructions and its data are loaded into the computer memory and run by the general-purpose computer. His paper, published in 1946, is perhaps the most detailed description of such a computer 8 . 5.1.2. 早期的电子计算机 5.1.2. Early Electronic Computers 第二次世界大战大大加速了早期计算机的发展。然而，由于第二次世界大战中军事行动的保密性质，战时紧张活动所催生的许多创新的细节，直到多年以后才被公开承认。一个很好的例子是巨人计算机（Colossus），它由英国工程师汤米·弗劳尔斯（Tommy Flowers）设计，用于帮助破译纳粹德国用来加密高层情报通信的洛伦兹（Lorenz）密码。艾伦·图灵的部分工作为它的设计提供了帮助。Colossus 建成于 1943 年，可以说是第一台可编程的、数字的、全电子的计算机。不过，它是一台专用计算机，专为破译密码而设计。英国皇家海军女子服务队（Women’s Royal Naval Service，WRNS，人称「Wrens」）担任 Colossus 的操作员。尽管《 Tunny 总报告 》（ General Report of the Tunny ） 14 指出几名 Wrens 在密码工作方面表现出了才能，但她们没有一个人被授予密码分析员的职位，而是被分派去做 Colossus 更琐碎的操作任务 5 , 15 。 World War II accelerated much of the development of early computers. However, due to the classified nature of military operations in World War II, many of the details of innovations that occurred as a result of the frenetic activity during the war was not publicly acknowledged until years later. A good example of this is Colossus, a machine designed by British engineer Tommy Flowers to help break the Lorenz cipher, which was used by Nazi Germany to encode high-level intelligence communication. Some of Alan Turing’s work aided in its design. Built in 1943, Colossus is arguably the first programmable, digital, and fully electronic computer. However, it was a special-purpose computer, designed specifically for code breaking. The Women’s Royal Naval Service (WRNS, known as the “Wrens”) served as operators of Colossus. In spite of the General Report of the Tunny 14 noting that several of the Wrens showed ability in cryptographic work, none of them were given the position of cryptographer, and instead were delegated more menial Colossus operation tasks 5 , 15 . 在大西洋彼岸，美国的科学家和工程师也在努力打造自己的计算机。哈佛大学教授霍华德·艾肯（Howard Aiken，他同时也是美国海军预备役的海军中校）设计了 Mark I，一台机电式的、通用的可编程计算机。它建成于 1944 年，曾协助原子弹的设计。艾肯在建造这台计算机时基本不知道图灵的工作，他的动力是让查尔斯·巴贝奇的分析机变成现实 6 。Mark I 的一个关键特性是完全自动，能在无人干预的情况下连续运行好几天 6 。这将成为未来计算机设计的一项基本特性。 On the other side of the Atlantic, American scientists and engineers were hard at work creating computers of their own. Harvard professor Howard Aiken (who was also a Naval Commander in the U.S. Navy Reserves) designed the Mark I, an electromechanical, general-purpose programmable computer. Built in 1944, it aided in the design of the atomic bomb. Aiken built his computer largely unaware of Turing’s work and was motivated by the goal of bringing Charles Babbage’s analytical engine to life 6 . A key feature of the Mark I was that it was fully automatic and able to run for days without human intervention 6 . This would be a foundational feature in future computer design. 与此同时，宾夕法尼亚大学的美国工程师约翰·莫奇利（John Mauchly）和普雷斯珀·埃克特（Presper Eckert）于 1945 年设计并建造了 电子数字积分计算机 （Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer，ENIAC）。ENIAC 可以说是现代计算机的前身。它是数字的（尽管它用的是十进制而不是二进制）、全电子的、可编程的、通用的。尽管最初版本的 ENIAC 没有存储程序能力，但在 1940 年代结束之前就为它加上了这一功能。ENIAC 由美国陆军弹道研究实验室出资建造，主要用于计算弹道轨迹。后来，它还被用来协助氢弹的设计。 Meanwhile, American engineers John Mauchly and Presper Eckert of the University of Pennsylvania designed and built the Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer (ENIAC) in 1945. ENIAC is arguably the forerunner of modern computers. It was digital (though it used decimal rather than binary), fully electronic, programmable, and general purpose. While the original version of ENIAC did not have stored-program capabilities, this feature was built into it before the end of the decade. ENIAC was financed and built for the U.S. Army’s Ballistic Research Laboratory and was designed primarily to calculate ballistic trajectories. Later, it would be used to aid in the design of the hydrogen bomb. 第二次世界大战期间，男性被征召入伍，于是女性被雇来作为人类计算员支援战事。随着第一批电子计算机的出现，女性成为了第一批程序员，因为编程当时被视为文秘工作。因此毫不奇怪，编程领域的许多早期创新，例如第一个编译器、程序模块化的概念、调试和汇编语言，都归功于女性发明者。例如，格蕾丝·霍珀（Grace Hopper）开发了第一个编译器（A-0）和第一种高级编程语言（FLOW-MATIC），后者对第一种与机器无关的编程语言 COBOL 的设计产生了重大影响。霍珀也是 Mark I 的程序员，并撰写了描述其操作的书。 As men were drafted into the armed forces during World War II, women were hired to help in the war effort as human computers. With the arrival of the first electronic computers, women became the first programmers, as programming was considered secretarial work. It should come as no surprise that many of the early innovations in programming, such as the first compiler, the notion of modularizing programs, debugging, and assembly language, are credited to women inventors. Grace Hopper, for example, developed the first compiler (A-0) and the first high-level programming language (FLOW-MATIC), the latter which heavily influenced the design of COBOL, the first machine-independent programming language. Hopper was also a programmer for the Mark I and wrote the book that described its operation. ENIAC 的程序员是六位女性：Jean Jennings Bartik、Betty Snyder Holberton、Kay McNulty Mauchly、Frances Bilas Spence、Marlyn Wescoff Meltzer 和 Ruth Lichterman Teitelbaum。与 Wrens 不同，ENIAC 的女性程序员在工作中获得了很大的自主权：她们只拿到了 ENIAC 的接线图，就被要求弄清楚它是如何工作的、如何给它编程。除了在如何为世界上最早的电子通用计算机之一编程（和调试）这一问题上的创新之外，ENIAC 的程序员们还提出了算法流程图的思想，并发展了子程序和嵌套等重要的编程概念。与格蕾丝·霍珀一样，Jean Jennings Bartik 和 Betty Snyder Holberton 后来都在计算领域有过很长的职业生涯，是早期的计算先驱。遗憾的是，女性在早期计算中所做贡献的全貌并不为人所知。由于无法得到晋升，许多女性在第二次世界大战后离开了这一领域。想进一步了解早期的女性程序员，我们推荐读者阅读珍妮特·阿巴特（Janet Abbate）的《 Recoding Gender 》 11 、观看 LeAnn Erickson 执导的 PBS 纪录片《 Top Secret Rosies 》 12 ，以及凯西·克莱曼（Kathy Kleiman）的《 The Computers 》 13 。 The ENIAC programmers were six women: Jean Jennings Bartik, Betty Snyder Holberton, Kay McNulty Mauchly, Frances Bilas Spence, Marlyn Wescoff Meltzer, and Ruth Lichterman Teitelbaum. Unlike the Wrens, the ENIAC women were given a great deal of autonomy in their task; given just the wiring diagrams of ENIAC, they were told to figure out how it worked and how to program it. In addition to their innovation in solving how to program (and debug) one of the world’s first electronic general-purpose computers, the ENIAC programmers also developed the idea of algorithmic flow charts, and developed important programming concepts such as subroutines and nesting. Like Grace Hopper, Jean Jennings Bartik and Betty Snyder Holberton would go on to have long careers in computing, and are some of the early computing pioneers. Unfortunately, the full extent of women’s contributions in early computing is not known. Unable to advance, many women left the field after World War II. To learn more about early women programmers, we encourage readers to check out Recoding Gender 11 by Janet Abbate, Top Secret Rosies , a PBS documentary 12 directed by LeAnn Erickson, and “The Computers” by Kathy Kleiman 13 . 对计算机的潜力感兴趣的不只是英国人和美国人。在德国，康拉德·楚泽（Konrad Zuse）开发出了第一台机电式通用数字可编程计算机 Z3，于 1941 年完成。楚泽的设计独立于图灵等人的工作。值得注意的是，楚泽的设计使用的是二进制（而不是十进制），是第一台使用二进制的此类计算机。然而，Z3 在柏林遭受的空袭中被摧毁，楚泽直到 1950 年才得以继续他的工作。他的工作在很多年后才得到广泛认可。他被普遍视为德国的计算机之父。 The British and the Americans were not the only ones interested in the potential of computers. In Germany, Konrad Zuse developed the first electromechanical general-purpose digital programmable computer, the Z3, which was completed in 1941. Zuse came up with his design independently of the work of Turing and others. Notably, Zuse’s design used binary (rather than decimal), the first computer of its kind to use the binary system. However, the Z3 was destroyed during aerial bombing of Berlin, and Zuse was unable to continue his work until 1950. His work largely went unrecognized until years later. He is widely considered the father of computing in Germany. 5.1.3. 那么，冯·诺依曼知道些什么？ 5.1.3. So What Did von Neumann Know? 从我们对现代计算机体系结构起源的讨论中可以看出，1930 年代和 1940 年代出现的多项创新，促成了我们今天所知的计算机的兴起。1945 年，约翰·冯·诺依曼（John von Neumann）发表了一篇论文《EDVAC 报告书的第一份草案》（First draft of a report on the EDVAC） 9 ，其中描述的体系结构正是现代计算机的基础。EDVAC 是 ENIAC 的继任者。它与 ENIAC 的不同之处在于，它是二进制而非十进制的计算机，并且是一台存储程序计算机。今天，这份对 EDVAC 体系结构设计的描述被称为 冯·诺依曼体系结构 。 From our discussion of the origin of modern computer architecture, it is apparent that in the 1930s and 1940s there were several innovations that led to the rise of the computer as we know it today. In 1945, John von Neumann published a paper, “First draft of a report on the EDVAC” 9 , which describes an architecture on which modern computers are based. EDVAC was the successor of ENIAC. It differed from ENIAC in that it was a binary computer instead of decimal, and it was a stored-program computer. Today, this description of EDVAC’s architectural design is known as the von Neumann architecture . 冯·诺依曼体系结构 （von Neumann architecture）描述的是一种通用计算机，即设计用来运行任何程序的计算机。它还采用存储程序模型，也就是说，程序指令和数据都被加载到计算机上运行。在冯·诺依曼模型中，指令和数据没有区别：两者都被加载到计算机的内部存储器中，程序指令从存储器中取出，由计算机的功能单元执行，功能单元在程序数据上执行程序指令。 The von Neumann architecture describes a general-purpose computer, one that is designed to run any program. It also uses a stored-program model, meaning that program instructions and data are both loaded onto the computer to run. In the von Neumann model there is no distinction between instructions and data; both are loaded into the computer’s internal memory, and program instructions are fetched from memory and executed by the computer’s functional units that execute program instructions on program data. 约翰·冯·诺依曼的贡献穿插在前面几个计算故事之中。他是匈牙利裔数学家，曾任普林斯顿高等研究院（Institute for Advanced Study）和普林斯顿大学的教授，也曾是艾伦·图灵早期的导师之一。后来，冯·诺依曼成为曼哈顿计划的研究科学家，这让他结识了霍华德·艾肯和 Mark I；之后他又担任 ENIAC 项目的顾问，并与埃克特和莫奇利保持经常的通信。他那篇描述 EDVAC 的著名论文，源于他在离散变量自动电子计算机（Electronic Discrete Variable Automatic Computer，EDVAC）上的工作；EDVAC 由埃克特和莫奇利向美国陆军提出，在宾夕法尼亚大学建造。EDVAC 包含了几项体系结构设计创新，它们构成了几乎所有现代计算机的基础：它是通用的，使用二进制数制，具有内部存储器，并且是全电子的。在很大程度上，由于冯·诺依曼是这篇论文的唯一作者 9 ，论文所描述的体系结构设计主要被归功于冯·诺依曼，并被称为冯·诺依曼体系结构。需要指出的是，图灵在 1946 年非常详细地描述了一台类似机器的设计。然而，由于冯·诺依曼的论文发表在图灵的论文之前，冯·诺依曼获得了这些创新的主要功劳。 John von Neumann’s contributions weave in and out of several of the previous stories in computing. A Hungarian mathematician, he was a professor at both the Institute of Advanced Study and Princeton University, and he served as an early mentor to Alan Turing. Later, von Neumann became a research scientist on the Manhattan Project, which led him to Howard Aiken and the Mark I; he would later serve as a consultant on the ENIAC project, and correspond regularly with Eckert and Mauchly. His famous paper describing EDVAC came from his work on the Electronic Discrete Variable Automatic Computer (EDVAC), proposed to the U.S. Army by Eckert and Mauchly, and built at the University of Pennsylvania. EDVAC included several architectural design innovations that form the foundation of almost all modern computers: it was general purpose, used the binary numeric system, had internal memory, and was fully electric. In large part because von Neumann was the sole author of the paper 9 , the architectural design the paper describes is primarily credited to von Neumann and has become known as the von Neumann architecture. It should be noted that Turing described in great detail the design of a similar machine in 1946. He was a brilliant mathematician and scientist. His contributions to mathematics range from set theory to quantum mechanics and game theory. A lot of the early designers of the computer worked in isolation from one another. Isaacson argues that by witnessing the slowness of the Mark I computer, von Neumann was able to intuitively realize the value of a truly electronic computer, and the need to store and modify programs in memory.
