The von Neumann Architecture 冯·诺依曼体系结构是大多数现代计算机的基础。本节简要刻画这种体系结构的主要组成部分。 The von Neumann architecture serves as the foundation for most modern computers. In this section, we briefly characterize the architecture’s major components. 冯·诺依曼体系结构（如 图 1 所示）由五个主要部件组成： The von Neumann architecture (depicted in Figure 1 ) consists of five main components: 处理单元 （processing unit）执行程序指令。 The processing unit executes program instructions. 控制单元 （control unit）驱动处理单元执行程序指令。处理单元和控制单元一起构成 CPU。 The control unit drives program instruction execution on the processing unit. Together, the processing and control units make up the CPU. 存储单元 （memory unit）存储程序数据和指令。 The memory unit stores program data and instructions. 输入单元 （input unit）把程序数据和指令加载到计算机上，并启动程序的执行。 The input unit(s) load program data and instructions on the computer and initiate program execution. 输出单元 （output unit）存储或接收程序的结果。 The output unit(s) store or receive program results. 各个单元之间由总线连接，单元之间用总线互相发送控制信息和数据信息。 总线 （bus）是在通信端点（值的发送方和接收方）之间传送二进制值的通信通道。例如，连接存储单元和 CPU 的数据总线可以用 32 根并行导线来实现，它们一起传送一个 4 字节的值，每根导线传送 1 位。通常，体系结构有各自独立的总线，用于在单元之间传送数据、内存地址和控制信息。各单元用控制总线发送控制信号，请求其他单元执行某个动作或通知其他单元某个动作；用地址总线向存储单元发送读或写请求的内存地址；用数据总线在单元之间传送数据。 Buses connect the units, and are used by the units to send control and data information to one another. A bus is a communication channel that transfers binary values between communication endpoints (the senders and receivers of the values). For example, a data bus that connects the memory unit and the CPU could be implemented as 32 parallel wires that together transfer a 4-byte value, 1-bit transferred on each wire. Typically, architectures have separate buses for sending data, memory addresses, and control between units. The units use the control bus to send control signals that request or notify other units of actions, the address bus to send the memory address of a read or write request to the memory unit, and the data bus to transfer data between units. 图 1. 冯·诺依曼体系结构由处理单元、控制单元、存储单元、输入单元和输出单元组成。控制单元和处理单元构成 CPU，CPU 包含 ALU、通用 CPU 寄存器和一些专用寄存器（IR 和 PC）。各单元由总线连接，总线用于单元之间的数据传送和通信。 Figure 1. The von Neumann architecture consists of the processing, control, memory, input, and output units. The control and processing units make up the CPU, which contains the ALU, the general-purpose CPU registers, and some special-purpose registers (IR and PC). The units are connected by buses used for data transfer and communication between the units. 5.2.1. CPU 5.2.1. The CPU 控制单元和处理单元一起实现了 CPU，即计算机中在程序数据上执行程序指令的部分。 The control and processing units together implement the CPU, which is the part of the computer that executes program instructions on program data. 5.2.2. 处理单元 5.2.2. The Processing Unit 冯·诺依曼机器的 处理单元 由两部分组成。第一部分是 算术逻辑单元 （arithmetic/logic unit，ALU），它执行加法、减法和逻辑或等数学运算。现代 ALU 通常能执行大量的算术运算。处理单元的第二部分是一组寄存器。 寄存器 （register）是一种小而快的存储单元，用来存放程序数据以及 ALU 正在执行的指令。关键在于，在冯·诺依曼体系结构中，指令和数据没有区别。从任何意义上讲，指令 就是 数据。因此，每个寄存器都能存放一个数据字。 The processing unit of the von Neumann machine consists of two parts. The first is the arithmetic/logic unit (ALU), which performs mathematical operations such as addition, subtraction, and logical or, to name a few. Modern ALUs typically perform a large set of arithmetic operations. The second part of the processing unit is a set of registers. A register is a small, fast unit of storage used to hold program data and the instructions that are being executed by the ALU. Crucially, there is no distinction between instructions and data in the von Neumann architecture. For all intents and purposes, instructions are data. Each register is therefore capable of holding one data word. 5.2.3. 控制单元 5.2.3. The Control Unit 控制单元 驱动程序指令的执行：它从存储器中加载指令，并把指令的操作数和操作送入处理单元。控制单元还包含一些存储空间，用于记录执行状态并确定下一步要采取的动作： 程序计数器 （program counter，PC）保存下一条要执行的指令的内存地址， 指令寄存器 （instruction register，IR）存放从存储器中加载的、当前正在执行的指令。 The control unit drives the execution of program instructions by loading them from memory and feeding instruction operands and operations through the processing unit. The control unit also includes some storage to keep track of execution state and to determine its next action to take: the program counter (PC) keeps the memory address of the next instruction to execute, and the instruction register (IR) stores the instruction, loaded from memory, that is currently being executed. 5.2.4. 存储单元 5.2.4. The Memory Unit 内部存储器是冯·诺依曼体系结构的一项关键创新。它在靠近处理单元的地方提供程序数据存储，大大缩短了执行计算所需的时间。 存储单元 同时存储程序数据和程序指令——存储程序指令是冯·诺依曼体系结构存储程序模型的关键部分。 Internal memory is a key innovation of the von Neumann architecture. It provides program data storage that is close to the processing unit, significantly reducing the amount of time to perform calculations. The memory unit stores both program data and program instructions — storing program instructions is a key part of the stored-program model of the von Neumann architecture. 不同系统的存储器大小各不相同。不过，系统的 ISA 限制了它能表示的地址范围。在现代系统中，内存的最小可寻址单位是一个字节（8 位），因此每个地址对应一个字节的唯一存储位置。于是，32 位体系结构通常支持的最大地址空间大小是 2 32 ，相当于 4 GB（GiB）的可寻址内存。 The size of memory varies from system to system. However, a system’s ISA limits the range of addresses that it can express. In modern systems, the smallest addressable unit of memory is one byte (8 bits), and thus each address corresponds to a unique memory location for one byte of storage. As a result, 32-bit architectures typically support a maximum address space size of 2 32 , which corresponds to 4 gigabytes (GiB) of addressable memory. 译注 64 位体系结构理论上可寻址 2 64 字节，但实际的处理器并没有用满 64 位地址。例如在 x86-64 Linux 上，使用 4 级页表时每个进程的用户空间约为 128 TB（47 位地址），启用 5 级页表后扩大到 64 PB。 Linux 内核文档：x86_64 内存映射 存储器 （memory）这个术语有时指系统中整个存储层次结构，它可以包括处理单元中的寄存器，也可以包括硬盘驱动器（HDD）或固态硬盘（SSD）这样的辅助存储设备。在 存储与存储器层次结构 一章中，我们会详细讨论存储器层次结构。目前，我们把「存储器」（或「内存」）与内部的 随机存取存储器 （random access memory，RAM）当作同义词使用，即中央处理器可以访问的存储器。RAM 之所以是随机存取的，是因为所有 RAM 存储位置（地址）都可以被直接访问。把 RAM 想象成一个线性的地址数组会很有帮助，每个地址对应一个字节的内存。 The term memory sometimes refers to an entire hierarchy of storage in the system. It can include registers in the processing unit as well as secondary storage devices like hard disk drives (HDD) or solid-state drives (SSD). In the Storage and Memory Hierarchy Chapter , we discuss the memory hierarchy in detail. For now, we use the term “memory” interchangeably with internal random access memory (RAM) — memory that can be accessed by the central processing unit. RAM storage is random access because all RAM storage locations (addresses) can be accessed directly. It is useful to think of RAM as a linear array of addresses, where each address corresponds to one byte of memory. 原书旁注 · 历史上的字长（Word sizes through history） 字长 （word size）由 ISA 定义，是处理器作为一个整体来处理的标准数据大小的位数。标准字长多年来几经变化。EDVAC 的字长被提议为 30 位。在 1950 年代，36 位字长很常见。随着 1960 年代 IBM 360 的问世，字长或多或少地标准化了，并开始从 16 位扩展到 32 位，再到今天的 64 位。如果你更仔细地研究 Intel 体系结构，可能会注意到其中一些早期决策的遗迹，因为 32 位和 64 位体系结构都是作为最初 16 位体系结构的扩展而加入的。 Word size , which is defined by an ISA, is the number of bits of the standard data size that a processor handles as a single unit. The standard word size has fluctuated over the years. For EDVAC, the word size was proposed at 30 bits. In the 1950s, 36-bit word sizes were common. With the innovation of the IBM 360 in the 1960s, word sizes became more or less standardized, and started to expand from 16 bits, to 32 bits, to today’s 64 bits. If you examine the Intel architecture in more detail, you may notice the remnants of some of these old decisions, as 32-bit and 64-bit architectures were added as extensions of the original 16-bit architecture. 5.2.5. 输入和输出（I/O）单元 5.2.5. The Input and Output (I/O) Units 控制单元、处理单元和存储单元构成了计算机的基础，而输入和输出单元使计算机能够与外部世界交互。具体来说，它们提供了把程序的指令和数据加载到存储器中、把数据存储到存储器之外，以及向用户显示结果的机制。 While the control, processing, and memory units form the foundation of the computer, the input and output units enable it to interact with the outside world. In particular, they provide mechanisms for loading a program’s instructions and data into memory, storing its data outside of memory, and displaying its results to users. 输入单元 由一组设备构成，使用户或程序能把外部世界的数据送入计算机。如今最常见的输入设备是键盘和鼠标。摄像头和麦克风也是例子。 The input unit consists of the set of devices that enable a user or program to get data from the outside world into the computer. The most common forms of input devices today are the keyboard and mouse. Cameras and microphones are other examples. 输出单元 由一组设备构成，它们把计算结果从计算机传回外部世界，或者把结果存储到内部存储器之外。例如，显示器就是一种常见的输出设备。其他输出设备包括扬声器和触觉反馈装置。 The output unit consists of the set of devices that relay results of computation from the computer back to the outside world or that store results outside internal memory. For example, the monitor is a common output device. Other output devices include speakers and haptics. 一些现代设备，例如触摸屏，同时充当输入和输出设备，让用户可以通过同一个设备既输入数据又接收数据。 Some modern devices, such as the touchscreen, act as both input and output, enabling users to both input and receive data from a single unified device. 固态硬盘和硬盘是另一类同时充当输入和输出设备的例子。当它们存储着由操作系统加载到计算机内存中运行的程序可执行文件时，它们充当输入设备；当它们存储着写入了程序结果的文件时，它们充当输出设备。 Solid-state and hard drives are another example of devices that act as both input and output devices. These storage devices act as input devices when they store program executable files that the operating system loads into computer memory to run, and they act as output devices when they store files to which program results are written. 5.2.6. 冯·诺依曼机器的运转：执行一个程序 5.2.6. The von Neumann Machine in Action: Executing a Program 构成冯·诺依曼体系结构的五个单元协同工作，实现一个由 取指—译码—执行—存储 （fetch-decode-execute-store）组成的动作循环，共同执行程序指令。这个循环从程序的第一条指令开始，不断重复，直到程序退出： The five units that make up the von Neumann architecture work together to implement a fetch-decode-execute-store cycle of actions that together execute program instructions. This cycle starts with a program’s first instruction, and is repeated until the program exits: 控制单元从存储器中 取出 下一条指令 。控制单元有一个特殊的寄存器——程序计数器（PC），其中存放着下一条要取出的指令的地址。它把这个地址放到 地址总线 上，并在 控制总线 上向存储单元发出一个 读 命令。存储单元随后读取指定地址处存放的字节，并通过 数据总线 把它们发送给控制单元。指令寄存器（IR）存放从存储单元收到的指令字节。控制单元还会增加 PC 的值，使它存放下一条要取的新指令的地址。 The control unit fetches the next instruction from memory . The control unit has a special register, the program counter (PC), that contains the address of the next instruction to fetch. It places that address on the address bus and places a read command on the control bus to the memory unit. The memory unit then reads the bytes stored at the specified address and sends them to the control unit on the data bus . The instruction register (IR) stores the bytes of the instruction received from the memory unit. The control unit also increments the PC’s value to store the address of the new next instruction to fetch. 控制单元对存储在 IR 中的指令进行 译码 （decode） 。它对编码了要执行哪种操作的指令位、以及编码了操作数位置的指令位进行译码。指令位是根据 ISA 对其指令编码的定义来译码的。控制单元还会从操作数所在的位置（CPU 寄存器、存储器，或编码在指令位中）取出数据操作数的值，作为处理单元的输入。 The control unit decodes the instruction stored in the IR . It decodes the instruction bits that encode which operation to perform and the bits that encode where the operands are located. The instruction bits are decoded based on the ISA’s definition of the encoding of its instructions. The control unit also fetches the data operand values from their locations (from CPU registers, memory, or encoded in the instruction bits), as input to the processing unit. 处理单元 执行 指令 。ALU 在指令的数据操作数上执行指令的操作。 The processing unit executes the instruction . The ALU performs the instruction operation on instruction data operands. 控制单元把结果 存储 到存储器中 。处理单元执行指令的结果被存储到存储器中。控制单元把结果值放到 数据总线 上，把存储位置的地址放到 地址总线 上，并在 控制总线 上发出一个 写 命令，从而把结果写入存储器。存储单元收到后，就把这个值写入存储器的指定地址处。 The control unit stores the result to memory . The result of the processing unit’s execution of the instruction is stored to memory. The control unit writes the result to memory by placing the result value on the data bus , placing the address of the storage location on the address bus , and placing a write command on the control bus . When received, the memory unit writes the value to memory at the specified address. 输入和输出单元并不直接参与程序指令的执行。它们参与程序执行的方式，是加载程序的指令和数据，以及存储或显示程序的计算结果。 The input and output units are not directly involved in the execution of program instructions. Instead, they participate in the program’s execution by loading a program’s instructions and data and by storing or displaying the results of the program’s computation. 图 2 和 图 3 以一条操作数存放在 CPU 寄存器中的示例加法指令为例，展示了冯·诺依曼体系结构执行指令的四个阶段。在 取指 阶段，控制单元读取存放在 PC 中的内存地址（1234）处的指令。它把地址发送到地址总线上，并在控制总线上发出 READ 命令。存储单元收到请求后，读取地址 1234 处的值，并通过数据总线把它发送给控制单元。控制单元把指令字节放进 IR 寄存器，并用下一条指令的地址（本例中是 1238）更新 PC。在 译码 阶段，控制单元把指令中指定要执行哪种操作的位送入处理单元的 ALU，并利用指定哪些寄存器存放操作数的指令位，把操作数的值从处理单元的寄存器读入 ALU（本例中操作数的值是 3 和 4）。在 执行 阶段，处理单元中的 ALU 对操作数执行运算，得出结果（3 + 4 等于 7）。最后，在 存储 阶段，控制单元把处理单元得出的结果（7）写入存储单元：内存地址（5678）通过地址总线发送，WRITE 命令通过控制总线发送，要存储的数据值（7）通过数据总线发送。存储单元收到这个请求后，把 7 存放到内存地址 5678 处。在这个例子中，我们假定存放结果的内存地址编码在指令位中。 Figure 2 and Figure 3 show the four phases of instruction execution by the von Neumann architecture for an example addition instruction whose operands are stored in CPU registers. In the fetch phase, the control unit reads the instruction at the memory address stored in the PC (1234). It sends the address on the address bus, and a READ command on the control bus. The memory unit receives the request, reads the value at address 1234, and sends it to the control unit on the data bus. The control unit places the instruction bytes in the IR register and updates the PC with the address of the next instruction (1238 in this example). In the decode phase, the control unit feeds bits from the instruction that specify which operation to perform to the processing unit’s ALU, and uses instruction bits that specify which registers store operands to read operand values from the processing unit’s registers into the ALU (the operand values are 3 and 4 in this example). In the execute phase, the ALU part of the processing unit executes the operation on the operands to produce the result (3 + 4 is 7). Finally, in the store phase the control unit writes the result (7) from the processing unit to the memory unit. The memory address (5678) is sent on the address bus, a WRITE command is sent on the control bus, and the data value to store (7) is sent on the data bus. The memory unit receives this request and stores 7 at memory address 5678. In this example, we assume that the memory address to store the result is encoded in the instruction bits. 图 2. 以一条示例加法指令为例，冯·诺依曼体系结构执行指令的取指和译码阶段。操作数、结果和内存地址以十进制值表示，存储器内容以二进制值表示。 Figure 2. The fetch and decode stages of execution of the von Neumann architecture for an example addition instruction. The execute and store stages of execution of the von Neumann architecture for an example addition instruction. Operand, result, and memory addresses are shown as decimal values, memory contents are shown as binary values.

Circuits 数字电路实现了体系结构的核心功能。它们在硬件中实现 指令集架构 （ISA），也实现整个系统中的存储和控制功能。设计数字电路需要运用多层抽象：实现复杂功能的电路由实现部分功能的较小电路构成，这些较小电路又由更简单的电路构成，如此层层向下，直到所有数字电路的基本构件——逻辑门。 图 1 展示了一个抽象掉实现细节的电路。这个电路被表示为一个 黑盒 ，上面标着它的功能或名称，只画出它的输入和输出，隐藏了内部实现的细节。 Digital circuits implement core functionality of the architecture. Storage Circuits 存储电路 （storage circuit）用来构建存储二进制值的计算机存储器。用存储电路构建的这类计算机存储器称为 静态 RAM （static RAM，SRAM），它被用来构建 CPU 的寄存器存储和片上缓存。系统通常用 动态 RAM （dynamic RAM，DRAM）作为主存（RAM）。DRAM 基于电容的设计要求周期性地刷新它所存储的值，「动态」这个名字由此而来。SRAM 是基于电路的存储，不需要刷新它的值，因此称为静态 RAM。基于电路的存储器比基于电容的存储器更快，但也更贵。因此，SRAM 往往用于 存储器层次结构 顶端的存储（CPU 寄存器和片上缓存），而 DRAM 用于主存（RAM）存储。本章重点关注像 SRAM 这样基于电路的存储器。 Storage circuits are used to construct computer memory for storing binary values. The type of computer memory built from storage circuits is called static RAM (SRAM). It is used to build CPU register storage and on-chip cache memory. Systems typically use dynamic RAM (DRAM) for main memory (RAM) storage. The capacitor-based design of DRAM requires that it be periodically refreshed with the value it stores, hence the “dynamic” moniker. SRAM is circuit-based storage that does not need to have its values refreshed, thus it is referred to as static RAM. Circuit-based memory is faster but more expensive than capacitor-based memory. As a result, SRAM tends to be used for storage at the top of the memory hierarchy (CPU registers and on-chip cache memory), and DRAM for main memory (RAM) storage. In this chapter, we focus on circuit-based memory like SRAM. 要存储一个值，电路必须包含一个反馈回路，使这个值被电路保持住。换句话说，存储电路的值既取决于它的输入值，也取决于它当前存储的值。当电路存储着一个值时，它当前存储的值和它的输入一起，产生一个与当前存储值相同的输出（即电路继续存储同一个值）。当一个新值被写入存储电路时，电路的输入值会短暂地改变，从而改变电路的行为，使一个新值被写入并存储在电路中。一旦写入完成，电路就恢复到稳定状态，存储着新写入的值，直到下一次写入该电路为止。 To store a value, a circuit must contain a feedback loop so that the value is retained by the circuit. In other words, a storage circuit’s value depends on its input values and also its currently stored value. When the circuit stores a value, its currently stored value and its inputs together produce an output that matches the currently stored value (i.e. the circuit continues to store the same value). When a new value is written into a storage circuit, the circuit’s input values change momentarily to modify the behavior of the circuit, which results in a new value being written into and stored in the circuit. Once written, the circuit resumes a steady state of storing the newly written value until the next write to the circuit occurs. RS 锁存器 RS Latch 锁存器（latch）是一种存储（或者说记住）一位值的数字电路。一个例子是 复位—置位锁存器 （reset-set latch，即 RS 锁存器）。RS 锁存器有两个输入值 S 和 R，以及一个输出值 Q，Q 也就是锁存器中存储的值。RS 锁存器还可以额外输出 NOT(Q)，即存储值的反。 图 1 展示了一个存储单个位的 RS 锁存器电路。 A latch is a digital circuit that stores (or remembers) a 1-bit value. One example is a reset-set latch (or RS latch). An RS latch has two input values, S and R, and one output value, Q, which is also the value stored in the latch. An RS latch may additionally output NOT(Q), the negation of the stored value. Figure 1 shows an RS latch circuit for storing a single bit. 图 1. RS 锁存器电路存储一位值。 Figure 1. An RS latch circuit stores a 1-bit value. 关于 RS 锁存器，首先要注意的是从输出到输入的反馈回路：上面 NAND 门的输出（Q）是下面 NAND 门的输入（a），而下面 NAND 门的输出（~Q）是上面 NAND 门的输入（b）。当输入 S 和 R 都为 1 时，RS 锁存器存储着值 Q。换句话说，当 S 和 R 都为 1 时，RS 锁存器的输出值 Q 是稳定的。为了看清这一行为，参见 图 2 ，它展示了一个存储着值 1 的 RS 锁存器（Q 为 1）。当 R 和 S 都为 1 时，下面 NAND 门的反馈输入值（a）是 Q 的值，即 1，所以下面 NAND 门的输出为 0（1 NAND 1 为 0）。上面 NAND 门的反馈输入值（b）是下面 NAND 门的输出，即 0。上面 NAND 门的另一个输入是 S 的值 1。上面门的输出为 1（1 NAND 0 为 1）。因此，当 S 和 R 都为 1 时，这个电路持续存储着 Q 的值（本例中为 1）。 The first thing to note about the RS latch is the feedback loop from its outputs to its inputs: the output of the top NAND gate (Q) is input (a) to the bottom NAND gate, and the output of the bottom NAND gate (~Q) is input (b) to the top NAND gate. When inputs S and R are both 1, the RS latch stores the value Q. In other words, when S and R are both 1, the RS latch output value Q is stable. To see this behavior, consider Figure 2 ; this shows an RS latch that stores the value 1 (Q is 1). When R and S are both 1, the feedback input value (a) to the bottom NAND gate is the value of Q, which is 1, so the output of the bottom NAND gate is 0 (1 NAND 1 is 0). The feedback input value (b) to the top NAND gate is the output of the bottom NAND gate, which is 0. The other input to the top NAND gate is 1, the value of S. The output of the top gate is 1 (1 NAND 0 is 1). Thus, when S and R are both 1, this circuit continuously stores the value of Q (1 in this example). 图 2. 存储一位值的 RS 锁存器。锁存器存储一个值时，R 和 S 都为 1。存储的值就是输出 Q。 Figure 2. An RS latch that stores a 1-bit value. R and S are both 1 when the latch stores a value. The stored value is output Q. 要改变 RS 锁存器中存储的值，就把 R 或 S 中恰好一个的值设为 0。锁存器存储了新值之后，R 和 S 再恢复为 1。RS 锁存器周围的控制电路确保 R 和 S 永远不会同时为 0：它们中最多只有一个的值为 0，而 R 或 S 中有一个为 0，就意味着正在向 RS 锁存器写入一个值。要在 RS 锁存器中存储值 0，就把输入 R 设为 0（S 的值保持为 1）。要在 RS 锁存器中存储值 1，就把输入 S 设为 0（R 的值保持为 1）。例如，假设 RS 锁存器当前存储着 1。要把 0 写入锁存器，就把 R 的值设为 0。这意味着值 0 和 1 被输入下面的 NAND 门，它计算 (0 NAND 1) 的结果，即 1。这个输出值 1 同时也是上面 NAND 门的输入 b（如 图 3 B 所示）。有了新的输入值 b = 1 和输入值 S = 1，上面的 NAND 门为 Q 算出新的输出值 0，它也作为输入 a 送入下面的 NAND 门（如 图 3 C 所示）。a 的值为 0、b 的值为 1，锁存器现在存储着 0。当 R 最终恢复为 1 时，RS 锁存器继续存储值 0（如 图 3 D 所示）。 To change the value stored in an RS latch, the value of exactly one of R or S is set to 0. When the latch stores the new value, R and S are set back to 1. Control circuitry around the RS latch ensures that R and S can never simultaneously be 0: at most one of them will have a value 0, and a value of 0 for one of R or S means that a value is being written into the RS latch. To store the value 0 in an RS latch, input R is set to 0 (and the value of S stays at 1). To store the value 1 in an RS latch, input S is set to 0 (and the value of R stays at 1). For example, assume that the RS latch currently stores 1. To write 0 into the latch, R’s value is set to 0. This means that the values 0 and 1 are input to the lower NAND gate which computes the result of (0 NAND 1), or is 1. This output value of 1 is also input b to the top NAND gate (shown in Figure 3 B). With a new b input value of 1 and the S input value 1, the upper NAND gate computes a new output value 0 for Q, which is also fed as input a into the lower NAND gate (shown in Figure 3 C). With a’s value 0 and b’s value 1, the latch now stores 0. When R is eventually set back to 1 the RS latch continues to store the value 0 (shown in Figure 3 D). 图 3. 要向 RS 锁存器写入 0，就暂时把 R 设为 0。 Figure 3. To write 0 to an RS latch, momentarily set R to 0. 门控 D 锁存器 Gated D Latch 门控 D 锁存器 （gated D latch）在 RS 锁存器之外增加了一些电路，确保它永远不会同时在 R 和 S 上收到 0。 图 4 展示了门控 D 锁存器的构造。 A gated D latch adds circuitry to an RS latch to ensure that it never receives an input of 0 to both R and S simultaneously. Figure 4 shows the construction of a gated D latch. 图 4. 门控 D 锁存器存储一位值。它的第一组 NAND 门控制对 RS 锁存器的写入，确保 R 和 S 的值永远不会同时为 0。 Figure 4. A gated D latch stores a 1-bit value. Its first set of NAND gates control writes to the RS latch and ensure that the values of R and S are never both simultaneously 0. 门控 D 锁存器的数据输入（D）是要存入电路的值（0 或 1）。写使能（Write Enable，WE）输入控制向 RS 锁存器写入值。当 WE 为 0 时，两个 NAND 门的输出都是 1，使 RS 锁存器的 S 和 R 输入值都为 1（RS 锁存器保存着一个值）。只有当 WE 为 1 时，门控 D 锁存器才会把 D 的值写入 RS 锁存器。由于数据输入（D）的值在送入下面的 NAND 门之前被取反，上下两个 NAND 门中只有一个的输入为 1。这意味着当 WE 位为 1 时，R 和 S 中恰好有一个为 0。例如，当 D 为 1、WE 为 1 时，上面的 NAND 门计算 (1 NAND 1)，下面的 NAND 门计算 (0 NAND 1)。于是，上面 NAND 门给 S 的输入为 0，下面 NAND 门给 R 的输入为 1，结果就把值 1 写入了 RS 锁存器。当 WE 输入为 0 时，两个 NAND 门都输出 1，使 R 和 S 保持为 1。换句话说，当 WE 为 0 时，D 的值对 RS 锁存器中存储的值没有影响；只有当 WE 为 1 时，D 的值才会被写入锁存器。要向门控 D 锁存器写入另一个值，就把 D 设为要存储的值，并把 WE 设为 1。 The data input (D) to the gated D latch is the value to store into the circuit (either 0 or 1). The Write Enable (WE) input controls writing a value into the RS latch. When WE is 0, the output from both NAND gates is 1, resulting in S and R input values of 1 to the RS latch (the RS latch stores a value). The gated D latch writes the value of D into the RS latch only when WE is 1. Because the data input (D) value is inverted before it is sent to the bottom NAND gate, the input of only one of the top or bottom NAND gates input is 1. This means that when the WE bit is 1, exactly one of R or S is 0. For example, when D is 1 and WE is 1, the top NAND computes (1 NAND 1) and the bottom NAND gate computes (O NAND 1). As a result, the input to S from the top NAND gate is 0 and the input to R from the bottom NAND gate is 1, resulting in writing the value 1 into the RS latch. When the WE input is 0, both NAND gates output 1, keeping R and S at 1. In other words, when WE is 0, the value of D has no effect on the value stored in the RS latch; only when WE is 1 is the value of D written into the latch. To write another value into the gated D latch, set D to the value to store and WE to 1. CPU 寄存器 CPU Register 多位存储电路是由几个 1 位存储电路连接在一起构成的。例如，把 32 个 1 位 D 锁存器组合在一起，就得到一个可以用作 32 位 CPU 寄存器的 32 位存储电路，如 图 5 所示。寄存器电路有两个输入值：一个 32 位数据值和一个 1 位写使能信号。在内部，每个 1 位 D 锁存器以寄存器 32 位 Data in （数据输入）中的一位作为它的 D 输入，并以寄存器的 WE 输入作为它的 WE 输入。寄存器的输出就是存储在构成寄存器电路的 32 个 1 位 D 锁存器中的 32 位值。 Multibit storage circuits are built by linking several 1-bit storage circuits together. For example, combining 32 1-bit D latches together yields a 32-bit storage circuit that could be used as a 32-bit CPU register, as shown in Figure 5 . The register circuit has two input values: a 32-bit data value and a 1-bit Write Enable signal. Internally, each 1-bit D latch takes as its D input one bit of the register’s 32-bit Data in input, and each 1-bit D latch takes the register’s WE input as its WE input. The register’s output is the 32-bit value stored across the 32 1-bit D latches that make up the register circuit. 图 5. CPU 寄存器由多个门控 D 锁存器构成（32 位寄存器由 32 个构成）。当它的 WE 输入为 1 时，Data 输入被写入寄存器。它的 Data 输出就是存储的值。 Figure 5. A CPU register is built from multiple gated D latches (32 of them for a 32-bit register). When its WE input is 1, the Data input is written into the register. Its Data output is the stored value.

Building a Processor: Putting It All Together 中央处理器 （CPU）实现了冯·诺依曼体系结构中的处理单元和控制单元，即驱动程序指令在程序数据上执行的那些部分（见 图 1 ）。 The central processing unit (CPU) implements the processing and control units of the von Neumann architecture, the parts that drive the execution of program instructions on program data (see Figure 1 ). 图 1. CPU 实现了冯·诺依曼体系结构中的处理单元和控制单元部分。 Figure 1. The CPU implements the processing and control unit parts of the von Neumann architecture. CPU 由基本的算术/逻辑电路、存储电路和控制电路构件组成。它的主要功能部件包括：执行算术和逻辑运算的 算术逻辑单元 （ALU）；用于存储程序数据的一组通用 寄存器 ；实现指令执行时用到的一些控制电路和专用寄存器；以及驱动 CPU 电路执行程序指令的 时钟 （clock）。 The CPU is constructed from basic arithmetic/logic, storage, and control circuit building blocks. Its main functional components are the arithmetic logic unit (ALU), which performs arithmetic and logic operations; a set of general-purpose registers for storing program data; some control circuitry and special-purpose registers that are used in the implementation of instruction execution; and a clock that drives the circuitry of the CPU to execute program instructions. 本节介绍 CPU 的主要组成部分，包括 ALU 和寄存器文件，并说明如何把它们组合起来实现一个 CPU。下一节讨论 CPU 如何执行程序指令，以及如何用时钟驱动程序指令的执行。 In this section, we present the main parts of the CPU, including the ALU and register file, and show how they are combined to implement a CPU. In the next section, we discuss how the CPU executes program instructions and how the clock is used to drive the execution of program instructions. 5.5.1. ALU 5.5.1. The ALU ALU 是一个复杂的电路，它实现对有符号整数和无符号整数的所有算术和逻辑运算。另有一个单独的浮点单元对浮点值执行算术运算。ALU 接收整数操作数值和一个 操作码 （opcode）值，操作码指定要执行的运算（例如加法）。ALU 输出在操作数输入上执行指定运算得到的结果值，以及编码了运算结果相关信息的 条件码 （condition code）值。常见的条件码表示 ALU 的结果是否为负、是否为零，或者运算是否产生了进位输出位。例如，对于 C 语句 The ALU is a complex circuit that implements all arithmetic and logic operations on signed and unsigned integers. A separate floating-point unit performs arithmetic operations on floating-point values. The ALU takes integer operand values and an opcode value that specifies the operation to perform (e.g. addition). The ALU outputs the resulting value of performing the specified operation on the operand inputs and condition code values that encode information about the result of the operation. Common condition codes specify whether the ALU result is negative, zero, or if there is a carry-out bit from the operation. For example, given the C statement x = 6 + 8; CPU 开始执行这次加法时，把操作数值（6 和 8）以及编码了 ADD 运算的位送入 ALU 电路。ALU 算出结果并输出，同时输出条件码，表示结果非负、非零，且没有产生进位输出。每个条件码用一个位编码。位值为 1 表示条件成立，位值为 0 表示 ALU 的结果不满足该条件。在我们的例子中，位模式 000 表示执行 6+8 对应的三个条件：结果不为负（0）、不为零（0），进位输出值为零（0）。 the CPU begins executing the addition by feeding the operand values (6 and 8) and the bits that encode an ADD operation to the ALU circuit. The ALU computes the result and outputs it along with condition codes to indicate that the result is nonnegative, is nonzero, and causes no carry-out. Each condition code is encoded in a single bit. A bit value of 1 indicates that the condition holds, and a bit value of 0 indicates that it does not hold for the ALU result. In our example, the bit pattern 000 specifies the set of three conditions associated with executing 6+8: the result is not negative (0), is not zero (0), and the carry-out value is zero (0). ALU 在执行运算时设置的条件码，有时会被后续根据特定条件选择动作的指令使用。例如，一条 ADD 指令可以计算下面这个 if 语句中的 (x + 8) 部分： Condition codes, set by the ALU as part of its execution of an operation, are sometimes used by subsequent instructions that choose an action based on a particular condition. For example, an ADD instruction can compute the (x + 8) part of the following if statement: if( (x + 8) != 0 ) { x++; } ALU 执行 ADD 指令时，会根据 (x + 8) 相加的结果设置条件码。在 ADD 指令之后执行的条件跳转指令会检测 ADD 指令设置的条件码位，并根据它们的值决定是否跳转（跳过 if 语句体中的指令）。例如，如果 ADD 指令把零条件码设为 0，条件跳转指令就不会跳过 if 语句体对应的指令（零条件码为 0 表示 ADD 的结果不为零）。如果零条件码为 1，它就会跳过 if 语句体的指令。为了实现跳过一组指令，CPU 会把 if 语句体指令之后第一条指令的内存地址写入 程序计数器 （PC），PC 中存放的是下一条要执行的指令的地址。 The ALU’s execution of the ADD instruction sets condition codes based on the result of adding (x + 8) . A conditional jump instruction executed after the ADD instruction tests the condition code bits set by the ADD instruction and either jumps (skips over executing the instructions in the if body) or not based on their value. For example, if the ADD instruction sets the zero condition code to 0, the conditional jump instruction will not jump past the instructions associated with the if body (0 for the zero condition code means that the result of the ADD was not zero). If the zero condition code is 1, it will jump past the if body instructions. To implement a jump past a set of instructions, the CPU writes the memory address of the first instruction after the if body instructions into the program counter (PC), which contains the address of the next instruction to execute. ALU 电路把几个算术和逻辑电路（用于实现它的运算集合）与一个多路复用器电路组合起来，由多路复用器选出 ALU 的输出。一个简单的 ALU 并不试图只选择性地激活与特定运算对应的那个算术电路，而是把它的操作数输入值送入它内部所有的算术和逻辑电路。ALU 内部所有算术和逻辑电路的输出都被输入到它的多路复用器电路，由多路复用器选出 ALU 的输出。ALU 的操作码输入被用作多路复用器的信号输入，以选择哪个算术/逻辑运算的结果作为 ALU 的输出。条件码输出则基于 MUX 的输出，再配合检测输出值的电路来确定每个条件码位。 An ALU circuit combines several arithmetic and logic circuits (for implementing its set of operations) with a multiplexer circuit to pick the ALU’s output. Rather than trying to selectively activate only the arithmetic circuit associated with the specific operation, a simple ALU sends its operand input values to all of its internal arithmetic and logic circuits. The output from all of the ALU’s internal arithmetic and logic circuits are input to its multiplexer circuit, which chooses the ALU’s output. The opcode input to the ALU is used as the signal input to the multiplexer to select which arithmetic/logic operation to select as the ALU’s output. Condition code output is based on the MUX output combined with circuitry to test the output’s value to determine each condition code bit. 图 2 展示了一个示例 ALU 电路，它对两个 32 位操作数执行四种不同的运算（ADD、OR、AND 和 EQUALS）。它还产生一个条件码输出，表示运算结果是否为零。注意，ALU 把操作码送到一个多路复用器，由它选择输出 ALU 的四个运算结果中的哪一个。 Figure 2 shows an example ALU circuit that performs four different operations (ADD, OR, AND, and EQUALS) on two 32-bit operands. It also produces a single condition code output that indicates whether the result of the operation is zero. Notice that the ALU directs the opcode to a multiplexer that selects which of the ALU’s four arithmetic results it outputs. 图 2. 一个对两个 32 位操作数执行 ADD、OR、AND 和 EQUALS 的四功能 ALU。它有一个条件码输出位，表示结果是否为 0。 Figure 2. A four-function ALU that performs ADD, OR, AND, and EQUALS on two 32-bit operands. It has one condition code output bit that specifies whether the result is 0. ALU 的操作码输入来自 CPU 正在执行的指令中的某些位。例如，一条 ADD 指令的二进制编码可能由四部分组成： The opcode input to the ALU comes from bits in the instruction that the CPU is executing. For example, the binary encoding for an ADD instruction might consist of four parts: | OPCODE BITS | OPERAND A SOURCE | OPERAND B SOURCE | RESULT DESTINATION | 根据 CPU 体系结构的不同，操作数来源位可能编码一个 CPU 寄存器、存放操作数值的内存地址，或者字面操作数值。例如，在执行 6 + 8 的指令中，字面值 6 和 8 可以直接编码在指令的操作数说明位中。 Depending on the CPU architecture, operand source bits might encode a CPU register, the memory address storing the operand value, or literal operand values. For example, in an instruction to perform 6 + 8, the literal values 6 and 8 could be encoded directly into the operand specifier bits of the instruction. 对于我们的 ALU，由于它支持四种运算，操作码需要两位，因为两位可以编码四个不同的值（00、01、10、11），每个值对应一种运算。一般来说，执行 N 种不同运算的 ALU 需要 log 2 ( N ) 个操作码位，来指定从 ALU 输出哪个运算的结果。 For our ALU, the opcode requires two bits because the ALU supports four operations, and two bits can encode four distinct values (00, 01, 10, 11), one for each operation. In general, an ALU that performs N distinct operations, needs log 2 ( N ) opcode bits to specify which operation result to output from the ALU. 图 3 展示了 ADD 指令的操作码位和操作数位如何作为我们这个 ALU 的输入。 Figure 3 shows an example of how the opcode and operand bits of an ADD instruction are used as input into our ALU. 图 3. ALU 用指令中的操作码位来选择输出哪个运算的结果。在这个例子中，ADD 指令的不同位被分别送入 ALU 的操作数输入和操作码输入，执行 6 与 8 的加法。 Figure 3. Opcode bits from an instruction are used by the ALU to choose which operation to output. In this example, different bits from an ADD instruction are fed into the ALU operand and opcode inputs to perform addition of 6 and 8. 5.5.2. 寄存器文件 5.5.2. The Register File 在存储器层次结构的顶端，CPU 的一组通用寄存器存放临时值。CPU 提供的寄存器数量非常少，通常为 8–32 个（例如，IA32 体系结构提供 8 个，MIPS 提供 16 个，ARM 提供 13 个）。指令常常从通用寄存器中获取操作数值，或者把结果存入通用寄存器。例如，一条 ADD 指令可能编码为 「把寄存器 1 中的值与寄存器 2 中的值相加，并把结果存入寄存器 3」 。 At the top of the memory hierarchy, the CPU’s set of general-purpose registers store temporary values. CPUs provide a very small number of registers, commonly 8-32 (e.g., the IA32 architecture provides 8, MIPS provides 16, and ARM provides 13). Instructions often get their operand values from, or store their results to, general-purpose registers. For example, an ADD instruction may be encoded as “add the value from Register 1 to the value from Register 2 and store the result in Register 3” . 译注 这里列出的寄存器数目只是举例，而且与具体的体系结构版本有关：本书第 7 章会讲到 x86-64 有 16 个通用寄存器，第 9 章会讲到 ARM64（AArch64）有 31 个通用寄存器（x0–x30）；原书说的「ARM 13 个」指的是 32 位 ARM 中 r0–r12 这 13 个寄存器（另有 SP、LR、PC 三个专用寄存器）。 CPU 的一组通用寄存器被组织成一个 寄存器文件 （register file）电路。寄存器文件由一组用于存储数据值的 寄存器电路 ，以及一些控制对其寄存器进行读写的 控制电路 组成。这个电路通常有一条数据输入线，用于写入其某个寄存器的值；还有两条数据输出线，用于同时从其寄存器中读出两个值。 The CPU’s set of general-purpose registers is organized into a register file circuit. A register file consists of a set of register circuits for storing data values and some control circuits for controlling reads and writes to its registers. The circuit typically has a single data input line for the value to write into one of its registers, and two data output lines for simultaneously reading two values from its registers. 图 4 展示了一个含四个寄存器的寄存器文件电路的例子。它的两个输出值（Data out 0 和 Data out 1 ）由两个多路复用器电路控制。它的每个读选择输入（Sr 0 和 Sr 1 ）分别送入其中一个 MUX，为相应的输出选出寄存器的值。寄存器文件的数据输入（Data in 线）被送到每个寄存器电路，而它的写使能（WE）输入先经过一个多路分配器（DMUX）电路，再送到各个寄存器电路。DMUX 电路接收一个输入值，选择把这个值送到 N 个输出中的哪一个，其余 N-1 个输出都为 0。寄存器文件的写选择输入（S w ）被送到 DMUX 电路，用来选择 WE 值的目标寄存器。当寄存器文件的 WE 输入值为 0 时，不会有值被写入任何寄存器，因为每个寄存器的 WE 位也都是 0（因此 Data in 对寄存器中存储的值没有影响）。当 WE 位为 1 时，DMUX 只向写选择输入（S w ）指定的那个寄存器输出值为 1 的 WE 位，从而只把 Data in 的值写入被选中的寄存器。 Figure 4 shows an example of a register file circuit with four registers. Its two output values (Data out 0 and Data out 1 ) are controlled by two multiplexer circuits. Each of its read selection inputs (Sr 0 and Sr 1 ) is fed into one of the MUXs to pick the register value for the corresponding output. The data input to the register file (the Data in line) is sent to every register circuit, and its write enable (WE) input is fed through a demultiplexer (DMUX) circuit first before being sent to each register circuit. A DMUX circuit takes one input value and chooses which of N outputs to send the value to, sending the remaining N-1 outputs 0. The write selection input (S w ) to the register file is sent to the DMUX circuit to choose the WE value’s destination register. When the register file’s WE input value is 0, no value is written into a register because each register’s WE bit also gets 0 (thus, Data in has no effect on the values stored in the registers). When the WE bit is 1, the DMUX outputs a WE bit value of 1 to only the register specified by the write selection input (S w ), resulting in the Data in value being written to the selected register only. 图 4. 寄存器文件：一组 CPU 通用寄存器，用于存储指令的操作数和结果值。 Figure 4. The register file: the set of CPU general-purpose registers used to store instruction operand and result values. 专用寄存器 Special-Purpose Registers 除了寄存器文件中的通用寄存器之外，CPU 还包含一些专用寄存器，用于存储指令的地址和内容。 程序计数器 （PC）存放下一条要执行的指令的内存地址， 指令寄存器 （IR）存放 CPU 当前正在执行的指令的各个位。在指令执行过程中，IR 中存放的指令位被用作 CPU 不同部分的输入。我们会在下一节 指令执行 中更详细地讨论这些寄存器。 In addition to the set of general-purpose registers in the register file, a CPU contains special-purpose registers that store the address and content of instructions. The program counter (PC) stores the memory address of the next instruction to execute, and the instruction register (IR) stores the bits of the current instruction being executed by the CPU. The bits of the instruction stored in the IR are used as input into different parts of the CPU during the instruction’s execution. We discuss these registers in more detail in the next section on instruction execution . 5.5.3. CPU 5.5.3. The CPU 有了 ALU 和寄存器文件电路，我们就可以构建 CPU 的主要部分，如 图 5 所示。由于指令的操作数常常来自通用寄存器中存储的值，寄存器文件的输出把数据送到 ALU 的输入。类似地，由于指令的结果常常存入寄存器，ALU 的结果输出被作为输入送到寄存器文件。CPU 还有额外的电路，用于在 ALU、寄存器文件和其他部件（例如主存）之间移动数据。 With the ALU and register file circuits, we can build the main parts of the CPU, as shown in Figure 5 . Because instruction operands often come from values stored in general-purpose registers, the register file’s outputs send data to the ALU’s inputs. Similarly, because instruction results are often stored in registers, the ALU’s result output is sent as input to the register file. The CPU has additional circuitry to move data between the ALU, register file, and other components (e.g., main memory). 图 5. ALU 和寄存器文件构成了 CPU 的主要部分。ALU 执行运算，寄存器文件存储操作数和结果值。另外的专用寄存器存储指令的地址（PC）和内容（IR）。注意，指令可能从寄存器文件以外的位置（例如主存）获取操作数或存储结果。 Figure 5. The ALU and register file make up the main parts of the CPU. The ALU performs operations, and the register file stores operand and result values. Additional special-purpose registers store instruction addresses (PC) and contents (IR). Note that instructions might retrieve operands from or store results to locations other than the register file (e.g., main memory). CPU 的这些主要部分构成了它的 数据通路 （data path）。数据通路由 CPU 中执行算术和逻辑运算的部分（ALU）、存储数据的部分（寄存器）以及连接这些部分的总线组成。CPU 还实现了一条 控制通路 （control path），驱动 ALU 在寄存器文件中存储的操作数上执行程序指令。此外，控制通路还根据指令的需要向 I/O 设备发出命令并协调内存访问。例如，有些指令可能直接从内存位置获取操作数值（或者直接把结果存入内存位置），而不是通用寄存器。在下一节中，我们对 CPU 指令执行的讨论集中在从寄存器文件获取操作数值并把结果存入寄存器文件的指令上。CPU 需要额外的控制电路来从其他位置读取操作数值或向其他位置写入指令结果，但无论来源和目标位置是什么，指令执行的主要步骤都是相同的。 These main parts of the CPU make up its data path . The data path consists of the parts of the CPU that perform arithmetic and logic operations (the ALU) and store data (registers), and the buses that connect these parts. The CPU also implements a control path that drives the execution of program instructions by the ALU on operands stored in the register file. Additionally, the control path issues commands to I/O devices and coordinates memory accesses as needed by instructions. For example, some instructions may get their operand values directly from (or store their results directly to) memory locations rather than general-purpose registers. In the next section, we focus our discussion of CPU instruction execution on instructions that get operand values and store results to the register file. The CPU requires additional control circuitry to read operand values or to write instruction results to other locations, but the main instruction execution steps behave the same regardless of the source and destination locations.

The Processor’s Execution of Program Instructions 指令的执行分若干个阶段进行。不同的体系结构实现的阶段数各不相同，但大多数都把指令执行的取指（Fetch）、译码（Decode）、执行（Execute）和写回（WriteBack）几个阶段实现为四个或更多的独立阶段。在讨论指令执行时，我们重点关注这四个执行阶段，并以一条 ADD 指令为例。我们的示例 ADD 指令的编码如 图 1 所示。 Instruction execution is performed in several stages. Different architectures implement different numbers of stages, but most implement the Fetch, Decode, Execute, and WriteBack phases of instruction execution in four or more discrete stages. In discussing instruction execution, we focus on these four stages of execution, and we use an ADD instruction as our example. Our ADD instruction example is encoded as shown in Figure 1 . 图 1. 三寄存器运算的一种示例指令格式。指令用二进制编码，它的不同位子集对应于指令不同部分的编码：运算（操作码）、两个源寄存器（操作数），以及存放运算结果的目标寄存器。示例展示了一条 ADD 指令按这种格式的编码。 Figure 1. An example instruction format for a three-register operation. The instruction is encoded in binary with subsets of its bits corresponding to encodings of different parts of the instruction: the operation (opcode), the two source registers (the operands), and the destination register for storing the result of the operation. The example shows the encoding of an ADD instruction in this format. 要执行一条指令，CPU 首先从内存中把下一条指令 取 到一个专用寄存器——指令寄存器（IR）——中。要取的指令的内存地址存放在另一个专用寄存器——程序计数器（PC）——中。PC 记录下一条要取的指令的内存地址，并在执行取指阶段时递增，从而存放紧接着的下一条指令的内存地址。例如，如果所有指令都是 32 位长，那么 PC 的值就加 4（每个字节 8 位，有一个唯一的地址），以存放紧跟在正在取的那条指令之后的指令的内存地址。递增 PC 值的是独立于 ALU 的算术电路。PC 的值也可能在写回阶段改变。例如，有些指令会跳转到特定的地址，比如与循环、 if - else 或函数调用的执行相关的地址。 图 2 展示了执行的取指阶段。 To execute an instruction, the CPU first fetches the next instruction from memory into a special-purpose register, the instruction register (IR). The memory address of the instruction to fetch is stored in another special-purpose register, the program counter (PC). The PC keeps track of the memory address of the next instruction to fetch and is incremented as part of executing the fetch stage, so that it stores the value of the very next instruction’s memory address. For example, if all instructions are 32 bits long, then the PC’s value is incremented by 4 (each byte, 8 bits, has a unique address) to store the memory address of the instruction immediately following the one being fetched. Arithmetic circuits that are separate from the ALU increment the PC’s value. The PC’s value may also change during the WriteBack stage. For example, some instructions jump to specific addresses, such as those associated with the execution of loops, if - else , or function calls. Figure 2 shows the fetch stage of execution. 图 2. 指令执行的取指阶段：从内存中读出 PC 寄存器中存放的内存地址处的指令，存入 IR。在这一阶段结束时，PC 的值也会递增（如果指令为 4 字节，下一个地址就是 1238；实际的指令大小因体系结构和指令类型而异）。 Figure 2. The fetch stage of instruction execution: the instruction at the memory address value stored in the PC register is read from memory and stored into the IR. The PC’s value is also incremented at the end of this stage (if instructions are 4 bytes, then the next address is 1238; the actual instruction size varies by architecture and instruction type). 取出指令之后，CPU 把存放在 IR 寄存器中的指令位 译码 为四部分：指令的高位编码操作码，指定要执行的运算（例如 ADD、SUB、OR……），其余的位被分为三个子集，分别指定两个操作数的来源和结果的目标。在我们的例子中，两个来源和结果目标都使用寄存器。操作码被送到作为 ALU 输入的导线上，源位被送到作为寄存器文件输入的导线上。源位被送到两个读选择输入（Sr 0 和 Sr 1 ），它们指定从寄存器文件中读出哪些寄存器的值。译码阶段如 图 3 所示。 After fetching the instruction, the CPU decodes the instruction bits stored in the IR register into four parts: the high-order bits of an instruction encode the opcode, which specifies the operation to perform (e.g. ADD, SUB, OR, …​), and the remaining bits are divided into three subsets that specify the two operand sources and the result destination. In our example, we use registers for both sources and the result destination. The opcode is sent on wires that are input to the ALU and the source bits are sent on wires that are inputs to the register file. The source bits are sent to the two read selection inputs (Sr 0 and Sr 1 ) that specify which register values are read from the register file. The Decode stage is shown in Figure 3 . 图 3. 指令执行的译码阶段：把 IR 中的指令位分成若干部分，作为输入送到 ALU 和寄存器文件。IR 中的操作码位被送到 ALU 的选择输入，以选择要执行的运算。IR 中的两组操作数位被送到寄存器文件的选择输入，以选出读取操作数值的寄存器。IR 中的目标位在写回阶段被送到寄存器文件，它们指定 ALU 结果要写入的寄存器。 Figure 3. The Decode stage of instruction execution: separate the instruction bits in the IR into components and send them as input to the ALU and register file. The opcode bits in the IR are sent to the ALU selection input to choose which operation to perform. The two sets of operand bits in the IR are sent to the selection inputs of the register file to pick the registers from which to read the operand values. The destination bits in the IR are sent to the register file in the WriteBack stage. They specify the register to which to write the ALU result. 译码阶段确定了要执行的运算和操作数来源之后，ALU 在下一个阶段—— 执行 阶段——执行运算。ALU 的数据输入来自寄存器文件的两个输出，它的选择输入来自指令的操作码位。这些输入在 ALU 中传播，产生用该运算组合操作数值所得的结果。在我们的例子中，ALU 输出把 Reg1 中存放的值与 Reg3 中存放的值相加的结果，并输出与结果值相关的条件码值。执行阶段如 图 4 所示。 After the Decode stage determines the operation to perform and the operand sources, the ALU performs the operation in the next stage, the Execution stage. The ALU’s data inputs come from the two outputs of the register file, and its selection input comes from the opcode bits of the instruction. These inputs propagate through the ALU to produce a result that combines the operand values with the operation. In our example, the ALU outputs the result of adding the value stored in Reg1 to the value stored in Reg3, and outputs the condition code values associated with the result value. The Execution stage is shown in Figure 4 . 图 4. 指令执行的执行阶段：ALU 在其输入值（来自寄存器文件的输出）上执行指定的运算（来自指令的操作码位）。 Figure 4. The Execution stage of instruction execution: the ALU performs the specified operation (from the instruction opcode bits) on its input values (from the register file outputs). 在 写回 阶段，ALU 的结果被存入目标寄存器。寄存器文件在 Data in 输入上接收 ALU 的结果输出，在写选择（S w ）输入上接收目标寄存器（来自 IR 中的指令位），在 WE 输入上接收 1。例如，如果目标寄存器是 Reg0，那么 IR 中编码 Reg0 的位就作为 S w 输入送到寄存器文件以选出目标寄存器。ALU 的输出作为 Data in 输入送到寄存器文件，WE 位被设为 1，以允许把 ALU 结果写入 Reg0。写回阶段如 图 5 所示。 In the WriteBack stage, the ALU result is stored in the destination register. The register file receives the ALU’s result output on its Data in input, the destination register (from instructions bits in the IR) on its write-select (S w ) input, and 1 on its WE input. For example, if the destination register is Reg0, then the bits encoding Reg0 in the IR are sent as the S w input to the register file to pick the destination register. The output from the ALU is sent as the Data in input to the register file, and the WE bit is set to 1 to enable writing the ALU result into Reg0. The WriteBack stage is shown in Figure 5 . 图 5. 指令执行的写回阶段：执行阶段的结果（ALU 的输出）被写入寄存器文件中的目标寄存器。ALU 的输出是寄存器文件的 Data in 输入，指令的目标位送到寄存器文件的写选择输入（S w ），WE 输入设为 1，以允许把 Data in 的值写入指定的目标寄存器。 Figure 5. The WriteBack stage of instruction execution: the result of the execution stage (the output from the ALU) is written to the destination register in the register file. The ALU output is the register file’s Data in input, the destination bits of the instruction go to the register file’s write-selection input (S w ), and the WE input is set to 1 to enable writing the Data in value to the specified destination register. 5.6.1. 时钟驱动的执行 5.6.1. Clock-Driven Execution 时钟驱动着 CPU 执行指令，触发每个阶段的开始。换句话说，CPU 用时钟来确定与各个阶段相关的电路的输入何时已经准备好、可以被电路使用，并且用它来控制电路的输出何时代表某个阶段的有效结果、可以用作执行下一阶段的其他电路的输入。 A clock drives the CPU’s execution of instructions, triggering the start of each stage. In other words, the clock is used by the CPU to determine when inputs to circuits associated with each stage are ready to be used by the circuit, and it controls when outputs from circuits represent valid results from one stage and can be used as inputs to other circuits executing the next stage. CPU 时钟度量的是离散时间，而不是连续时间。换句话说，存在时刻 0，接着是时刻 1，然后是时刻 2，后续的每个时钟滴答依此类推。处理器的 时钟周期时间 （clock cycle time）度量两个时钟滴答之间的时间。处理器的 时钟速度 （clock speed，或称 时钟频率 ，clock rate）等于 1/(时钟周期时间) ，通常以兆赫（MHz）或吉赫（GHz）为单位。1 MHz 的时钟频率表示每秒一百万个时钟滴答，1 GHz 表示每秒十亿个时钟滴答。时钟频率衡量的是 CPU 能运行多快，也是对 CPU 每秒最多能执行多少条指令的估计。例如，在我们这个示例 CPU 这样简单的标量处理器上，一个 2 GHz 的处理器最多可能达到每秒二十亿条指令（即每纳秒两条指令）的指令执行速率。 A CPU clock measures discrete time as opposed to continuous time. In other words, there exists a time 0, followed by a time 1, followed by a time 2, and so on for each subsequent clock tick. A processor’s clock cycle time measures the time between each clock tick. A processor’s clock speed (or clock rate ) is 1/(clock cycle time) . It is typically measured in megahertz (MHz) or gigahertz (GHz). A 1-MHz clock rate has one million clock ticks per second, and 1-GHz has one billion clock ticks per second. The clock rate is a measure of how fast the CPU can run, and is an estimate of the maximum number of instructions per second a CPU can execute. For example, on simple scalar processors like our example CPU, a 2-GHz processor might achieve a maximum instruction execution rate of two billion instructions per second (or two instructions every nanosecond). 尽管提高单台机器的时钟频率会提升它的性能，但单靠时钟频率来比较不同处理器的性能并没有意义。例如，有些体系结构（如 RISC）执行指令所需的阶段比另一些体系结构（如 CISC）少。在执行阶段较少的体系结构中，较慢的时钟每秒完成的指令数，可能与另一种时钟频率更高但执行阶段更多的体系结构相同。不过，对于某个特定的微处理器而言，把它的时钟速度提高一倍，大致会使它的指令执行速度提高一倍。 Although increasing the clock rate on a single machine will improve its performance, clock rate alone is not a meaningful metric for comparing the performance of different processors. For example, some architectures (such as RISC) require fewer stages to execute instructions than others (such as CISC). In architectures with fewer execution stages a slower clock may yield the same number of instructions completed per second as on another architecture with a faster clock rate but more execution stages. For a specific microprocessor, however, doubling its clock speed will roughly double its instruction execution speed. 原书旁注 · 时钟频率与处理器性能（Clock Rates and Processor Performance） 历史上，提高时钟频率（同时设计出由更快的时钟驱动的、更复杂更强大的微体系结构）一直是计算机体系结构设计者提升处理器性能的非常有效的手段。例如，1974 年的 Intel 8080 CPU 运行在 2 MHz（时钟频率为每秒两百万个周期）。1995 年推出的 Intel Pentium Pro 的时钟频率是 150 MHz（每秒一亿五千万个周期），2000 年推出的 Intel Pentium 4 的时钟频率是 1.3 GHz（每秒 13 亿 个周期）。时钟频率在 2000 年代中后期达到顶峰，代表是时钟频率为 4.4 GHz 的 IBM z10 等处理器。 然而如今，由于处理更快时钟带来的散热问题，CPU 的时钟频率已经达到了极限。这一极限被称为 功耗墙 （power wall）。功耗墙促使人们从 2000 年代中期开始发展多核处理器。多核处理器的每块芯片上有多个「简单的」CPU 核心，每个核心由一个时钟驱动，其时钟频率与上一代核心相比并没有提高。多核处理器设计是一种无需提高 CPU 时钟频率就能提升 CPU 性能的方法。 Historically, increasing the clock rate (along with designing more complicated and powerful microarchitectures that a faster clock can drive) has been a very effective way for computer architects to improve processor performance. For example, in 1974, the Intel 8080 CPU ran at 2 MHz (a clock rate of two million cycles per second). The clock rate of the Intel Pentium Pro, introduced in 1995, was 150 MHz (150 million cycles per second), and the clock rate of the Intel Pentium 4, introduced in 2000, was 1.3 GHz or (1.3 billion cycles per second). Clock rates peaked in the mid to late 2000s with processors like the IBM z10, which had a clock rate of 4.4 GHz. Today, however, CPU clock rates have reached their limit due to problems associated with handling heat dissipation of faster clocks. This limit is known as the power wall . The power wall resulted in the development of multicore processors starting in the mid 2000s. Multicore processors have multiple “simple” CPU cores per chip, each core driven by a clock whose rate has not increased from the previous-generation core. Multicore processor design is a way to improve CPU performance without having to increase the CPU clock rate. 时钟电路 The Clock Circuit 时钟电路利用振荡器电路产生非常精确而规则的脉冲模式。通常由晶体振荡器产生振荡器电路的基准频率，时钟电路利用振荡器的脉冲模式，输出高低电压交替的模式，对应于 1 和 0 交替出现的二进制值模式。 图 6 展示了一个产生规则的 1、0 输出模式的示例时钟电路。 A clock circuit uses an oscillator circuit to generate a very precise and regular pulse pattern. Typically, a crystal oscillator generates the base frequency of the oscillator circuit, and the pulse pattern of the oscillator is used by the clock circuit to output a pattern of alternating high and low voltages corresponding to an alternating pattern of 1 and 0 binary values. Figure 6 shows an example clock circuit generating a regular output pattern of 1 and 0. 图 6. 时钟电路规则的 1、0 输出模式。每个 1 和 0 的序列构成一个时钟周期。 Figure 6. The regular output pattern of 1 and 0 of a clock circuit. Each sequence of 1 and 0 makes up a clock cycle. 时钟周期 （clock cycle，或称滴答，tick）是时钟电路模式中的一个 1 和 0 子序列。从 1 到 0 或从 0 到 1 的跳变称为 时钟边沿 （clock edge）。时钟边沿触发 CPU 电路中的状态变化，驱动指令的执行。上升沿（新时钟周期开始时从 0 到 1 的跳变）表示指令执行某一阶段的输入值已经准备就绪的状态。例如，上升沿跳变标志着 ALU 电路的输入值已经就绪。在时钟值为 1 期间，这些输入在电路中传播，直到电路的输出准备就绪。这称为电路的 传播延迟 （propagation delay）。例如，在时钟信号为 1 期间，ALU 的输入值在 ALU 的运算电路中传播，然后经过多路复用器，为组合输入值的运算产生正确的 ALU 输出。在下降沿（从 1 到 0 的跳变），该阶段的输出已经稳定，可以传播到下一个位置（ 图 7 中标为 “output ready”）。例如，ALU 的输出在下降沿时就绪。在时钟值为 0 期间，ALU 的输出传播到寄存器文件的输入。在下一个时钟周期，上升沿表示寄存器文件的输入值已经可以写入寄存器（ 图 7 中标为 “new input”）。 A clock cycle (or tick) is a 1 and 0 subsequence from the clock circuit pattern. The transition from a 1 to a 0 or a 0 to a 1 is called a clock edge . Clock edges trigger state changes in CPU circuits, driving the execution of instructions. The rising clock edge (the transition from 0 to 1 at the beginning of a new clock cycle) indicates a state in which input values are ready for a stage of instruction execution. For example, the rising edge transition signals that input values to the ALU circuit are ready. While the clock’s value is 1, these inputs propagate through the circuit until the output of the circuit is ready. This is called the propagation delay through the circuit. For example, while the clock signal is 1 the input values to the ALU propagate through the ALU operation circuits and then through the multiplexer to produce the correct output from the ALU for the operation combining the input values. On the falling edge (the transition from 1 to 0), the outputs of the stage are stable and ready to be propagated to the next location (shown as “output ready” in Figure 7 ). For example, the output from the ALU is ready on the falling edge. For the duration of the clock value 0, the ALU’s output propagates to register file inputs. On the next clock cycle the rising edge indicates that the register file input value is ready to write into a register (shown as “new input” in Figure 7 ). 图 7. 新时钟周期的上升沿触发它所控制的电路的输入发生变化，下降沿则在它所控制的电路的输出有效时触发。 Figure 7. The rising edge of a new clock cycle triggers changes in the inputs to the circuits it controls. The falling edge triggers when the outputs are valid from the circuits it controls. 时钟周期的长度（即时钟频率）受指令执行各阶段中最长的传播延迟所限。执行阶段以及在 ALU 中的传播通常是最长的阶段。因此，半个时钟周期的时间不能短于 ALU 输入值通过最慢的运算电路传播到 ALU 输出所需的时间（换句话说，输出要反映对输入执行运算的结果）。例如，在我们的四运算 ALU（OR、ADD、AND 和 EQUALS）中，行波进位加法器电路的传播延迟最长，它决定了时钟周期的最小长度。 The length of the clock cycle (or the clock rate) is bounded by the longest propagation delay through any stage of instruction execution. The execution stage and propagation through the ALU is usually the longest stage. Thus, half of the clock cycle time must be no faster than the time it takes for the ALU input values to propagate through the slowest operation circuit to the ALU outputs (in other words, the outputs reflect the results of the operation on the inputs). For example, in our four-operation ALU (OR, ADD, AND, and EQUALS), the ripple carry adder circuit has the longest propagation delay and determines the minimum length of the clock cycle. 由于完成 CPU 指令执行的一个阶段需要一个时钟周期，一个指令执行序列有四个阶段（取指、译码、执行、写回；见 图 8 ）的处理器，最多每四个时钟周期完成一条指令。 Because it takes one clock cycle to complete one stage of CPU instruction execution, a processor with a four-stage instruction execution sequence (Fetch, Decode, Execute, WriteBack; see Figure 8 ) completes at most one instruction every four clock cycles. 图 8. 四阶段的指令执行需要四个时钟周期才能完成。 Figure 8. Four-stage instruction execution takes four clock cycles to complete. 例如，如果时钟频率为 1 GHz，完成一条指令需要 4 纳秒（四个阶段各需 1 纳秒）。时钟频率为 2 GHz 时，完成一条指令只需要 2 纳秒。 If, for example, the clock rate is 1 GHz, one instruction takes 4 nanoseconds to complete (each of the four stages taking 1 nanosecond). With a 2-GHz clock rate, one instruction takes only 2 nanoseconds to complete. 尽管时钟频率是影响处理器性能的一个因素，但单靠时钟频率并不能有意义地衡量处理器的性能。更好的 CPU 性能衡量标准，是在程序的整个执行过程中测得的平均 每条指令周期数 （cycles per instruction，CPI）。通常，处理器无法在整个程序的执行过程中一直保持它的最大 CPI。达不到最大 CPI 是许多因素造成的，包括执行那些改变控制流的常见程序结构，如循环、 if - else 分支和函数调用。运行一组标准基准测试程序得到的平均 CPI 被用来比较不同的体系结构。CPI 是一个更准确的 CPU 性能衡量标准，因为它衡量的是执行一个程序的速度，而不是衡量单条指令执行的某一个方面。关于处理器性能以及为提升性能而设计处理器的更多细节，请参见计算机体系结构教材 1 。 Although clock rate is a factor in a processor’s performance, clock rate alone is not a meaningful measure of its performance. Instead, the average number of cycles per instruction (CPI) measured over a program’s full execution is a better measure of a CPU’s performance. Typically, a processor cannot maintain its maximum CPI for an entire program’s execution. A submaximum CPI is the result of many factors, including the execution of common program constructs that change control flow such as loops, if - else branching, and function calls. The average CPI for running a set of standard benchmark programs is used to compare different architectures. CPI is a more accurate measure of the CPU’s performance as it measures its speed executing a program versus a measure of one aspect of an individual instruction’s execution. See a computer architecture textbook 1 for more details about processor performance and designing processors to improve their performance. 译注 CPI 越 小 越好。原文说处理器「无法一直保持最大 CPI」，按意思应理解为无法一直保持 最好 的 CPI（即最小值）；实际执行中分支、缓存未命中等因素会让 CPI 变大。现代处理器每个周期能完成多条指令，人们也常用它的倒数 IPC（instructions per cycle，每周期指令数）来描述。 5.6.2. 把一切组合起来：完整计算机中的 CPU 5.6.2. Putting It All Together: The CPU in a Full Computer 数据通路（ALU、寄存器文件以及连接它们的总线）和控制通路（指令执行电路）构成了 CPU。它们共同实现了冯·诺依曼体系结构中的处理和控制部分。如今的处理器以蚀刻在硅芯片上的数字电路实现。处理器芯片上还包含一些快速的片上缓存存储器（用锁存器存储电路实现），用来在处理器附近存放最近使用过的程序数据和指令的副本。关于片上缓存存储器的更多信息，请参见 存储与存储器层次结构 一章。 The data path (ALU, register file, and the buses that connect them) and the control path (instruction execution circuitry) make up the CPU. Together they implement the processing and control parts of the von Neumann architecture. Today’s processors are implemented as digital circuits etched into silicon chips. The processor chip also includes some fast on-chip cache memory (implemented with latch storage circuits), used to store copies of recently used program data and instructions close to the processor. See the Storage and Memory Hierarchy Chapter for more information about on-chip cache memory. 图 9 展示了一个处于完整现代计算机中的处理器的例子，这台计算机的各个部件共同实现了冯·诺依曼体系结构。 Figure 9 shows an example of a processor in the context of a complete modern computer, whose components together implement the von Neumann architecture. 图 9. 完整现代计算机中的 CPU。总线连接着处理器芯片、主存以及输入和输出设备。 Figure 9. The CPU in a full modern computer. Buses connect the processor chip, main memory, and input and output devices. 5.6.3. 脚注 5.6.3. Footnotes 推荐一本：John Hennessy 和 David Patterson 合著的《Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach》（中译本《计算机体系结构：量化研究方法》）。 One suggestion is “Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach”, by John Hennessy and David Patterson.

x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C5-Arch/pipelining.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 5.7. Pipelining: Making the CPU Faster 我们的四阶段 CPU 执行一条指令需要四个周期：第一个周期从内存中取出指令；第二个周期对指令译码并从寄存器文件读取操作数；第三个周期由 ALU 执行运算；第四个周期把 ALU 的结果写回寄存器文件中的某个寄存器。执行一个由 N 条指令组成的序列需要 4N 个时钟周期，因为 CPU 按顺序一次执行一条指令。 Our four-stage CPU takes four cycles to execute one instruction: the first cycle is used to fetch the instruction from memory; the second to decode the instruction and read operands from the register file; the third for the ALU to execute the operation; and the fourth to write back the ALU result to a register in the register file. To execute a sequence of N instructions takes 4N clock cycles, as each is executed one at a time, in order, by the CPU. 图 1. 执行三条指令总共需要 12 个周期。 Figure 1. Executing three instructions takes 12 total cycles. 图 1 展示了三条指令总共用 12 个周期执行完，每条指令四个周期，CPI 为 4（CPI 是执行一条指令的平均周期数）。不过，可以改进 CPU 的控制电路，以获得更好（更低）的 CPI 值。 Figure 1 shows three instructions taking a total of 12 cycles to execute, four cycles per instruction, resulting in a CPI of 4 (CPI is the average number of cycles to execute an instruction). However, the control circuitry of the CPU can be improved to achieve a better (lower) CPI value. 在这种每条指令执行四个周期、接着下一条指令再执行四个周期、依此类推的执行模式中，实现每个阶段的 CPU 电路每四个周期才真正参与一次指令执行。例如，取指阶段之后，CPU 中的取指电路在接下来的三个时钟周期内不执行任何与指令执行相关的有用动作。然而，如果取指电路能在接下来的三个周期里继续执行后续指令的取指部分，CPU 就能每四个周期完成不止一条指令的执行。 In considering the pattern of execution in which each instruction takes four cycles to execute, followed by the next instruction taking four cycles, and so on, the CPU circuitry associated with implementing each stage is only actively involved in instruction execution once every four cycles. For example, after the Fetch stage, the fetch circuitry in the CPU is not used to perform any useful action related to executing an instruction for the next three clock cycles. If, however, the fetch circuitry could continue to actively execute the Fetch parts of subsequent instructions in the next three cycles, the CPU could complete the execution of more than a single instruction every four cycles. CPU 流水线 （pipelining）正是这样一种思想：在当前指令完全执行完之前，就开始执行下一条指令。CPU 流水线按顺序执行指令，但允许一系列指令的执行相互重叠。例如，在第一个周期，第一条指令进入它的取指阶段。在第二个周期，第一条指令进入译码阶段，同时第二条指令进入取指阶段。在第三个周期，第一条指令进入执行阶段，第二条指令进入译码阶段，第三条指令从内存中被取出。在第四个周期，第一条指令进入写回阶段并完成，第二条指令进入执行阶段，第三条进入译码阶段，第四条指令进入取指阶段。此时，CPU 的指令流水线已经填满——CPU 的每个阶段都在积极地执行程序指令，后一条指令比前一条落后一个阶段。当流水线满时，CPU 每个时钟周期完成一条指令的执行！ CPU pipelining is this idea of starting the execution of the next instruction before the current instruction has fully completed its execution. CPU pipelining executes instructions in order, but it allows the execution of a sequence of instructions to overlap. For example, in the first cycle, the first instruction enters its Fetch stage of execution. In the second cycle, the first instruction moves to its Decode stage, and the second instruction simultaneously enters its Fetch stage. In the third cycle, the first instruction moves to its Execution stage, the second instruction to its Decode stage, and the third instruction is fetched from memory. In the fourth cycle, the first instruction moves to its WriteBack stage and completes, the second instruction moves to its Execution stage, the third to its Decode, and the fourth instruction enters its Fetch stage. At this point, the CPU pipeline of instructions is full—​every CPU stage is actively executing program instructions where each subsequent instruction is one stage behind its predecessor. When the pipeline is full, the CPU completes the execution of one instruction every clock cycle! 图 2. 流水线：让指令的执行相互重叠，以达到每个周期完成一条指令。圆圈表示 CPU 已经达到每个周期完成一条指令的稳定状态。 Figure 2. Pipelining: overlapping instruction execution to achieve one instruction completed per cycle. The circle indicates that the CPU has reached the steady state of completing one instruction every cycle. 图 2 展示了指令在我们的 CPU 中流水线执行的例子。从第四个时钟周期开始，流水线被填满，也就是说 CPU 每个周期完成一条指令的执行，CPI 达到 1（ 图 2 中圆圈所示）。注意，在流水线执行中，执行单条指令所需的总周期数（指令的 延迟 ，latency）并没有减少——每条指令仍然需要四个周期才能执行完。流水线所做的，是让顺序的各条指令交错地经过流水线的不同阶段、重叠执行，从而提高指令的 吞吐量 （throughput），即 CPU 在给定时间内能执行的指令数。 Figure 2 shows an example of pipelined instruction execution through our CPU. Starting with the fourth clock cycle the pipeline fills, meaning that the CPU completes the execution of one instruction every cycle, achieving a CPI of 1 (shown in the circle in Figure 2 ). Notice that the total number of cycles required to execute a single instruction (the instruction latency ) has not decreased in pipelined execution—​it still takes four cycles for each instruction to execute. Instead, pipelining increases instruction throughput , or the number of instructions that the CPU can execute in a given period of time, by overlapping the execution of sequential instructions in a staggered manner, through the different stages of the pipeline. 自 1970 年代以来，计算机体系结构设计者一直把流水线作为大幅提升微处理器性能的手段。然而，流水线的代价是 CPU 的设计比不支持流水线执行的 CPU 更复杂，需要额外的存储和控制电路来支持流水线。例如，可能需要多个指令寄存器来存放当前处于流水线中的多条指令。流水线在 CPI 上带来的巨大改进，几乎总是值得这些额外的复杂性。因此，大多数现代微处理器都实现了流水线执行。 Since the 1970s, computer architects have used pipelining as a way to drastically improve the performance of microprocessors. However, pipelining comes at the cost of a more complicated CPU design than one that does not support pipelined execution. Additional storage and control circuitry is needed to support pipelining. For example, multiple instruction registers may be required to store the multiple instructions currently in the pipeline. This added complexity is almost always worth the large improvements in CPI that pipelining provides. As a result most modern microprocessors implement pipelined execution. 流水线的思想在计算机科学的其他场合也被用来加快执行速度，而且这一思想也适用于许多非计算机领域的应用。例如，考虑用一台洗衣机洗好几批衣服的任务。如果洗完一批衣服包括四个步骤（洗、烘干、叠好、收起来），那么在洗完第一批之后，第一批衣服在烘干机里烘的时候，第二批就可以放进洗衣机，通过让各批衣服的洗涤相互重叠，缩短洗完四批衣服的总时间。工厂的装配线也是流水线的一个例子。 The idea of pipelining is also used in other contexts in computer science to speed up execution, and the idea applies to many non-CS applications as well. Consider, for example, the task of doing multiple loads of laundry using a single washing machine. If completing one laundry consists of four steps (washing, drying, folding, and putting away clothes), then after washing the first load, the second load can go in the washing machine while the first load is in the dryer, overlapping the washing of individual laundry loads to speed up the total time it takes to wash four loads. Factory assembly lines are another example of pipelining. 在讨论 CPU 如何执行程序指令以及 CPU 流水线时，我们用的是一个简单的四阶段流水线和一条示例 ADD 指令。要执行在内存和寄存器之间加载和存储值的指令，需要使用五阶段流水线。五阶段流水线包括一个用于访问内存的访存（Memory）阶段：取指—译码—执行—访存—写回。不同的处理器可能有比典型的五阶段流水线更少或更多的流水线阶段。例如，最初的 ARM 体系结构只有三个阶段（取指、译码和执行，其中执行阶段同时完成 ALU 执行和寄存器文件写回的功能）。较新的 ARM 体系结构的流水线有五个以上的阶段。最初的 Intel Pentium 体系结构采用五阶段流水线，但后来的体系结构的流水线阶段要多得多。例如，Intel Core i7 有 14 级流水线。 In our discussion of how a CPU executes program instructions and CPU pipelining, we used a simple four-stage pipeline and an example ADD instruction. To execute instructions that load and store values between memory and registers, a five-stage pipeline is used. A five-stage pipeline includes a Memory stage for memory access: Fetch-Decode-Execute-Memory-WriteBack. Different processors may have fewer or more pipeline stages than a typical five-stage pipeline. For example, the initial ARM architecture had three stages (Fetch, Decode, and Execute, wherein the Execute stage performed both the ALU execution and the register file WriteBack functionality). More recent ARM architectures have more than five stages in their pipelines. The initial Intel Pentium architectures had a five-stage pipeline, but later architectures had significantly more pipeline stages. For example, the Intel Core i7 has a 14-stage pipeline.
