Looking Ahead: CPUs Today CPU 流水线是 指令级并行 （instruction-level parallelism，ILP）的一个例子，在指令级并行中，CPU 同时并行地执行多条指令。在流水线执行中，CPU 通过让多条指令的执行在流水线中重叠，来同时执行多条指令。一个简单的流水线 CPU 可以达到 1 的 CPI，即每个时钟周期完成一条指令的执行。现代微处理器通常同时采用流水线和其他 ILP 技术，并包含多个 CPU 核心，从而使处理器的 CPI 值小于 1。对于这些微体系结构，通常用平均 每周期指令数 （instructions per cycle，IPC）来描述它们的性能。IPC 值大，表明处理器能持续保持很高程度的指令同时执行。 CPU pipelining is one example of instruction-level parallelism (ILP), in which the CPU simultaneously executes multiple instructions in parallel. In a pipelined execution, the CPU simultaneously executes multiple instructions by overlapping their execution in the pipeline. A simple pipelined CPU can achieve a CPI of 1, completing the execution of one instruction every clock cycle. Modern microprocessors typically employ pipelining along with other ILP techniques and include multiple CPU cores to achieve processor CPI values of less than 1. For these microarchitectures, the average number of instructions per cycle (IPC) is the metric commonly used to describe their performance. A large IPC value indicates that a processor achieves a high sustained degree of simultaneous instruction execution. 晶体管是集成电路（芯片）上所有电路的构件。现代 CPU 的处理单元和控制单元由电路构成，而这些电路又由子电路和用晶体管实现的基本逻辑门构成。晶体管还实现了 CPU 寄存器所用的存储电路，以及存放最近访问过的数据和指令副本的快速片上缓存（我们会在 第 11 章 中详细讨论缓存）。 Transistors are the building blocks of all circuitry on an integrated circuit (a chip). The processing and control units of modern CPUs are constructed from circuits, which are built from subcircuits and basic logic gates that are implemented with transistors. Transistors also implement the storage circuits used in CPU registers and in fast on-chip cache memory that stores copies of recently accessed data and instructions (we discuss cache memory in detail in Chapter 11 ). 一块芯片上能容纳的晶体管数量，是衡量其性能的一个粗略指标。 摩尔定律 （Moore’s Law）是戈登·摩尔（Gordon Moore）在 1975 年提出的观察：每块集成电路上的晶体管数量大约每两年翻一番 1,2 。每块芯片上的晶体管数量每两年翻一番，意味着计算机体系结构设计者能设计出一块新芯片，它的存储电路和计算电路可用的空间是原来的两倍，能力也大致翻倍。历史上，体系结构设计者利用多出来的晶体管，借助 ILP 技术设计出更复杂的单处理器，以提升整体性能。 The number of transistors that can fit on a chip is a rough measure of its performance. Moore’s Law is the observation, made by Gordon Moore in 1975, that the number of transistors per integrated circuit doubles about every two years 1,2 . A doubling in the number of transistors per chip every two years means that computer architects can design a new chip with twice as much space for storage and computation circuitry, roughly doubling its power. Historically, computer architects used the extra transistors to design more complex single processors using ILP techniques to improve overall performance. 5.9.1. 指令级并行 5.9.1. Instruction-Level Parallelism 指令级并行（ILP）是一组设计技术的统称，这些技术用来支持在单个处理器上并行执行单个程序的指令。ILP 技术对程序员是透明的，也就是说，程序员写的是顺序的 C 程序，而处理器在一个或多个执行单元上同时、并行地执行它的若干条指令。流水线是 ILP 的一个例子，一串程序指令同时执行，每条指令处于不同的流水线阶段。流水线处理器每个周期可以执行一条指令（可以达到 1 的 IPC）。其他类型的微处理器 ILP 设计每个时钟周期可以执行不止一条指令，IPC 值可以大于 1。 Instruction level parallelism (ILP) is a term for a set of design techniques used to support parallel execution of a single program’s instructions on a single processor. ILP techniques are transparent to the programmer, meaning that a programmer writes a sequential C program but the processor executes several of its instructions simultaneously, in parallel, on one or more execution units. Pipelining is one example of ILP, where a sequence of program instructions execute simultaneously, each in a different pipeline stage. A pipelined processor can execute one instruction per cycle (can achieve an IPC of 1). Other types of microprocessor ILP designs can execute more than a single instruction per clock cycle and achieve IPC values higher than 1. 向量处理器 （vector processor）是一种通过特殊的向量指令实现 ILP 的体系结构，向量指令以一维数组（向量）数据作为操作数。向量指令由向量处理器在多个执行单元上并行执行，每个单元对向量操作数中的单个元素执行算术运算。过去，向量处理器常用于大型并行计算机。1976 年的 Cray-1 是第一台基于向量处理器的超级计算机，Cray 在整个 1990 年代一直用向量处理器设计它的超级计算机。然而，这种设计最终无法与其他并行超级计算机的设计竞争，如今向量处理器主要出现在图形处理器（GPU）这样的加速器设备中，它们特别擅长对存储在一维数组中的图像数据进行计算。 A vector processor is an architecture that implements ILP through special vector instructions that take one-dimensional arrays (vectors) of data as their operands. Vector instructions are executed in parallel by a vector processor on multiple execution units, each unit performing an arithmetic operation on single elements of its vector operands. In the past, vector processors were often used in large parallel computers. The 1976 Cray-1 was the first vector processor-based supercomputer, and Cray continued to design its supercomputers with vector processors throughout the 1990s. However, eventually this design could not compete with other parallel supercomputer designs, and today vector processors appear primarily in accelerator devices such as graphics processing units (GPUs) that are particularly optimized for performing computation on image data stored in 1D arrays. 超标量 （superscalar）是 ILP 处理器设计的另一个例子。超标量处理器是一个拥有多个执行单元和多条执行流水线的单处理器。超标量处理器从一个顺序程序的指令流中取出一组指令，把它们拆分成多个独立的指令流，由它的各个执行单元并行执行。超标量处理器是一种 乱序处理器 （out-of-order processor），即它不按照指令在顺序指令流中出现的顺序来执行指令。乱序执行需要找出那些没有依赖关系、可以安全地并行执行的指令序列。超标量处理器包含动态创建多个独立指令流、送入多个执行单元的功能。这一功能必须进行依赖分析，以确保在这些顺序流中，凡是执行依赖于前面某条指令结果的指令，都按正确的顺序执行。例如，一个有五个流水线执行单元的超标量处理器，可以在一个周期内执行一个顺序程序中的五条指令（可以达到 5 的 IPC）。然而，由于指令之间的依赖，超标量处理器并不总能让它的所有流水线都满载。 Superscalar is another example of an ILP processor design. A superscalar processor is a single processor with multiple execution units and multiple execution pipelines. A superscalar processor fetches a set of instructions from a sequential program’s instruction stream, and breaks them up into multiple independent streams of instructions that are executed in parallel by its execution units. A superscalar processor is an out-of-order processor , or one that executes instructions out of the order in which they appear in a sequential instruction stream. Out-of-order execution requires identifying sequences of instructions without dependencies that can safely execute in parallel. A superscalar processor contains functionality to dynamically create the multiple streams of independent instructions to feed through its multiple execution units. This functionality must perform dependency analysis to ensure the correct ordering of any instruction whose execution depends on the result of a previous instruction in these sequential streams. As an example, a superscalar processor with five pipelined execution units can execute five instructions from a sequential program in a single cycle (can achieve an IPC of 5). However, due to instruction dependencies, it is not always the case that a superscalar processor can keep all of its pipelines full. 超长指令字 （very long instruction word，VLIW）是另一种与超标量类似的 ILP 微体系结构设计。不过，在 VLIW 体系结构中，由编译器负责构造处理器并行执行的多个独立指令流。VLIW 体系结构的编译器分析程序指令，静态地构造出一条 VLIW 指令，它由多条指令组成，每个独立流各贡献一条。VLIW 带来比超标量更简单的处理器设计，因为 VLIW 处理器在执行程序指令时，不需要进行依赖分析来构造多个独立的指令流。VLIW 处理器只需要增加电路来取出下一条 VLIW 指令，把它拆成多条指令，分别送入各条执行流水线。然而，由于把依赖分析推给了编译器，VLIW 体系结构需要专门的编译器才能获得良好的性能。 Very long instruction word (VLIW) is another ILP microarchitecture design that is similar to superscalar. In VLIW architectures, however, the compiler is responsible for constructing the multiple independent instruction streams executed in parallel by the processor. A compiler for a VLIW architecture analyzes the program instructions to statically construct a VLIW instruction that consists of multiple instructions, one from each independent stream. VLIW leads to simpler processor design than superscalar because the VLIW processor does not need to perform dependency analysis to construct the multiple independent instruction streams as part of its execution of program instructions. Instead, a VLIW processor just needs added circuitry to fetch the next VLIW instruction and break it up into its multiple instructions that it feeds into each of its execution pipelines. However, by pushing dependency analysis to the compiler, VLIW architectures require specialized compilers to achieve good performance. 超标量和 VLIW 都有一个问题：并行性能的程度常常受到它们所执行的顺序应用程序的严重限制。程序中指令之间的依赖限制了让所有流水线保持满载的能力。 One problem with both superscalar and VLIW is that the degree of parallel performance is often significantly limited by the sequential application programs they execute. Dependencies between instructions in the program limit the ability to keep all of the pipelines full. 5.9.2. 多核与硬件多线程 5.9.2. Multicore and Hardware Multithreading 通过设计采用越来越复杂的 ILP 技术的单处理器，并提高 CPU 时钟速度来驱动这些越来越复杂的功能，计算机体系结构设计者设计出的处理器的性能一直跟上了摩尔定律，直到 2000 年代初。此后，如果不大幅增加处理器的功耗，CPU 的时钟速度就无法再提高 3 。这导致了当今多核和多线程微体系结构的时代，两者都需要程序员进行 显式并行编程 ，才能加快单个程序的执行。 By designing single processors that employed increasingly complicated ILP techniques and increasing the CPU clock speed to drive this increasingly complicated functionality, computer architects designed processors whose performance kept pace with Moore’s Law until the early 2000s. After this time, CPU clock speeds could no longer increase without greatly increasing a processor’s power consumption 3 . This led to the current era of multicore and multithreaded microarchitectures, both of which require explicit parallel programming by a programmer to speed up the execution of a single program. 硬件多线程 （hardware multithreading）是一种支持执行多个硬件线程的单处理器设计。 线程 （thread）是一条独立的执行流。例如，两个正在运行的程序各自有自己独立执行的线程。这两个程序的执行线程可以由操作系统调度，在多线程处理器上「同时」运行。硬件多线程的一种实现方式，是处理器每个周期在各个线程的指令流之间交替执行指令。在这种情况下，不同硬件线程的指令并不是每个周期都同时执行，而是处理器被设计成能在执行不同线程执行流的指令之间快速切换。与在单线程处理器上执行相比，这通常能让它们整体上执行得更快。 Hardware multithreading is a single-processor design that supports executing multiple hardware threads. A thread is an independent stream of execution. For example, two running programs each have their own thread of independent execution. These two programs’ threads of execution could then be scheduled by the operating system to run “at the same time” on a multithreaded processor. Hardware multithreading may be implemented by a processor alternating between executing instructions from each of its threads’ instruction streams each cycle. In this case, the instructions of different hardware threads are not all executed simultaneously each cycle. Instead, the processor is designed to quickly switch between executing instructions from different threads’ execution streams. This usually results in a speed-up of their execution as a whole as compared to their execution on a singly threaded processor. 多线程既可以在标量微处理器上、也可以在超标量微处理器上用硬件实现。硬件至少需要支持从多个独立的指令流（每个执行线程一个）中取指令，并为每个线程的执行流配备独立的寄存器组。这些体系结构是 显式多线程 （explicitly multithreaded） 4 的，因为与超标量体系结构不同，每条执行流都由操作系统独立调度，运行一个单独的逻辑程序指令序列。多条执行流可以来自多个顺序程序，也可以来自单个多线程并行程序中的多个软件线程（我们会在 第 14 章 中讨论多线程并行编程）。 Multithreading can be implemented in hardware on either scalar- or super-scalar type microprocessors. At a minimum, the hardware needs to support fetching instructions from multiple separate instruction streams (one for each thread of execution), and have separate register sets for each thread’s execution stream. These architectures are explicitly multithreaded 4 because, unlike superscalar architectures, each of the execution streams is independently scheduled by the operating system to run a separate logical sequence of program instructions. The multiple execution streams could come from multiple sequential programs or from multiple software threads from a single multithreaded parallel program (we discuss multithreaded parallel programming in Chapter 14 ). 基于超标量处理器的硬件多线程微体系结构有多条流水线和多个执行单元，因此它们可以同时、并行地执行来自几个硬件线程的指令，使 IPC 值大于 1。基于简单标量处理器的多线程体系结构实现的是 交错多线程 （interleaved multithreading）。这类微体系结构通常共享一条流水线，并且总是共享处理器唯一的 ALU（CPU 在 ALU 上切换执行不同的线程）。这种多线程无法达到大于 1 的 IPC 值。由基于超标量的微体系结构支持的硬件多线程通常称为 同时多线程 （simultaneous multithreading，SMT） 4 。遗憾的是，SMT 这个词经常被用来同时指代这两种硬件多线程，单凭这个术语并不总能判断一个多线程微体系结构实现的是真正的同时多线程还是交错多线程。 Hardware multithreaded microarchitectures that are based on superscalar processors have multiple pipelines and multiple execution units, and thus they can execute instructions from several hardware threads simultaneously, in parallel, resulting in an IPC value greater than 1. Multithreaded architectures based on simple scalar processors implement interleaved multithreading . These microarchitectures typically share a pipeline and always share the processor’s single ALU (the CPU switches between executing different threads on the ALU). This type of multithreading cannot achieve IPC values greater than 1. Hardware threading supported by superscalar-based microarchitectures is often called simultaneous multithreading (SMT) 4 . Unfortunately, SMT is often used to refer to both types of hardware multithreading, and the term alone is not always sufficient to determine whether a multithreaded microarchitecture implements true simultaneous or interleaved multithreading. 多核处理器 （multicore processor）包含多个完整的 CPU 核心。与多线程处理器一样，每个核心都由操作系统独立调度。不过，多核处理器的每个核心都是一个完整的 CPU 核心，拥有独立的、完整的执行程序指令的功能。多核处理器包含这些 CPU 核心的多个副本，外加一些让各核心共享缓存数据的硬件支持。多核处理器的每个核心可以是标量的、超标量的或硬件多线程的。 图 1 展示了一台多核计算机的例子。 Multicore processors contain multiple complete CPU cores. Like multithreaded processors, each core is independently scheduled by the OS. However, each core of a multicore processor is a full CPU core, one that contains its own complete and separate functionality to execute program instructions. A multicore processor contains replicas of these CPU cores with some additional hardware support for the cores to share cached data. Each core of a multicore processor could be scalar, superscalar, or hardware multithreaded. Figure 1 shows an example of a multicore computer. 图 1. 一台配有多核处理器的计算机。处理器包含多个完整的 CPU 核心，每个核心都有自己私有的缓存。各核心之间相互通信，并通过片上总线共享一个更大的共享缓存。 Figure 1. A computer with a multicore processor. The processor contains multiple complete CPU cores, each with its own private cache memory. The cores communicate with each and share a larger shared cached memory via on-chip buses. 多核微处理器设计是处理器体系结构的性能在不提高处理器时钟频率的情况下继续跟上摩尔定律的主要途径。多核计算机可以同时运行几个顺序程序，操作系统把不同程序的指令流调度到各个核心上。如果单个程序被写成显式多线程（软件级线程）的并行程序，多核计算机还能加快这个程序的执行。例如，操作系统可以把单个程序的各个线程调度到多核处理器的各个核心上同时运行，与执行同一程序的顺序版本相比，加快了程序的执行。在 第 14 章 中，我们会讨论面向多核以及其他具有共享主存的并行系统的显式多线程并行编程。 Multicore microprocessor design is the primary way in which the performance of processor architectures can continue to keep pace with Moore’s Law without increasing the processor clock rate. A multicore computer can simultaneously run several sequential programs, the OS scheduling each core with a different program’s instruction stream. It can speed up execution of a single program if the program is written as an explicitly multithreaded (software-level threads) parallel program. For example, the OS can schedule the threads of an individual program to run simultaneously on individual cores of the multicore processor, speeding up the execution of the program compared to its execution of a sequential version of the same program. In Chapter 14 , we discuss explicit multithreaded parallel programming for multicore and other types of parallel systems with shared main memory. 5.9.3. 几个处理器实例 5.9.3. Some Example Processors 如今，处理器是用 ILP、硬件多线程和多核技术混合构建的。事实上，已经很难找到不是多核的处理器了。台式机级处理器通常有二到八个核心，其中许多核心还支持较低程度的单核多线程。例如，AMD Zen 多核处理器 5 以及 Intel 支持超线程（hyperthreaded）的多核 Xeon 和 Core 处理器 6 都支持每个核心两个硬件线程。Intel 的超线程核心实现的是交错多线程。因此，它的每个核心只能达到 1 的 IPC，但由于每块芯片上有多个 CPU 核心，整个处理器可以达到更高的 IPC。 Today, processors are built using a mix of ILP, hardware multithreading, and multicore technologies. In fact, it is difficult to find a processor that is not multicore. Desktop-class processors typically have two to eight cores, many of which also support a low level of per-core multithreading. For example, AMD Zen multicore processors 5 and Intel’s hyperthreaded multicore Xeon and Core processors 6 both support two hardware threads per core. Intel’s hyperthreaded cores implement interleaved multithreading. Thus, each of its cores can only achieve an IPC of 1, but with multiple CPU cores per chip, the processor can achieve higher IPC levels. 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· 大小核与上百核的服务器 异构多核 ：今天的处理器常把不同类型的核心放在同一块芯片上。例如 Apple 2020 年的 M1 有 8 个 CPU 核心，其中 4 个高性能核心、4 个高能效核心；轻负载交给高能效核心，重负载再动用高性能核心。原书「台式机 2–8 核」的说法也早已过时。 Apple Newsroom：Apple unleashes M1 服务器核数 ：AMD 2024 年 10 月发布的第五代 EPYC（9005 系列）中，顶配的 EPYC 9965 有 192 个 「Zen 5c」核心。 AMD：5th Gen AMD EPYC 发布 为服务器和超级计算机等高端系统设计的处理器包含许多核心，每个核心都有很高程度的多线程。例如，用于高端服务器的 Oracle SPARC M7 处理器 7 有 32 个核心。它的每个核心有八个硬件线程，其中两个可以同时执行，使处理器的最大 IPC 值达到 64。世界上最快的两台超级计算机（截至 2019 年 6 月） 8 使用的是 IBM 的 Power 9 处理器 9 。Power 9 处理器每块芯片最多有 24 个核心，每个核心最多支持八路同时多线程。24 核版本的 Power 9 处理器可以达到 192 的 IPC。 Processors designed for high-end systems, such as those used in servers and supercomputers, contain many cores, where each core has a high degree of multithreading. For example, Oracle’s SPARC M7 processor 7 , used in high-end servers, has 32 cores. Each of its cores has eight hardware threads, two of which can execute simultaneously, resulting in a maximum IPC value of 64 for the processor. The two fastest supercomputers in the world (as of June 2019) 8 , use IBM’s Power 9 processors 9 . Power 9 processors have up to 24 cores per chip, and each core supports up to eight-way simultaneous multithreading. A 24-core version of the Power 9 processor can achieve an IPC of 192. 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· 今天最快的超算 原书提到的 2019 年 6 月榜首是采用 IBM Power 9 的系统。在 2026 年 6 月的 TOP500 榜单上，第一名是位于中国国家超级计算深圳中心的 LineShine（约 1380 万个核心，Linpack 实测 2,198.4 PFlop/s，即约 2.2 EFlop/s），第二名是美国的 El Capitan（AMD 第四代 EPYC CPU + AMD Instinct MI300A）。 TOP500 List - June 2026 脚注与参考文献 Footnotes and References 摩尔在 1965 年最初观察到的是每年翻一番，1975 年他把这一观察修正为每两年多翻一番，后者被称为摩尔定律。 Moore first observed a doubling every year in 1965, that he then updated in 1975 to every > 2 years, which became known as Moore’s Law. 摩尔定律一直成立到 2012 年前后，此后晶体管密度的提升开始放缓。摩尔预测摩尔定律将在 2020 年代中期终结。 Moore’s Law held until around 2012 when improvements in transistor density began to slow. x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C5-Arch/pipelining_advanced.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 5.8. Advanced Pipelined Instruction Considerations 回想一下， 流水线 通过让多条指令的执行相互重叠来提升处理器的性能。在 前面 关于流水线的讨论中，我们描述了一个简单的四阶段流水线，包含取指（F）、译码（D）、执行（E）和写回（W）这几个基本阶段。在下面的讨论中，我们还考虑第五个阶段——访存（M），它表示对数据存储器的访问。因此，我们的五阶段流水线由以下几个阶段组成： Recall that pipelining improves the performance of a processor by overlapping the execution of multiple instructions. In our earlier discussion on pipelining, we described a simple four-stage pipeline with the basic stages of Fetch (F), Decode (D), Execute (E) and WriteBack (W). In our discussion that follows, we also consider a fifth stage, Memory (M), which represents an access to data memory. Our five-stage pipeline therefore comprises the following stages: 取指（F）： 从存储器中读取一条指令（由程序计数器指向）。 Fetch (F): reads an instruction from memory (pointed to by the program counter). 译码（D）： 读取源寄存器并设置控制逻辑。 Decode (D): reads source registers and sets control logic. 执行（E）： 执行指令。 Execute (E): executes the instruction. 访存（M）： 读或写数据存储器。 Memory (M): reads from or writes to data memory. 写回（W）： 把结果存入目标寄存器。 WriteBack (W): stores a result in a destination register. 回想一下，编译器把代码行转换成一系列供 CPU 执行的机器码指令。汇编代码是机器码的人类可读版本。下面的片段展示了一系列虚构的汇编指令： Recall that the compiler transforms lines of code into a series of machine code instructions for the CPU to execute. Assembly code is a human-readable version of machine code. The snippet below displays a series of made-up assembly instructions: MOV M[0x84], Reg1 # move value at memory address 0x84 to register Reg1 ADD 2, Reg1, Reg1 # add 2 to value in Reg1 and store result in Reg1 MOV 4, Reg2 # copy the value 4 to register Reg2 ADD Reg2, Reg2, Reg2 # compute Reg2 + Reg2, store result in Reg2 JMP L1<0x14> # jump to executing code at L1 (code address 0x14) 如果你在理解这段代码时遇到困难，不必担心——我们会在 后面的章节 中更详细地介绍汇编。目前，只需关注以下几点事实： Don’t worry if you are having trouble parsing the snippet — we cover assembly in greater detail in upcoming chapters . For now, it suffices to focus on the following set of facts: 每种 ISA 都定义了一组指令。 Every ISA defines a set of instructions. 每条指令对一个或多个操作数（即寄存器、存储器或常数值）进行操作。 Each instruction operates on one or more operands (i.e. registers, memory, or constant values). 并非所有指令执行时都需要相同数量的流水线阶段。 Not all instructions require the same number of pipeline stages to execute. 在前面的讨论中，我们假定每条指令执行所需的周期数都相同；然而，实际情况通常并非如此。例如，第一条 MOV 指令需要全部五个阶段，因为它需要把数据从存储器移到寄存器。相比之下，接下来的三条指令只需要四个阶段（F、D、E、W）就能执行完，因为它们的运算只涉及寄存器，而不涉及存储器。最后一条指令（ JMP ）是一种 分支 或 条件 指令，它的作用是把控制流转移到代码的另一部分。具体来说，存储器代码区中的地址指向可执行文件中不同的 指令 。由于 JMP 指令不更新通用寄存器，写回阶段被省略，结果只需要三个阶段（F、D、E）。我们会在后面关于汇编的 章节 中更详细地介绍条件指令。 In our previous discussion, it was assumed that every instruction takes the same number of cycles to execute; however, this is usually not the case. For example, the first MOV instruction requires all five stages, as it requires the movement of data from memory to a register. In contrast, the next three instructions require only four stages (F, D, E, W) to execute given that the operations involve only registers, and not memory. The last instruction ( JMP ) is a type of branch or conditional instruction. Its purpose is to transfer the flow of control to another part of the code. Specifically, addresses in the code region of memory reference different instructions in an executable. Since the JMP instruction does not update a general-purpose register, the WriteBack stage is omitted, resulting in only three stages (F, D, E) being required. We cover conditional instructions in greater detail in the upcoming chapters on assembly. 当某条指令被迫等待另一条指令执行完毕才能继续时，就产生了 流水线停顿 （pipeline stall）。编译器和处理器会尽一切可能避免流水线停顿，以使性能最大化。 A pipeline stall results when any instruction is forced to wait for another to finish executing before it can continue. Compilers and processors do whatever they can to avoid pipeline stalls in order to maximize performance. 5.8.1. 流水线问题：数据冒险 5.8.1. Pipelining Consideration: Data Hazards 当两条指令试图在指令流水线中访问共同的数据时，就会发生 数据冒险 （data hazard）。例如，考虑上面代码片段中的第一对指令： A data hazard occurs when two instructions attempt to access common data in an instruction pipeline. As an example, consider the first pair of instructions from the code snippet above: MOV M[0x84], Reg1 # move value at memory address 0x84 to register Reg1 ADD 2, Reg1, Reg1 # add 2 to value in Reg1 and store result in Reg1 图 1. 两条指令同时到达同一流水线阶段而引发流水线冒险的例子。 Figure 1. An example of a pipeline hazard arising from two instructions simultaneously reaching the same pipeline stage. 回想一下，这条 MOV 指令需要五个阶段（因为它涉及对存储器的访问），而 ADD 指令只需要四个。在这种情形下，两条指令会试图同时写寄存器 Reg1 （见 图 1 ）。 Recall that this MOV instruction requires five stages (as it involves an access to memory), whereas the ADD instruction requires only four. In this scenario, both instructions will attempt to write to register Reg1 at the same time (see Figure 1 ). 为了防止上述情形，处理器首先强制每条指令都经过五个流水线阶段来执行。对于通常不到五个阶段的指令，CPU 会加入一条「空操作」（ NOP ）指令（也称为流水线「气泡」，bubble）来顶替那个阶段。 The processor prevents the aforementioned scenario by first forcing every instruction to take five pipeline stages to execute. For instructions that normally take fewer than five stages, the CPU adds a “no-operation” ( NOP ) instruction (also called a pipeline “bubble”) to substitute for that phase. 不过，问题仍未完全解决。由于第二条指令的目标是把 2 加到寄存器 Reg1 中存储的值上， MOV 指令必须先完成对寄存器 Reg1 的 写入 ， ADD 指令才能正确执行。接下来的两条指令也存在类似的问题： However, the problem is still not fully resolved. Since the goal of the second instruction is to add 2 to the value stored in register Reg1 , the MOV instruction needs to finish writing to register Reg1 before the ADD instruction can execute correctly. A similar problem exists in the next two instructions: MOV 4, Reg2 # copy the value 4 to register Reg2 ADD Reg2, Reg2, Reg2 # compute Reg2 + Reg2, store result in Reg2 图 2. 处理器可以通过在指令之间转发操作数，减轻流水线冒险造成的损失。 Figure 2. The processor can reduce the damage caused by pipeline hazards by forwarding operands between instructions. 这两条指令先把值 4 加载到寄存器 Reg2 中，再把它乘以 2（通过与自身相加）。同样，为了强制每条指令都经过五个流水线阶段，加入了气泡。在这种情况下，无论有没有气泡，第二条指令的执行阶段都发生在第一条指令把所需的值（ 4 ）写入寄存器 Reg2 之前 。 These two instructions load the value 4 into register Reg2 and then multiply it by 2 (by adding to itself). Once again, bubbles are added to enforce that each instruction takes five pipeline stages. In this case, regardless of the bubbles, the second instruction’s execute phase occurs before the first instruction finishes writing the required value ( 4 ) to register Reg2 . 加入更多的气泡并不是一个好的解决方案，因为它会让流水线停顿。处理器采用的是一种称为 操作数转发 （operand forwarding）的技术，让流水线直接读取前一个操作的结果。看一下 图 2 ：在指令 MOV 4, Reg2 执行时，它把结果转发给指令 ADD Reg2, Reg2, Reg2 。这样，在 MOV 指令写寄存器 Reg2 的同时， ADD 指令就可以使用它从 MOV 指令那里收到的 Reg2 的新值。 Adding more bubbles is a suboptimal solution, because it stalls the pipeline. Instead, processors employ a technique called operand forwarding , in which the pipeline reads the result from the previous operation. Looking at Figure 2 , while the instruction MOV 4, Reg2 executes, it forwards its results to the instruction ADD Reg2, Reg2, Reg2 . So, while the MOV instruction is writing to register Reg2 , the ADD instruction can use the updated value of Reg2 that it received from the MOV instruction. 5.8.2. 流水线冒险：控制冒险 5.8.2. Pipelining Hazards: Control Hazards 流水线是针对一条接一条依次出现的指令而优化的。程序中由 if 语句或循环等条件结构引起的控制流变化，会严重影响流水线的性能。我们来看另一个示例代码片段，先看 C 代码： The pipeline is optimized for instructions that occur one after another. Control changes in a program arising from conditionals such as if statements or loops can seriously affect the pipeline performance. Let’s take a look at a different example code snippet, first in C: int result = *x; // x holds an int int temp = *y; // y holds another int if (result <= temp) { result = result - temp; } else { result = result + temp; } return result; 这段代码只是从两个不同的指针读出整数数据，比较它们的值，然后根据比较结果进行不同的算术运算。上面的代码片段可能被翻译成如下的汇编指令： This snippet simply reads integer data from two different pointers, compares the values, and then does different arithmetic based on the result. Here is how the above code snippet may translate into assembly instructions: MOV M[0x84], Reg1 # move value at memory address 0x84 to register Reg1 MOV M[0x88], Reg2 # move value at memory address 0x88 to register Reg2 CMP Reg1, Reg2 # compare value in Reg1 to value in Reg2 JLE L1<0x14> # switch code execution to L1 if Reg1 less than Reg2 ADD Reg1, Reg2, Reg1 # compute Reg1 + Reg2, store result in Reg1 JMP L2<0x20> # switch code execution to L2 (code address 0x20) L1: SUB Reg1, Reg2, Reg1 # compute Reg1 - Reg2, store in Reg1 L2: RET # return from function 这串指令把数据从存储器加载到两个不同的寄存器中，比较它们的值，然后根据第一个寄存器中的值是否小于第二个寄存器中的值进行不同的算术运算。在上面的例子中， if 语句用两条指令表示：比较（ CMP ）指令和小于等于时条件跳转（ JLE ）指令。我们会在 后面关于汇编 的章节中更详细地介绍条件指令；目前只需理解： CMP 指令 比较 两个寄存器，而 JLE 指令是一种特殊的分支指令， 当且仅当 条件（本例中为小于等于）为真时，它才把代码执行切换到程序的另一部分。 This sequence of instructions loads data from memory into two separate registers, compares the values, and then does different arithmetic based on whether the value in the first register is less than the value in the second. The if statement is represented in the above example with two instructions: the compare ( CMP ) instruction and a conditional jump less than ( JLE ) instruction. We cover conditional instructions in greater detail in the upcoming assembly chapters; for now it is sufficient to understand that the CMP instruction compares two registers, while the JLE instruction is a special type of branch instruction that switches code execution to another part of the program if and only if the condition (i.e. less than or equal, in this case) is true. 原书警示 · 不要被细节吓倒！（Don’t get overwhelmed by the details!） 初次看到汇编代码会感到发怵，这是可以理解的。如果你也有这种感觉，尽量别担心！我们会在 后面的章节 中更详细地介绍汇编。关键是要明白：包含条件语句的代码与其他任何代码片段一样，会被翻译成一系列汇编指令。然而，与其他代码片段不同，条件语句 并不 保证以某种特定的方式执行。条件语句执行方式的不确定性，对流水线有很大的影响。 Looking at assembly for the first time can be understandably intimidating. If this is how you feel, try not to worry! We cover assembly in much greater detail in coming chapters . The key takeaway is that code containing conditional statements translates to a series of assembly instructions just like any other code snippet. However, unlike other code snippets, conditional statements are not guaranteed to execute in a particular way. The uncertainty surrounding how a conditional statement executes has large ramifications for the pipeline. 图 3. 由条件分支引起的控制冒险的例子。 Figure 3. An example of a control hazard resulting from a conditional branch. 当流水线遇到分支（或条件）指令时，就会发生 控制冒险 （control hazard）。这时，流水线必须「猜测」分支是否会发生跳转。如果分支不跳转，处理器就继续按顺序执行接下来的指令。考虑 图 3 中的例子。如果分支跳转，接下来应该执行的是 SUB 指令。然而，在 JLE 指令执行完之前，无法知道分支是否会跳转。而到那时， ADD 和 JMP 指令已经被加载到流水线中了。如果分支 确实 跳转，就必须先把流水线中这些「垃圾」指令清除掉，即 冲刷 （flush），然后才能用新指令重新填充流水线。冲刷流水线的代价很高。 A control hazard occurs when the pipeline encounters a branch (or conditional) instruction. When this happens, the pipeline has to “guess” whether the branch will be taken. If the branch is not taken, the process continues to execute the next instructions in sequence. Consider the example in Figure 3 . If the branch is taken, the next instruction that executes should be the SUB instruction. However, it is impossible to know whether the branch is taken until the JLE instruction finishes executing. At that point, the ADD and JMP instructions have already been loaded into the pipeline. If the branch is taken, these “junk” instructions in the pipeline need to be removed, or flushed , before the pipeline can be reloaded with new instructions. Flushing the pipeline is expensive. 硬件工程师可以选择实现以下几种方案，帮助处理器应对控制冒险： There are a few options that hardware engineers can choose to implement to help the processor deal with control hazards: 让流水线停顿 ：一种简单的解决办法是，每当遇到分支，就加入大量 NOP 气泡让流水线停顿，直到处理器确定分支是否跳转。虽然让流水线停顿能解决问题，但也会导致性能下降（见 图 4 ）。 Stall the pipeline : As a simple solution, whenever there is a branch, add lots of NOP bubbles and stall the pipeline until the processor is sure that the branch is taken. Although stalling the pipeline will fix the issue, it will also lead to a performance hit (see Figure 4 ). 分支预测 （branch prediction）：最常见的解决办法是使用 分支预测器 （branch predictor），它根据以往的执行情况预测分支的走向。现代分支预测器非常好，也非常准确。然而，这种方法近年来引发了一些安全漏洞（例如 Spectre 1 ）。 图 4 描绘了分支预测器可能如何处理前面讨论的控制冒险。 Branch prediction : The most common solution is to use a branch predictor , which will predict which way a branch will go, based on previous executions. Modern branch predictors are really good and accurate. However, this approach has recently caused some security vulnerabilities (e.g. Spectre 1 ). Figure 4 depicts how a branch predictor may deal with the control hazard discussed. 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· Spectre 是怎么回事 Spectre 和同时公布的 Meltdown 于 2018 年 1 月公开，Google Project Zero 早在 2017 年 6 月 1 日就把问题报告给了 Intel、AMD 和 ARM。它们利用的正是本节讲的分支预测和推测执行：CPU 在猜测的路径上「先做了再说」，错误路径上执行的指令虽然最后会被撤销，却会在缓存中留下痕迹，攻击者可以通过测量访问时间读出本不该读到的数据。这类漏洞的根源在硬件设计上，只能靠微码更新、编译器和操作系统的缓解措施来降低风险，代价往往是一部分性能。 Meltdown and Spectre · Project Zero：Reading privileged memory with a side-channel 激进执行 （eager execution）：在激进执行中，CPU 同时执行分支的两侧，并进行有条件的数据传送而不是有条件的控制转移（在 x86 和 ARMv8-A 中分别通过 cmov 和 csel 指令实现）。有条件的数据传送使处理器能在不打乱流水线的情况下继续执行。不过，并非所有代码都能利用激进执行，在涉及指针解引用和副作用的情况下，它可能是危险的。 Eager execution : In eager execution, the CPU executes both sides of the branch and performs a conditional transfer of data rather than control (implemented through the cmov and the csel instructions in x86 and ARMv8-A, respectively). A conditional transfer of data enables the processor to continue execution without disrupting the pipeline. However, not all code is capable of taking advantage of eager execution, which can be dangerous in the case of pointer dereferences and side effects. 图 4. 处理控制冒险的几种可能方案。 Figure 4. Potential solutions for handling control hazards. 参考文献 References Peter Bright. Google: Software is never going to be able to fix Spectre-type bugs Ars Technica 2019.

x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C6-asm_intro/index.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 6. Under the C: Diving into Assembly 在 C 之下，在 C 之下 Under the C, under the C 难道你不知道这样更好 Don’t you know it’s better 跟寄存器 Dealing with registers 和汇编打交道？ And assembly? 译注 这几句套用了迪士尼动画《小美人鱼》中螃蟹 Sebastian 演唱的《Under the Sea》（在海底）的歌词，把 sea 换成了同音的 C。下一行的「—— Sebastian（大概吧）」就是在调侃这一点。 —— Sebastian（大概吧） -Sebastian, probably 在计算机发展的早期、编译器发明之前，许多程序员用 汇编语言 （assembly language）编写代码，它直接规定了计算机在执行过程中遵循的指令集合。汇编语言是程序员在不直接写 1 和 0 的前提下，最接近机器层面的编程方式，它是 机器码 （machine code）的一种可读形式。要写出高效的汇编代码，程序员必须深入理解底层机器体系结构的运作方式。 Prior to the invention of the compiler in the early days of computing, many programmers coded in assembly language , which directly specifies the set of instructions that a computer follows during execution. Assembly language is the closest a programmer gets to coding at the machine level without writing code directly in 1s and 0s, and is a readable form of machine code . To write efficient assembly code, programmers must intimately understand the operation of the underlying machine architecture. 编译器的发明从根本上改变了程序员编写代码的方式。 编译器 （compiler）把人类可读的编程语言（通常用英文单词写成）翻译成计算机能理解的语言（即机器码）。编译器依据编程语言的规则、操作系统的规范以及机器的指令集，把人类可读的代码翻译成机器码，并在这个过程中提供一定的错误检测和类型检查。大多数现代编译器生成的汇编代码，与过去手写的汇编代码一样高效。 The invention of the compiler fundamentally changed the way programmers write code. A compiler translates a human-readable programming language (usually written using English words) into a language that a computer understands (i.e., machine code). Compilers translate the human-readable code into machine code using the rules of the programming language, the specification of the operating system, and the instruction set of the machine, and provide some error detection and type checking in the process. Most modern compilers produce assembly code that is as efficient as the handwritten assembly code of yesteryear. 学习汇编的好处 The Benefits of Learning Assembly 编译器有这么多好处，学习汇编有什么用可能就不那么显而易见了。然而，学习和理解汇编代码有几个很有说服力的理由。下面举几个例子。 Given all the benefits of compilers, it may not be obvious why learning assembly is useful. However, there are several compelling reasons to learn and understand assembly code. Here are a few examples. 1. 更高层的抽象隐藏了有价值的程序细节 1. Higher-Level Abstraction Hides Valuable Program Details 高级编程语言提供的抽象对降低编程的复杂度大有裨益。但与此同时，这种简化让程序员很容易在没有完全理解其选择在机器层面产生何种影响的情况下做出设计决策。缺乏汇编知识，常常使程序员无法了解程序如何运行的宝贵信息，也限制了他们理解自己的代码实际在做什么的能力。 The abstraction provided by high-level programming languages is a boon for reducing the complexity of programming. At the same time, this simplification makes it easy for programmers to make design decisions without fully understanding the ramifications of their choices at the machine level. Lacking knowledge of assembly often prevents a programmer from understanding valuable information on how a program runs, and limits their ability to understand what their code is actually doing. 举个例子，看看下面这个程序： As an example, take a look at the following program: #include <stdio.h> int adder() { int a; return a + 2; } int assign() { int y = 40; return y; } int main(void) { int x; assign(); x = adder(); printf("x is: %d\n", x); return 0; } 这个程序的输出是什么？乍一看， assign 函数似乎没有任何作用，因为 main 中没有任何变量保存它的返回值。 adder 函数返回 a + 2 的值，尽管变量 a 没有初始化（不过在某些机器上编译器会把 a 初始化为 0）。打印 x 应该得到一个不确定的值。然而，在大多数 64 位机器上编译并运行它，得到的结果始终是 42 ： What is the program’s output? At first glance, the assign function appears to have no effect, as its return value is not stored by any variable in main . The adder function returns the value of a + 2 , although the variable a is uninitialized (though on some machines the compiler will initialize a to 0). Printing out x should result in an undefined value. However, compiling and running it on most 64-bit machines consistently produces an answer of 42 : 译注 读取未初始化的局部变量是未定义行为， 42 只是在不开优化时、两个函数的栈帧恰好重叠在同一块内存上的结果。译者在 Apple Silicon Mac 上试过：默认（ -O0 ）编译输出 x is: 42 ，加上 -O2 优化后输出的就是一个毫无规律的值。所以这个例子是用来理解栈帧的，千万别在真实代码里依赖这种行为。 $ gcc -o example example.c $ ./example x is: 42 乍一看，这个程序的输出似乎毫无道理，因为 adder 和 assign 函数看起来毫不相干。理解栈帧以及函数在底层如何执行，会帮助你明白答案为什么是 42 。我们会在接下来的几章中再次讨论这个例子。 The output of this program seems nonsensical at first glance, as the adder and assign functions appear to be disconnected. Understanding stack frames and how functions execute under the hood will help you understand why the answer is 42 . We will revisit this example in the upcoming chapters. 2. 有些计算系统的资源太有限，无法使用编译器 2. Some Computing Systems Are Too Resource-Constrained for Compilers 最常见的「计算机」，是那些我们不容易认出是计算机的设备。这些设备无处不在，从汽车、咖啡机到洗衣机和智能手表。传感器、微控制器和其他嵌入式处理器在我们的生活中扮演着越来越重要的角色，它们都需要软件才能运转。然而，这类设备中的处理器往往太小，无法执行用高级编程语言编写并编译出的代码。在许多情况下，这些设备需要独立的汇编程序，不依赖常见编程语言所需的运行时库。 The most common types of “computer” are those we cannot readily identify as computers. These devices exist everywhere from cars and coffee makers to washing machines and smart watches. Sensors, microcontrollers, and other embedded processors play an increasingly dominant role in our lives, and all require software to operate. However, the processors contained in such devices are often so small that they cannot execute the compiled code written by higher-level programming languages. In many cases, these devices require standalone assembly programs that are not dependent on the runtime libraries required by common programming languages. 3. 漏洞分析 3. Vulnerability Analysis 有一部分安全专业人员每天都在设法找出各类计算机系统中的漏洞。许多攻击程序的途径都与程序存储其运行时信息的方式有关。学习汇编能让安全专业人员理解漏洞是如何产生的，以及它们可能被如何利用。 A subset of security professionals spend their days trying to identify vulnerabilities in various types of computer systems. Many avenues for attacking a program involve the way the program stores its runtime information. Learning assembly enables security professionals to understand how vulnerabilities arise and how they can be exploited. 另一些安全专业人员则花时间对恶意软件中的恶意代码进行「逆向工程」。掌握汇编的实用知识，对这些软件工程师迅速开发出保护系统免受攻击的对策至关重要。最后，不了解自己写的代码如何被翻译成汇编的开发者，可能会在不知不觉中写出有漏洞的代码。 Other security professionals spend time “reverse engineering” malicious code in malware and other malicious software. A working knowledge of assembly is essential to enable these software engineers to quickly develop countermeasures to protect systems against attack. Lastly, developers who lack an understanding of how the code they write translates to assembly may end up unwittingly writing vulnerable code. 4. 系统级软件中的关键代码序列 4. Critical Code Sequences in System-Level Software 最后，计算机系统中有些部件无法被编译器充分优化，需要手写汇编。在某些系统层面，对性能至关重要、需要针对具体机器进行细致优化的地方，存在手写的汇编代码。例如，所有计算机的启动序列都是用汇编代码编写的。操作系统中用于线程或进程上下文切换的部分常常包含手写的汇编。对于这些短小而对性能至关重要的代码序列，人往往能写出比编译器优化得更好的汇编代码。 Lastly, there are some components of a computer system that just cannot be optimized sufficiently by compilers and require handwritten assembly. Some system levels have handwritten assembly code in areas where detailed machine-specific optimizations are critical for performance. For example, the boot sequence on all computers is written in assembly code. Operating systems often contain handwritten assembly for thread or process context-switching. Humans are often able to produce better-optimized assembly code than compilers for these short and performance-critical sequences. 接下来几章你将学到什么 What You Will Learn in the Coming Chapters 接下来的三章介绍三种不同风格的汇编。 第 7 章 和 第 8 章 介绍 x86_64 及其早期形式 IA32。 第 9 章 介绍 ARMv8-A 汇编，它是大多数现代 ARM 设备采用的 ISA，包括树莓派这样的单板计算机。 第 10 章 给出学习汇编的小结和一些关键要点。 The next three chapters cover three different flavors of assembly. Chapter 7 and Chapter 8 cover x86_64 and its earlier form, IA32. Chapter 9 covers ARMv8-A assembly, which is the ISA found on most modern ARM devices, including single-board computers like the Raspberry Pi. Chapter 10 contains a summary and some key takeaways for learning assembly. 译注 · 用 Mac 学汇编的建议 Apple Silicon Mac 的 CPU 是 ARM64，第 9 章（ARMv8-A）的内容最贴近你手头的机器（不过 macOS 的汇编语法和调用约定在细节上与 Linux 略有不同）；第 7、8 章的 x86 汇编则需要 x86 Linux 环境才能运行，或者至少用 gcc -S -target x86_64-linux-gnu 交叉生成汇编来对照阅读。 每种汇编风格实现的是不同的指令集架构（ISA）。回想一下， ISA 定义了指令集合及其二进制编码、CPU 寄存器集合，以及执行指令对 CPU 和存储器状态的影响。 Each of these different flavors of assembly implement different instruction set architectures (ISAs). Recall that an ISA defines the set of instructions and their binary encoding, the set of CPU registers, and the effects of executing instructions on the state of the CPU and memory. 在接下来的三章中，你会看到所有 ISA 之间的总体相似之处，包括都把 CPU 寄存器用作许多指令的操作数，以及每种 ISA 都提供类似类型的指令： In the following three chapters, you will see general similarities across all the ISAs, including that CPU registers are used as operands of many instructions, and that each ISA provides similar types of instructions: 执行算术和逻辑运算（如加法或按位与）的指令 instructions for computing arithmetic and logic operations, such as addition or bitwise AND 控制流指令，用于实现分支，如 if-else、循环以及函数调用和返回 instructions for control flow that are used to implement branching such as if-else, loops, and function call and return 数据移动指令，用于在 CPU 寄存器和存储器之间加载和存储值 instructions for data movement that load and store values between CPU registers and memory 向栈中压入和从栈中弹出值的指令。这些指令用来实现执行调用栈：函数调用时，一个新的栈帧（存放正在运行的函数的局部变量和参数）被加到栈顶；函数返回时，一个栈帧从栈顶移除。 instructions for pushing and popping values from the stack. These instructions are used to implement the execution call stack, where a new frame of stack memory (that stores a running function’s local variables and parameters) is added to the top of the stack on a function call, and a frame is removed from the top of the stack on a function return. C 编译器把 C 源代码翻译成某种特定 ISA 的指令集。编译器把 C 语句（包括循环、 if - else 、函数调用和变量访问）翻译成由该 ISA 定义、并由设计来执行该 ISA 指令的 CPU 所实现的一组特定指令。例如，编译器把 C 翻译成 x86 指令，在 Intel x86 处理器上执行；或者把 C 翻译成 ARM 指令，在 ARM 处理器上执行。 A C compiler translates C source code to a specific ISA instruction set. The compiler translates C statements, including loops, if - else , function calls, and variable access, to a specific set of instructions that are defined by the ISA and implemented by a CPU that is designed to execute instructions from the specific ISA. For example, a compiler translates C to x86 instructions for execution on an Intel x86 processor, or translates C to ARM instructions for execution on an ARM processor. 现代更新（截至 2026-11）· 在浏览器里看 C 被编译成什么汇编 读接下来几章时，可以配合开源网站 Compiler Explorer（ https://godbolt.org/ ）做练习。它在 GitHub 上的项目说明是「在浏览器里交互式地运行编译器，并与生成的汇编交互」（Run compilers interactively from your web browser and interact with the assembly）。 在网页里输入一段 C 代码，旁边就会显示编译器为它生成的汇编。2026 年 11 月抓取时，页面默认的编译器是 x86-64 gcc 16.2。用户可以换用别的编译器、填写编译选项，也可以设置成源码一改动就自动重新编译，还能生成 godbolt.org/z/… 形式的链接，把代码和输出分享给别人。 本书的 C 示例可以直接贴进去，把生成的汇编和书中的清单逐行对照。要注意，编译器版本和优化选项不同，生成的汇编也会不同。 来源： Compiler Explorer ； GitHub：compiler-explorer/compiler-explorer 在阅读本书汇编部分的各章时，你可能会注意到一些关键术语被重新定义了一遍，一些插图也被重复使用。为了更好地帮助其他计算机科学教师，我们把每一章都设计成可以在特定的学院和大学中独立使用。虽然每章的大部分内容都是独有的，但我们希望各章之间的共同之处，能帮助读者加深对不同汇编风格之间相似性的印象。 As you read the chapters in the assembly part of the book, you may notice that some key terms are defined again and that some figures are reproduced. To best aid other CS educators, we designed each chapter to be used independently at particular colleges and universities. While most of the material in each chapter is unique, we hope the commonalities between the chapters help reinforce the similarities between the different flavors of assembly in the mind of readers. 准备好学习汇编了吗？让我们直接潜下去！点击下面的链接访问你感兴趣的章节： Ready to learn assembly? Let’s dive right in! Follow the links below to visit particular chapters of interest: x86-64 汇编 x86-64 Assembly IA32 汇编 IA32 Assembly ARMv8-A 汇编 ARMv8-A Assembly

x: 说明 本文是个人学习用的 非官方 中英对照译文，原文： https://diveintosystems.org/book/C7-x86_64/basics.html 。 原书采用 CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 许可（禁止演绎）， 请勿公开传播本译文 。 标为「译注」「现代更新」的内容是译者补充，不代表原书作者观点；代码与原文逐字一致，未作改动。 7.1. Diving into Assembly: Basics 为了初步了解 x64 汇编，我们修改 第 6 章 中的 adder 函数，简化它的行为。修改后的函数（ adder2 ）如下： For a first look at x64 assembly, we modify the adder function from Chapter 6 to simplify its behavior. The modified function ( adder2 ) is shown below: #include <stdio.h> //adds two to an integer and returns the result int adder2(int a) { return a + 2; } int main(void){ int x = 40; x = adder2(x); printf("x is: %d\n", x); return 0; } 要编译这段代码，使用以下命令： To compile this code, use the following command: $ gcc -o adder adder.c 接下来，用 objdump 命令查看这段代码对应的汇编： Next, let’s view the corresponding assembly of this code by using the objdump command: $ objdump -d adder > output $ less output 用 less 查看文件 output 时，输入 /adder2 搜索与 adder2 相关的代码片段。与 adder2 相关的部分应该类似下面这样： Search for the code snippet associated with adder2 by typing /adder2 while examining the file output using less . The section associated with adder2 should look similar to the following: adder2 函数的汇编输出 Assembly output for the adder2 function 0000000000400526 <adder2>: 400526: 55 push %rbp 400527: 48 89 e5 mov %rsp,%rbp 40052a: 89 7d fc mov %edi,-0x4(%rbp) 40052d: 8b 45 fc mov -0x4(%rbp),%eax 400530: 83 c0 02 add $0x2,%eax 400533: 5d pop %rbp 400534: c3 retq 如果你还不明白这是怎么回事，不必担心。我们会在后面的小节中更详细地介绍汇编。目前，我们先来研究一下这些单独指令的结构。 Don’t worry if you don’t understand what’s going on just yet. We will cover assembly in greater detail in later sections. For now, let’s study the structure of these individual instructions. 上例中的每一行都包含一条指令在程序内存中的 64 位地址、与这条指令对应的字节，以及指令本身的文本表示。例如， 55 是指令 push %rbp 的机器码表示，这条指令位于程序内存中的地址 0x400526 处。注意， 0x400526 是与 push %rbp 指令相关的完整 64 位地址的缩写；为了便于阅读，前导零被省略了。 Each line in the preceding example contains an instruction’s 64-bit address in program memory, the bytes corresponding to the instruction, and the plaintext representation of the instruction itself. For example, 55 is the machine code representation of the instruction push %rbp , and the instruction occurs at address 0x400526 in program memory. Note that 0x400526 is an abbreviation of the full 64-bit address associated with the push %rbp instruction; the leading zeroes are ignored for readability. 要注意，一行 C 代码常常会被翻译成多条汇编指令。运算 a + 2 用 mov -0x4(%rbp), %eax 和 add $0x2, %eax 两条指令表示。 It is important to note that a single line of C code often translates to multiple instructions in assembly. Instruction Structure 每条指令由一个指明它做什么的操作码（ opcode ）和一个或多个告诉指令如何去做的 操作数 （operand）组成。例如，指令 add $0x2, %eax 的操作码是 add ，操作数是 $0x2 和 %eax 。 Each instruction consists of an operation code (or opcode ) that specifies what it does, and one or more operands that tell the instruction how to do it. Real World: Buffer Overflow C 语言不会自动做数组越界检查。访问数组边界以外的内存是有问题的，常常导致段错误之类的错误。然而，聪明的攻击者可以注入恶意代码，故意越过数组（也称为 缓冲区 ，buffer）的边界，迫使程序以非预期的方式执行。在最坏的情况下，攻击者可以运行代码获得 root 权限 ，也就是对计算机系统的操作系统级访问权。利用程序中已知的缓冲区越界错误来达到目的的软件，称为 缓冲区溢出攻击 （buffer overflow exploit）。 The C language does not perform automatic array bounds checking. Accessing memory outside of the bounds of an array is problematic and often results in errors such as segmentation faults. However, a clever attacker can inject malicious code that intentionally overruns the boundary of an array (also known as a buffer ) to force the program to execute in an unintended manner. In the worst cases, the attacker can run code that allows them to gain root privilege , or OS-level access to the computer system. A piece of software that takes advantage of the existence of a known buffer overrun error in a program is known as a buffer overflow exploit . 本节我们使用 GDB 和汇编语言，完整剖析缓冲区溢出攻击的机制。阅读本章之前，建议先看看讲解 用 GDB 检查汇编代码 的那一章。 In this section, we use GDB and assembly language to fully characterize the mechanics of a buffer overflow exploit. Prior to reading this chapter we encourage you to explore the chapter discussing GDB for inspecting assembly code . 7.10.1. 著名的缓冲区溢出案例 7.10.1. Famous Examples of Buffer Overflow 缓冲区溢出攻击出现于 20 世纪 80 年代，直到 21 世纪头几年一直是计算机行业的头号祸害。虽然许多现代操作系统已经能防御最简单的缓冲区溢出攻击，但粗心的编程错误仍然可能让现代程序门户大开。最近在 Skype 1 、Android 2 、Google Chrome 3 等软件中都发现过缓冲区溢出漏洞。 Buffer overflow exploits emerged in the 1980s and remained a chief scourge of the computing industry through the early parts of the 2000s. While many modern operating systems have protections against the simplest buffer overflow attacks, careless programming errors can still leave modern programs wide open to attack. Buffer overflow exploits have recently been discovered in Skype 1 , Android 2 , Google Chrome 3 , and others. 下面是几个著名的历史案例。 Here are some notable historic examples of buffer overflow exploits. 莫里斯蠕虫 （The Morris Worm） 莫里斯蠕虫 4 于 1988 年从 MIT 释放到 ARPANet 上（为的是掩盖它出自康奈尔大学一名学生之手），它利用了 UNIX finger 守护进程（ fingerd ）中的一个缓冲区越界漏洞。在 Linux 和其他类 UNIX 系统中， 守护进程 （daemon）是一类在后台持续运行的进程，通常执行清理和监控任务。 fingerd 守护进程返回关于某台计算机或某个人的友好报告。最要命的是，这个蠕虫的复制机制会把它多次发送到同一台计算机上，把系统拖到无法使用的地步。尽管作者声称这个蠕虫只是一次无害的智力练习，但复制机制让它极易传播，也很难清除。此后多年，还有其他蠕虫利用缓冲区溢出攻击未经授权进入系统，著名的有 Code Red（2001）、MS-SQLSlammer（2003）和 W32/Blaster（2003）。 The Morris Worm The Morris Worm 4 was released in 1988 on ARPANet from MIT (to hide that it was written by a student at Cornell) and exploited a buffer overrun vulnerability that existed in the UNIX finger daemon ( fingerd ). In Linux and other UNIX-like systems, a daemon is a type of process that continuously executes in the background, usually performing clean-up and monitoring tasks. The fingerd daemon returns a user-friendly report on a computer or person. Most crucially, the worm had a replication mechanism that caused it to be sent to the same computer multiple times, bogging down the system to an unusable state. Although the author claimed that the worm was meant as a harmless intellectual exercise, the replication mechanism enabled the worm to spread easily and made it difficult to remove. In future years, other worms would employ buffer overflow exploits to gain unauthorized access into systems. Notable examples include Code Red (2001), MS-SQLSlammer (2003), and W32/Blaster (2003). AOL 聊天大战 （AOL Chat Wars） 前微软工程师 David Auerbach 5 详细讲述了他在 20 世纪 90 年代末把微软的 Messenger Service（MMS）与 AOL Instant Messenger 打通时遭遇的一次缓冲区溢出。那时，想和亲友即时通信（IM），AOL Instant Messenger（AIM）是 不二之选 。微软想在这个市场站稳脚跟，就在 MMS 中设计了一个功能，让 MMS 用户能和他们的 AIM「好友」聊天。AOL 很不高兴，给服务器打了补丁，让 MMS 无法再连上。微软工程师想出办法让 MMS 客户端模仿 AIM 客户端发给 AOL 服务器的消息，使 AOL 难以区分消息来自 MMS 还是 AIM。AOL 的回应是改变 AIM 发送消息的方式，MMS 工程师则相应地修改客户端消息，使之再次与 AIM 的一致。这场「聊天大战」一直持续，直到 AOL 开始利用 自家客户端里 的一个缓冲区溢出错误来验证发来的消息是否来自 AIM 客户端。由于 MMS 客户端没有同样的漏洞，聊天大战就此结束，AOL 获胜。 AOL Chat Wars David Auerbach 5 , a former Microsoft engineer, detailed his experience with a buffer overflow during his efforts to integrate Microsoft’s Messenger Service (MMS) with AOL Instant Messenger in the late 1990s. Back then, AOL Instant Messenger (AIM) was the service to use if you wanted to instant message (or IM) friends and family. Microsoft tried to gain a foothold in this market by designing a feature in MMS that enabled MMS users to talk to their AIM “buddies.” Displeased, AOL patched their servers so that MMS could no longer connect to them. Microsoft engineers figured out a way for MMS clients to mimic the messages sent by AIM clients to AOL servers, making it difficult for AOL to distinguish between messages received by MMS and AIM. AOL responded by changing the way AIM sent messages, and MMS engineers duly changed their client’s messages to once again match AIM’s. This “chat war” continued until AOL started using a buffer overflow error in their own client to verify that sent messages came from AIM clients. Since MMS clients did not have the same vulnerability, the chat wars ended, with AOL as the victor. 7.10.2. 初探：猜谜游戏 7.10.2. The header file other.h contains the definition of the getSecretCode and calculateValue functions, but it is unavailable to us. How then can a user beat the program? Brute forcing the solution will take too long. One strategy is to analyze the secret executable in GDB and step through the assembly to reveal the secret number and string. The process of examining assembly code to reveal knowledge of how it works is commonly referred to as reverse engineering assembly. Readers comfortable enough with their GDB and assembly reading skills should be able to figure out what the secret number and the secret string should be by using GDB to reverse engineer their values. 不过，还有另一种更狡猾的取胜方法。 However, there is a different, sneakier way to win. 7.10.3. 仔细看看（C 之下） 7.10.3. A Smarter Buffer Overflow: Second Attempt 第一个例子用垃圾数据覆盖了保存的 %rbp 和返回地址，粉碎了栈，导致程序崩溃。如果攻击者的目的只是让程序崩溃，到这一步就已经满意了。但我们的目标是骗猜谜游戏返回 0，表示我们赢了。为此，我们要用比垃圾值更有意义的数据填充调用栈。例如，可以覆盖栈，把返回地址替换成 endGame 的地址。这样，当程序试图从 main 返回时，它会去执行 endGame ，而不是因段错误崩溃。 Our first example smashed the stack by overwriting the %rbp register and return address with junk, causing the program to crash. An attacker whose goal is to simply crash a program would be satisfied at this point. However, our goal is to trick the guessing game to return 0, indicating that we won the game. We accomplish this by filling the call stack with data more meaningful than junk values. For example, we could overwrite the stack so that the return address is replaced with the address of endGame . Common Instructions 本节讨论几条常用的汇编指令。 表 1 列出了 x86（因而也是 x64）汇编中最基础的指令。 In this section, we discuss several common assembly instructions. Table 1 lists the most foundational instructions in x86 (and thus x64) assembly. 表 1. 最常用的指令 Table 1. Most Common Instructions 指令 含义 mov S, D S → D（把 S 的值复制到 D） add S, D S + D → D（把 S 加到 D 上，结果存入 D） sub S, D D - S → D（ 从 D 中减去 S，结果存入 D） Instruction Translation mov S, D S → D (copies value of S into D) add S, D S + D → D (adds S to D and stores result in D) sub S, D D - S → D (subtracts S from D and stores result in D) 因此，指令序列 Therefore, the sequence of instructions mov -0x4(%rbp),%eax add $0x2,%eax 的含义是： translates to: 把 内存 中位置 %rbp + -0x4 处的值（M[ %rbp - 0x4]）复制到寄存器 %eax 。 Copy the value at location %rbp + -0x4 in memory (M[ %rbp - 0x4]) to register %eax . 把值 0x2 加到寄存器 %eax 上，结果存入寄存器 %eax 。 Add the value 0x2 to register %eax , and store the result in register %eax . 表 1 中的三条指令也是那些维护程序栈（即 调用栈 ，call stack）组织结构的指令的基础。回想一下，寄存器 %rbp 和 %rsp 分别指 帧 指针和 栈 指针，编译器把它们保留用于调用栈的管理。回想我们之前对 程序内存 的讨论，调用栈通常存放局部变量和参数，帮助程序跟踪自己的执行（见 图 1 ）。在 x86-64 系统上，执行栈向 较低 的地址增长。和所有栈数据结构一样，操作都发生在栈的「顶部」。 The three instructions shown in Table 1 also form the building blocks for instructions that maintain the organization of the program stack (i.e., the call stack ). Recall that registers %rbp and %rsp refer to the frame pointer and stack pointer, respectively, and are reserved by the compiler for call stack management. Recall from our earlier discussion on program memory that the call stack typically stores local variables and parameters and helps the program track its own execution (see Figure 1 ). On x86-64 systems, the execution stack grows toward lower addresses. Like all stack data structures, operations occur at the “top” of the stack. 图 1. 程序地址空间的组成部分 Figure 1. The parts of a program’s address space x86-64 ISA 提供了两条指令（ 表 2 ）来简化调用栈的管理。 The x86-64 ISA provides two instructions ( Table 2 ) to simplify call stack management. 表 2. 栈管理指令 Table 2. Stack Management Instructions 指令 Instruction 含义 Translation push S push S 把 S 的一个副本压入栈顶。等价于： Pushes a copy of S onto the top of the stack. Equivalent to: sub $0x8, %rsp mov S, (%rsp) pop D pop D 把栈顶元素弹出，放到位置 D。等价于： Pops the top element off the stack and places it in location D. Equivalent to: mov (%rsp), D add $0x8, %rsp 注意， 表 1 中的三条指令需要两个操作数，而 表 2 中的 push 和 pop 指令各自只需要一个操作数。 Notice that while the three instructions in Table 1 require two operands, the push and pop instructions in Table 2 require only one operand apiece. 7.2.1. 把一切组合起来：一个更具体的例子 7.2.1. Putting It All Together: A More Concrete Example 我们来仔细看看 adder2 函数： Let’s take a closer look at the adder2 function: //adds two to an integer and returns the result int adder2(int a) { return a + 2; } 以及它对应的汇编代码： and its corresponding assembly code: 0000000000400526 <adder2>: 400526: 55 push %rbp 400527: 48 89 e5 mov %rsp,%rbp 40052a: 89 7d fc mov %edi,-0x4(%rbp) 40052d: 8b 45 fc mov -0x4(%rbp),%eax 400530: 83 c0 02 add $0x2,%eax 400533: 5d pop %rbp 400534: c3 retq 这段汇编代码由一条 push 指令、接着的三条 mov 指令、一条 add 指令、一条 pop 指令，最后是一条 retq 指令组成。要理解 CPU 如何执行这组指令，我们需要重温 程序内存 的结构。回想一下，每次程序执行时，操作系统都会为新程序分配地址空间（也称为 虚拟内存 ，virtual memory）。 虚拟内存 和与之相关的 进程 概念会在第 13 章中更详细地介绍；目前，只需把进程看作对运行中程序的抽象，把虚拟内存看作分配给单个进程的内存。每个进程都有自己的一块称为 调用栈 的内存区域。记住，调用栈位于进程/虚拟内存中，而不像寄存器那样位于 CPU 上。 The assembly code consists of a push instruction, followed by three mov instructions, an add instruction, a pop instruction, and finally a retq instruction. To understand how the CPU executes this set of instructions, we need to revisit the structure of program memory . Recall that every time a program executes, the operating system allocates the new program’s address space (also known as virtual memory ). Virtual memory and the related concept of processes are covered in greater detail in Chapter 13; for now, it suffices to think of a process as the abstraction of a running program and virtual memory as the memory that is allocated to a single process. Every process has its own region of memory called the call stack . Keep in mind that the call stack is located in process/virtual memory, unlike registers (which are located on the CPU). 图 2 描绘了执行 adder2 函数之前调用栈和寄存器的一个示例状态。 Figure 2 depicts a sample state of the call stack and registers prior to the execution of the adder2 function. 图 2. 执行之前的执行栈 Figure 2. Execution stack prior to execution 注意，栈向 较低 的地址增长。寄存器 %eax 中是一个垃圾值。按照惯例， adder2 函数的唯一参数（ a ）存放在寄存器 %rdi 中。由于 a 是 int 类型，它被存放在组成部分寄存器 %edi 中，如 图 2 所示。同样，由于 adder2 函数返回 int ，返回值使用的是组成部分寄存器 %eax 而不是 %rax 。 Notice that the stack grows toward lower addresses. Register %eax contains a junk value. The single parameter to the adder2 function ( a ) is stored in register %rdi by convention. Since a is of type int , it is stored in component register %edi , which is shown in Figure 2 . Likewise, since the adder2 function returns an int , component register %eax is used for the return value instead of %rax . 为了让图更易读，程序内存代码段中与指令相关的地址（0x400526–0x400534）被缩写成了（0x526–0x534）。同样，程序内存调用栈段中的地址也从 0x7fffffffdd28–0x7fffffffdd1c 缩写成了 0xd28–0xd1c。实际上，调用栈的地址在程序内存中比代码段的地址高得多。 The addresses associated with the instructions in the code segment of program memory (0x400526-0x400534) have been shortened to (0x526-0x534) to improve figure readability. Likewise, the addresses associated with the call stack segment of program memory have been shortened to 0xd28-0xd1c from 0x7fffffffdd28 - 0x7fffffffdd1c. In truth, call stack addresses occur at much higher addresses in program memory than code segment addresses. 请密切注意寄存器 %rsp 和 %rbp 的初始值：它们分别是 0xd28 和 0xd40。在后面的各个图中，红色（左上角）箭头直观地指出当前正在执行的指令。 %rip 寄存器（即指令指针）显示下一条要执行的指令。最初， %rip 中存放的是地址 0x526，对应于 adder2 函数中的第一条指令。 Pay close attention to the initial values of registers %rsp and %rbp : they are 0xd28 and 0xd40, respectively. The red (upper-left) arrow in the following figures visually indicates the currently executing instruction. The %rip register (or instruction pointer) shows the next instruction to execute. Initially, %rip contains address 0x526, which corresponds to the first instruction in the adder2 function. 第一条指令（ push %rbp ）把 %rbp 中的值（即 0xd40）的一个副本放到栈顶。执行之后， %rip 寄存器前进到下一条要执行的指令的地址（0x527）。 push 指令把栈指针减 8（栈「增长」8 个字节），使 %rsp 的新值为 0xd20。回想一下， push %rbp 指令等价于： The first instruction ( push %rbp ) places a copy of the value in %rbp (or 0xd40) on top of the stack. After it executes, the %rip register advances to the address of the next instruction to execute (0x527). The push instruction decrements the stack pointer by 8 (“growing” the stack by 8 bytes), resulting in a new %rsp value of 0xd20. Recall that the push %rbp instruction is equivalent to: sub $8, %rsp mov %rbp, (%rsp) 换句话说，就是把栈指针减去 8，然后把 %rbp 内容的一个副本放到对栈指针解引用所指向的位置 (%rsp) 。 In other words, subtract 8 from the stack pointer and place a copy of the contents of %rbp in the location pointed to by the dereferenced stack pointer, (%rsp) . 回想一下， mov 指令的结构是 mov S,D ，其中 S 是源位置，D 是目标位置。因此，下一条指令（ mov %rsp, %rbp ）把 %rbp 的值更新为 0xd20。寄存器 %rip 前进到下一条要执行的指令的地址，即 0x52a。 Recall that the structure of the mov instruction is mov S,D , where S is the source location, and D is the destination. Thus, the next instruction ( mov %rsp, %rbp ) updates the value of %rbp to 0xd20. This is a bit more complicated than the last mov instruction. Let’s parse it piece by piece. First, recall that the first parameter to any function is stored in register %rdi . Since a is of type int , the compiler stores the first parameter in component register %edi . Next, the operand -0x4(%rbp) translates to M[ %rbp - 0x4]. Since %rbp contains the value 0xd20, subtracting 4 from it yields 0xd1c. Therefore, the mov instruction copies the value of register %edi (or 0x28) to location 0xd1c on the stack. The instruction pointer advances to address 0x52d, the next address to be executed. 注意，存放值 0x28 并不影响栈指针（ %rsp ）。因此，就程序而言，这个栈的「顶部」仍然是地址 0xd20。 Note that storing the value 0x28 does not affect the stack pointer ( %rsp ). Therefore, as far as the program is concerned, the “top” of this stack is still address 0xd20. 下一条 mov 指令（ mov -0x4(%rbp), %eax ）复制栈位置 0xd1c 处的值（即 M[ %rbp - 0x4]，也就是 0x28），并把它存入寄存器 %eax 。寄存器 %rip 前进到下一条要执行的指令，即 0x530。 The next mov instruction ( mov -0x4(%rbp), %eax ) copies the value at stack location 0xd1c (i.e., M[ %rbp - 0x4] or 0x28) and stores it in register %eax . Register %rip advances to the next instruction to be executed, or 0x530. 接下来执行 add $0x2, %eax 。回想一下， add 指令的形式是 add S,D ，它把 S + D 的值放到目标 D 中。所以， add $0x2, %eax 把常数值 0x2 加到 %eax 中存放的值（即 0x28）上，结果值 0x2A 被存入寄存器 %eax 。寄存器 %rip 前进，指向下一条要执行的指令，即 0x533。 Next, add $0x2, %eax is executed. Recall that the add instruction has the form add S,D and places the quantity S + D in the destination D. So, add $0x2, %eax adds the constant value 0x2 to the value stored in %eax (or 0x28), resulting in the value 0x2A being stored in register %eax . Register %rip advances to point to the next instruction to be executed, or 0x533. 接下来执行的指令是 pop %rbp 。这条指令把值从调用栈顶「弹出」，放到目标寄存器 %rbp 中。回想一下，这条指令等价于下面这两条指令的序列： The next instruction that executes is pop %rbp . This instruction “pops” the value off the top of the call stack and places it in destination register %rbp . Recall that this instruction is equivalent to the following sequence of two instructions: mov (%rsp), %rbp add $8, %rsp 回想一下，栈顶是 0xd20，因为 %rsp 中存放的就是这个值。因此，这条指令一执行， (%rsp) 的值（即 M[0xd20]）就被复制到寄存器 %rbp 中。于是， %rbp 现在存放的是值 0xd40。栈指针 增加 8，因为栈向较低的地址增长（相应地，向较高的地址 收缩 ）。 %rsp 的新值是 0xd28， %rip 现在指向最后一条要执行的指令的地址（即 0x534）。 Recall that the top of the stack is 0xd20, since that is the value stored in %rsp . Therefore, once this instruction executes, the value (%rsp) (i.e., M[0xd20]) is copied into register %rbp . Thus, %rbp now contains the value 0xd40. The stack pointer increments by 8, since the stack grows toward lower addresses (and consequently shrinks toward higher ones). The new value of %rsp is 0xd28, and %rip now points to the address of the last instruction to execute (i.e., 0x534). 最后执行的指令是 retq 。我们会在后面讨论函数调用的小节中更详细地讲 retq 做了什么，目前只需知道它为从函数返回准备好调用栈。按照惯例，寄存器 %rax 总是存放返回值（如果有的话）。在这个例子中，由于 adder2 的返回类型是 int ，返回值存放在组成部分寄存器 %eax 中，函数返回值 0x2A，即 42。 The last instruction executed is retq . We will talk more about what happens with retq in future sections when we discuss function calls, but for now it suffices to know that it prepares the call stack for returning from a function. By convention, the register %rax always contains the return value (if one exists). In this case, because adder2 is of type int , the return value is stored in component register %eax , and the function returns the value 0x2A, or 42. 在继续之前，注意寄存器 %rsp 和 %rbp 的最终值分别是 0xd28 和 0xd40，与 函数开始执行时的值相同 ！对于调用栈来说，这是正常的、预期中的行为。调用栈的作用是在程序的上下文中，存放每个函数执行时的临时变量和数据。一旦函数执行完毕，栈就会回到函数调用之前的状态。因此，常常会在函数的开头看到下面这两条指令： Before we continue, note that the final values in registers %rsp and %rbp are 0xd28 and 0xd40, respectively, which are the same values as when the function started executing ! This is normal and expected behavior with the call stack. The purpose of the call stack is to store the temporary variables and data of each function as it executes in the context of a program. Once a function completes executing, the stack returns to the state it was in prior to the function call. As a result, it is common to see the following two instructions at the beginning of a function: push %rbp mov %rsp, %rbp 在函数的结尾看到下面这两条指令： and the following two instructions at the end of a function: pop %rbp retq

Arithmetic Instructions x86 ISA 实现了若干条与 ALU 执行的算术运算相对应的指令。 表 1 列出了阅读汇编时可能遇到的几条算术指令。 The x86 ISA implements several instructions that correspond to arithmetic operations performed by the ALU. Common Arithmetic Instructions. 指令 含义 add S, D S + D → D sub S, D D - S → D inc D D + 1 → D dec D D - 1 → D neg D -D → D imul S, D S × D → D idiv S %rax / S：商 → %rax ，余数 → %rdx Instruction Translation add S, D S + D → D sub S, D D - S → D inc D D + 1 → D dec D D - 1 → D neg D -D → D imul S, D S × D → D idiv S %rax / S: quotient → %rax , remainder → %rdx add 和 sub 指令对应于加法和减法，各自接收两个操作数。接下来的三项是单寄存器指令，分别对应 C 中的自增（ x++ ）、自减（ x-- ）和取负（ -x ）运算。乘法指令对两个操作数进行运算，并把乘积放到目标中。如果乘积需要超过 64 位来表示，结果会被截断为 64 位。 The add and sub instructions correspond to addition and subtraction and take two operands each. The next three entries show the single-register instructions for the increment ( x++ ), decrement ( x-- ), and negation ( -x ) operations in C. The multiplication instruction operates on two operands and places the product in the destination. If the product requires more than 64 bits to represent, the value is truncated to 64 bits. 除法指令的工作方式略有不同。在执行 idiv 指令之前，假定寄存器 %rax 中存放着被除数。对操作数 S 执行 idiv ，会用 S 去除 %rax 的内容，把商放到寄存器 %rax 中，余数放到寄存器 %rdx 中。 The division instruction works a little differently. Prior to the execution of the idiv instruction, it is assumed that register %rax contains the dividend. Calling idiv on operand S divides the contents of %rax by S and places the quotient in register %rax and the remainder in register %rdx . 译注 更准确地说，64 位的 idiv 把 %rdx 和 %rax 拼成的 128 位数（ %rdx 是高 64 位）当作被除数。所以在 idiv 之前，编译器通常会先用一条 cqto （Intel 语法叫 cqo ）指令把 %rax 符号扩展到 %rdx 。读汇编时看到紧挨着 idiv 的 cqto / cltd ，就是这个原因。 7.3.1. 移位指令 7.3.1. Bit Shifting Instructions 移位指令让编译器能执行移位运算。乘法和除法指令通常需要很长时间才能执行完。对于是 2 的幂的乘数和除数，移位为编译器提供了一条捷径。例如，要计算 77 * 4 ，大多数编译器会把这个运算翻译成 77 << 2 ，以避免使用 imul 指令。同样，要计算 77 / 4 ，编译器通常会把这个运算翻译成 77 >> 2 ，以避免使用 idiv 指令。 Bit shifting instructions enable the compiler to perform bit shifting operations. Multiplication and division instructions typically take a long time to execute. Bit shifting offers the compiler a shortcut for multiplicands and divisors that are powers of 2. For example, to compute 77 * 4 , most compilers will translate this operation to 77 << 2 to avoid the use of an imul instruction. Likewise, to compute 77 / 4 , a compiler typically translates this operation to 77 >> 2 to avoid using the idiv instruction. 记住，左移和右移会根据目标是算术（有符号）移位还是逻辑（无符号）移位，被翻译成不同的指令。 Keep in mind that left and right bit shift translate to different instructions based on whether the goal is an arithmetic (signed) or logical (unsigned) shift. 表 2. 移位指令 Table 2. Bit Shift Instructions 指令 含义 算术还是逻辑？ sal v, D D << v → D 算术 shl v, D D << v → D 逻辑 sar v, D D >> v → D 算术 shr v, D D >> v → D 逻辑 Instruction Translation Arithmetic or Logical? sal v, D D << v → D arithmetic shl v, D D << v → D logical sar v, D D >> v → D arithmetic shr v, D D >> v → D logical 每条移位指令接收两个操作数，一个通常是寄存器（用 D 表示），另一个是移位量（ v ）。在 64 位系统上，移位量编码为单个字节（因为移位超过 63 位没有意义）。移位量 v 必须是一个常数，或者存放在寄存器 %cl 中。 Each shift instruction takes two operands, one which is usually a register (denoted by D) and the other which is a shift value ( v ). On 64-bit systems, the shift value is encoded as a single byte (since it doesn’t make sense to shift past 63). The shift value v must either be a constant or stored in register %cl . 原书注 · 不同版本的指令有助于在汇编层面区分类型（Different Versions of Instructions Help Distinguish Types at an Assembly Level） 在汇编层面，没有类型的概念。不过，回想一下，编译器会根据类型使用组成部分寄存器。同样，回想一下，右移的行为取决于值是有符号还是无符号的。在汇编层面，编译器用不同的指令来区分逻辑移位和算术移位！ At the assembly level, there is no notion of types. However, recall that the compiler will use component registers based on types. Similarly, recall that shift right works differently depending on whether or not the value is signed or unsigned. At the assembly level, the compiler uses separate instructions to distinguish between logical and arithmetic shifts! 7.3.2. 位运算指令 7.3.2. Bitwise Instructions 位运算指令让编译器能对数据执行位运算。编译器使用位运算的一种方式是进行某些优化。例如，编译器可能会选择用运算 77 & 3 来实现 77 mod 4，而不用代价更高的 idiv 指令。 Bitwise instructions enable the compiler to perform bitwise operations on data. One way the compiler uses bitwise operations is for certain optimizations. For example, a compiler may choose to implement 77 mod 4 with the operation 77 & 3 in lieu of the more expensive idiv instruction. 表 3 列出了常用的位运算指令。 Table 3 lists common bitwise instructions. 表 3. 位运算 Table 3. Bitwise Operations 指令 含义 and S, D S & D → D or S, D S ` xor S, D S ^ D → D not D ~ D → D Instruction Translation and S, D S & D → D or S, D S ` xor S, D S ^ D → D not D ~ D → D 记住，按位取反 not 与取负（ neg ）不同。 not 指令只翻转各位，不加 1。小心不要混淆这两条指令。 Remember that bitwise not is distinct from negation ( neg ). The not instruction flips the bits but does not add 1. Be careful not to confuse these two instructions. 原书警示 · 只在 C 代码确实需要时才使用位运算！（Use bitwise operations only when needed in your C code!） 读完本节，你可能很想把 C 代码中常见的算术运算替换成移位和其他位运算。我们 不 建议这样做。大多数现代编译器都足够聪明，会在合适的时候用位运算替换简单的算术运算，程序员不必亲自去做。一般来说，程序员应当尽可能把代码的可读性放在首位，避免过早优化。 After reading this section, it may be tempting to replace common arithmetic operations in your C code with bitwise shifts and other operations. This is not recommended. Most modern compilers are smart enough to replace simple arithmetic operations with bitwise operations when it makes sense, making it unnecessary for the programmer to do so. As a general rule, programmers should prioritize code readability whenever possible and avoid premature optimization. 7.3.3. 加载有效地址指令 7.3.3. The Load Effective Address Instruction lea 跟它有什么关系（有什么关系）？ What’s lea got to do (got to do) with it? lea 不就是加载一个有效地址吗？ What’s lea, but an effective address loading? ～向 Tina Turner 致歉 ~With apologies to Tina Turner 译注 这两句套用了 Tina Turner 的名曲《What’s Love Got to Do with It》（爱情与它何干），把 love 换成了读音相近的 lea。 最后我们来看 加载有效地址 （load effective address）指令，即 lea 指令，它可能是最让学生头疼的算术指令。传统上，它被用作快速计算某个内存位置地址的方法。 lea 指令使用的操作数结构与我们迄今见过的相同，但它 不 进行内存查找。无论操作数中的数据是什么类型（无论是常数值还是地址）， lea 都只是执行算术运算。 We finally come to the load effective address or lea instruction, which is probably the arithmetic instruction that causes students the most consternation. It is traditionally used as a fast way to compute the address of a location in memory. The lea instruction operates on the same operand structure that we’ve seen thus far but does not include a memory lookup. Regardless of the type of data contained in the operand (whether it be a constant value or an address), lea simply performs arithmetic. 例如，假设寄存器 %rax 中存放常数值 0x5，寄存器 %rdx 中存放常数值 0x4，寄存器 %rcx 中存放值 0x808（它恰好是一个地址）。 表 4 描绘了一些 lea 操作示例、它们的含义以及对应的值。 For example, suppose register %rax contains the constant value 0x5, register %rdx contains the constant value 0x4, and register %rcx contains the value 0x808 (which happens to be an address). Table 4 depicts some example lea operations, their translations, and corresponding values. 表 4. lea 操作示例 Table 4. Example lea Operations 指令 含义 值 lea 8(%rax), %rax 8 + %rax → %rax 13 → %rax lea (%rax, %rdx), %rax %rax + %rdx → %rax 9 → %rax lea (,%rax,4), %rax %rax × 4 → %rax 20 → %rax lea -0x8(%rcx), %rax %rcx - 8 → %rax 0x800 → %rax lea -0x4(%rcx, %rdx, 2), %rax %rcx + %rdx × 2 - 4 → %rax 0x80c → %rax Instruction Translation Value lea 8(%rax), %rax 8 + %rax → %rax 13 → %rax lea (%rax, %rdx), %rax %rax + %rdx → %rax 9 → %rax lea (,%rax,4), %rax %rax × 4 → %rax 20 → %rax lea -0x8(%rcx), %rax %rcx - 8 → %rax 0x800 → %rax lea -0x4(%rcx, %rdx, 2), %rax %rcx + %rdx × 2 - 4 → %rax 0x80c → %rax 在所有情况下， lea 指令都是对源 S 所指定的操作数执行算术运算，并把结果放到目标操作数 D 中。 mov 指令与 lea 指令完全相同， 只是 如果源操作数是内存形式， mov 指令 必须 把源操作数的内容当作内存位置来处理。与之不同， lea 执行同样（有时很复杂）的操作数算术运算，但 不 进行内存查找，这使得编译器能巧妙地用 lea 来替代某些类型的算术运算。 In all cases, the lea instruction performs arithmetic on the operand specified by the source S and places the result in the destination operand D. The mov instruction is identical to the lea instruction except that the mov instruction is required to treat the contents in the source operand as a memory location if it is in a memory form. In contrast, lea performs the same (sometimes complicated) operand arithmetic without the memory lookup, enabling the compiler to cleverly use lea as a substitution for some types of arithmetic.
